She grins at Carl and apologizes, and Donut, smelling of lilacs, cheers that they can go dancing.

entities.name: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet
aka: Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet

tagline.text: The Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet is Donut's first armour: silver fae-steel scale draped over her back half like a skirt, with a slot for her tail and two points of Dexterity. Not the best protection, its description admits, but it makes her backside look oh so pretty.
Donut's old crupper has made way for a chain mail one, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. Its two points of Dexterity were great on the first floor and are laughably weak now.

description.text: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet. Boy is that a fucking mouthful. By the gods. +2 to Dexterity. Light and flexible, this scale armor is made from Fae Steel. While not as strong as Elven mail or even good Orcish steel, it's the strongest alloy that fairy folk can wear. It's not the best protection, but it'll make your ass look oh so pretty.

beats.headline: Her first piece of armour
beats.text: Donut's boss box holds her first piece of armour. After several minutes of fury over the tattoo on her back, she moves on, and with a pop silver scale appears draped over the back half of her body, reaching about halfway to the floor: like a skirt, almost, open under her stomach, with a slot especially for her tail. She turns in circles trying to look at it. How does it look? Does it cover the tattoo? It doesn't, Carl tells her, not even close, but it looks great.
beats.gist: Donut's boss box holds a silver scale skirt, her first armour; it leaves her tattoo uncovered.

beats.headline: Lifted for a tattoo
beats.text: Edgar has to tattoo Donut, quickly, and the best place is her right flank, over a patch about as big as his foot. Someone lift her camouflage suit and crupper for me, he says. Donut agrees only if Carl gets a matching one, and then the ghillie suit disappears, and the crupper. She turns her tail to Rosetta and refuses Carl's idea of a tramp stamp. Rosetta goes to work with scissors and then a razor, while Donut asks Edgar whether it could be a flower.
beats.gist: Rosetta clips and shaves Donut's right flank for Edgar's tattoo after her ghillie suit and crupper vanish.

beats.headline: Retired for chain mail
beats.text: A box has given Donut a plain silver crupper of fine chain mail, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. Her old one, the Enchanted Fae-Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, has been on her backside since the goblin-baby incident on the very first floor, and its plus two to dexterity was great at the time and is laughably weak now. She removes the old mail, briefly showing the shaved patch with its tattoo of a dog licking itself, and the new armour appears. It's much lighter, she says. More elegant.
beats.gist: Donut trades her Enchanted Fae-Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet for a box's silver chain mail crupper.

relations.note: together they make her jingle when she walks

recap.text: Donut's boss box holds her first piece of armour, and she spends several minutes furious over the tattoo on her back. With a pop, silver scale appears over her back half, hanging halfway to the floor like a skirt, with a slot for her tail. She turns in circles and asks if it covers the tattoo. Carl tells her it doesn't, not even close, but it looks great.

Edgar must tattoo Donut quickly, and the best place is her right flank, over a patch about as big as his foot. He asks someone to lift her camouflage suit and crupper, and Donut agrees only if Carl gets a matching one; the ghillie suit and crupper vanish. She turns her tail to Rosetta and refuses Carl's tramp stamp idea. Rosetta goes to work with scissors, then a razor, while Donut asks Edgar whether it could be a flower.

A box gives Donut a plain silver crupper of fine chain mail, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion. She removes her old Enchanted Fae-Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, worn since the goblin-baby incident on the very first floor, its plus two to dexterity now laughably weak. For a moment the shaved patch shows, with its tattoo of a dog licking itself, and the new armour appears. It is much lighter, she says, and more elegant.

tagline.text: A Sapper's Table is a workbench sold in safe room stores, and Carl's new Demolitions Workshop menu will not open unless he is standing in front of one.

Carl has a Sapper's Table of his own now, out of a Gold Sapper's Box: a crafting table like his engineering and alchemy tables, where the explosives and traps he makes don't lose stability or go off early.
Carl's Sapper's Table stands in his crafting space, where he expects to spend most of his time, and he spends two upgrade coupons to take it to level three.
At level five, Carl's sapper's table is still better for building explosives from scratch than the bench in his new bomber's studio.

beats.headline: A menu that needs a table
beats.text: Carl's explosives skills have reached five, and he has a new one, IED, at level three. An entire new menu appears in his interface, titled Demolitions Workshop. He clicks on it and receives an error: he may only access this menu when he is standing in front of a Sapper's Table, a workbench he may purchase from a Safe Room store. Interesting. That is something to explore if they ever make it that far.
beats.gist: Carl's explosives skills reach five, unlocking IED, but his Demolitions Workshop menu requires a Sapper's Table.

beats.headline: It nearly knocks him over
beats.text: Carl's trap achievement pays out a Gold Sapper's Box with two items in it. The first is a Sapper's table that practically knocks him over when it appears, a table just like his engineering and alchemy tables. Its description says explosives and traps created at it don't lose stability and can't be prematurely set off. The second item is ten proximity triggers, which only attach to a trap at a Sapper's Table.
beats.gist: Carl's trap achievement pays out a Gold Sapper's Box holding a Sapper's table and ten proximity triggers.

beats.headline: Against one wall
beats.text: In the crafting space, Carl shoves the alchemy table against a wall, and it clicks loudly into place with upgrade menus over it; he loads it with every alchemy item he owns. Then the sapper's table goes against one wall and his engineering table against the other. He expects to spend most of his time at the sapper table, but for now he stands at the engineering one, laying out the Goo-inator 3000, the Gorgon Marital Aid and a dozen slightly-too-small goblin tools.
beats.gist: Carl shoves the alchemy table against a wall, then sets up his engineering table opposite it.

beats.headline: Level three
beats.text: At the saferoom in station 281, inside a glass-fronted donut shop, Carl asks the bopca, Nodd, for a black coffee and the crafting table menu. It is a long list, most of it useless, at about 25,000 gold a table. He slides one of his two free table coupons across for the one he has been looking for. Then he presents his two upgrade coupons, hesitates over whether this is the right move, and asks to upgrade his Sapper's table to level three. A note in the cookbook has already told him what a level-three table does: it lets you infuse bombs.
beats.gist: Carl presents his upgrade coupons and asks Nodd to raise his Sapper's table to level three.

beats.headline: A copy, less scorched
beats.text: Carl's training room can teach him his workshop tables as well, and they need only be installed in his crafting studio. He finds Sapper's Table on the list and clicks it. A familiar level-five table pops up out of the ground, identical to his own, though less scorched, and his hand doesn't come away sticky with the residue the hobgoblin disco ball left. Instead of the usual multi-armed trainer, a badger with an eyepatch and a hook for a hand fades in, decides Carl is practically ready to teach him, and tells him the weapon he wants needs a different table altogether.
beats.gist: Carl clicks Sapper's Table, and a badger says his weapon needs another table.

recap.text: Carl's explosives skill reaches five, and a new skill, IED, arrives at level three. It opens a menu titled Demolitions Workshop, but he clicks it and gets an error: he must stand in front of a Sapper's Table, sold in a Safe Room store. His trap achievement then pays out a Gold Sapper's Box, and the table inside nearly knocks him over. The box also holds ten proximity triggers.

Carl shoves the alchemy table against a wall and loads it with every alchemy item he owns, lays the Goo-inator 3000, the Gorgon Marital Aid and a dozen slightly-too-small goblin tools on the engineering table. In a glass-fronted donut shop in station 281, he orders coffee from the bopca Nodd and spends a free coupon on the table he wants. Hesitating, he hands both upgrade coupons across to raise his Sapper's table to level three, which lets him infuse bombs.

Carl clicks Sapper's Table on his training room's list, and a level-five copy of his own table pops up from the ground in his crafting studio, less scorched, with no residue from the hobgoblin disco ball to stick to his hand. A badger with an eyepatch and a hook for a hand fades in instead of the multi-armed trainer. He decides Carl is practically ready to teach him, then says the weapon Carl wants needs a different table.

tagline.text: The Tome of Minion Army comes to Donut in a Beguiler Box. Its spell makes hostile enemies fight for her, but it costs fifty spell points, she has twenty-four, and the book will not let her read it.

Donut has read the Tome of Minion Army. The spell takes five minutes to cast and roots her in place while it does, and at level one each intelligent mob in its circle has a two percent chance to turn on its friends.
Donut has cast Minion Army at last, rooted for four minutes, and the demon birds caught low in its circle turned on each other.

beats.headline: Twenty-six points short
beats.text: Donut's Beguiler Box holds a tome called Minion Army. Its spell costs fifty spell points to cast and makes hostile enemies fight for you instead of against you. A great spell, but Donut currently has twenty-four points. She tries reading it anyway and it won't let her: apparently you can't teach yourself spells you can't cast. She pouts for a good minute straight. Don't worry, Carl says. They will trade it for something better, or keep it until she can use it.
beats.gist: Donut's Beguiler Box holds Minion Army, a fifty-point spell she cannot cast with her twenty-four points.

beats.headline: Read at fifty-two
beats.text: Carl wakes from a nap to Donut's discovery. Her Intelligence is forty, her butterfly charm and new tiara add four, and the Good Rest and shower buffs add twenty percent to her base, which a bug keeps off the stat list but not off her spell points. Fifty-two. Of course she has read the tome already. The spell is simple on the surface and convoluted underneath: five minutes to cast, stuck in place while casting, a five-hour cooldown, intelligent mobs only, and at level one a two percent chance for each to turn on its friends.
beats.gist: Donut's Intelligence reaches fifty-two, and she has already read the Minion Army tome.

beats.headline: Not the same as Conscript
beats.text: Doctor Bones is honing a spell whose effect on weak subjects lasts pretty much forever. Carl asks its name: Donut has one similar, called Minion Army, that she hasn't tried yet. Minion Army is a battlefield sabotage spell, quite effective, says Doctor Bones, but it has a long casting time and it is temporary. His is simply called Conscript. Carl feels a sudden revulsion. He has read about that spell, used a lot against crawlers on the ninth floor.
beats.gist: Donut has an untried spell, Minion Army, while Doctor Bones's Conscript lasts nearly forever, and Carl feels revulsion.

beats.headline: Rooted for four minutes
beats.text: Donut glows as she casts Minion Army for the first time. She has held it back since the first floor because it roots her in place, for four minutes now, and with Imani and Samantha enhancing it the two percent should be about five. A countdown appears over her, Rooted in Place, and the sluggalos charge the demons early. When the ice and the corpses settle she thinks she cast it for nothing, until the experience starts coming in: birds in the lower part of the tornado over the building are fighting each other.
beats.gist: Donut casts Minion Army for the first time and roots herself for four minutes while the sluggalos charge.

recap.text: Donut's Beguiler Box holds a tome called Minion Army, a spell that costs fifty spell points and makes hostile enemies fight for you instead of against you. Donut has twenty-four points, so she tries reading it anyway, and it won't let her: you can't teach yourself a spell you can't cast. She pouts for a good minute straight, and Carl tells her they will trade it for something better, or keep it until she can use it.

Carl wakes to find Donut has already read the Tome of Minion Army. Her Intelligence reads fifty-two: forty, four from the butterfly charm and tiara, and twenty percent of base from the Good Rest and shower buffs, which a bug hides from the stat list but not her spell points. It takes five minutes to cast, roots her, and cools down five hours. It hits only intelligent mobs, two percent of whom turn on friends at level one.

Doctor Bones tells Carl he is honing a spell that lasts pretty much forever on weak subjects. He calls it Conscript, and Carl feels a sudden revulsion, having read that it was used a lot against crawlers on the ninth floor. Donut casts Minion Army for the first time, rooted in place for four minutes, and thinks she wasted it until the experience comes in: birds in the tornado are fighting each other.

tagline.text: Agatha leans on a shopping cart heaped with blankets and odds and ends, a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow in its head among them. Her spray paint lives in it, in a blue IKEA bag, and she insists the paint is hers.

Carl's inventory history still lists everything that was in Agatha's cart while he held it: blankets, clothes, IKEA bags, spray paint, and three pieces of Valtay Corporation technology that sort to the very top by value.

Agatha already had this cart on Earth before the collapse. With the countdown running, she took her supplies out of her dimensional space, put them in the IKEA bag and shoved it to the bottom of the cart. Carl's inventory history still lists the three Valtay devices it carried.

beats.headline: A cart full of blankets
beats.text: Carl and Donut find the Meadow Lark party, and among them is an old woman wrapped head to toe in scarves under a red checkered trapper hat, leaning on a shopping cart filled to the brim with blankets and odds and ends, a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow stuck in its head among them. Carl wonders how anyone got the wheelchairs and the cart down here. Agatha pulls a blue IKEA bag from the cart and sprays a smiley face on the wall. When Brandon tells her not to waste the paint, she says it is hers, and that he stole it from her.
beats.gist: Agatha sprays a smiley face on the wall and tells Brandon the paint is hers; he stole it.

beats.headline: Into Carl's inventory
beats.text: The borough boss is a rolling ball of tusklings, and it rushes past right where the party was standing, missing Agatha and her cart by inches while she cackles with joy. Carl orders her to sit down in the middle and not move, grabs the heavy cart from both sides, lifts it into the air and spends a few precious seconds putting it into his inventory. Thief, she cries. Thief. Yolanda promises he will give it back. Squeezed in with the six of them, Agatha goes on wailing about her damn shopping cart.
beats.gist: Agatha wails over her shopping cart after Carl, dodging the tusklings' rolling boss, stuffs it into his inventory.

beats.headline: Given back, with suspicion
beats.text: The fight over, Agatha shuffles up to Carl shaking her fist, half her head caked in blood, and demands it back. He pulls the cart into existence a foot off the ground and it crashes down. She clutches an IKEA bag off the top and peers inside as if he might have stolen something, and pokes suspiciously at the flamingo. She could keep all of it in her own inventory, Carl points out. She hasn't gone through the tutorial, Yolanda says. She doesn't have an inventory yet.
beats.gist: Carl drops Agatha's cart; she checks the IKEA bag, pokes the flamingo, and has no inventory yet.

beats.headline: Bully and a Thief
beats.text: Among the achievements after the borough boss fight, one confuses Carl for a moment. Bully and a Thief: he has stolen property from a fellow crawler who is a lower level than him. What's next, tough guy, the System asks, kicking puppies? The reward is a Bronze Asshole's Box. Then he realises he got it for taking Agatha's shopping cart.
beats.gist: Carl earns an achievement for stealing from a lower-level crawler: Agatha's shopping cart.

beats.headline: Three items in the history
beats.text: Carl's inventory has grown a History tab. Sorted by value, its top three entries are things he has never seen: a Trans Tunnel 7C Orator Relay by Valtay Corp., a Valtay Perso-Shield Platinum Edition and a Mag 3040 Valtay Corp Pulse Pistol. The relay is a communication device, and illegal. Then Donut sees a blue dot coming, and he knows where they came from: Agatha's cart, all of it, held in his inventory through the boss fight. She wheels it in, squeaking, and calls him a cart thief. He offers to fix the wheel. No need to fix her squeak, she says.
beats.gist: Carl's inventory holds Agatha's whole cart; she wheels it in squeaking and calls him a cart thief.

beats.headline: Still squeaking, still pushing
beats.text: Carl moves to step down the stairs, and they suddenly turn into a ramp. A familiar crawler is pushing a squeaking shopping cart toward them: Agatha, level eight now, still human, still without a class, with the pink flamingo standing at the front of the cart. I see you lot are still kicking, she cackles. The whole group watches open-mouthed as she heads for the stairwell. Imani moves to intercept her, and Carl holds out a hand to stop her. Don't, he warns.
beats.gist: Agatha, level eight, pushes her squeaking cart and pink flamingo toward the stairwell; Carl stops Imani intercepting her.

beats.headline: The bottom of the cart
beats.text: A countdown reaches every asset: commencement, Earth System initialization, edifice collapse, and this is not a drill. Agent number 22, also known as Agatha, shakes her head and reads it again. The night is freezing, and she has put her failing human shell into torpor against the cold. She takes her supplies out of her dimensional space, pulls herself to her feet with old, shaking hands, places the items in the IKEA bag and shoves it to the bottom of her shopping cart. The collapse is under two Earth hours away. She has been here almost ten Earth years, waiting.
beats.gist: Agatha, agent number 22, packs her supplies into an IKEA bag as the collapse countdown begins.

relations.note: in his inventory through the borough boss fight
three Valtay devices among its contents

recap.text: Agatha, an old woman in a red checkered trapper hat, leans on a shopping cart packed with blankets and a plastic pink flamingo with an arrow stuck in its head. When the borough boss, a rolling ball of tusklings, rushes past, Carl lifts the cart into his inventory, and she wails "thief" until the fight ends. He returns it, and the System gives him Bully and a Thief and a Bronze Asshole's Box.

Carl goes to step down the stairs, and they turn into a ramp. Agatha comes up it, pushing a squeaking shopping cart with a pink flamingo standing at the front. She is level eight, still human, still without a class. She cackles that the lot of them are still kicking, and the group watches open-mouthed as she heads for the stairwell. Imani moves to intercept her, and Carl holds out a hand and warns her not to.

Agent number 22, also known as Agatha, reads a countdown that reaches every asset: commencement, Earth System initialization, edifice collapse, and this is not a drill. In the freezing night she takes her supplies out of her dimensional space, pulls herself up with old, shaking hands, and shoves them in an IKEA bag to the bottom of her shopping cart. The collapse is under two Earth hours away, and she has waited almost ten Earth years for it.

tagline.text: A bracelet out of a silver Adventurer box adds two points to Donut's Dexterity, bringing it to twelve. It wraps snugly round her front leg.
Donut wears bracelets on all four legs now, and the plus-two Dexterity one is on a back leg.

beats.headline: Finally, melee damage
beats.text: Donut hisses with rage at the piles of torches that keep appearing in front of her; most of her haul is the same old crap. One exception is a bracelet from a Silver Adventurer box she received for finally dealing melee damage. It adds two to her dexterity, bringing it to twelve, and when she equips it, it wraps snugly round her front leg. A Silver Survivor's Box gives her a dozen Heal scrolls as well.
beats.gist: Donut's first bracelet, from a Silver Adventurer box, adds two dexterity, raising it to twelve.

beats.headline: Room for an anklet
beats.text: Carl has pried a wooden anklet off a dead tree woman, and he wants to see if the game will let Donut wear it. He suspects it will: she already has one bracelet wrapped round her forward leg, though he can barely see it through all the fur. Donut looks at the anklet with distaste. Wood?
beats.gist: Carl wants Donut to wear a wooden anklet from a dead tree woman, but Donut dislikes the wood.

beats.headline: All four legs
beats.text: Donut's gold box pops out a sparkling silver bracelet with little purple gems, and she equips it at once. The obsidian bracelet that lets her cast Fireball moves to her right foreleg and the new one goes on the left. The fallen oak anklet stays tucked on one back leg and her plus-two dexterity bracelet on the other. With bracelets on all four legs, she can't add any more. Doesn't it look divine?
beats.gist: Donut equips a sparkling silver bracelet with purple gems on her left foreleg, filling all four legs.

recap.text: Donut hisses with rage at the piles of torches that keep appearing in front of her, since most of her haul is the same old crap. A Silver Adventurer box, her reward for finally dealing melee damage, holds a bracelet that adds two to her dexterity, bringing it to twelve. When she equips it, it wraps snugly round her front leg. A Silver Survivor's Box hands her a dozen Heal scrolls.

Carl has pried a wooden anklet off a dead tree woman and wants to see whether the game will let Donut wear it. He thinks it will, since she already has one bracelet wrapped round her forward leg, though he can barely see it through all the fur. Donut looks at the anklet with distaste and asks, "Wood?

Donut's gold box pops out a sparkling silver bracelet with little purple gems, and she puts it on her left foreleg at once. The obsidian bracelet that lets her cast Fireball moves to her right foreleg. The fallen oak anklet stays on one back leg and her plus-two dexterity bracelet on the other, so with a bracelet on all four legs she cannot add any more.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust are a hundred small, low-damage black throwing stars. Every monster hurt by one makes the set hit that monster type eight percent harder, compounded, but the stars are very fragile.
A star that takes a single chip loses its red enchantment. Fifty of Carl's shuriken became the spikes on the front of the redoubt for the borough boss, and only about twenty of those stayed unbroken.

description.text: Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust (x100) Small, low-damage throwing stars. These bad boys aren't anything special upon first glance. They're the same black stars you wannabe ninjas purchased at the knife shop and the swap meet when you were kids. The same throwing stars you'd drill into the drywall of your room until your mom caught you and took them away. And while these shuriken don't have the ability to turn you into a ninja, nor do they have the capacity to make your mom stop drinking, they are enchanted with a Bloodlust enhancement. For every monster you damage with a shuriken from this set, the damage against that monster type rises by 8%.

beats.headline: A pile of ninja stars
beats.text: The boss box holds a pile of ninja stars, a hundred of them, the same black stars every wannabe ninja once drilled into his bedroom drywall. They are enchanted with Bloodlust: for every monster damaged with one, the damage against that monster type rises by eight percent. Carl asks Mordecai whether that means eight percent of the original amount or eight percent compounded, because that is a big deal after a while. Huh, says Mordecai, and checks. Good news: it is compounded. The bad news is that the stars are very fragile. Carl suspects it is not that great an enchantment, with only a hundred of them to throw and collect.
beats.gist: Carl finds a hundred fragile ninja stars that raise damage eight percent per monster hit, compounded.

beats.headline: Spikes on the redoubt
beats.text: Brandon reads the description and is awed: compounding damage means poke something two hundred times and it's literally millions of points. So he, Chris and Carl spend a good five minutes throwing fifty of the stars deep into the pitted wooden cover of the redoubt's front table, black spikes to pierce the boss each time it hits. Only about twenty stay unbroken. In the fight the star-covered tabletop lies broken, and a tuskling rolls onto the stars still glowing red, squealing, so Carl stamps it deeper into the wood. Its health drops slowly, then plummets as the exponential bonus kicks in.
beats.gist: Brandon, Chris and Carl throw fifty stars into a table, then Carl stamps a tuskling onto them.

beats.headline: Every star salvaged
beats.text: Imani drops a find on the floor in disgust, and Donut hops over and takes it into her own inventory. Everything, right? she asks, and Carl nods. He salvages all the ninja stars he can find and all the remaining pieces of the redoubt, and his inventory grows a new tab labelled Worthless Garbage. Then he spends a few minutes quietly looking round the arena for the remains of the party that went before them.
beats.gist: Carl salvages every ninja star and redoubt piece, then looks for the earlier party's remains.

recap.text: Mordecai confirms the Bloodlust on the hundred ninja stars compounds at eight percent, though the stars are very fragile. Brandon, Chris and Carl spend five minutes throwing fifty into the redoubt's pitted wooden table cover, and only about twenty stay unbroken. In the fight a tuskling rolls onto the glowing stars, and Carl stamps it deeper until its health plummets. He salvages every star, and his inventory grows a tab labelled Worthless Garbage.

entities.name: Heal scroll
entities.role: A heal for whoever it is read on

tagline.text: A Heal scroll heals whoever it is read on, and there is no countdown between one scroll and the next, as there is with potions. Donut won a dozen from a Silver Survivor's Box, and Carl's bronze one brought five more.
A Heal scroll works on Donut, but read on Mongo it does nothing.

beats.headline: A dozen for nearly dying
beats.text: After the boss fight, Donut's boxes are mostly the same old crap, with a couple of exceptions. A Silver Survivor's Box, awarded for ending a boss battle with less than five percent of her health, gives her a dozen Heal scrolls. They are good to have: there is no countdown between reading one and the next, and even better, they can use them on each other. Those twelve are good, Mordecai says, and he suspects they are about to get a few more. Carl's own Bronze Survivor's Box, for having less than ten percent health when the boss died, brings five more, seventeen in all.
beats.gist: Donut's Silver Survivor's Box gives her twelve Heal scrolls, and Carl's Bronze box adds five, seventeen total.

beats.headline: Not on Mongo
beats.text: Street urchins are attacking Mongo and Donut because of the wood and metal Carl stacked round the cat, and Donut is getting skewered. Carl reads a Heal scroll, one of those from the Survivor's Box, focusing on her. She glows, and the spikes squeeze out of her body and scatter on the floor like pine needles. He tries a second on Mongo, and it doesn't work. He can't use a potion on the pet either. Hang in there, buddy.
beats.gist: Donut is skewered by street urchins; Carl's Heal scroll expels the spikes, but a second on Mongo fails.

beats.headline: Onto the roof
beats.text: The Divider's corpse blows and throws Carl onto a roof across the street. Donut grabs the neighborhood map, leaps out of the pool and finishes off the last three monsters, two with magic missiles and the third with Mongo. Then she leaps to the roof where Carl landed and uses a heal scroll to bring his health back up. He stays unconscious for another three minutes despite being healed, and wakes staring at the sky, a level higher.
beats.gist: Donut uses a heal scroll on the unconscious Carl on a roof; he wakes a level higher.

beats.headline: Topping off Katia
beats.text: Carl has eight scrolls of healing ready and Donut another six when the train runs into the ghouls. Gore blasts into the engine like a firehose, and Katia, who has been fine, is suddenly unconscious at half health and dropping: something is shocking her. Where the hell is that healer? Carl casts his heal scroll on Katia and her health returns to the top, though she stays unconscious and it keeps dropping. At ten percent he slams another to top her off, and when her health keeps dwindling with no debuff showing, he reads another, then another. He will soon be out.
beats.gist: Carl heals Katia with scroll after scroll as she stays unconscious and her health keeps dropping.

beats.headline: One of the precious ones
beats.text: A rocket blows everything back across the room. Louis is screaming, burned and full of shrapnel. Firas has been blown across the room and is unconscious, but otherwise looks okay. Donut, astride Mongo, both unharmed at the back of the room, goes to Firas and uses one of their precious healing scrolls on him. Carl drops one of his last hobgoblin smoke curtains at his feet. Let's get out of here.
beats.gist: Donut heals unconscious Firas with a scroll; Carl drops a hobgoblin smoke curtain.

beats.headline: Misfire, then up
beats.text: Everything unfreezes after the goddess's visit, and beside Carl, Donut has gone rigid, unable to move, her health draining slowly, her title changed from Warlord to Champion. He tries to apply a healing scroll at once, but it misfires, and he has to wait. Outside, the ball has broken apart and thousands of bodies are flying up toward them. When Donut coughs, he slams on the healing scroll, and her health starts to rocket up.
beats.gist: Donut freezes and drains health; Carl's healing scroll misfires, then works when she coughs.

beats.headline: Healing Chaco
beats.text: The parade passes Lamashtu the donkey with Grigori standing on her, and Carl meets the psychotic AI's eyes. Chaco is at Grigori's feet, his health still in the red. Never taking his eyes off Grigori's, Carl pulls up a healing scroll, selects Chaco and heals him. Grigori's eyes never leave his own, and he does not react. Then Carl points at the effigy of the Unwashed and speaks to the galaxy.
beats.gist: Carl heals Chaco, who is still in the red, with a scroll while staring Grigori down.

relations.note: it does not work on him
no countdown between scrolls, where potions have one

recap.text: Donut's boss-fight boxes are mostly the same old crap, but a Silver Survivor's Box, for ending the fight with less than five percent of her health, gives her a dozen Heal scrolls. Carl's Bronze Survivor's Box, for having less than ten percent health when the boss died, adds five, making seventeen. There is no countdown between one scroll and the next, and they can be read on each other.

Street urchins skewer Donut, so Carl reads a Heal scroll on her, and the spikes squeeze out and scatter on the floor like pine needles. A second scroll on Mongo does nothing. When the Divider's corpse blows Carl onto a roof, Donut kills the last three monsters, two with magic missiles and one with Mongo, then leaps over and heals him with a scroll. He stays unconscious three more minutes, then wakes staring at the sky, a level higher.

When the train runs into the ghouls, gore blasts into the engine like a firehose, and Katia drops unconscious at half health with something shocking her. Carl, who has eight healing scrolls to Donut's six, reads one on her and her health returns to the top, but it keeps dropping. At ten percent he slams another, and with no debuff showing he reads another, then another. He will soon be out.

Donut, astride Mongo, walks up to Firas and reads one of their precious healing scrolls on him after a rocket blows everything back across the room. Louis is left screaming, burned and full of shrapnel, and Firas lies unconscious but otherwise whole. Carl drops one of his last hobgoblin smoke curtains at his feet, and says to get out of here.

Donut lies rigid beside Carl after the goddess's visit, unable to move, her health draining and her title changed from Warlord to Champion. Carl tries a healing scroll at once, but it misfires, so he waits while thousands of bodies fly up toward them from the broken ball outside. When Donut coughs, he slams on the scroll, and her health starts to rocket up.

Carl meets the eyes of Grigori, the psychotic AI standing on Lamashtu the donkey as the parade passes. Chaco lies at Grigori's feet with his health still in the red. Without looking away, Carl pulls up a healing scroll, selects Chaco and heals him, and Grigori does not react. Carl then points at the effigy of the Unwashed and speaks to the galaxy.

tagline.text: The Puddle Jumper tome is a spell book out of Donut's Bronze Boss Box, and she reads it before Carl can ask what it is. It teaches her Puddle Jumper, which teleports her and up to three others anywhere in her line of sight, for 20 mana, on a ten-second delay and a five-hour cooldown.

beats.headline: Read before the description
beats.text: Donut's Bronze Boss Box has given her yet another spell book, and she hasn't read it yet. She announces she was born a cat and will die a cat, and that Carl must choose a cat race too; when he says he is sticking with human, she does her approximation of a shrug and glows as she reads the tome. Did she at least read the description? Mordecai nods. Puddle Jumper, a good one: herself and up to three others, anywhere in her line of sight, further at higher levels, almost as good as Teleport at level 15. Twenty mana, a ten-second delay, a five-hour cooldown.
beats.gist: Donut reads her new spell book, Puddle Jumper, which teleports her and up to three others within sight.

beats.headline: A wet pop between fairies
beats.text: The two biggest problems with Puddle Jumper are the cooldown and the mana. Once Donut is in that room she cannot teleport out for five hours, and the spell costs 20 of her 26 points. Carl stays behind; with his extra fairy aggro, nobody knows what would happen if they both showed themselves. Donut casts it, fades through the ten-second countdown and vanishes with a loud, wet pop, reappearing at the far end of the room right between the two laminak fairies as the clurichauns jump to their feet.
beats.gist: Donut casts Puddle Jumper, spending 20 of her 26 points, and pops in between the two fairies.

recap.text: Donut reads the Puddle Jumper spell book from her Bronze Boss Box while Carl sticks with human. Mordecai says it carries her and up to three others for twenty mana, with a five-hour cooldown. Carl stays behind because of his extra fairy aggro, so Donut spends 20 of her 26 points and vanishes with a wet pop. She reappears between the two laminak fairies as the clurichauns jump to their feet.

tagline.text: The Speedbump is Brandon's name for the portable fortress he, his brother and Carl built from goblin tables and gym equipment: angled, four feet high, drilled to go up in less than twenty seconds and come together in twenty more, and meant to wedge a rolling boss against the ceiling.
What survives of the Speedbump travels in pieces in Carl's inventory, and an angled section that is still intact serves him as a shield in a boss fight.

beats.headline: Almost five hours of building
beats.text: Brandon and his brother Chris are the facility's maintenance guys. Carl describes his idea, spreads out the looted goblin tools, and they go straight to work. It takes almost five hours to build the pieces of a portable, modular fortress: workshop tables on new legs from the weight equipment, weight benches bolted on like shutters, a roof of weight-rack cross bars, barbell poles to brace it. Brandon calls it the Speedbump. They practise until the main structure goes up in less than twenty seconds and the rest in twenty more. Fifty of Carl's shuriken go into the front table's wooden covering as spikes; only about twenty stay unbroken.
beats.gist: Brandon and Chris build the Speedbump fortress from weight benches and workshop tables.

beats.headline: Wedged under the ball
beats.text: On a fifteen-foot square of floor with no grooves, they build it in the order they practised while Agatha wails about her shopping cart, which Carl has just put into his inventory. With her inside, there is no room for the final, centre pole. The ball hits. The structure slides with a horrifying screech, all four ceiling braces pop out, and one throws Yolanda over. The ball is wedged between the roof and the tunnel, the roof sagging. They stab up through the lattice until, as the top collapses, the boss bursts like a balloon and tuxedoed tusklings rain down on them.
beats.gist: Donut and Carl build a fortress around Agatha, but the ball wedges it and the boss bursts.

beats.headline: Edited out from under it
beats.text: The recap episode shows them huddled underneath the redoubt as Donut screams that it's coming. Brandon's older brother, Chris, speaks up, only the second time Carl has heard him, and says there is more to it. Agatha was edited out of the scene. She was next to him under the speedbump, but she wasn't there when they showed it. Oh yeah, says Brandon. Weird.
beats.gist: Brandon's brother Chris tells Carl the recap edited Agatha out, though she huddled beside him under the speedbump.

beats.headline: A shield in the corner
beats.text: Krakaren's tentacles are smashing through the walls and Carl is buzzed on his own smoothie. Running for the back corner of the room with Donut, he pulls an angled, still-intact section of the redoubt from his inventory and puts it up as a shield; the clurichauns' slingshot rocks ping off the steel table, and a screaming tentacle slams it and rockets them both against the back wall. When he has sent a zombie off toward the door with a lit jug, he dives behind it again and pulls the alchemy table over the top to make a clamshell.
beats.gist: Carl hides behind a redoubt section and an alchemy table from Krakaren's tentacles.

beats.headline: A pyramid round the cat
beats.text: Donut will not wake, and Signet says she will remain where she is. When Carl lifts her anyway, a health bar appears and starts falling, and Signet tells him a water lily must not be removed, lest it die; he puts her back. Before he goes, he pulls the last of the redoubt pieces from his inventory, wood and metal, and erects an ugly, quick and dirty pyramid around the cat's chair. It won't protect her from a determined mob, but it is better than nothing. Mongo jumps to the top of it and looks down through the jagged hole.
beats.gist: Donut will not wake, so Carl leaves her in place and builds a rough pyramid around her chair.

relations.note: fifty thrown into the front table as spikes

recap.text: Brandon and his brother Chris, the facility's maintenance guys, spend almost five hours building Carl's idea from looted goblin tools: workshop tables on weight-equipment legs, weight benches bolted on like shutters, a roof of weight-rack cross bars. With Agatha and her shopping cart inside, no room remains for the centre pole, and the ball's hit slides the Speedbump with a screech. They stab up through the lattice until the boss bursts like a balloon.

Donut will not wake, and Signet says she will stay where she is. Carl lifts her anyway, a health bar appears and starts to fall, and Signet warns that a water lily must not be removed, lest it die, so he sets her back. He pulls the last redoubt pieces, wood and metal, from his inventory and throws up an ugly, quick pyramid around her chair. Mongo jumps to the top and looks down through the jagged hole.

tagline.text: A Borough Field Guide is looted from a dead borough boss, and Donut gets one of her own. It outlines the quadrants of the map round it, and hovering over one gives the levels and types of the mobs inside, though only for a limited area.
The field guide from the bowl's borough boss shows the level and description of every mob in the area, and it covers the entire bowl.

description.text: Borough Field Guide. Ahh, look at you. The intrepid explorer. Alone. Lost. Afraid. But there is no reason to be frightened. Not today, not now. Not when the trusty field guide has added monster types to this area of the map. Now when you gaze upon the unknown, that fear is somewhat lessened. Instead of delving into the strange, mysterious dark, being devoured by an unseen horror, you will now know exactly what it is as it chews upon your tasty innards.

beats.headline: An Attenborough whisper
beats.text: The crushed tusklings lie everywhere, and Carl reaches down to loot the persistent item from the boss's corpse; Donut already has hers. The AI reads its description in a whispery David Attenborough impression: Borough Field Guide. Carl zooms his minimap out, and the quadrants round the arena are outlined now. Hovering over one to the far southeast, where nobody has been, brings a tooltip through the fog of war: Mobs Level 2-5. Axebeak. Useful, but like the neighborhood map the area is limited, and one has to reach the center and kill the boss to get it.
beats.gist: Carl loots the boss's corpse and gets the Borough Field Guide, which shows mob levels in far quadrants.

beats.headline: Map, guide, stars
beats.text: In the middle of the enormous pile of dead mimic, a single object appears on the map. Neighborhood bosses drop the neighborhood map, borough bosses the field guide, and thanks to both the cookbook and Mordecai, Carl already knows what this one will be. It is the Map of the Stars, which adds boss locations and descriptions to a large area of the map. It is a little late to be useful, but he wades into the gore and picks it up anyway.
beats.gist: Carl picks up the Map of the Stars, which he already knew a borough boss would drop.

beats.headline: The whole bowl
beats.text: The party has taken the field guide from the borough boss corpse. Now they can see the level and description of every mob in the area, and the guide covers the entire bowl. Right now, in the dark, it shows fist-sized monsters called Night Frights emerging from the sand dunes everywhere, mobs that run at their prey, attach themselves and explode, like the rot stickers of the first floor.
beats.gist: The party's field guide shows every mob in the bowl, including exploding Night Frights.

recap.text: Carl loots the persistent item from the boss's corpse among the crushed tusklings; Donut already has hers. The AI reads the Borough Field Guide's description in a whispery David Attenborough impression. Carl zooms his minimap out, and hovering over the far southeastern quadrant, where nobody has been, brings a tooltip through the fog of war: Mobs Level 2-5, Axebeak. It covers a limited area, and one must reach the center and kill the boss to get it.

A single object appears on the map in the middle of an enormous pile of dead mimic. Neighborhood bosses drop the neighborhood map and borough bosses the field guide, and thanks to the cookbook and Mordecai, Carl knows what this one is: the Map of the Stars, which adds boss locations and descriptions to a large area of the map. It is a little late to be useful, but he wades into the gore and picks it up anyway.

The party takes the field guide from the borough boss corpse. It shows the level and description of every mob in the entire bowl. In the dark, it shows fist-sized Night Frights coming up out of the sand dunes everywhere. They run at their prey, attach themselves and explode, like the rot stickers of the first floor.

entities.name: Cheat Code Potion
entities.role: A skill boost that will not keep

tagline.text: A Cheat Code Potion raises one recently-used combat or magic skill by three, chosen at random and permanent. It expires shortly after it is generated, so it has to be drunk on the spot.

description.text: Cheat Code Potion Warning: This item has a short shelf life. This item will expire shortly after it was generated. In other words, this isn't something you can hoard. Don't be a wuss. Drink it now. Causes one, recently-used combat or magic-themed skill to increase by three. Choice is random and permanent.

beats.headline: Seventeen minutes to drink it
beats.text: The silver boss box holds a hundred gold coins and a potion with a red timer flashing at the bottom of its description, already down to seventeen minutes. Cheat Code Potion: don't be a wuss, drink it now. Carl adds it to his hotlist and drinks, and it crackles in his mouth like a whole packet of Pop Rocks. His Pugilism goes up by three, to level ten. With Iron Punch, Powerful Strike and his unarmed bonus, his fists now pack as much damage as Brandon's lightning maul.
beats.gist: Carl drinks the Cheat Code Potion before its timer runs out, raising Pugilism to level ten.

beats.headline: Already at ten
beats.text: Among the classes on offer, Prizefighter adds three to Pugilism, which would be a huge bonus, Carl thinks, considering the Cheat Code potion has already taken the skill to ten. He would pick the class in a second if he thought he could just punch his way through the dungeon. He knows already that he can't.
beats.gist: Carl sees Prizefighter adds three to Pugilism, already ten, but knows punching won't carry him.

beats.headline: Precious, and perishable
beats.text: Why is Pawna's Tears so valuable, Katia wants to know, when they have seen skill potions, potions that max a skill out, and Cheat Code potions that give three levels? Because it is plus five to any skill he chooses, Mordecai answers. Legendary potions that max a skill exist only for a few skills. The Cheat Code is also precious, plus three to a random skill. However, it has a short shelf life, so it has to be taken immediately.
beats.gist: Pawna's Tears adds five to a chosen skill; Cheat Code adds three to a random one.

recap.text: Carl drinks the Cheat Code Potion from the silver boss box the moment he sees its red timer, already down to seventeen minutes, and adds it to his hotlist first. It crackles in his mouth like a whole packet of Pop Rocks and raises his Pugilism by three, to level ten. With Iron Punch, Powerful Strike and his unarmed bonus, his fists now hit as hard as Brandon's lightning maul.

Among the classes on offer, Prizefighter adds three to Pugilism. The Cheat Code potion has already taken that skill to ten, so Carl thinks the bonus would be huge. He would pick the class in a second if he thought he could just punch his way through the dungeon, but he already knows he can't.

Katia asks Mordecai why Pawna's Tears is so valuable when they have seen skill potions, potions that max a skill out, and Cheat Code potions that give three levels. Mordecai answers that it is plus five to any skill he chooses. Legendary potions that max a skill exist for only a few skills. The Cheat Code potion is precious too, plus three to a random skill, but its shelf life is short, so it must be taken immediately.

entities.name: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph

tagline.text: The Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph is a little zippered folder of twelve tools. Used nightly in a safe room, it gives Carl's bare feet extra damage, three levels of Smush, bones that will not break and a five-second warning before any trap set off by a footfall, all for thirty hours.

description.text: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph. This kit contains 12 essential items for proper foot care. The magical enhancements of this item may only be imbued within a Safe or Personal Space. Warning: All of these enhancements require you to remain barefoot. Why? Because you know why. From a pumice stone to a cuticle pusher, this personal hygiene kit will keep your feet both luscious and in perfect fighting shape. Nightly care of your feet and toenails will result in the following bonuses: +15% Damage to bare-foot attacks for 30 hours. +3 to the Smush skill for 30 hours. +Unbreakable buff (feet only) for 30 hours. This buff keeps your pretty little metatarsals nice and unbroken. …

beats.headline: One last item
beats.text: Carl has one last item to examine from the haul, and he swears under his breath before he has even pulled it into his hand: a little black folder with a zipper, full of miniature tools. Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph, twelve essential items for proper foot care, working only in a safe room or personal space and only while he stays barefoot. He sighs. The very last buff, an alarm and a five-second delay before any trap set off by a footfall, is a great prize.
beats.gist: Carl examines the Pedicure Kit of the Sylph, whose last buff delays footfall traps.

beats.headline: Imani shows him how
beats.text: Little sharp rocks are everywhere. Carl kicks one away, and below him his shiny toes glitter. He had tried to get Donut to show him how to use the kit, and she laughed at him. It was Imani, of all people, who sat down with him, pulling the tools out one at a time and matter-of-factly explaining how they worked. The buffs activate after about fifteen minutes of work. He doesn't need to use every tool. He just has to make a show of it.
beats.gist: Carl learns from Imani that his pedicure kit's buffs start after fifteen minutes of shown effort.

beats.headline: Saved by a pedicure
beats.text: Carl wakes in the hallway, healed by one of Donut's healing scrolls, his one-armed jacket scorched to hell. His toes sparkle. He thinks he was saved by that damn pedicure kit. The table should have severed his feet right at the ankles. Instead it bounced off and broke his legs, and without that, he would have bled out.
beats.gist: Carl wakes healed by Donut's scroll and credits the pedicure kit for saving him.

beats.headline: The buffs ran out
beats.text: On the red line, a level-six baby chomps onto Carl's foot, which should do nothing because of his… and then he is crying out in excruciating pain as it gnaws on the meat of his sole. He stamps it into a burst of tomato soup, spreads his toes to check they are all there, and heals. It has been a long time since he let his pedicure buffs expire. He had forgotten what it felt like to be vulnerable down there.
beats.gist: Carl's expired pedicure buffs let a level-six baby gnaw his sole until he stamps it.

beats.headline: Stuck at fourteen
beats.text: Among more achievements than he expected is one for killing a swordfish guy with his foot, worth a bronze spicy box. Carl's Smush base is now level twelve. His bonus for using the pedicure kit supposedly raises it three more, but the skill is still listed as fourteen. As always, skills go wonky when item buffs try to push them toward fifteen. And these card fights are paying seriously padded experience.
beats.gist: Carl's Smush skill stays listed at fourteen, though his pedicure kit bonus should raise it to fifteen.

beats.headline: Negated by a costume
beats.text: Inside the stinking kangaroo costume, his boxers and kneepads somehow on the outside of it, Carl gets two warnings at once: his boxer effects have been negated by his costume, and so have his pedicure effects. He pulls a banger sphere from his inventory, praying it will appear outside the costume and not in his hand under the skin. It appears in the paw.
beats.gist: Carl's kangaroo costume negates his boxer and pedicure effects, and his banger sphere appears in the paw.

recap.text: Carl pulls the Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph from the haul, a zippered black folder of miniature tools that works only while he stays barefoot. Imani, not the laughing Donut, explains the tools, and he learns he only has to make a show of using them. A table that should have severed his feet at the ankles bounces off and breaks his legs instead, and he wakes healed by Donut's scroll, his toes sparkling.

Carl's level-six baby chomps onto his foot on the red line, and at first it does nothing, then he cries out in pain as it gnaws on the meat of his sole. He stamps it into a burst of tomato soup, spreads his toes to check they are all there, and heals. His pedicure buffs have expired, and he had forgotten what it felt like to be vulnerable down there.

Carl finds more achievements waiting than he expected, including one for killing a swordfish guy with his foot, worth a bronze spicy box. His Smush base sits at level twelve, and the pedicure kit's bonus is supposed to add three, yet the skill still reads fourteen. Skills always go wonky when item buffs push them toward fifteen. The card fights pay seriously padded experience.

Inside the stinking kangaroo costume, with his boxers and kneepads worn on the outside of it, Carl gets two warnings at once: the costume has negated his boxer effects, and it has negated his pedicure effects. He pulls a banger sphere from his inventory, praying it will appear outside the costume and not in his hand under the skin. It appears in the paw.

tagline.text: The Goo-Inator 3000 is a shaping tool from a silver mechanics box, an oversized silver lollipop with a button on the handle. It only works at a workbench, so for now it waits in Carl's inventory.
At his engineering table, the Goo-Inator lets Carl work metal like dough: flatten it into a sheet, or bend it freehand.

description.text: The Goo-Inator 3000. This is a shaping tool. May only be used at a workbench. Assists in shaping materials into something else. You might want to keep the business end away from your face.

beats.headline: A lollipop with a button
beats.text: Going through his loot after the borough boss, Carl finds a really interesting item in a silver mechanics box: a tool that looks like a silver, oversized lollipop with a button on the handle. It shapes materials into something else, only at a workbench, and the System suggests keeping the business end away from his face. He can't buy a personal space until the fourth floor, so it goes back into his inventory to wait.
beats.gist: Carl finds a lollipop-shaped tool that reshapes materials at a workbench, then pockets it.

beats.headline: Iron like dough
beats.text: In the empty crafting room Carl sets up three tables and stands at the engineering one, Mordecai's catch-all for fashioning items with magical tools. He lays out the Goo-Inator and the Gorgon Marital Aid and clunks the massive, unenchanted breastplate of a swordsman guard onto the table. Pointed at it, the Goo-Inator makes the plate blink and offers a menu of shapes; he could flatten it like dough. He picks Freeform and puts a slight bend in it. The metal groans but does not break. Martha Stewart, says the achievement: a bronze crafter's box, with pliers, a tape measure and a bucket of pink glitter.
beats.gist: Carl bends a swordsman guard's breastplate slightly with the Goo-Inator and earns Martha Stewart.

recap.text: Carl goes through his loot after the borough boss and finds a silver mechanics box holding the Goo-Inator 3000, a tool shaped like an oversized silver lollipop with a button on the handle. It shapes materials into something else, but only at a workbench, and the System suggests keeping the business end away from his face. Carl can't buy a personal space until the fourth floor, so he puts it back into his inventory to wait.

Carl sets up three tables in the empty crafting room and lays the Goo-Inator and the Gorgon Marital Aid beside a swordsman guard's massive, unenchanted breastplate. Pointed at the plate, the Goo-Inator makes it blink and offers a menu of shapes. Carl picks Freeform and puts a slight bend in the iron, which groans but does not break. The achievement Martha Stewart pays a bronze crafter's box of pliers, a tape measure and pink glitter.

tagline.text: The Second Chance tome arrives by mail: a boss box has made Donut a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, one spellbook a level. It teaches Second Chance, which raises a lower-level dead monster to fight for the party for as many minutes as the spell's level.

beats.headline: The Book of the Floor Club
beats.text: Donut leaps onto the safe room's mailbox and its front opens on its own. A tome floats out. A boss box has made her a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club: one spellbook per level, mailed to her. She reads it at once, and says ew. Carl reminds her, again, to read the description first. It's Second Chance, ten mana: she can raise a lower-level monster from the dead to fight for them for as many minutes as the spell's level. It's disgusting, she says, until Carl suggests raising a dead dingo to kill another dingo, like the Lucia Mar kid with her two dogs. This is the best spell ever.
beats.gist: Donut's mailed spellbook teaches Second Chance, which raises a dead monster to fight for her.

beats.headline: Undead minion, level one
beats.text: Donut has headshot three clurichauns and has fourteen mana left, so Carl asks if she wants to try her new Second Chance spell. Her whole body glows neon purple. One of the dead clurichauns twitches, glows to match and stumbles to its feet, its scorched head listing, a one-minute timer over it: Undead Minion of Crawler Princess Donut. Donut finds it most unpleasant and has no sort of controls, but told to rip up the bodies of its friends, it does, and within seconds it is dead again, the job unfinished. For the next hour she raises one after every skirmish so Carl can practise his slingshot on it, and the spell reaches level three: the minions now last three minutes.
beats.gist: Donut raises a dead clurichaun with Second Chance, and Carl slings stones at its repeated resurrections.

recap.text: Donut leaps onto the safe room's mailbox, and a tome floats out: a boss box has made her a member of the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, one spellbook per level. The spell is Second Chance, ten mana, and it raises a dead monster to fight for as many minutes as its level. She casts it, glows neon purple, and a scorched clurichaun stumbles up, then dies again, its job unfinished.

tagline.text: Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine is a 180-proof accelerant made by Krakaren's operation from grub slime and a secret source, and carried by her clurichaun consultants in clay jugs. Carl and Donut take twenty-five of them, and Carl wants torches.
No more Rev-Up Moonshine is being made this season, and Mordecai tells a shopkeeper that Carl and Donut are the reason. Three of the bottles they kept buy a pharmaceutical starter kit.

description.text: Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine. Type: Accelerant. Effect: Highly flammable liquid. Explosive fumes. Status: Will not activate until introduced to flame. At 180 proof, this moonshine will take the hair off your chest and then put it back on. The Rev-Up version is distilled using two types of sugars: the slime trails left behind by the passage of the Brindle Grub, and a secretive, proprietary source. Created exclusively on the dungeon's second floor by the Rev-Up company, jugs of this concoction are highly sought after by the drinking establishments that populate the third, sixth, ninth, twelfth, fifteenth, and eighteenth floors. …

beats.headline: Twenty-five clay jugs
beats.text: Donut loots the dead clurichaun consultants: each of them has a clay jug of something called toilet-grade moonshine. Over the next hour she finds a pamphlet, Rev-Up, promising the benefits of becoming a Rev-Up Moonshine Consultant, see Krakaren or one of her downline consultants. By the time they stop to think they have twenty-five jugs. The description says they are valuable and sought after on deeper floors. Donut is sure the Desperado Club will buy them all and make them rich. Carl grins and asks whether she has any extra torches.
beats.gist: Donut loots twenty-five jugs of toilet-grade moonshine from dead clurichauns and expects the Desperado Club to buy them.

beats.headline: A third of a glass
beats.text: With the boss's tentacles breaking through the walls, Carl pulls a glass smoothie container into his right hand and a jug of unaltered moonshine into his left, pulls the cork with his teeth and fills the glass a third of the way, to a little line on the side. A tentacle bursts in overhead and moonshine sloshes out; he pours a little more, then throws the jug toward the entrance, where it shatters. The rest of the recipe is a dead fairy.
beats.gist: Carl pours a third of a glass of moonshine while tentacles break in, then throws the jug.

beats.headline: Three bottles for a suitcase
beats.text: Mordecai sends Carl a private note, and two bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine appear on Quint's table. Carl has been using them quite a bit in battle, but he kept a stash to sell, and besides these two he still has twenty-three. Quint sniffs one: that Krakaren bitch said no more was being made this season. Mordecai says Carl and Donut are why it was shut down, and they have the last of it, which isn't exactly true. Make it four, says Quint. Three, says Donut, half asleep, and the potion to stop the world being wavy. Deal: a starter kit, a chest of chemicals and herbs.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut trade two Rev-Up Moonshine bottles for a starter kit of chemicals and herbs.

beats.headline: Worth more plain
beats.text: At the Silk Road, Carl puts one of his boom jugs on Pustule's table and asks what she'd give him for it. She examines it, says nice design, rubs the bottle, whimpers, and licks it. Then she snaps back to business. His material cost is much too high: a different accelerant would burn less hot and cost ninety percent less, and the plain bottles of moonshine, sold as they are, would be worth much more. She'd sell the jug for about 7,500 gold and offer him half. He keeps it.
beats.gist: At the Silk Road, Pustule offers Carl half of 7,500 gold for a boom jug; he keeps it.

relations.note: three bottles

recap.text: Donut loots the dead clurichaun consultants and collects twenty-five clay jugs of toilet-grade moonshine, sure the Desperado Club will buy them all. With the boss's tentacles breaking through the walls, Carl pulls the cork with his teeth and fills a glass smoothie container a third full, pours a little more after a tentacle bursts in and sloshes some out, then throws the jug toward the entrance, where it shatters. The rest of the recipe is a dead fairy.

Quint's table gets two bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine when Mordecai sends Carl a private note. Carl still holds twenty-three more, and Quint trades him a starter kit, a chest of chemicals and herbs, after Donut, half asleep, haggles from four bottles down to three. At the Silk Road, Pustule examines a boom jug, whimpers, and licks the bottle. She then tells Carl the plain moonshine would sell for much more, and he keeps the jug.

tagline.text: The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is a recipe left in a dusty box beside a bicycle-powered blender. It takes two ingredients, and Carl reckons it is how a crawler is meant to get immunity from the Taint before fighting the boss.

The Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie is one part moonshine and one part fairy, blended pink on a child-sized bike. It gives ten doses of temporary immunity to health-seeping debuffs and disease, with the Buzzed debuff thrown in.
What is left of the smoothie from the second floor goes into Carl's infusion experiments, and mixed with a smoke curtain it is a dud.

description.text: Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie. One part moonshine, and one part fairy, this smoothie offers 10 doses for the price of one! Each sip of this delicious concoction imbues the following effects: Temporary immunity to all health-seeping conditions and debuffs. Temporary protection against all communicable diseases. Inflicts the Buzzed debuff. …

beats.headline: Two boxes in a corner
beats.text: In the corner of the clurichauns' room, Carl pulls a dangling banner, Rev-Up Smoothies! Invigorating!, off the wall and looks over two child-sized stationary bikes. A pulley runs from each tire to a little platform: a bicycle-powered blender, apparently never used. One wooden box holds twelve glass containers with screw-on lids and a lid with blades; the second holds six glasses, no blade, and a sheet of paper, the Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie Recipe. It needs two items. No wonder they discontinued this. Gross. It's all game setup, he tells Donut, and takes everything, one of the bikes included.
beats.gist: Carl pulls down a banner, finds a pedal-powered blender and two boxes, and takes everything, one bike included.

beats.headline: Blend until pink
beats.text: Tentacles are breaking through the walls when Carl shouts that he needs to make a goddamned smoothie. A third of a glass of moonshine; the dead laminak shoved in headfirst, her shoulders cracking; the bladed top screwed on. He sits on the much-too-small bike with his knees at his chest, recites the recipe aloud, and pedals. The fairy spins away, green, then red, then pink, and it starts to sparkle. Running, with the Taint already on him, he takes a sip that tastes like a diseased skunk, and shoves it at Donut to drink too.
beats.gist: Carl blends moonshine and a dead laminak into a smoothie on a bike, then makes Donut drink it.

beats.headline: Infection negated
beats.text: The smoothie does not lift the Taint Carl already carries, so he still cannot heal, but a pair of icons flashes for his immunity, and both of them are Buzzed: he laughs at his own death measles joke, and Donut slurs as she fires her missiles. Then a new tentacle, covered in hundreds of tiny orifices, sprays a fine green mist through the chamber. You've been infected with the Vigorous Measles! Infection negated due to immunity!
beats.gist: A tentacle sprays green mist, but the smoothie's immunity negates the Vigorous Measles.

beats.headline: A dud infusion
beats.text: Two smoke curtains are infusing at Carl's table, an idea from the cookbook he has been experimenting with. In the first he is trying a smoke curtain with a splash of the Rev-Up immunity smoothie he made on the second floor, the potion that gives temporary disease immunity and makes you drunk off your ass. He can tell right away it is a bust: the curtain is blacked out and has gained the Dud status, which is what usually happens. The second infusion, a recipe from the cookbook, works.
beats.gist: Carl tries a smoke curtain infused with his Rev-Up immunity smoothie, but it blacks out and turns Dud.

relations.note: immunity to the Vigorous Measles her tentacle sprays

recap.text: Carl pulls a banner off the clurichauns' wall and takes two boxes and one child-sized bike. With tentacles breaking through the walls, he pedals the too-small bike, blending moonshine and a dead laminak into a pink, sparkling smoothie. He sips it and shoves it at Donut. The Taint stays on him, both are Buzzed, and a tentacle's green mist of Vigorous Measles is negated due to immunity.

Carl sets two smoke curtains infusing at his table, both ideas from the cookbook he has been experimenting with. In the first he tries a splash of the Rev-Up immunity smoothie he made on the second floor, the potion that gives temporary disease immunity and makes the drinker drunk off their ass. The curtain blacks out and takes the Dud status, as usually happens. The second infusion, a recipe from the cookbook, works.

tagline.text: The Enchanted BigBoi Boxers are white, covered in little red hearts and self-sizing, because a were-creature's underwear has to survive the transformation. They give two Constitution and let the wearer cast a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours.

An upgrade has made Carl's boxers probably his most valuable item, Mordecai reckons: five more Dexterity, five more Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit. It adds a hundred percent damage bonus to every attack from below the waist and allows only a single layer over the crotch, so with the boxers on, no trousers.

description.text: Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. Have you ever read an Incredible Hulk comic and thought to yourself, everything rips off of his body except his pants? No way. Well, spoiler alert. You're not wrong. Size-altering and were-creatures, such as the BigBoi are required to wear enchanted, self-sizing items lest they wish to turn the dungeon into a nudist colony when they transform. That means everything they wear requires an enchantment. Everything, including their naughty little undies. + 2 to Constitution Wearer may cast a level 15 Protective Shell once every 30 hours.

Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. This item has been Upgraded once. All right, you already know the description of this item. Something something Incredible Hulk, blah, blah, blah. Now you want to know how this item has been upgraded. Right? So here are the original benefits of these naughty little undies: + 2 to Constitution Wearer may cast a level 15 Protective Shell once every 30 hours. That's some good shit right there. But we can do better than that. Here's a few additional benefits. + 5 to Dexterity + 5 to Intelligence + 3 more (for a total of + 5) to Constitution + The Freeballing Benefit

beats.headline: Really? Fucking really?
beats.text: Carl opens the boss box, tells himself not to say anything out loud, and says it to the ceiling anyway. Behind him Mordecai laughs, then adds that it is actually a really good prize: a white pair of boxers covered in little red hearts, the Enchanted BigBoi Boxers, plus two Constitution and a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours. Don't look, Carl says. He pulls his scorched and threadbare boxers off and slips the new ones on, and the old ones fall apart in his hands.
beats.gist: Carl opens the boss box and puts on white boxers covered in red hearts.

beats.headline: Upgraded, with a catch
beats.text: A Platinum Quest Box holds five thousand gold and a Scroll of Upgrade with a twenty-minute timer: one random equipped item gets better. Carl asks whether he can strip down to a single item to steer it. Yes, says Mordecai, but he wouldn't: the upgrade is never very good when people do that. Carl activates it, and his Enchanted BigBoi Boxers glow. Five Dexterity, five Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit, which allows a single layer over the crotch. You motherfucker, Carl tells the ceiling. Well played. You shouldn't have said you really wanted those pants, says Mordecai, and he and Donut laugh so hard Mongo wakes up.
beats.gist: Carl activates the scroll and his boxers gain stats and the Freeballing benefit, to Mordecai's amusement.

beats.headline: Train the spell, upgrade the shorts
beats.text: One training room here combines a regular training room, the magic workshop, the explosives studio and several others into one. Carl's ordinary spells are listed as trainable alongside the spells that come from equipment, like Protective Shell. Apparently, train one of those here and it is the equipment itself that gets upgraded: in the case of Protective Shell, his boxer shorts.
beats.gist: Carl's boxers can be upgraded by training the Protective Shell spell in the combined training room.

beats.headline: The squad's flag
beats.text: Every squad on this level gets a bundle of small flags to stick into the monsters, and nobody gets to design their own. The Royal Court's flag is a little bigger than Carl's hand, and it is an actual miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways, as if from a clothesline, with the Royal Court of Princess Donut embroidered top and bottom like a motorcycle-club patch and Carl's bomb patch over the crotch. Carl finds it tacky. Elle says her squad's flag has a bag of adult diapers on it, Donut reports, and Imani's has a butterfly, and she wants to know why they couldn't get something like that.
beats.gist: Donut's squad flag is a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers with Carl's bomb patch, which Carl finds tacky.

beats.headline: Worn over a kangaroo
beats.text: Carl shoves his arms into a stinking costume and pulls the kangaroo head over his own. There is a loud click. His boxers and kneepads are now on the outside of the costume, his jacket still on the inside, his cloak round his neck. Then two warnings: his boxer effects have been negated by the costume, and so have his pedicure effects.
beats.gist: Carl pulls on the kangaroo costume, and its click negates his boxer and pedicure effects.

beats.headline: Resized for a dachshund
beats.text: Carl has turned into a long-haired dachshund, with a high voice, a German accent, no thumbs and legs far too short to drive. As with the kangaroo costume, he is still wearing his boxers. They have resized themselves and sit awkwardly on his hips, and what dangles out of one leg of them is beyond his control. His kneepads remain, tiny on his back legs; none of his rings do.
beats.gist: Carl, now a dachshund, still wears his self-resized boxers and kneepads, but no rings.

relations.note: the Royal Court's flag is a miniature pair of them

recap.text: Carl opens the boss box, tells himself to keep quiet, and says "Really? Fucking really?" to the ceiling anyway. Mordecai laughs behind him, then admits the prize is a good one: white boxers covered in little red hearts, the Enchanted BigBoi Boxers, with two Constitution and a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours. Carl tells him not to look, pulls off his scorched, threadbare boxers, and puts the new pair on. The old ones fall apart in his hands.

Carl asks whether he can strip down to one item to steer a Scroll of Upgrade, and Mordecai says yes but advises against it. Carl activates it anyway, and his Enchanted BigBoi Boxers glow. They gain five Dexterity, five Intelligence, three Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit, which allows a single layer over the crotch. Mordecai and Donut laugh so hard Mongo wakes up.

One training room folds a regular training room, the magic workshop and the explosives studio, along with others, into a single space. Carl's ordinary spells sit in its list beside the spells that come from equipment, like Protective Shell. Training one of the equipment spells upgrades the equipment itself, so training Protective Shell upgrades his Enchanted BigBoi Boxers.

Carl's squad gets the same bundle of small flags as every other squad, with no say in the design. The Royal Court's flag is a little bigger than his hand: a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways as if from a clothesline, with the Royal Court of Princess Donut embroidered top and bottom and Carl's bomb patch over the crotch. Carl finds it tacky, and Donut wants to know why they couldn't get a butterfly like Imani's.

Carl pulls a stinking kangaroo costume on, head over his own, and a loud click sounds. His boxers and kneepads now sit outside it, and two warnings say it has negated his boxer effects and his pedicure effects. As a long-haired dachshund, he finds the boxers resized and awkward on his hips, what dangles from one leg beyond his control. His kneepads stay, tiny on his back legs; his rings do not.

entities.name: Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic

tagline.text: The Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic gives Donut two extra points of Constitution for thirty hours, as long as someone brushes her with it for ten minutes every night. It works much as Carl's pedicure kit does.
An upgrade out of a Scab box has the brush adding a further ten percent to Donut's Constitution, on top of its two points for a brushing.

beats.headline: Ten minutes every night
beats.text: Donut combs through her achievements and boxes and finds nothing noteworthy except one item. Her boss box holds an Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic, which works much like Carl's pedicure kit: as long as someone brushes her for ten minutes every night, she gets an extra two points of Constitution for thirty hours. It is better than nothing, Carl reckons, but even with the buff her Constitution is only four.
beats.gist: Donut's Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic adds two Constitution for thirty hours after ten minutes' nightly brushing.

beats.headline: She demands more brushing
beats.text: On the screen the shots keep coming, crawlers being slaughtered, and Carl can barely taste his fried chicken. At the table, Donut sits being lovingly groomed with her new brush by the safe room's Bopca Protector. The constitution buff activated many minutes ago. She demands he keep brushing. People are asleep in all twenty of the safe room's rooms for rent.
beats.gist: Donut sits being groomed with her new brush by the Bopca Protector while Carl barely tastes his chicken.

beats.headline: Part of the schedule
beats.text: Mordecai rambles about maintaining a schedule, and has somehow found what appears to be a dry erase board to mark it on. Wake, eat, apply buffs, which means showering and brushing Donut while Carl works on his feet, then an hour in the training room on one skill. Today Mordecai wants Smush. Apparently only one skill can be trained a day, even where skills overlap.
beats.gist: Mordecai plans the day on a dry erase board: today's hour of training goes to Smush.

beats.headline: Ten percent more
beats.text: In the Scab box, Donut receives an upgrade to her brush: the Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic now adds a further ten percent to her constitution, on top of the measly two points it normally gives for getting brushed each morning. The same haul brings a coupon for a free Town Upgrade and a skill potion for her Love Vampire skill.
beats.gist: In the Scab box, Donut's Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic upgrades to add ten percent more constitution.

beats.headline: Bomo, be a darling
beats.text: Donut has a program to go on, so she turns to Bomo, who is busy playing on the Gamecube: be a darling and brush me out. They say their goodbyes while Bomo brushes her. The cretin does it happily, though he is not nearly as enthusiastic about it as the Sledge had been.
beats.gist: Donut has Bomo brush her out while he plays the Gamecube; he does, less eagerly than the Sledge.

recap.text: Donut finds one item in her boss box: an Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic, which adds two points of Constitution for thirty hours if someone brushes her ten minutes every night. Carl reckons it beats nothing, though her Constitution is only four. At the table, the safe room's Bopca Protector brushes her while crawlers die on the screen and Carl barely tastes his fried chicken. The buff began many minutes ago, but Donut demands more.

Mordecai lays out a daily schedule and has found what looks like a dry erase board to write it on.
