The first set gave Mongo a damage buff and the chance to poison or paralyze, though neither seems to happen often, because the mobs are usually dead by the time he is chomping down on them. The two new caps add 15 percent movement speed and 15 percent strength to the level-29 dinosaur. Once again Donut makes Carl put them in, and he has to fish a piece of robot Donut out of Mongo's mouth first.
beats.gist: Donut's second platinum box holds fang caps again, adding 15 percent speed and strength to Mongo.

recap.text: Carl and Donut open her Platinum Quest Box and find 5,000 gold, a skill potion and a pair of fang caps. Mordecai says they don't suit her, so Carl snaps them into the sleeping Mongo's mouth, where they resize like Legos. In a muted zone, Carl sends Mongo at a dark elf, and the dinosaur tilts his head like he is eating a taco and caves in its head.

Donut's next platinum quest box holds a pair of fang caps and a skill potion, as the last one did. The first set gave Mongo a damage buff and a chance to poison or paralyze, but the mobs are usually dead before he chomps down. The new caps add 15 percent movement speed and 15 percent strength to the level-29 dinosaur. Donut makes Carl put them in, after he fishes a piece of robot Donut out of Mongo's mouth.

tagline.text: Hobgoblin dynamite comes in white sticks instead of goblin red, with a larger yield and far more stability. Carl's first whole box of it came with three globs of hobgoblin pus, remote-controlled detonators.
A stick of hobgoblin dynamite is practically a mini nuke: thrown half a block, it knocks Carl off his feet and brings down a building's front. It is utterly impractical in a regular fight.
Hobgoblin dynamite is much more stable than the goblin kind and should survive several impacts, so Carl builds it into his bigger bombs.
Carl cuts hobgoblin sticks down at need, carefully slicing one into twenty pieces.

beats.headline: White instead of red
beats.text: Sifting through his rewards, Carl finds more goblin dynamite and smoke bombs, and, in the bronze boss box from his fight with Heather, a whole box of hobgoblin dynamite along with three globs of Hobgoblin Pus, the remote-controlled explosive detonators. He has never seen hobgoblin dynamite before. The sticks are white instead of red, with a larger yield, and they are much more stable.
beats.gist: Carl finds a box of white, stabler hobgoblin dynamite and three Hobgoblin Pus detonators in Heather's bronze box.

beats.headline: Highway robbery
beats.text: Pustule's tables at the Silk Road hold boxes of goblin and hobgoblin dynamite, smoke bombs, detonators and pancake-like claymores at 5,000 gold each. A case of goblin dynamite is twenty-five sticks for 500 gold. The hobgoblin sticks are twenty for 2,000, which Carl calls highway robbery. Her fused hob-lobbers, she says, work like hobgoblin dynamite: impact resistant, extra stable, light the fuse and toss.
beats.gist: Pustule's Silk Road tables sell hobgoblin dynamite at twenty sticks for 2,000 gold, which Carl calls highway robbery.

beats.headline: Practically mini nukes
beats.text: From a rooftop near the saferoom, Carl does not want to waste his hob-lobbers on a handful of shambling berserkers, so he tries a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, which he has never used. He hurls it with his upgraded strength at a shambler half a block away. The explosion knocks him off his feet, the front of a distant building caves in and fills the street with debris, and the shambler and the one behind it are obliterated. The power is great, he decides, but the sticks are utterly impractical in regular fights.
beats.gist: Carl throws hobgoblin dynamite at a shambler; the blast kills two berserkers and collapses a building front.

beats.headline: Two robots, three sticks
beats.text: For the two robots, Carl uses three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite and a detonator. He sets the charges without incident, moves all the way back to the platform and sets them off. The automatons never turned on or fought back, and they come back as scrap, their bottom halves mostly intact and hunks of metal everywhere: the hobgoblin dynamite is especially good at tearing stuff up. Once the metal cools he collects all he can, cogs, wheels and two damaged dwarven batteries.
beats.gist: Carl blasts two idle robots to scrap with three hobgoblin dynamite sticks and collects cogs, wheels and batteries.

beats.headline: A stick in every mine
beats.text: Carl's new mines look like tire-shaped cross sections of the spiked naval contact mines of the early twentieth century, the plunger lifted from the cookbook and changed just enough. Each is an oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers, with a single, hopefully stable stick of hobgoblin dynamite added for extra measure. When a train depresses a spike, an impact-detonated hob-lobber shatters and the whole mine shreds. The system calls it a Jelly Bomb, and gives him no credit for inventing it.
beats.gist: Carl's new mines pack hob-lobbers and hobgoblin dynamite into metal tubes; the system calls them Jelly Bombs.

beats.headline: A train full of explosives
beats.text: Elle tells Carl by chat that some crazy asshole is throwing a train full of explosives their way. He laughs and ties the last piece of hobgoblin dynamite onto the pile. It is much more stable than the goblin stuff and should, in theory, survive multiple impacts, and the bundle rides up high so it won't go off until triggered: a long pole with an impact-detonated hob-lobber at the end, too high for the ordinary blister ghouls, low enough for a giant stage-three monster, or the back of the other train.
beats.gist: Carl laughs at Elle's warning and ties the last hobgoblin dynamite onto a high-riding pile.

beats.headline: A block per barrel
beats.text: They jump into burning, smoky chaos. The whole block is on fire and blown apart, a thick fog fills the air and bodies are everywhere. Carl's barrel explosives were crammed with gunpowder, hobgoblin dynamite and delay-detonated smoke curtains, packed for the most destruction: unstable as anything, but a single one can take out an entire block. They lived only because they hid inside a real saferoom.
beats.gist: Hobgoblin dynamite, packed into barrel bombs with gunpowder, can flatten a block; the pair survive inside a saferoom.

beats.headline: Over the trench
beats.text: Cries for shields run up and down the trench as giant, exploding monsters close in, and arrows, bolts and spears do nothing to them. Heads up, Carl calls, pulls a stick of full-strength hobgoblin dynamite and tosses it over the edge like a grenade. Everyone ducks and covers their ears. The blast rocks the ground, experience notifications fly by with a new achievement, and through the periscope the ones immediately in front are gone, though more keep coming. He prepares a second stick.
beats.gist: Carl throws a stick of hobgoblin dynamite into the exploding monsters and prepares a second.

relations.note: the bronze boss box for her fight

recap.text: Carl finds a whole box of hobgoblin dynamite in the bronze boss box from his fight with Heather, its sticks white instead of red, larger in yield and much more stable. Pustule sells twenty sticks for 2,000 gold, which Carl calls highway robbery. From a rooftop, he hurls one at a shambler half a block away. The blast knocks him off his feet, caves in a distant building's front and obliterates two shamblers.

Carl sets three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite under two robots, fires them from the platform, and collects cogs, wheels and two damaged dwarven batteries from the scrap. He packs one stick into each tire-shaped mine among the hob-lobbers, and the system names the design a Jelly Bomb without crediting him. Told by Elle that a train full of explosives is coming, he laughs and ties the last stick to the pile on a long pole.

They jump into burning, smoky chaos: the whole block is on fire and blown apart, fog hangs thick, and bodies lie everywhere. Carl's barrel explosives were crammed with gunpowder, hobgoblin dynamite and delay-detonated smoke curtains, unstable as anything, and a single one can take out an entire block. They live only because they hid inside a real saferoom.

Carl hears cries for shields run up the trench as giant, exploding monsters close in, and arrows, bolts and spears do nothing to them. He calls a warning, pulls a stick of full-strength hobgoblin dynamite and tosses it over the edge like a grenade while everyone ducks. The blast rocks the ground and sets a new achievement flying by. Through the periscope the ones in front are gone, though more keep coming, and he prepares a second stick.

tagline.text: A Scroll of Upgrade improves one random item a crawler has equipped, a little or a lot, and its short shelf life means it must be read at once. Carl's first makes his BigBoi Boxers probably his most valuable item, with the catch that he can no longer wear trousers.
Scrolls of Upgrade have been good to Carl. One won on the Wheel of Fortune takes his toe ring from +3 Strength to +10.
Not every Scroll of Upgrade is a great one: the third Carl reads only adds three Dexterity to his Trollskin Shirt.

description.text: Scroll of Upgrade! Warning: This item has a short shelf life. Maybe it's not as good as getting something new, but sometimes it's better to just take something you're already comfortable with and improve upon it. Kind of like buying your girl new tits. Once you read this scroll, one random, currently-equipped item will receive an upgrade. That upgrade could be small. It could be huge. But since this item has a short shelf life, you gotta do it now or forever hold your peace.

beats.headline: Freeballing
beats.text: Carl's Platinum Quest Box holds 5,000 gold and a Scroll of Upgrade, and a twenty-minute timer appears over it the moment he picks it up. Could he take off everything but one item? Mordecai has seen people try, and the upgrade is never very good. Carl reads it. His Enchanted BigBoi Boxers glow: plus five Dexterity, plus five Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit, a 100 percent damage bonus to attacks from below the waist, and only a single layer allowed over his crotch. No trousers. Mordecai and Donut laugh until Mongo wakes up. Usually these scrolls come deeper, Mordecai adds, but the two of them already have a name.
beats.gist: Carl's Platinum Quest Box holds a Scroll of Upgrade that makes his boxers glow with Freeballing.

beats.headline: Off the wheel
beats.text: The Wheel of Fortune settles on green, and a Scroll of Upgrade appears on the table in front of Carl with a twenty-minute countdown. He knows the rule this time: don't take anything off first. He reads it, his foot buzzes, and his toe ring glows. The Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk goes from +3 Strength to +10, and from +3 to +5 Powerful Strike, which puts the skill at 13. The closer it gets to 20, the more godly his damage becomes.
beats.gist: Carl reads a Scroll of Upgrade, and his toe ring goes to +10 Strength.

beats.headline: A decent one
beats.text: The best prize in the neighborhood boss boxes is a Scroll of Upgrade. They have been good to Carl so far. This one adds +3 Dexterity to his Trollskin Shirt. That is a decent upgrade, especially since he had been planning to put a couple of points into dexterity anyway, but it isn't a great one.
beats.gist: Carl uses a boss box's Scroll of Upgrade to add +3 Dexterity to his Trollskin Shirt.

recap.text: Carl opens a Platinum Quest Box holding 5,000 gold and a Scroll of Upgrade, and a twenty-minute timer starts over it. Mordecai warns that stripping down to one item never gives a good upgrade, but Carl reads it anyway. His Enchanted BigBoi Boxers glow with plus five Dexterity, plus five Intelligence, three more Constitution, and a 100 percent damage bonus to attacks from below the waist. Mordecai and Donut laugh until Mongo wakes up.

The Wheel of Fortune settles on green, and a Scroll of Upgrade appears in front of Carl with a twenty-minute countdown. He keeps everything on and reads it. His foot buzzes as the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk climbs from +3 to +10 Strength and from +3 to +5 on its strike skill, which now stands at 13. A neighborhood boss box yields another scroll, which adds +3 Dexterity to his Trollskin Shirt: decent, not great.

tagline.text: Blitz sticks are what the Desperado Club's pharmacists sell in place of earth tobacco: eat one for five points of Intelligence for a while, or smoke it for a fifteen percent chance at a permanent point, with a side effect or two. Mordecai says they are magically addictive.
Katia smokes blitz sticks she found on one of Eva's victims, and they show her what she asks them to. Only Daniel knows.
A blitz stick is like weed plus a hallucinogen that shows you memories that do not exist, which is why it is so damn addictive. The cure is a patch worn on the skin.

description.text: Blitz Stick. It's like candy, but for your mind. If you eat this, your Intelligence temporarily rises by five points. If you smoke it, there's a 15% chance your Intelligence will permanently rise by 1. There might be a side effect or two. Or three.

beats.headline: Three on the house
beats.text: The Desperado Club has no earth tobacco, the waitress says, but it has blitz sticks: shall she send a pharmacist over? Carl declines. Mordecai sends for Quint, the drug dealer on duty, and tells Carl to stay away from them: hallucinogens, magically addictive. Three bottles of moonshine buy Mordecai a starter kit. Then Quint throws in three licorice sticks on the house, not earth tobacco but worth a try: blitz sticks. Carl pulls them into his inventory before Mordecai can object.
beats.gist: Quint, the drug dealer, throws in three free blitz sticks, hallucinogens, and Carl pockets them before Mordecai objects.

beats.headline: Gold or drugs
beats.text: To get into Hump Town a dromedarian wants payment, gold or drugs, the dungeon's version of the old bumper sticker. Donut senses a deal and straightens on Carl's shoulder; he holds up a hand to stop her and holds up a single blitz stick instead, one of the couple he got from Quint. The camel squints at it, pops it in his mouth and lights it. Good shit. Welcome to Hump Town, and stay out of city hall. He wanders off smoking it and shows it proudly to another camel.
beats.gist: A dromedarian wants gold or drugs at Hump Town, so Carl offers a blitz stick.

beats.headline: Show me Annie
beats.text: Before the party, Daniel told Katia she was squeezing too tight and hurting him. After that, she pulled a blitz stick and lit it. Only Daniel knows: it is one of her two big secrets in this dungeon. She found the sticks on Sally, one of Eva's victims, a healer who had worked at the airport and turned to Eva despite everything. She is dead now, like the rest of them. The drugs were the only thing left in her inventory. Eva left them there, a present for Katia, and a trap. Show me Annie, Katia thinks, and the blitz stick obliges. Every time.
beats.gist: Daniel tells Katia she is squeezing too tight, and she lights a blitz stick from Eva's trap.

beats.headline: Memories that never happened
beats.text: Mordecai sets out what Katia has been taking. Blitz sticks are like weed plus a hallucinogen that shows you memories that do not exist, which is why they are so damn addictive. The cure is a patch she will have to wear on her skin for a while, and Imani has it ready to go. Katia has been on the blitz for a while, so it is going to be hard to get out of her system.
beats.gist: Mordecai says blitz sticks give Katia weed-like highs and false memories; Imani has a patch ready.

beats.headline: Show me Mistress Henspar
beats.text: Weeper Commander Volteeg drives his tank toward the warlord's caravan. You're getting too close to my caravan, the warlord protests. I know, Volteeg answers. That's the point. He reaches down and picks up a blitz stick, pops it into his mouth, lights it, and says to himself, Show me Mistress Henspar.
beats.gist: Volteeg lights a blitz stick in his mouth as his tank nears the warlord's caravan.

recap.text: Quint, the Desperado Club's drug dealer on duty, comes over after the waitress says the club has no earth tobacco but does stock blitz sticks. Mordecai warns Carl off them as magically addictive hallucinogens, then buys himself a starter kit with three bottles of moonshine. Quint adds three licorice-looking blitz sticks on the house, and Carl pulls them into his inventory before Mordecai can object.

Hump Town's dromedarian gatekeeper wants payment in gold or drugs. Donut straightens on Carl's shoulder, sensing a deal, but Carl holds up a hand to stop her and offers one blitz stick, one of the couple he got from Quint. The camel squints at it, pops it in his mouth and lights it. He waves them in, warns them off city hall, and wanders away smoking it, showing it proudly to another camel.

Daniel tells Katia she is squeezing too tight and hurting him, and she pulls a blitz stick and lights it. The sticks came off Sally, a healer who worked at the airport and turned to Eva despite everything, one of Eva's victims, now dead like the rest. Eva left the drugs as the only thing in Sally's inventory, a present for Katia and a trap. Katia thinks "Show me Annie," and the blitz stick obliges, every time.

Mordecai tells Katia what she has been taking: blitz sticks, which work like weed with a hallucinogen that shows her memories that never happened, and that is why they are so damn addictive. The cure is a patch she will have to wear on her skin, and Imani has it ready. Katia has been on the blitz for a while, so it will be hard to get out of her system.

Weeper Commander Volteeg drives his tank toward the warlord's caravan. The warlord protests that he is getting too close, and Volteeg answers that he knows, and that is the point. He picks up a blitz stick, pops it into his mouth and lights it, then says to himself, Show me Mistress Henspar.

tagline.text: Quint's starter kit is a suitcase that is really a large chest, filled to the brim with chemicals and herbs: everything you need for a pharmaceutical empire, he says. Mordecai got it for three bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine, a potion for Donut thrown in.
The starter kit's supplies sit on the alchemy table in the crafting room now, for Mordecai to work with.

beats.headline: A suitcase for an empire
beats.text: You still offer the starter kit, Mordecai asks Quint, the club's pharmacist, who did not expect anyone to afford one until the fifth or sixth floor. Two bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine appear on the table. Make it four, says Quint. Three, says a sleepy Donut, and you give me the potion to stop the world being wavy. Deal. Carl asks what they are buying: a suitcase with everything you need to start your own pharmaceutical empire, says Quint. Just don't sell in his territory. Mordecai is putting together a library. The suitcase is actually a large chest, filled to the brim with chemicals and herbs.
beats.gist: Mordecai buys Quint's starter kit: four bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine, and a chest of chemicals and herbs.

beats.headline: Onto the alchemy table
beats.text: In the crafting room, still empty, Mordecai tells Carl to set up his three tables and leave everything labelled an alchemical supply on the alchemy table, and he will start on a few things. Carl shoves the table against a wall and pulls everything in the alchemy category out of his inventory, from rat meat to the chest of supplies they bought from the drug dealer. By the time he is done, the simple table looks as if a mad scientist has set up shop at a swap meet.
beats.gist: Mordecai has Carl set up three tables, and Carl piles every alchemical supply onto one.

relations.note: three bottles

recap.text: Mordecai asks Quint, the club's pharmacist, whether the starter kit is still on offer, though Quint never expected anyone to afford one before the fifth or sixth floor. Two bottles of Rev-Up Moonshine appear on the table. Quint asks for four, the sleepy Donut holds out for three and the potion that stops the world being wavy, and the deal is struck. The suitcase is a large chest, filled to the brim with chemicals and herbs.

Mordecai tells Carl to set up his three tables in the empty crafting room and put everything labelled an alchemical supply on the alchemy table. Carl shoves the table against a wall and pulls everything in the alchemy category out of his inventory, from rat meat to the chest of supplies bought from the drug dealer. When he finishes, the simple table looks like a mad scientist has set up shop at a swap meet.

entities.name: Framed photograph of Bea and Brad

tagline.text: Donut's first gold fan box holds a small, framed photograph of Miss Beatrice, lifted from her Instagram: Bea in a bikini, laughing, on her ex-boyfriend Brad's lap. It is the photo that made Carl break up with her, and Donut loves it.
Donut keeps the framed photograph of Bea on a small table beside the bed, which is where she makes Carl put it.

beats.headline: Voted in by the fans
beats.text: The first fan boxes open at the pub, and Donut's holds a small, framed picture. Of Bea. The square photo comes straight from her Instagram, and it is the one that made Carl break up with her: Bea in a bikini, laughing, on her ex-boyfriend's lap with her arm draped round his shoulder, taking the selfie. Brad, handle Brad_the_Chad69. Donut is thrilled and shows everyone. Look, Mongo, it's your grandmother! Mordecai watches Carl, not the picture. It doesn't bother Carl, and that feels almost monumental. Mongo hisses at it a couple of times until Donut admonishes him.
beats.gist: Donut's fan box holds a framed photo of Bea on Brad's lap, and Carl feels nothing.

beats.headline: By the bed
beats.text: Donut lays the room out. The bathroom goes in the corner; Carl has to put the cat tree beside the Ultra-Stabilized Bed, which has a semi-transparent mattress like clear Jell-O, and then the framed picture of Bea on a small table next to the bed. Then she tells Carl to get in bed, Mongo too, because they are all tired. Carl points out that he has his own room now.
beats.gist: Donut arranges the room and puts the cat tree and Bea's picture by the bed.

beats.headline: Never put away
beats.text: Carl clicks a screen of viewer comments off, with Donut snuggled in his arm. Her candle sits right by the screen, and beside it the photograph of Bea and Brad, which she has never put away. That's okay. Carl pushes the photo aside, pulls a lighter and lights the candle, and the scent of home fills the room.
beats.gist: Donut keeps Bea and Brad's photograph by her candle, and Carl pushes it aside to light the candle.

recap.text: Framed photograph of Bea and Brad comes out of Donut's fan box at the pub, a square picture from Bea's Instagram, the one that made Carl break up with her. In it Bea laughs in a bikini on her ex-boyfriend Brad_the_Chad69's lap, her arm draped round his shoulder. Donut shows everyone and tells Mongo it is his grandmother; Mongo hisses until Donut admonishes him. Mordecai watches Carl, who finds it doesn't bother him.

Donut lays out the room. The bathroom goes in the corner, and Carl has to put the cat tree beside the Ultra-Stabilized Bed, whose semi-transparent mattress looks like clear Jell-O. The framed picture of Bea goes on a small table next to the bed. Donut tells Carl to get in bed, and Mongo too, because they are all tired. Carl points out that he has his own room now.

Carl clicks off a screen of viewer comments, Donut snuggled in his arm. Her candle sits by the screen, and beside it stands the photograph of Bea and Brad, which she has never put away. Carl decides that's okay. He pushes the photograph aside, pulls out a lighter and lights the candle, and the scent of home fills the room.

tagline.text: The Gate Pass is a slip of paper from GumGum's inventory, signed by Magistrate Featherfall: the holder is doing this on his orders. It keeps the Over City's swordsmen off a crawler carrying a corpse, inside the township that issued it.

description.text: Gate Pass. When one walks about the streets of any town within the Over City, the mindless Swordsman guards tend to get a bit squirrely if you're carrying a corpse with you. When it comes to their black and white view of justice, the rule of law is absolute. Unless you have a gate pass. This letter gets the city guard off your back as long you're not being too overt with your current criminal enterprise. Pass only works within the township in which it was issued.

beats.headline: On GumGum's body
beats.text: GumGum the orc lies dead in an alley with her chest ripped open and no blood, likely the work of three Krasue. Her inventory holds four gold coins and two pieces of paper, and Carl takes both. One is a Gate Pass. Back at the inn he reads it: the Swordsman guards get squirrely about anyone carrying a corpse, unless they have one of these. The paper itself reads that the holder is doing this on the magistrate's orders, signed Magistrate Featherfall. A Get-Out-of-Jail card, Carl calls it.
beats.gist: GumGum's body yields a Gate Pass, signed by Magistrate Featherfall, which lets Carl carry corpses past guards.

beats.headline: A corpse for the desk
beats.text: Look at my desk, you fools, says Miss Quill, because there is a dead prostitute on it. The moment they found the body that morning, with a gruesome note scrawled onto her flesh, Carl called a swordsman over, pointed to the corpse, showed the guard the Gate Pass, and took the body into his inventory. He does not know for certain that it does anything. But if the guards have seen him with the body and, in their odd way, endorsed it, tossing it onto her desk should not count as a crime. Hopefully. Without a word, the two guards turn and walk back down the stairs.
beats.gist: Miss Quill finds a dead body on her desk, put there by Carl.

recap.text: Carl finds GumGum the orc dead in an alley, her chest ripped open and bloodless, and takes the Gate Pass and one other paper from her inventory. At the inn he reads that the pass says the holder acts on Magistrate Featherfall's orders. Next morning he shows it to a swordsman, drops a dead prostitute onto Miss Quill's desk, and the two guards turn and walk away.

tagline.text: The Mysterious Letter is a folded, blood-soaked paper from GumGum's inventory, written in squiggles and triangles nobody can read. Mordecai recognises necroscript, something an undead magic user would write, and suspects a lich.
The letter is a used Suppurating Eye scroll, and Mordecai thinks the blood on it is the caster's own. Whenever it is out of Carl's inventory, whoever cast it can see and hear what happens around it.

description.text: Mysterious Letter. GumGum the orc had this blood-soaked letter in her possession. It's in an odd language. Is it a clue? Is it a grocery list? You can't fucking read it, so who knows?

beats.headline: Squiggles and triangles
beats.text: The second paper from GumGum's body is a Mysterious Letter, folded and stained red with blood, a short note in a language that is all squiggles and triangles. The System is no help: a clue, or a grocery list? Mordecai recognises the squiggles, and sounds nervous. Necroscript, something an undead magic user would write out, probably a type of scroll, readable only with the language skill. Krasue are usually henchwomen for something else, he says, and the two of them might have a lich problem. That night Carl stares at the symbols, trying to memorise them.
beats.gist: Carl tries to memorise a blood-stained letter in necroscript, which Mordecai says means a lich problem.

beats.headline: A spy camera in blood
beats.text: Mordecai has worked the letter out. Carl swore, in a safe room, to hunt down whoever killed GumGum, and within moments a dead woman was dropped on the building with No you won't carved into her. He had been clutching the letter as he said it. It is a used necroscript scroll of Suppurating Eye, a common lich spell: the caster leaks a bodily fluid onto a surface and can see and hear anything near it, and he thinks the blood on this one is the caster's. It does not work from inside an inventory. Donut wants to use it, so on a rooftop she and Carl talk for whoever is listening.
beats.gist: Mordecai identifies the letter as a Suppurating Eye scroll, a spy camera in blood.

beats.headline: Swallowed whole
beats.text: Donut splits Mongo into three and pulls the real one back into his carrier, and Carl sets two lit smoke curtains billowing over the rooftops. Then he pulls the letter out. We're jumping onto the roof now, he says, crumples it up and tosses it in the air. One of the clockwork Mongos grabs it and swallows it whole, and the pair leap across the alley and a full story up to the top of the magistrate's building, one of them howling into the night.
beats.gist: Donut splits Mongo into three, Carl throws smoke and a crumpled letter, and a clockwork Mongo swallows it.

recap.text: Mordecai reads the Mysterious Letter as a used necroscript scroll of Suppurating Eye, a common lich spell that lets the caster see and hear near the blood. Carl had been clutching it when he swore to hunt GumGum's killer. On a rooftop, Donut splits Mongo into three and Carl lights two smoke curtains. He crumples the letter and tosses it up, and a clockwork Mongo swallows it whole.

tagline.text: The Scroll of Meat Hooks came off a dead city elf who used the spell to lure Mongo away into an alley. Cast, it draws every nearby carnivorous pet-class monster to the source of a burning stench.

Read from a plane, with Donut's charisma giving it a range of almost three kilometres, the Scroll of Meat Hooks trails a stench behind them like a blown engine, and draws a giant two-headed puppy out of the water after it.

description.text: Scroll of Meat Hooks. Let's be real. Every pet owner already has this spell, at least when it comes to their own pets. Sometimes it's the sound of a can opener. Or a command, such as "chow time, Fido!" Sometimes it's the wisp of a jar of peanut butter being cracked open. No matter what the trigger is, the effect is the same. You do something, and your pets come running. Meat Hooks works on the same principle. You cast, and pets come to you. …

beats.headline: Off a dead city elf
beats.text: Vicente the city elf has almost 1,500 gold in his inventory and one other item, a scroll, which Donut takes. It is for a spell called Meat Hooks, the one he had been casting when Mongo rushed into the alley: it summons all nearby carnivorous pet-class monsters away from their owners to the source of a burning stench. I knew he was a good boy, says Donut. He'd been summoned, and he couldn't help it. Carl tells her to hold onto it. You never know when it might be useful.
beats.gist: Donut takes Vicente's Meat Hooks scroll, which summons pet monsters to a burning stench.

beats.headline: Read from a plane
beats.text: Orthrus, an enormous two-headed puppy, has to be got out of the water and out of his bubble, and Donut still has the scroll from the third floor. Carl rereads it first: thirty seconds plus ten per point of the caster's intelligence, a hundred metres plus twenty per point of charisma. With Donut's numbers that is just over nine minutes and almost three kilometres. Read the scroll, he calls from the plane, and the stench trails behind them like a blown engine. Donut is going to vomit. The puppy pulls itself off the necropolis, tips over the edge of the bubble and tumbles out. Quest complete.
beats.gist: Donut rereads the scroll's range, then Carl reads it from a plane, and Orthrus tumbles out.

beats.headline: Still spewing
beats.text: Orthrus whimpers below. Donut heals him back up to seventy percent, and the renewed health renews the dog's interest in chasing them at once. The Meat Hooks spell is still spewing from Donut's paw. Carl turns the plane sharply between two bubbles, growing more confident at the controls, and then a metal-skinned dirigible shaped like a fish comes out of nowhere in front of them, full of more crawlers.
beats.gist: Donut heals Orthrus to seventy percent, which renews his chase, and a fish-shaped dirigible appears ahead.

recap.text: Vicente the dead city elf carries almost 1,500 gold and one other item, a scroll, which Donut takes. It holds Meat Hooks, the spell he was casting when Mongo rushed into the alley, which pulls every nearby carnivorous pet-class monster away from its owner toward a burning stench. Donut says Mongo was a good boy who couldn't help being summoned. Carl tells her to hold onto the scroll, since it might be useful.

Carl rereads the Meat Hooks scroll and works out that Donut's numbers give just over nine minutes and almost three kilometres. She reads it from the plane, the stench trailing like a blown engine, and Orthrus, the two-headed puppy, tumbles out of his bubble. Donut heals him to seventy percent, which sends him chasing them at once. Carl swerves between two bubbles, and a metal-skinned dirigible shaped like a fish looms ahead, full of more crawlers.

tagline.text: Hundreds of swordsmen guards stand in stasis in a warehouse, their yellow aura all leading to one point in the ceiling, and Carl reckons a soul crystal is up there somewhere.

A soul crystal is elf technology, a charger that runs on the souls of everything killed nearby. The one over the swordsmen's warehouse is overloading, and the map puts it at the epicentre of an explosion with a blast radius of forty-five square kilometres.
The guard depot's soul crystal went off inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case, and the two together are Carl's Doomsday Scenario now.
Soul crystals power the fourth floor's ghoul generators too, and the generators do not take kindly to being blown up.

The soul crystals elves use are mined from Scolopendra's lair, made when certain kinds of people die and their souls are filtered through the centipede. Once installed as a power source they are worth nothing, except as an explosive.

description.text: Soul Crystal. C-Grade. Elf technology. It's like a wireless charger. Instead of electricity, it runs on the soul power of everything killed within the area. And instead of charging your iPhone, this particular gem tops off the town's Swordsmen guards each night. Some of that power is also leeching into something else. If this crystal is physically touched by living flesh, it will shatter and cease to work.

beats.headline: A point in the ceiling
beats.text: Through the open door of the warehouse's first level, even in the dark, Carl can see the inactive Swordsmen guards: hundreds of them in silent formation, like the terracotta army, with no dots over them on his map. A yellow aura swirls round their metallic bodies, and all of it leads to a point in the ceiling. There would be a soul crystal up there somewhere. At night, Mordecai says, the guards are in stasis and invulnerable, so locking them in and blowing them up over and over is out.
beats.gist: Carl sees hundreds of dormant Swordsmen guards, their yellow auras all leading to a ceiling point.

beats.headline: The Amplifier
beats.text: In the room above the warehouse a golf-ball-sized amber jewel floats, tethered to Remex's chest by a thread of golden light, a stalk of light running down through the floor. Carl examines it: a C-grade soul crystal that charges the swordsmen each night and shatters if living flesh touches it. With Miss Quill gone, Remex says, there is no siphon tonight. The roof is the antennae, he explains, and the soul crystal stores the power: that is the Amplifier. The map puts the gem at the epicentre of the coming blast. Breaking it, Mordecai thinks, would only make it blow early. A red timer appears over it.
beats.gist: Remex's soul crystal, the Amplifier, stores the roof's power and would only blow early if broken.

beats.headline: Half of a bomb
beats.text: The explosion goes off silently inside the glass case Carl closed round the gem. Light streams from the container like a miniature, caged sun, one lance-like ray straight into Remex's chest, and the floorboards bubble and burn. The case and the gem have transformed. Carl reads Status: Explosion Imminent in the two seconds before he grabs it and pulls it into his inventory, burning the skin off his fingers. It is Carl's Doomsday Scenario now, created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case.
beats.gist: Carl burns his fingers pocketing a caged, overloaded soul crystal, now his Doomsday Scenario.

beats.headline: The ghoul generators
beats.text: The fourth floor's Blister Ghouls come out of soul crystal-powered ghoul generators, one ghoul for every non-undead mob that dies on the floor, and every mob on the floor is suffering from something that will kill it. Goddamn soul crystals, Carl thinks: they powered the swordsmen on the third floor and Miss Quill's spell, and one became the bomb still sitting in his inventory, which he has not dared take out at his sapper's table. The generators are run by soul crystals, he tells Elle, and they don't take kindly to being blown up.
beats.gist: Soul crystals power the ghoul generators, and Carl tells Elle they dislike being blown up.

beats.headline: A blast far off
beats.text: An explosion far away is still loud and powerful enough to be felt where Carl is. A team of something like 300 to 400 crawlers had set out to fight their way to the blister ghoul generator at one of the station 72s, to remove the crystal or disable the machine. I think they blew the soul crystal, Carl says; he warned them it was dangerous. He tells Imani and Elle to send a group to find the line there: if the generator blew, everything over there is dead, but the stairwells might still be open.
beats.gist: Carl hears a far-off explosion and fears the crawlers blew the soul crystal.

beats.headline: Not in vain
beats.text: Elle's away team, with the help of Tizquick the dwarf, finds the right coloured line to the exploded station 72, where plenty of other crawlers had the same idea. The ceiling has caved in, but the circle of stairwells remains, and people have cleared the rubble. Word goes out that it is a place to descend without fighting, and crawlers flock to it. The ones who died blowing the soul crystal did not, at least, die in vain.
beats.gist: Crawlers flock to station 72's cleared stairwells; the dead did not die in vain.

beats.headline: Mined from the centipede
beats.text: In a hologram of goods on offer sits a grape-sized, colourless gem that glitters as it moves. Carl takes it for a soul crystal at first. Those are without value once installed as a power source, unless used as an explosive; unused ones are supposedly rare and treasured. This one is listed as something else. Mordecai explains: the soul crystals elves use to power their things are mined from Scolopendra's lair, created when certain types of people die and their souls are filtered through the centipede's body. Memorial crystals are similar, but made by fallen gods and demigods.
beats.gist: Mordecai explains that elves mine soul crystals, made from certain dead people's filtered souls, in Scolopendra's lair.

relations.note: his capacitor leeches off the souls flowing into it

recap.text: Hundreds of Swordsmen guards stand in stasis below, a yellow aura leading to a point in the ceiling. Above, a golf-ball-sized amber soul crystal floats, tethered to Remex's chest, and Carl shuts a glass case round it. The blast goes off silently inside the case, one ray striking Remex's chest, and Carl grabs the gem, burning the skin off his fingers. It is his Doomsday Scenario now, made of the soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case.

Carl tells Elle that soul crystals run the ghoul generators and don't take kindly to being blown up. A far-off explosion reaches him: 300 to 400 crawlers had gone to wreck the generator at a station 72. Tizquick the dwarf helps Elle's away team find the line there, where the ceiling has caved in but the circle of stairwells stands, cleared of rubble. Crawlers flock to descend without fighting, so the dead did not die in vain.

Carl finds a grape-sized, colourless gem that glitters as it moves in a hologram of goods on offer, and he takes it for a soul crystal. Soul crystals are worthless once installed as a power source, unless used as an explosive, but this gem is listed as something else. Mordecai explains that elves mine their power-source crystals from Scolopendra's lair, where the souls of certain dead people are filtered through the centipede's body.

tagline.text: A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is a small, expensive protective case forged in the fires of Sheol and sold by travelling Spider Reaper Minions. Carl's is one of Miss Quill's, pulled from the debris of her building with Kimaris inside, and every time it opens there is a 1.5 percent chance of Sheol Fire.
The case Carl closed round an overloading soul crystal is half of Carl's Doomsday Scenario now, a caged explosion sitting in his inventory.

description.text: Sheol Glass Reaper Case. Forged in the fires of Sheol, the mysterious 15th level of the World Dungeon, these protective, expensive artifacts are built and sold by traveling Spider Reaper Minions. They also sell lollipops, which are said to be out of this world. When you absolutely, positively want to keep something safe, put it in this box. It will protect against most—but not all—forms of abuse. Warning: Every time you open this case, there is a 1.5% chance you will be blasted with the Sheol Fire spell. That's not a good thing. The item within the case will remain protected.

beats.headline: Opened, then read
beats.text: Sorted by value, the top item in Carl's inventory is Miss Quill's stuffed horse-riding soldier, Kimaris, and the second is the glass case it is stored in. The little door isn't locked, just a hinged flap held by a cheap-looking hook and eyebolt. Carl opens it, pulls the plush into his inventory, and only then reads the case: forged in Sheol, sold by Spider Reaper Minions, a 1.5 percent chance of Sheol Fire every time it opens. He should have read that first. He remembers a flash of light when they landed in the debris, and decides the System brought the case to his attention on purpose.
beats.gist: Carl opens the glass case first, then reads its 1.5 percent Sheol Fire risk.

beats.headline: Like catching a firefly
beats.text: Four and a half minutes are left on the soul gem's red timer. Careful not to touch it, Carl closes the case round the floating gem like catching a firefly in his two hands, shuts the door and hooks it closed. He tries to pull the whole thing into his inventory and gets an error. He lets go. The case drops a couple of inches, clinks against the gem and floats there with it, while cracks form along the gem's edge. Most forms of abuse, the description said. He sits down on the floor, and Donut jumps into his lap to watch.
beats.gist: Carl shuts the soul gem in the glass case, fails to store it, and sits as cracks spread.

beats.headline: A caged sun
beats.text: Remex's scream jolts Carl's eyes open. They are not dead. The case has fallen to the floor, glowing red hot, light streaming from it like a miniature, caged sun, and the floorboards are bubbling. Case and gem have transformed themselves. Carl reads Status: Explosion Imminent in the two seconds before he grabs it, and pulls it into his inventory as the skin burns off his fingers. The new item is Carl's Doomsday Scenario, created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case.
beats.gist: Carl's eyes open to a red-hot case, fused with the gem into Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

beats.headline: Five more, unopened
beats.text: Bautista explains his stuffed animals. His most valuable, a legendary, came in a weird glass case. He has five more legendary rares and is afraid to open their cases: the description says there is a chance of being blasted with fire, and a Sage Sprite told him it could still trigger in a safe room, where he would be safe but case and item both would be ruined. He thinks he might open them in his inventory, but is too scared to try. It is the same kind of case Carl's Kimaris figure came in, the one that now holds Carl's Doomsday Scenario.
beats.gist: Bautista fears opening his five unopened legendary rares because their glass cases might blast him with fire.

relations.note: five more, still closed round his legendary plush toys

recap.text: Carl opens the case, pulls the stuffed horse-riding soldier Kimaris into his inventory, and only then reads that it carries a 1.5 percent chance of Sheol Fire per opening. With four and a half minutes left on the soul gem's timer, he hooks the gem inside it. Remex's scream wakes him to a red-hot case glowing like a caged sun, and he grabs it, skin burning off his fingers, and pulls it into his inventory as Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

Bautista explains that his most valuable stuffed animal, a legendary, came in a weird glass case, and that he has five more legendary rares he will not open. The description warns of a fire blast, and a Sage Sprite told him it could still go off in a safe room, ruining case and item. Carl's Kimaris figure came in the same kind of case, which now holds his Doomsday Scenario.

tagline.text: A Red Line Engineer's Key is what the magically locked service plate under a red line car's gangway floor asks for, and the System is happy to point out that Carl does not have one.
The keys are colour coded, Carl says, so each one works only on its own line's trains, and it takes one to get into the engine car at the front.
Carl holds two now: the Ochre Line Engineer's Key from a dead engineer, and a large bronze Steam Engineer's Key from the Nightmare's cab, good for all four hundred of the Tangle's steam trains.
An engineer's key is a pass as well. Equipped or held outside inventory, it lets a crawler through the gated portals over the abyss, which lead to a trainyard.

Keys are rescue gear now: crawlers trapped at the abyss need a hat or a key to get through the portals, and at station 75 Carl collects fifteen coloured-line keys from his fellow crawlers along with more than seven hundred hats.

description.text: Steam Engineer's Key. Allows access to Iron Tangle employee-only areas and actions on all 400 steam-type trains of the Tangle.

beats.headline: A plate that wants a key
beats.text: Aboard a red line subway car, with monsters in the next one, Carl gets down on his knees and pulls up the panel in the gangway floor, hoping to find the train's electrical system and the controls for the couplers. Under it is a small metal door with a lock, like a breaker box. He puts his hand on it and gets an error: the service plate is magically locked, and he needs a Red Line Engineer's Key. Do you have a key? No you don't. So back off. Carl puts the panel back. It will have to be the nuclear option.
beats.gist: Carl lifts a gangway panel and finds a locked plate that demands a Red Line Engineer's Key.

beats.headline: Colour coded
beats.text: From what Gore-Gore has let slip, Katia reckons they can get back to the start if they can get into an engine car. They need an engineer's key, she says; he probably has it in his inventory, and with it they could break into the first car while the train is still moving. Carl agrees, but the keys are colour coded, so an ochre key will only work on ochre trains, and crashing a train to get one stops the rest of the line, which would make the key useless. Doesn't a crash only stop the trains behind it, asks Donut? Take the key and jump ahead on the Nightmare Express or one of the other fast loop trains. That's brilliant, says Carl.
beats.gist: Katia wants an engineer's key from Gore-Gore, and Donut proposes jumping ahead of a crash.

beats.headline: Off the third rail
beats.text: One clockwork Mongo explodes when it touches metal on the third rail; the other drags Gore-Gore's corpse up against the wall of the channel, and Carl loots it: 498 gold and three items. An Ochre Line Engineer's Key, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, and the neighborhood map. The map is the surprise. It fills his interface not with the area around him but with the whole ochre line, every stop from station 11 to 435, and where every train on it is right now.
beats.gist: Carl loots a Mongo's corpse and finds an Ochre Line Engineer's Key and a map.

beats.headline: Bronze, in the gore
beats.text: Carl is in the Nightmare Express's cab and has just boxed up its bricks. In the mess of gore, where the driver or the war mage was pushed against the box at the back, he finds a small satchel holding 350 gold and a large, bronze key: a Steam Engineer's Key. It allows access to the Tangle's employee-only areas and actions on all four hundred of its steam-type trains. Only then does he relax enough to look around. He is alive, and he has stolen a goddamned train.
beats.gist: Carl finds a Steam Engineer's Key in the cab's gore, having stolen a train.

beats.headline: Three keys in the list
beats.text: At Abyss Station, Carl reads a portal over the pit. It is gated by conveyance type and to key holders: a crawler must be on a gated conveyance, or have a key equipped or held outside inventory, and compatible keys have been marked. Sorting his inventory on the way back down the stairs, he finds three: the Ochre Key, the Steam Train Key, and the souvenir hat from the start of the floor. His message to every crawler on his chat list sets out the ways through, and one of them is to kill an engineer and take his key, without crashing the train.
beats.gist: Carl finds three keys in his inventory and lists the ways through for his chat list.

beats.headline: The Vermillion key
beats.text: Hekla is dead, Donut has her corpse up and lurching at the Daughters, and Carl is tugging at its crossbow when he sees the square access panel in the gangway floor. Katia has to get the Vermillion key from Hekla's corpse, he tells her, and it has to be her, because she killed Hekla. Get the key first. The engine doors were blocked so they never locked, but uncoupling the car still needs it. Once the cab door is slid shut and locked against the Daughters' spells, he asks whether she got it. I got it, says Katia. Not that it matters now.
beats.gist: Katia must take the Vermillion key from Hekla's corpse, since she killed Hekla, and she does.

beats.headline: In Donut's mouth
beats.text: The last of the hat-wearing crawlers have gone through the portal to yard H, and the party follows on the cart. Carl puts his own hat on. Donut does not want to remove her tiara, so instead she sighs and holds an engineer's key in her mouth, and Mongo goes into his carrier. Carl suspects that since the cart itself is allowed through, they need neither hat nor key, but there is a cliff on the other side and no sense risking it. He eases the cart through, and just like that, it is done.
beats.gist: Donut holds a key in her mouth as Carl eases the cart through the portal.

relations.note: the Ochre Line key
the Steam Engineer's Key, in the cab
through the gated portals over the abyss
the Vermillion key, taken by Katia
both are marked as keys to the abyss portals

recap.text: Carl lifts a gangway panel on a red line car and finds a lock that wants a Red Line Engineer's Key he lacks. He loots an Ochre Line key from Gore-Gore's corpse, then a bronze Steam Engineer's Key from the gore in the Nightmare Express's cab. Katia takes a Vermillion key from Hekla's corpse. Donut holds a key in her mouth as the cart rolls through the portal.

tagline.text: The moment the floor begins, the System hands out one each for an achievement: a blue and white toddler's hat embroidered with I rode the Iron Tangle. Carl examines his. It is not magical. It is junk.
The souvenir hat is a key. Equipped, it carries a crawler through the gated portals over the abyss, and some crawlers have already sold theirs, for five thousand gold apiece.
With the Kravyad's portal closed and the trains stopped, a crawler without a hat may have no way off the line, and more than a hundred and fifty of Bautista's group have none.
Carl is carrying more than seven hundred of them, given up by crawlers who heard what they were for, to hand out to the people trapped at the abyss.
The hats have done their work. The crawlers Carl brought through give theirs to Donut, one by one, in tribute, and she gathers every one into her inventory.
Nobody is buying the hats any more, not even for a single gold, and Carl has not had the heart to tell Donut.

beats.headline: Choo Choo
beats.text: The party lands in a hurtling subway car, Mongo screeching in anger and fear, Donut trembling on Carl's shoulder, Katia clutching a pole, and the System greets them with an achievement: I'm on a train! Choo Choo, Motherfucker. The reward is a Train Conductor's Souvenir Hat. Wear it with pride! Getting dressed in the car, Carl briefly examines his, and it is junk. It is not magical. It is a simple, blue and white hat of the kind one would see on a toddler, with the words I rode the Iron Tangle embroidered on it.
beats.gist: Carl's party lands in a subway car, and the System rewards him with a junk toddler's hat.

beats.headline: The stupid hat was a key
beats.text: Going down the stairs from the abyss, Carl sorts his inventory by the items the portal has marked, and finds three keys to it: the Ochre Key, the Steam Train Key, and that stupid souvenir hat. Holy shit. All they needed to do was equip the hat. He messages everybody on his chat list: equip the hat, ride a train to the end of the line, and you will get through, though the train car will not, and you will land in a station full of thousands of zombies. Mei W answers that her whole party sold theirs. They were offering five thousand gold each.
beats.gist: Carl learns the souvenir hat is a key, and tells everyone to ride a train wearing it.

beats.headline: No hat, no way out
beats.text: Bautista sends an update. They tried to paralyse the Kravyad, she ended up dying, and the portal closed. Over 150 of them do not have their souvenir hats, the trains have stopped coming on all the tracks, and they are heading for the abyss portal on foot, about fifty kilometres. Does he have a hat, Carl asks. Nope. A guy at the bar was bragging about how much they were buying them for, and a bunch of them sold. Dumb. Get to the abyss, Carl tells him, and send those who have hats through on foot.
beats.gist: Bautista reports over 150 of them sold their souvenir hats, so Carl tells him to reach the abyss.

beats.headline: Seven hundred in twenty minutes
beats.text: With people trapped at the end of the line, the plan is to take the battered Vermillion car all the way there and hand out as many hats as possible. At station 75 Carl trades fist bumps and loudly asks for people's hats and any keys they have gathered. They are standoffish at first; once they learn why, they coordinate and spread the word, and in twenty minutes he has over 700 hats and fifteen keys. Donut whispers that they could sell them for over three million. The System awards him Mentally Unstable Clothing Hoarder, and declines to reward the behaviour. It's weird.
beats.gist: Carl trades fist bumps at station 75 and gets over 700 hats and fifteen keys in twenty minutes.

beats.headline: Plan C, and a tribute
beats.text: Carl changes the plan: he has enough hats in his inventory for everybody, so they go through the abyss portal and skip the mimic waiting at the cart portal. Donut wants the hats back afterwards. Millions of gold, Carl. He tosses thirty on the ground behind the cart for stragglers, puts his own on, and they go through. Then Bautista takes his off and sets it in front of Donut. For you, Princess Donut. A line forms, each crawler bowing and dropping the stupid train hat in tribute. It was Katia's idea. Donut gathers them all into her inventory, tail swishing.
beats.gist: Carl swaps the plan, hands out train hats, and the crawlers bow and drop theirs before Donut.

beats.headline: Not for a single gold
beats.text: The whole group is waiting at the open stairwell for them. Carl, Carl, Donut cries as they approach: we never tried to sell my hats! Carl had, actually, tried to sell one while she was in the training room. The proprietor laughed at him and said nobody was buying them any more. Not even for a single gold. He hasn't the heart to tell her. They will try on the next floor, he says.
beats.gist: Carl fails to sell Donut's hat while she trains and keeps the failure from her.

beats.headline: Luca Di
beats.text: An entry in Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess is Luca Di's: a human Pastamancer, final level 62. You probably don't remember me, Princess, it begins, but I was one of the ones to give you my train hat on the fourth floor. She saved his life, he writes, and the life of his mother, Giulia DiMarco, as well. They never got along when he was growing up, and when her dementia came they placed her in a home. Guilt finally got the best of him, and he went to visit her on that day.
beats.gist: Luca Di writes that Donut saved his life and his mother's after he gave her his train hat.

relations.note: equipped, through the gated portals over the abyss
more than seven hundred, collected at station 75
given to her in tribute

recap.text: Carl finds on the stairs down from the abyss that the stupid souvenir hat is one of three keys to the portal. Mei W's party sold theirs for five thousand gold each, and Bautista's group lost theirs and the portal. At station 75 Carl collects over 700 hats and fifteen keys, and everyone goes through the abyss portal. Donut gathers the hats in tribute, while Carl keeps quiet that nobody would buy one, not even for a single gold.

Luca Di, a human Pastamancer who died at level 62, has an entry in Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess. He writes that she saved his life and his mother Giulia DiMarco's, after he gave her his train hat on the fourth floor. The two never got along, and her dementia put her in a home. Guilt got the best of him, and he went to visit her.

tagline.text: The Bang Bro tome comes out of the bronze boss box Carl earned for killing Miss Quill. Read, it teaches a five-mana spell that adds fire and electrical damage to whatever he has equipped, and Mordecai says it will work on his gauntlet.

description.text: Bang Bro Cost: 5 Mana Target: Temporarily Enchant Equipped Item Duration: 5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell. Requires 5 minute cooldown. Adds both fire and electrical damage to any currently-equipped item. May not be cast on flesh. Well, actually it can be cast on (your own) flesh, but I really wouldn't recommend it. May inflict Burn and Shock on targets. Can also be used to cook hotdogs and other items.

beats.headline: Out of Quill's boss box
beats.text: Among the loot from the quest is the bronze boss box from killing Miss Quill, and inside it a magical tome for a spell called Bang Bro. Carl sets it aside, and after a new skill comes back to it: five mana, five minutes and a minute more per level, fire and electrical damage on any equipped item, and it cooks hotdogs. He shows Mordecai. It will work on the gauntlet, Mordecai says, but not on the xistera, not the way Carl loads it, and on his foot only while his invulnerable buff is up. It is a good spell in his mana price range. Carl reads the tome and adds the spell to his list.
beats.gist: Carl reads the Bang Bro tome from Quill's boss box and adds the spell to his list.

beats.headline: Lit up for Gore-Gore
beats.text: A smoke curtain, Donut's Hole in front of the charging mantaur, Carl's Fear, and then he casts Bang Bro on his gauntlet, which glows with electrical fire, and downs a mana refill. Gore-Gore swings blind through the smoke, squealing about treachery, magic and wizardry. Carl punches him in the kidney of his lower torso; the body feels like a sack stuffed with gravel, and the health bar drops maybe five percent. A notification hangs on his interface, 1.5, and he remembers to be careful: every punch from that gauntlet has a 1.5 percent chance to summon Grull.
beats.gist: Carl casts Bang Bro on his gauntlet and punches Gore-Gore, who barely flinches; each punch risks summoning Grull.

beats.headline: A skull on the fist
beats.text: Mid-race, sugar hermits surge in the gaps between the giant tubes, and a skull comes into the cab through the missing windshield. Carl punches it with his gauntlet and it explodes, but the purple thing living inside the skull is still attached to the metal fist, and it starts to slither, octopus-like, toward his arm. He casts Bang Bro, which electrifies the weapon. The creature drops off, dead, sizzling.
beats.gist: Carl punches a skull, and when the purple creature clings to his fist, Bang Bro electrifies it.

relations.note: A bronze boss box for killing her

recap.text: Carl reads the tome from Miss Quill's bronze boss box. Bang Bro costs five mana, lasts five minutes plus one per level, adds fire and electrical damage to an equipped item, and cooks hotdogs. Mordecai says it works on the gauntlet, not the xistera. Carl casts it on the gauntlet and punches Gore-Gore in the kidney, and the health bar drops five percent.

Carl punches a skull that has come through the missing windshield into the cab mid-race, while sugar hermits surge in the gaps between the giant tubes. The skull explodes, but the purple thing that lived inside it stays attached to his metal fist and starts to slither, octopus-like, toward his arm. He casts Bang Bro, which electrifies the gauntlet, and the creature drops off, dead and sizzling.

tagline.text: Mordecai says the personal space's second tier will offer something called a Bomber's Studio, which would let Carl practise blowing things up.

Carl's Advanced Bomber's Studio is a room ten feet wide and as long as a bowling lane. It holds a virtual range where any explosive he copies can be set off and paused mid-blast, and at the back a bench for taking real bombs apart.
When Carl leaves Donut's party, the bomber's studio stays on her side with most of his crafting tables, so that if he dies she does not lose it all.

beats.headline: Something for tier two
beats.text: Katia spends one of her coupons on a Training Room, which trains any skill that is not a magic spell for an hour a day, supposedly as if the crawler were really fighting with it. It costs 250,000 gold, and it will not train anything explosive. Mordecai says tier two will have something called a Bomber's Studio, which would let Carl practise blowing shit up. It joins the list of upgrades Carl still wants, beside the expensive kitchen ones that serve food with buffs and the kennel ones that do the same for Mongo.
beats.gist: Katia's Training Room costs 250,000 gold and won't train explosives; Mordecai says tier two's Bomber's Studio will.

beats.headline: A class with a room
beats.text: At the filthy screen where he picks his class specialty, Carl has three choices. Mordecai insists on the melee one. The Guerilla gets the Advanced Trap Maker's Workshop, which is only a table. The Agent Provocateur gets plus one intelligence a level, a skill level for his Sapper's table, plus two to Explosives Handling, faster explosives training and access to the advanced Bomb Maker's Workshop: an entire room, where he could precisely tune his explosives, and which a few recipes in his cookbook need. With a minute left and the coin slot's orange light blinking, he clicks the third choice. Sorry, Mordecai.
beats.gist: Carl picks the Agent Provocateur, trading Mordecai's melee choice for a bomb room, with a minute left.

beats.headline: A private bowling alley
beats.text: Carl has bought the advanced bomber's studio alongside a magic workshop, which leaves them only 100K gold. The room is only about ten feet wide but long, like a private bowling alley. Nothing in its testing area really explodes: he can copy a design or a bomb, build a virtual village, set it off, pause it and see which way it blows, though the system sometimes gives only a range, and the cookbook stresses it is no guarantee. Being advanced, it can also test virtual bombs he does not have, though for now only with items in his inventory. At the very back is a level-one bench for examining and dissecting explosives. On it he sets Carl's Doomsday Scenario, out of his inventory for the first time since he grabbed it, copies it into the simulator and puts it back, his hands trembling.
beats.gist: Carl buys the advanced bomber's studio and builds a simulator-bench to test and copy his Doomsday Scenario.

beats.headline: Freshly upgraded, still waiting
beats.text: Before heading out into Old Havana, Carl wants to get into the craft room and play with his new automaton pieces, and his bomber's studio has just been upgraded, so he wants to go in there too. Mordecai is already making noises about the crafting table upgrade coupons. Carl tells him they should get their bearings first, and goes back to ring the exit stairwell with traps instead.
beats.gist: Carl puts off the new studio and Mordecai's coupons, and rings the exit stairwell with traps.

beats.headline: Part of Rosetta's price
beats.text: Rosetta wants the toraline and what is left of the ink Shi Maria brewed for Carl's tattoo. Then she wants access to his saferoom, so they can get to work. Give me access to your bomber's studio, too, she says. And three million gold. She glares at the finger-sized sliver of vegetable he hands over. Better make it four million.
beats.gist: Rosetta demands the toraline, leftover ink, and both rooms, then raises her price to four million.

beats.headline: Justice Light needs nothing
beats.text: Losing the saferoom entrance will put base a half-hour ride away by tracked vehicle, and more. Justice Light will lose access to Carl's sapper's table and the bomber's studio, and Rosetta easy access to the alchemy table and Mordecai. The one-winged skyfowl, sewing a folded piece of red paper to an orange one in the corner, tilts his head and stretches out his lone wing. It's okay, the eagle says. I already have everything I need.
beats.gist: Justice Light will lose its sapper's table and bomber's studio, but the one-winged eagle says he needs nothing.

beats.headline: Left on Donut's side
beats.text: Before Carl leaves the Royal Court of Princess Donut, the garage will not be affected by his leaving, and Imani is ready to join his segregated room back into the guild. Most of his crafting tables, the bomber's studio included, will remain on Donut's side. It will make things easier once he rejoins. Plus, if he dies, she will not lose it all. He clicks Yes.
beats.gist: Carl clicks Yes, leaving his bomber's studio on Donut's side so Imani can rejoin his room.

recap.text: Mordecai says tier two will have a Bomber's Studio, which would let Carl practise blowing shit up. Katia spends a coupon on a Training Room that trains any skill that is not a magic spell for an hour a day, but it costs 250,000 gold and will not train anything explosive. The studio joins the upgrades Carl still wants.

Carl picks the Agent Provocateur at the filthy screen with a minute left and the coin slot's orange light blinking, over Mordecai's insistence on the melee one. The choice buys him an entire room, the advanced bomber's studio, long and narrow like a private bowling alley. At its back bench, his hands trembling, he sets Carl's Doomsday Scenario down for the first time since he grabbed it, copies it into the simulator and puts it back.

Before heading out into Old Havana, Carl wants to get into the craft room and play with his new automaton pieces, and his bomber's studio has just been upgraded, so he wants to go in there too. Mordecai is already making noises about the crafting table upgrade coupons. Carl tells him they should get their bearings first, then goes back to ring the exit stairwell with traps.

Rosetta demands the toraline, the last of Shi Maria's tattoo ink, access to Carl's saferoom and bomber's studio, and three million gold. She glares at the finger-sized sliver of vegetable he hands over and raises the price to four million. Losing the saferoom entrance puts base a half-hour tracked ride away. The one-winged eagle, sewing red paper to orange, says he already has everything he needs.

Before Carl leaves the Royal Court of Princess Donut, the garage will not be affected by his leaving, and Imani is ready to join his segregated room back into the guild. Most of his crafting tables, the bomber's studio included, stay on Donut's side. That makes things easier once he rejoins, and if he dies, she will not lose it all. He clicks Yes.

entities.name: Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie

tagline.text: The Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie is the second smallest of the chains of leadership, and Carl has it for becoming magistrate of a Skyfowl town. Its one gem, a poor sapphire, gives him dexterity, the Talon Strike skill and 432 gold in taxes every ten days.

description.text: Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie. The second smallest of the chains of leadership, it is still considered a great honor to be the custodian of this burden. Each jewel encrusted upon this charm represents a settlement owned and controlled by the bearer. If one still maintains a settlement's jewel upon the collapse of the level, the holder of this necklace will permanently receive a tax stipend every ten days from that settlement based on size and population. […] One Attached Gem: Poor Sapphire. Medium Skyfowl Settlement (Third Floor). +5 to Dexterity. +Talon Strike (Level 5) Taxes received: 432 Gold every 10 days. May you be a kind and just leader.

beats.headline: From the Tyrant's box
beats.text: Becoming the town's new magistrate earned Carl a Platinum Tyrant's Box, and it holds 10,000 gold and a necklace: a simple silver-coloured chain, a quarter-sized charm, a tiny yellow jewel. It is the second smallest of the chains of leadership. Each jewel is a settlement the bearer controls, and one still held when the level collapses pays a tax stipend every ten days for good. To upgrade it he would have to conquer a large settlement. Carl guesses that explains why the townsfolk never recognised him as their leader: he probably had to put it on first. When he does, he gains five dexterity and the Talon Strike skill, and tucks it under his shirt. It feels heavier than it should.
beats.gist: Carl puts on the silver chain from the Tyrant's box and gains five dexterity and Talon Strike.

beats.headline: A sliver of amethyst
beats.text: Killing a mayor has earned Carl a gold Tyrant's box. It holds a sliver of an amethyst, smaller than the poor sapphire already on his necklace, and it gives him three points of dexterity and nothing else. Donut's red gem on her own leadership charm gave two intelligence, one dexterity and a few points in a spear-throwing skill she will never use, and its small settlement pays her only 403 gold every ten days, which annoys her.
beats.gist: Carl's Tyrant's box for killing a mayor holds only an amethyst sliver worth three dexterity.

relations.note: Its first gem is a Skyfowl settlement
Donut's, the middle size of the chains of leadership

recap.text: Carl wins the post of town magistrate and a Platinum Tyrant's Box holding 10,000 gold and a silver-coloured chain with a quarter-sized charm and a tiny yellow jewel. Each jewel is a settlement he controls. Carl guesses the townsfolk never saw him as their leader because he had not put it on. He does, gains five dexterity and the Talon Strike skill, and tucks it under his shirt, where it feels heavier than it should.

Killing a mayor earns Carl a gold Tyrant's box, and it holds a sliver of amethyst, smaller than the poor sapphire already on his necklace. The sliver gives him three points of dexterity and nothing else. Donut's red gem on her own leadership charm gave two intelligence, one dexterity and a few points in a spear-throwing skill she will never use, and her small settlement pays her only 403 gold every ten days, which annoys her.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita is a crystal tiara like the one Donut lost, with white jewels instead of purple. It adds intelligence, helps her spot mobs on the map, and keeps the worshippers of an obscure goddess from attacking on sight.
Donut wears the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly now. The Tiara of Mana Genita is kept, in case it is useful one day.

description.text: Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita. A crystal tiara fit for royalty. Made in honor of all the lost children of the world. Because nothing helps sooth the tears of grieving parents like watching someone else dress up all fancy. +3 Intelligence Increased ability to detect mobs on the map. Removes automatic hostility by worshippers of Mana Genita.

beats.headline: White instead of purple
beats.text: Donut's boxes are mostly random scrolls and useless items to sell, but one of them, Carl is not sure which, holds a new tiara, and it poofs onto her head. It looks like her last one, with white jewels instead of purple. It is not as good as the one she lost: three intelligence, a better eye for mobs on the map, and no automatic hostility from the worshippers of Mana Genita. Who is Mana Genita, Carl asks. A goddess, says Mordecai, a pretty obscure one he does not think he has ever run across, big on spells, he thinks. There are thousands of them, and only a few are dungeon regulars.
beats.gist: Donut's new tiara has white jewels instead of purple, and Mordecai calls Mana Genita obscure.

beats.headline: Kept for a rainy day
beats.text: Since the crown, the white Tiara of Mana Genita is what Donut usually wears. But a Flawless Jeweler's Gem from a legendary box needs a setting, a yellow-orange citrine she insists will clash. They keep the old tiara, which might be useful one day, and buy a blank one from the gnome jeweler at the Desperado Club; it takes Donut twenty minutes, and a threat to leave, to choose a simple silver one. They pay 25,000 gold to have the citrine installed, and her dislike of the colour ends with the description: the Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly.
beats.gist: Donut keeps her old tiara, then pays 25,000 gold to set a citrine in a silver one.

recap.text: Donut's boxes hold mostly random scrolls and useless items to sell, but one of them, Carl cannot tell which, holds a new tiara, and it poofs onto her head. It has white jewels where her lost one had purple, and it gives three intelligence, a better eye for mobs on the map, and no automatic hostility from the worshippers of Mana Genita. Mordecai, asked who that is, calls her an obscure goddess, big on spells.

Since the crown, Donut usually wears the white Tiara of Mana Genita. A Flawless Jeweler's Gem from a legendary box needs a setting, and the yellow-orange citrine is one she insists will clash. They keep the old tiara and buy a blank one from the gnome jeweler at the Desperado Club, where Donut takes twenty minutes, and a threat to leave, to choose a silver one. They pay 25,000 gold to install the citrine.

tagline.text: The Hole spellbook is Donut's Book of the Floor Club prize, waiting in a saferoom mailbox, and reading it teaches her Hole: a temporary hole in any surface she chooses. At level one it is not deep enough to get through most doors.

beats.headline: Read, not sold
beats.text: Donut has a spellbook coming to her, and remembering it, she rushes to the mailbox in the restaurant's shadowy corner, opens it, and grunts. When is she going to get a good spell, something with some kick, like Fireball? For once she asks Mordecai whether to read it or sell it. Read it, he says, and she glows. It is a spell called Hole, he explains, and it does exactly what it sounds like: a temporary hole on a surface of her choosing. A level-one hole is not thick enough to get through most doors, but it is a useful spell, especially if she is creative. Carl can already think of half a dozen uses.
beats.gist: Donut asks Mordecai whether to read or sell her spellbook, and he says read it, teaching her Hole.

beats.headline: On three
beats.text: The war mage Dismember stands on the far side of Carl's metal plate, promising to peel the skin off them and keep them alive afterwards. Carl lets him talk and counts on his fingers. On three, a hole appears in the metal. Carl reaches through, grabs the surprised elf-like creature by his long silver hair and pulls, and the moment the head is through, Donut snaps the spell off. The severed head drops to the floor with its mouth still open wide.
beats.gist: Dismember threatens to skin them, so Carl pulls him through a hole and Donut severs his head.

beats.headline: The bottom of the basket
beats.text: In the balloon basket with the gnomes, missiles in the air, two of Katia's spikes burst from the bundle and pierce the wicker, anchoring her, and Donut casts Hole in the bottom of the basket right underneath all of them. She has practised it up to a meter and a half across, which makes it thinner, and that does not matter here. The three gnomes drop through, astonished, as Crixus's grenade ball flies wide over Carl's shoulder; Carl pulls his feet up onto the bench. At the last moment Leon grabs the edge of the hole, until an ethereal cat paw pushes him off.
beats.gist: Donut casts Hole under the gnomes in the basket, and all three drop through.

beats.headline: Under her own feet
beats.text: The dog's jaws close right through Donut. There were five Donuts, not four, and she had laid the middle illusion over herself. She had also downed an invisibility potion, and she had cast Hole under her own feet just as the dog lunged. The view changes to the outside, and a translucent outline of Donut drops straight down and lands deftly on the ground beside the burning tree. Carl cannot believe that worked.
beats.gist: Donut hides among her illusions, turns invisible, and drops through a Hole cast under her own feet.

recap.text: Donut rushes to the mailbox in the restaurant's shadowy corner and grunts at her spellbook, since she wanted something with kick, like Fireball. Mordecai tells her to read it, and she learns Hole. Behind Carl's metal plate, the war mage Dismember promises to flay them. Carl counts to three, Donut opens a hole, and Carl hauls him through by his silver hair. Donut snaps the spell off, and the severed head drops, mouth still open.

Two of Katia's spikes pierce the wicker and anchor her, and Donut casts Hole in the bottom of the basket under them all. The three gnomes drop through, astonished, as Crixus's grenade ball flies wide over Carl's shoulder, and Carl pulls his feet up onto the bench. Leon grabs the edge of the hole until an ethereal cat paw pushes him off.

The dog's jaws close on Donut and pass right through her. There were five Donuts, not four, and she had laid the middle illusion over herself, drunk an invisibility potion, and cast Hole under her own feet as the dog lunged. She drops straight down and lands deftly on the ground beside the burning tree, while Carl cannot believe it worked.

entities.name: Upgrade coupon
entities.role: Slips of paper worth an upgrade

tagline.text: The AI's special box paid out seven slips of paper each: a coupon for a free level-three personal space, two for tier-one environmental upgrades, two for free tier-one crafting tables and two for table upgrades. Each is worth up to 250,000 gold, and two cannot be combined on one item.
Mordecai wanted everyone's table upgrade coupons for his alchemy table, but Carl spent his on the sapper's table and Katia hers on a makeup table.
