Coupons keep coming in boxes: Carl now has three third-tier personal space upgrade coupons and a town upgrade for a castle, on top of the lower-tier town upgrade from the Tina quest.

beats.headline: Seven slips of paper
beats.text: The AI's special box opens, and it is just seven slips of paper. Carl laughs out loud. A coupon for a free Personal Space, upgraded to level three. Two for a free tier-one environmental upgrade. Two for a free tier-one crafting table. Two for a table upgrade. Katia has received the same, and Mordecai, shown them, has to sit down. Cash them in now, he says: the space and the environmental upgrades travel with you, and so do the tables, which upgrade on their own every time you go down a floor. Save the two table upgrade coupons.
beats.gist: Katia and Carl open seven slips of paper; Mordecai says to cash all but two table upgrade coupons.

beats.headline: Three spaces make a five
beats.text: Donut drops her coupon on Wendita's counter, and the Bopca's hands tremble: a level-three space. Carl and Katia turn theirs in too, and conjoined, the three give the benefits of a level-five space. The fine print says each coupon is worth at most 250,000 gold and two may not be combined for a single item. One of Donut's buys the Ultra-Stabilized bed, two hours of sleep for full rest. Mordecai makes Carl save his last for the store. They pay 15,000 gold on top, and Wendita accepts the coupons with tears streaming down her face.
beats.gist: Donut, Carl and Katia pool three coupons into a level-five space, then pay 15,000 gold while Wendita weeps.

beats.headline: Two on the alchemy table
beats.text: Mordecai is hunched over the alchemy table and snaps at them to get back before they contaminate it. He used her two table upgrade coupons on the alchemy table, Donut says; he asked her permission earlier. So the table is now level three. She makes a face.
beats.gist: Donut says Mordecai spent her two table upgrade coupons on the alchemy table, making it level three.

beats.headline: A level-three makeup table
beats.text: Katia has bought a new table Mordecai told her about, a Makeup Table. At level three she can superimpose the face of any monster, crawler or NPC she has met on the glass, which makes sculpting easier, and it doesn't hurt when she sits at it. Level three? You used your upgrade coupons, Carl asks, trying not to sound horrified. Yes, she did. Mordecai is going to be pissed: he wanted to talk her into using them on his alchemy table. But they were her coupons.
beats.gist: Katia spends her upgrade coupons on a Makeup Table, not Mordecai's alchemy table.

beats.headline: Armorer's table, sapper's three
beats.text: Carl asks the Bopca Nodd for the crafting table menu: a long list, most of it useless, most about 25,000 gold, from the generic Tinker's Table to a Beekeeper Beesuit Mending Station. He slides one of his two free table coupons forward for the one he wants, an armorer's table. Then he presents his two upgrade coupons, hesitates over whether it is the right move, and asks to upgrade his Sapper's table to level three.
beats.gist: Carl spends a free coupon on an armorer's table, then two upgrade coupons on his Sapper's table.

beats.headline: Already spent
beats.text: Now that they know how to get to the front, Mordecai says, they only need to wait out the timer and hop down the stairs. Oh, and then give him their table upgrade coupons, so he can boost his alchemy table before they go down a floor. Carl exchanges a look with Katia. They have both already spent the upgrade coupons. Okay, says Carl: they will give him a quick recap, but he has to promise not to smack them again.
beats.gist: Mordecai wants their table upgrade coupons, but Carl and Katia have already spent them.

beats.headline: A fourth in a different colour
beats.text: The Legendary Hell Comes to Crawler Town box holds, as promised, a set of unenchanted bagpipes, and three third-tier personal space upgrade coupons plus a fourth one in a different colour. That's a town upgrade, says Mordecai: Carl will need it for his castle, and he and Donut already have a lower-tier one each from the Tina quest a few floors back. When Carl pulls the town upgrade coupon out, it tells him little, only that he must go to an owned town to use it.
beats.gist: Carl's box holds bagpipes and four coupons, one a town upgrade usable only in an owned town.

beats.headline: Three for Shanty Town
beats.text: Shanty Town is controlled by the Princess Posse now, and Baroness Victory calls it a smart trade: it circles Larracos and gives the NPCs an extra layer of security, one the Posse controls. We have three town upgrade coupons, Carl says, one each from the Tina quest and a tier-three one he just got in a box. Can they use them here? Absolutely, says Victory, and they might get something like the Larracos city defense system. But the coupons could also go on their base, and that may be the better choice.
beats.gist: Carl has three town upgrade coupons; Victory says they work in Shanty Town.

relations.note: Donut's two table upgrades went on his alchemy table
offered as a use for them

recap.text: The AI's box holds seven slips of paper; Carl laughs, and Mordecai has to sit down when he sees them. Donut, Carl and Katia turn in their space coupons, and Wendita weeps as the three conjoin into a level-five space. Donut's two table upgrades go to Mordecai's alchemy table, Katia buys a level-three Makeup Table, and Carl upgrades his Sapper's table. Mordecai asks for their table coupons anyway, and Carl admits both are spent.

Carl opens the Legendary Hell Comes to Crawler Town box and finds unenchanted bagpipes, three third-tier personal space upgrade coupons, and a fourth in a different colour. Mordecai calls it a town upgrade, which Carl will need for his castle. At Shanty Town, held by the Princess Posse, Baroness Victory says the three town coupons might buy something like the Larracos city defense system, though the base may be the better use.

tagline.text: The Battery Fabricator sits in a dusty corner of Limp Richard's general store at 75,000 gold, price not negotiable. Pour in mana potions, add a brick-sized metal block, and a charged battery is supposed to come out the other side.

Carl owns the Battery Fabricator now, traded for the rest of his westerns and a jug of moonshine. Four full mana potions and five minutes charge one dwarven battery, and the powered railway carts at this station can run on them.

beats.headline: In a dusty corner
beats.text: Limp Richard's general store sells nothing much worth having; Donut talks a padded mallet down from 250 gold to 150. In a dusty corner stands a thing called a Battery Fabricator, about the size of a microwave, listed at 75,000 gold. The shop's own description admits it does not really know how the thing works: taken from a dwarven automaton factory, mana potions in, a metal block in, a charged battery out, a box of fifty batteries included, price not negotiable. Each battery is about the size and weight of a brick. The system will not give a real description until it is bought. Carl wants it on sight and cannot justify the price.
beats.gist: Carl wants the 75,000-gold Battery Fabricator, a mystery dwarven machine, on sight but cannot justify the price.

beats.headline: Traded for westerns and moonshine
beats.text: Pulling the battery from a railway cart, Carl recognises it: a dwarven battery, at two percent. He has the fabricator now, traded for the rest of his westerns and a single jug of moonshine; the mole man practically begged, having finished the books Carl had already given him. Carl suspected the fabricator's odd placement in the first store they came to was no coincidence. The cookbook says each battery takes four full mana potions to charge, and it takes five minutes. Fifty came with it, most at ten to fifteen percent, five full and five at half; Carl charged two more, for twelve usable. If every powered cart here has one, that is another forty-plus for the stash.
beats.gist: Carl trades his remaining westerns and a jug of moonshine for a dwarven battery fabricator.

relations.note: Its carts run on dwarven batteries

recap.text: Donut haggles a padded mallet down from 250 gold to 150 at Limp Richard's, but the Battery Fabricator in the dusty corner, listed at 75,000 gold, stays out of reach. Carl pulls a dwarven battery at two percent from a railway cart and knows it on sight. He has the fabricator now, traded to a mole man for the rest of his westerns and one jug of moonshine; four mana potions charge a battery, and twelve are usable.

tagline.text: The Gangway Chock is Carl's own name for a sheet of metal, a swordsman's breastplate thinned and stretched, that wedges into the gangway between two train cars. With wedge-shaped door blocks on the outer doors, it lets the party keep a cleared car to itself.
One leftover door block from the Iron Tangle has been coated by Mordecai with a holy protection oil, which makes it a repellent against the undead.

beats.headline: Holding a car
beats.text: Carl has fabricated quick and dirty fortifications at the engineering workbench: four exterior door blocks and two gangway blocks, enough to hold a cleared car if the doors open on only one side. He closes the door to car three and pulls out a giant rectangle of metal with rounded edges, a swordsman's breastplate thinned to a fifth of an inch so it could be made big. It would take four or five normal humans to lift. He calls it the Gangway Chock, and it is too wide for anything but tiny monsters to slip past. The door blocks are tall wedges made from altered weight benches, held by crossbars through the handholds. He made them too slim, and they rattle.
beats.gist: Carl barricades car three with a rattling Gangway Chock and slim door blocks cut from weight benches.

beats.headline: A head through the plate
beats.text: Fail, and every crawler on the train becomes a flesher, so Carl runs for the back of the train pulling a chock. The first version is too big; it catches on the ceiling and crashes to the floor. The next size down is a flat plate rounded at the top, half an inch thick and around 800 pounds, and Katia helps him push it against the doorway. On the far side the war mage Dismember promises to flay them all. Carl counts to three on his fingers, a hole appears in the metal, and he reaches through and pulls the mage's head through it by the hair. The moment he does, Donut snaps the spell off, and the severed head drops to the floor.
beats.gist: Carl pulls the war mage Dismember's head through a hole in the barricade, and Donut's spell-cancel drops it.

beats.headline: Peeled like a baked potato
beats.text: Trapped in a building with Louis and Firas while the camels close in, Carl leaned one of his heavy chocks from the subway level against the door and braced it to the ceiling. Louis and Firas hit the deck as the chock is hit with an explosive. Fire licks through the room. The chock is bent over and knocked loose with a hole in its centre, peeled open like a baked potato. The brace from floor to ceiling holds. The door itself is shattered, and black, choking smoke fills the room.
beats.gist: Carl braces a chock against the door; an explosive peels it open, but the brace holds.

beats.headline: Blessed, against ghommids
beats.text: Ghommids are pounding at the temple, Donut's mana is low, and Carl pulls the blessed chock: a leftover metal door block from the Iron Tangle that Mordecai coated with a holy protection oil. It is more a repellent than a wall, but it should keep the undead from passing through like ghosts and from pouring into the temple, and it is plenty big enough. He shoves it against the door and leans on it while they pound. When the gem touches the obelisk and the temple restores itself, the metal chock disappears, and in its place stands an intact wooden door, propped open on a well-lit town.
beats.gist: Carl blocks the temple door with a blessed chock, which becomes a wooden door onto a town.

relations.note: He blessed a leftover door block

recap.text: Carl sets out the Gangway Chock, a swordsman's breastplate thinned to a fifth of an inch. When he fails, every crawler on the train becomes a flesher, and the first chock he drags crashes off the ceiling. He and Katia push an 800-pound plate against the doorway, and Carl pulls the war mage Dismember's head through a hole in it by the hair. Donut snaps the spell off, and the head drops.

Trapped in a building with Louis and Firas while the camels close in, Carl leans a heavy chock from the subway level against the door and braces it to the ceiling. Louis and Firas hit the deck as an explosive strikes the chock, and fire licks through the room. The chock is peeled open like a baked potato, but the brace holds. The door is shattered, and black smoke fills the room.

Ghommids pound at the temple and Donut's mana is low, so Carl shoves the blessed chock against the door and leans on it. It is a leftover metal door block from the Iron Tangle, coated by Mordecai in holy protection oil, and it should keep the undead from passing through like ghosts. When the gem touches the obelisk and the temple restores itself, the chock disappears, and an intact wooden door stands propped open on a well-lit town.

tagline.text: An Invisibility Potion does what it says. Carl's first is in the pocket of somebody's suitcase on a train, next to two mana potions.
Invisibility potions keep turning up in Carl's boxes, and he makes sure Donut always has a few. Smashed against someone, one works on them too.

description.text: Invisibility Potion. Guess what this does.

beats.headline: In someone's suitcase
beats.text: Carl unzips the suitcase and pulls out red lingerie: women's clothing, high-heeled shoes and brochures about things to do in Delaware. It is just someone's suitcase, he says, not a real prize. Then Donut points at a bulge in one of the pockets. Inside are three potions, two mana potions and something new. Invisibility Potion. Guess what this does. Oh hell yeah, says Carl, and now the system lets him put everything into his inventory, suitcase and clothes included.
beats.gist: Carl finds red lingerie, heels and Delaware brochures in a suitcase, then Donut spots an Invisibility Potion.

beats.headline: Thirty seconds, intelligence times two
beats.text: As light bursts from the mangled mantaur, the mimic's tongue lashes at Carl, slaps the still-forming god aside and sends it flying. Carl rolls, slams the last item in his hotlist and applies his potion of Invisibility just as the tongue smacks into the spot where he was. Dude! Where'd you go? He is invisible for thirty seconds, his intelligence times two, and he should have put more points into that stat. The mimic roars and belches, and a mass of mouth minions the size of rhinoceroses bursts out, several of them coming his way.
beats.gist: Carl applies Invisibility as the mimic's tongue smacks where he stood, for thirty seconds.

beats.headline: Soaked into a smoke curtain
beats.text: At the infusing trays Carl soaks a Hobgoblin smoke curtain in an invisibility potion, and his Infusion skill rises to level three. The ball, normally red, comes out shining with a multicoloured opalescence: a Hobgoblin Disco Ball, heavy multi-hued smoke that hides all movement inside and bounces to the beat, and blinds its caster as well as the monsters. Infusing smoke curtains makes them inherently unstable, which is why he is not yet trying it with real explosives.
beats.gist: Carl soaks a Hobgoblin smoke curtain in an invisibility potion, and his Infusion skill reaches level three.

beats.headline: Predator
beats.text: Carl has been collecting invisibility potions, and he makes sure Donut always has a few, because of Predator, one of their newer moves: on his call they both go invisible, Donut switches her sunglasses to infrared, and she rides his shoulder calling out by chat anything she sees. Sorry about this, Bomo, Carl says, and smashes an invisibility potion against the side of the rock monster's head. Bomo disappears. Carl drinks his own just as the timer hits zero, Donut does the same, and they are in Zockau.
beats.gist: Carl smashes an invisibility potion on Bomo's head, drinks his own, and Donut does too, vanishing into Zockau.

recap.text: Carl unzips a suitcase and pulls out red lingerie, high-heeled shoes and brochures about things to do in Delaware, until Donut points at a bulge in a pocket. Inside are two mana potions and an Invisibility Potion, and the system now lets him put the whole suitcase into his inventory. When the mimic's tongue lashes at him, he rolls, slams the potion from his hotlist and vanishes for thirty seconds, his intelligence doubled, as the tongue smacks the empty spot.

At the infusing trays, Carl soaks a Hobgoblin smoke curtain in an invisibility potion, and his Infusion skill rises to level three. The ball, normally red, comes out shining with multicoloured opalescence: a Hobgoblin Disco Ball, heavy multi-hued smoke that hides all movement inside, bounces to the beat, and blinds its caster along with the monsters. Infusing makes smoke curtains inherently unstable, so he holds off on trying it with real explosives.

Carl stocks invisibility potions and keeps a few in Donut's hands for Predator, one of their newer moves. On his call they both go invisible, Donut switches her sunglasses to infrared, and she rides his shoulder, calling out anything she sees by chat. Carl says sorry to Bomo and smashes a potion against the rock monster's head, and Bomo disappears. Carl and Donut drink theirs as the timer hits zero, and they are in Zockau.

entities.name: 1965 Harley Davidson FLH Panhead Electra Glide

tagline.text: Prize four on Chaco's carousel is a red and beige 1965 Harley Davidson with a small dent in the gas tank, and Carl knows that dent: he made it as a boy, knocking his father's motorcycle over. He does not pick it.

The Harley stands in the yard of Carl's father's trailer, which the dungeon has spliced into the floor from an earlier time, maybe a summer. Carl takes it into his inventory, and it files itself with his vehicles, not the temporary loot, so he thinks it is his to keep.
Carl's father's Harley starts at the first try, its gas tank full, and Carl rides off on it.
Carl rides his father's Harley across the arena at Scolopendra with Donut on his shoulder, and lays it down to make the throw.

beats.headline: Prize four
beats.text: On Chaco's prize carousel, after two skill potions, five hundred bombs and two thousand books, comes prize four: a 1965 Harley Davidson FLH Panhead Electra Glide, red and beige. Carl's heart stops at the small dent on the gas tank. He slipped once coming up the driveway and knocked his father's motorcycle over, and that was the one day his father was physically abusive: a belt, hard enough to draw blood. Is it really his? Donut thinks Carl on the bike and her on Mongo would be unstoppable. Carl has an urge to pick it only to push it onto the tracks in front of a train.
beats.gist: Carl sees his father's red and beige Harley as prize four and wants to wreck it.

beats.headline: Donut knows the bike
beats.text: Donut has worked out who the keyholder will be before Carl has, and the second clue is the motorcycle: the same one he was offered on the prize carousel on the fourth floor, with the big dent in it. She remembers how it affected him, though he said nothing at the time. Now it is sitting outside a trailer, and she just knows his father will be inside. She is trying to be more like Carl, she says, and not give them the satisfaction.
beats.gist: Donut guesses Carl's father is the keyholder because his motorcycle, dented, sits outside the trailer.

beats.headline: Into Carl's inventory
beats.text: In the trailer's yard the Harley is dirty and dusty, its leather seat cracked, weeds growing round its tyres, its Georgia plates expired years ago. Carl knows nothing about it except that it is a collector's item, that his father never shut up about it, and that it was his prized possession. He picks it up easily, remembering how heavy it was the day he knocked it over. It goes into his inventory, not into the temporary category like everything else from this floor, but in with the royal chariot and the bicycles: Shitty Transportation Items.
beats.gist: Carl picks up his father's dusty, expired-plated Harley easily, and it goes into his inventory as Shitty Transportation.

beats.headline: A full tank
beats.text: In his father's dresser Carl found the keys to the motorcycle and the Ford truck. Going out, he starts to pull the royal chariot from his inventory, then has a thought, pulls his father's motorcycle instead, sticks the keys in and tries to start it. To his utter astonishment it roars to life at once. The gas tank is full. He gets on, and off he goes.
beats.gist: Carl finds his father's keys, pulls the Harley instead of the chariot, and it starts at once.

beats.headline: A metallic penis extension
beats.text: In the small town of Guanajay, past midnight, Carl pulls out the Harley, and Donut, in Mongo's saddle, looks it up and down with distaste and asks whether he means to grow a mullet as well. The goblin copper chopper was custom-made for them, she says, with a sidecar and a tailor-made seat; this is a metallic penis extension that comes with a free probation officer and a traumatic brain injury. Carl reminds her she tried to get him to pick this exact motorcycle on the carousel. She denies it: she wanted the chaps. Samantha thinks it is sexy.
beats.gist: Carl pulls out his father's Harley in Guanajay, and Donut mocks it as a metallic penis extension.

beats.headline: Laid down at Scolopendra
beats.text: With sixty seconds of invulnerability left, Carl rides his motorcycle across the arena at Scolopendra, Donut on his shoulder and refusing to get off. Eris swaps every inventory, so Donut has his, and he has her combine the ball in slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve. She drops the ball into his scoop. Carl yanks the bike down hard, launching them both into the air, and flings the ball into the boss's mouth. Scolopendra splatters into a puddle, and the motorcycle spins off the other way as they tumble to a stop.
beats.gist: Carl rides his father's motorcycle at Scolopendra and flings a ball into its mouth.

recap.text: Carl's father's red and beige 1965 Harley Davidson FLH Panhead Electra Glide comes up as prize four on Chaco's carousel, after two skill potions, five hundred bombs and two thousand books. Carl's heart stops at the small dent on the gas tank, left the day his father took a belt to him. Donut pictures Carl on the bike and her on Mongo, but Carl wants to pick it only to push it onto the tracks.

Donut recognizes the dented Harley from the prize carousel and knows Carl's father is inside the trailer beside it. Carl lifts the dusty, weed-ringed bike into his inventory with the royal chariot and the bicycles. He finds the keys in his father's dresser, and the bike starts at once on a full tank. In Guanajay past midnight, Donut calls it a metallic penis extension with a free probation officer, and Samantha thinks it is sexy.

With sixty seconds of invulnerability left, Carl rides his father's motorcycle across the arena at Scolopendra, Donut on his shoulder and refusing to get off. Eris swaps every inventory, so Donut has Carl's, and she combines the ball in slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve, then drops the ball into his scoop. Carl yanks the bike down hard, launching them into the air, and flings the ball into the boss's mouth. Scolopendra splatters into a puddle.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle comes from Donut's fans: a garish blue-and-red seat with a pommel and a great many tassels, no straps and no reins, that clicks onto Mongo's back by itself. It boosts the rider's spells and the dinosaur's constitution, and his melee damage while someone is in it.
Mongo's saddle has an upgrade called Legendary Steed, which lets Donut hitch a cart to him without adding weight, and he can still jump.

description.text: Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle. Adjusted to fit Cat species. Magically affixes itself to the dreaded Mongoliensis, turning everyone's favorite murder chicken into a mount. Riders in the saddle are afforded the following bonuses: +15% to all offensive spell damage. Anti-Piercing Resistance. In addition, the saddle gives the following bonus to the attached Mongoliensis: +20% Constitution. +20% melee damage while saddle is occupied.

beats.headline: Our fans got us a saddle
beats.text: Donut's platinum fan box, where viewers pay a credit to vote, opens on a saddle, and she thanks everybody. It is blue and red, tassel-covered and obscenely garish, like something on a horse in a Fourth of July parade. Mordecai calls it a really good prize, but he has never seen anybody ride one. Carl likes the constitution and not the idea of Donut up there while Mongo fights; Mordecai tells her to practise jumping out of the saddle when he attacks. It is just a seat, a pommel and tassels. After a curly fry and a word from Donut, Mongo lets Carl set it on his back, and it clicks into place, the same sound a table makes in the crafting room.
beats.gist: Donut's fan box opens on a garish saddle, and Mongo, given a curly fry, lets Carl fit it.

beats.headline: A psychic bond
beats.text: In the crafting room, after ten minutes of coaxing, Donut leaps onto the saddle and a translucent strap wraps around her waist. Mongo bucks like a bronco. The strap's hold has a limit, and she is thrown several times. When he calms down he stands there miserable. How will she control him with no reins, Carl asks. She and Mongo have a psychic bond, she says, and Mongo tosses her halfway across the room onto Mordecai's alchemy table, then rolls onto his back trying to dislodge the saddle. On the ochre line platform her two Clockwork Mongos have little saddles on them too.
beats.gist: Donut, thrown repeatedly by the bucking Mongo, insists their psychic bond will control him without reins.

beats.headline: Legendary Steed
beats.text: Carl is sewing the four-leaf-clover patch onto his jacket when Donut calls him over: she has an upgrade for Mongo's saddle, and it is called Legendary Steed. It lets her add a cart to him, it adds no weight, and he can still jump. Mongo is in the garage helping Prepotente supervise the emergency gremlins. Can they use the missile cart, she asks. That one is already spoken for, Carl says, but if it survives, it is a good idea. Then Donut sees that his patch is not straight.
beats.gist: Donut's Legendary Steed upgrade lets her add a weightless cart to Mongo's saddle.

recap.text: Donut's platinum fan box opens on a blue and red saddle, tassel-covered and garish as something on a horse in a Fourth of July parade. After a curly fry and a word from Donut, Mongo lets Carl set it on his back, and it clicks into place. In the crafting room, Donut leaps on and a translucent strap wraps her waist, but Mongo bucks her off several times and finally tosses her onto Mordecai's alchemy table.

Carl is sewing the four-leaf-clover patch onto his jacket when Donut shows him Legendary Steed, a saddle upgrade that lets her add a cart to Mongo, adds no weight, and leaves him able to jump. Mongo is in the garage helping Prepotente supervise the emergency gremlins. Donut asks about the missile cart, and Carl says it is spoken for, but if it survives, it is a good idea. Then Donut sees that his patch is not straight.

tagline.text: A Fragmenting Potion Ball is a hard rubber ball that holds one full potion vial, made at Mordecai's alchemy table to be thrown. A potion works on a mob that is hit with one, and as far as Mordecai can tell, mobs do not get potion sickness.

description.text: Fragmenting Potion Ball. A full potion vial may be transferred to this ball.

beats.headline: A hard rubber ball
beats.text: The last of Mordecai's new items feels like a hardened rubber ball, and when Carl squeezes it, a split appears. The description is one line. Mordecai had to upgrade his table to three to make them; at five he can make them twice as fast, at six a hundred at a time. Pour in a potion and throw the ball. Nobody has to drink it: potions work on mobs if you throw them, and as far as Mordecai can tell, mobs do not get potion sickness. They break if thrown too hard, so never toss an armed one around unless it is at a bad guy. On another crawler he doubts it would work, and Donut refuses to be lobbed at; on Mongo it probably would.
beats.gist: Carl squeezes a rubber ball that splits open; Mordecai says you pour in a potion and throw it.

beats.headline: Special Brew, for a puppy
beats.text: Standing on the wing of a diving plane, with Donut screaming at the stick, Carl loads a potion ball filled with Mordecai's Special Brew into his xistera. It should heal Orthrus at once and make him near-invulnerable for thirty seconds, and Mordecai has confirmed it will work on the dog; Carl just has to hit him before Quan gets close enough for his electrical attack. He puts all his strength into the throw. The ball hits the puppy at the same moment Quan attacks. The dog glows and his health rockets to the top. It does not wake him up.
beats.gist: Carl hits Orthrus with Mordecai's Special Brew as Quan attacks; his health maxes out, but he stays asleep.

beats.headline: Invisible Mongo
beats.text: In the hydra fight Carl drops an invisibility potion, a potion ball holding another invisibility potion for Mongo, and a handful of Good Healing potions on the ground, and tells Donut to drink when she can and watch where she steps. Further into the fight she picks up the dropped potion with her mouth, tosses her head back and drinks it, then slaps the potion ball at Mongo. It breaks against his leg, and he disappears.
beats.gist: Carl leaves potions on the ground; Donut drinks one, then slaps a potion ball at Mongo, who vanishes.

beats.headline: Biscuit Packs
beats.text: Two waves of colourful skulls, each about twenty feet tall, come at the truck from both sides of the road, and one of the two ghouls riding outside the truck starts hurling his potion balls at them. These hold Biscuit Packs, something like the Denial of Service missiles but much thicker. Each ball bursts into a round foam blob about three metres across that hardens in seconds to the consistency of rock. They pop one after another, popcorn-like, snagging dozens of skulls at a time and building a barrier as they go.
beats.gist: Two skull waves close on the truck, and a ghoul hurls potion balls that burst into rock-hard foam.

relations.note: Potion balls dipped in an Emberus shrine's water

recap.text: Mordecai's last new item is a hardened rubber ball that splits open when Carl squeezes it. Pour in a potion and throw it, and the potion works on mobs, which as far as Mordecai can tell do not get potion sickness. The ball breaks if thrown too hard. Donut refuses to be lobbed at.

Carl stands on the wing of a diving plane, with Donut screaming at the stick, and loads a potion ball of Mordecai's Special Brew into his xistera. It should heal Orthrus at once and make him near-invulnerable for thirty seconds, if it lands before Quan's electrical attack. Carl throws with all his strength, and the ball hits as Quan attacks. The puppy glows and his health rockets to the top, but he does not wake.

In the hydra fight, Carl drops an invisibility potion, a potion ball holding a second invisibility potion for Mongo, and a handful of Good Healing potions on the ground, and tells Donut to drink when she can and watch where she steps. Donut picks up the dropped potion with her mouth, tosses her head back and drinks it. She then slaps the potion ball at Mongo, where it breaks against his leg and he disappears.

Two waves of colourful skulls, each about twenty feet tall, come at the truck from both sides of the road. One of the two ghouls riding outside it hurls potion balls holding Biscuit Packs, something like the Denial of Service missiles but much thicker. Each ball bursts into a foam blob about three metres across that hardens to rock in seconds. They pop one after another like popcorn, snagging dozens of skulls at a time and building a barrier.

tagline.text: Mordecai's Special Brew is his own potion: thirty seconds of nonstop healing and rapid regeneration that keeps a crawler's health topped up, though nothing in it saves anyone from an instant death. The price is about ten more hours of potion sickness, and no one can take more than two before they stop working.
Carl has drunk one under Grull's axe, and spent thirty seconds being broken and healed over and over.
The brew works thrown, too. Loaded into a potion ball and fired from Carl's xistera, it heals a giant puppy in one hit.
Thirty seconds of the brew is the window Edgar's surgery on Louis is built around.

description.text: Mordecai's Special Brew. A potion designed by a shifty Changeling who has a tendency to kill those who count on him the most, this special potion combines the effects of a Gold Standard Healing Potion and the Troll's Second Wind to create a de facto immortality for a period of thirty seconds. It has a few unfortunate side effects.

beats.headline: Thirty seconds, and a price
beats.text: Among Mordecai's gifts is a pair of potions of his own. He only had materials for two, he says, and needs at least four more. Carl ignores the first part of the description; he knows how the System labels things a crawler has made. What it does, Mordecai explains, is a constant stream of healing mixed with rapid regeneration for thirty seconds, healing almost anything and keeping health topped up. It is not invulnerability: it will not help against blowing yourself up or being decapitated. The side effects are severe. It adds about ten hours to the potion sickness countdown, and only two work before they stop altogether. He has been trying to fix that for ages.
beats.gist: Mordecai's potion heals almost anything for thirty seconds, but adds ten hours of sickness and works only twice.

beats.headline: On the hotlist
beats.text: Before agreeing to help Hekla's team, Carl rummages through his inventory and rearranges his hotlist. Into one slot goes the invisibility potion from the suitcase. Then Mordecai's Special Brew, for almost-invulnerability for about thirty seconds. He has to be careful with that one, because afterwards he cannot take another potion for ten hours. Okay, he says out loud. We'll help. Just don't get me killed so you can have Donut all to yourself.
beats.gist: Carl rearranges his hotlist, slotting in the invisibility potion and Mordecai's Special Brew, then agrees to help.

beats.headline: Broken and healed
beats.text: Grull lifts his axe. It will not hit Carl, but it will hit close enough to kill him, and Protective Shell will not help this time. He slams the potion. Gold-Standard! A thirty-second timer appears. The ground buckles and launches him into the wall of a train, the shockwave slams him again, and his back shatters over and over while he is healed again and again. Grull, blind in the smoke, steps on him with a flaming horseshoe and shatters his pelvis. A rolling train car flattens him. Each time, he heals.
beats.gist: Carl slams Mordecai's potion as Grull's axe falls, and its thirty-second timer heals him through every shattering blow.

beats.headline: Four hours to go
beats.text: Out in a driving sandstorm on the way to town, Carl catches a countdown timer in the upper left of his vision. It is his potion sickness indicator, left over from Mordecai's Special Brew. He still has over four hours before he can take another potion. At least the timer kept ticking while they were on Odette's show.
beats.gist: Carl catches his potion sickness timer from Mordecai's Special Brew in the sandstorm: over four hours remain.

beats.headline: If your health gets low
beats.text: The ceiling is about to give way over them. Take a water scroll, Carl tells Donut, and do it now; put the rest in your hotlist, fast. If your health gets low, don't take a health potion. Take Mordecai's Special Brew. Donut has changed her mind, she says; she would rather be buried alive than... Carl pulls her from his shoulder and wraps himself around her, muffling the rest, as the ceiling splinters and the sand pours in.
beats.gist: Donut is told to take a water scroll as the ceiling gives way, and Carl shields her.

beats.headline: Fired at a puppy
beats.text: In the plane, chasing Quan toward Orthrus, Carl sends Mordecai a frantic question and gets back one word: yes. He has Donut hand him the special brew and pulls it straight into his inventory, where he drags it onto the other item Mordecai gave him the same day he made the potion. They combine into a new item, a potion ball. As they dive at the dog, he loads it into the xistera and puts all his strength into the throw. The ball hits the puppy at the same moment Quan attacks. The dog glows, and his health rockets to the top. It does not wake him up.
beats.gist: Carl throws a potion ball made from Mordecai's special brew; it heals the puppy but doesn't wake him.

beats.headline: Into Louis's chest
beats.text: Edgar's plan for Louis runs on thirty seconds: Mordecai cuts him open, and once the naiad's organs are ready they administer the special brew, swap out the heart and lungs, Juice Box activates the new ones, and then the graft. Donut stands on a high chair over Louis's open chest, ready to drop the potion. Louis's heart stops before they are ready, and Bucket Boy yanks the old organs out and throws them over his shoulder. Potion! Edgar cries, and Donut pours Mordecai's Special Brew into the open, gushing chest as Imani places the new organs and Juice Box casts.
beats.gist: Donut pours Mordecai's Special Brew into Louis's gushing chest as Imani places the new organs.

recap.text: Mordecai gives Carl a pair of potions he made himself and explains that each brings thirty seconds of constant healing. It won't help against blowing yourself up or decapitation. Each adds about ten hours to the potion sickness countdown, and only two work before they stop. Carl slams one as Grull's axe comes down, and his shattered back, his pelvis under a flaming horseshoe, and the flattening by a rolling train car all heal.

Mordecai's Special Brew leaves a potion sickness timer in the upper left of Carl's vision, with over four hours left. Carl tells Donut to drink the brew if her health gets low, as the ceiling splinters. In the plane, he drags it onto Mordecai's other item, making a potion ball, and throws it from the xistera. It hits the puppy, whose health rockets up, but he stays asleep.

Edgar's plan for Louis runs on thirty seconds, but Louis's heart stops before anyone is ready. Bucket Boy yanks the old organs out and throws them over his shoulder. Edgar cries for the potion, and Donut, standing on a high chair over the open chest, pours Mordecai's Special Brew into the gushing chest as Imani places the new organs and Juice Box casts.

tagline.text: The Superb Constitution Buff Potion is a stat potion of Mordecai's making, orange and bubbly, that permanently adds one to four points of Constitution. No one may drink more than two, whatever their quality, so Mordecai says to drink nothing like it they find unless it is labelled Superb.

description.text: Superb Constitution Buff Potion. Drinking this mixture will permanently increase your Constitution by a random number between one and four. You may only drink two of these during your time in the dungeon. Why? Because drinking more would be cheating. And if anyone is going to cheat, it's going to be me.

beats.headline: Two for Donut
beats.text: Mordecai's second pair of potions are both for Donut. Stat potions, he says: you can only take two, so take them both now. When he has the ingredients he will make two of these for everybody, with all of the stats, and anything like them they find before then should go undrunk unless it is labelled Superb, the only kind he can make that might add four. The two-potion limit does not care about quality. There is another kind, the Cosmic Buff, which raises a random stat by ten, but he does not know the recipe and has only seen a handful.
beats.gist: Mordecai tells Donut to drink both stat potions now, since two is the limit.

beats.headline: Well, that was a waste
beats.text: Donut drinks the first. It only went up one point, she complains, and asks Mordecai if he is sure he made them right. They wait for her potion countdown to wear off while he rolls his eyes at the cat. The second raises it by three, a net gain of four, for a base Constitution of eight. With her anklet, the buff from her brush and the temporary ten from her Hooligan class on this floor, she has a Constitution of 21. Four points is good, says Mordecai, but it is still much too low.
beats.gist: Donut drinks two stat potions, ending with Constitution 21 after Mordecai calls her four-point gain still too low.

recap.text: Mordecai hands Donut his second pair of stat potions, since only two can be taken. The first raises her Constitution by one, and she asks whether he made it right while he rolls his eyes through her countdown. The second adds three, four in all, for a base of eight and 21 with her anklet, her brush's buff and the temporary ten from her Hooligan class. Four is good, Mordecai says, but much too low.

tagline.text: A Jelly Bomb is Carl's landmine for taking a train off its rails: a tire-shaped, oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers and a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, set off when a train presses one of its spikes. The System named it, presumably after a jelly donut, and gave him no credit for inventing it.
Two Jelly Bombs on the ochre line are enough. The train comes off the track, and Carl gets an achievement for manufacturing a derailment.

beats.headline: Landmines, a classic
beats.text: For the first derailment Carl keeps it simple. He wanted a metal ramp to lift the first car off the rails, but he has no measurements, so he goes with a classic: landmines, tire-shaped cross sections of the spiked contact mines of early twentieth-century naval warfare. Each is an oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers and one hopefully-stable stick of hobgoblin dynamite, its top half scored into triangles for shrapnel. A spike pressed by the train smashes an impact-detonated hob-lobber. The plunger idea came from the cookbook, changed just enough, and he built the plungers from the Gorgon Marital Aid. The System labels it a Jelly Bomb, presumably after a jelly donut. He gets no credit for inventing it.
beats.gist: Carl builds landmines from hob-lobbers, hobgoblin dynamite, and Gorgon Marital Aid plungers; the System calls them Jelly Bombs.

beats.headline: Lowered on a fishing pole
beats.text: According to the Demolitions Workshop menu the device is stable against anything except heavy impact, and Carl watches its status number nervously anyway. It does not lower. With a fishing pole he has cobbled together, he lowers the first one onto the track, as far from the third rail as he can, and places a second half a car's length into the tunnel. Neither has been tested. He is reasonably certain two will be enough to knock the train off the track, and hopes he does not kill the engineer. Or himself.
beats.gist: Carl lowers one Jelly Bomb onto the track with a fishing pole, places a second, and hopes.

beats.headline: Locomotive Breath
beats.text: Even from the top of the stairs the detonation is deafening. Below the platform comes a horrific screeching and crashing, smoke and dust billowing up, and then a second explosion, like a shotgun blast through the tumult. Carl reaches level 29, and the System hands him an achievement, Locomotive Breath, for finally managing to manufacture a train derailment, with the hope that it does not set off some unforeseen domino effect across the rest of the floor. The reward is a Gold Engineering Box. That was ominous, Carl thinks. Out of the tipped engine climbs the ochre line's engineer, Gore-Gore.
beats.gist: Carl reaches level 29 after his Jelly Bomb derails a train, earning Locomotive Breath.

beats.headline: The prototype trigger
beats.text: Carl wants to sandwich a horde of ghouls and monsters between two trains, partly to see whether he gets experience for it. Apart from the landmines that derailed that first train, he has hardly had a chance to use explosives on this floor. The trigger he ties to his bundle of hobgoblin dynamite is a piece of his first landmine prototype: a long pole with an impact-detonated hob-lobber at the end, too high to hit the ordinary blister ghouls, low enough for a stage-three monster. If it misses, the bomb goes off when the train crashes into the other one.
beats.gist: Carl rigs hobgoblin dynamite to a pole trigger, hoping to crush a horde between two trains.

relations.note: impact-detonated ones, smashed by the spikes
the plunger
his ochre line train
the plungers are built from it

recap.text: Carl has no measurements for the ramp he wanted, so he builds landmines: metal tubes of hob-lobbers and one stick of hobgoblin dynamite, with plungers made from the Gorgon Marital Aid. The System labels it a Jelly Bomb. He lowers one onto the track with a fishing pole and places a second half a car's length into the tunnel. The train derails, and Carl reaches level 29, with the achievement Locomotive Breath and a Gold Engineering Box.

tagline.text: Katia's Makeup Table is a crafting table Mordecai told her about. At level three, paid for with her table upgrade coupons, it lays the face of anyone she has met onto its glass to sculpt from, sitting at it does not hurt, and it stores three designs to call up on demand.
Katia can shape nearly anything on the fly now, but faces still come out best at her Makeup Table.

beats.headline: Sixty-five percent Hekla
beats.text: Katia has shaped herself into Hekla well enough to fool Carl until he reads the name over her head. Her ability, Walk in Their Shoes, only switches on at a ninety percent match, she explains, and this Hekla is sixty-five. She is working on it. She bought a new table Mordecai told her about, a Makeup Table. At level three it superimposes the face of any monster, crawler or NPC she has met on the glass, which makes sculpting much easier, it does not hurt to sit at, and it saves three designs. At level five it supposedly comes with a full-sized mirror. Level three? Carl asks, trying not to sound horrified: did she use her upgrade coupons? Yes, she did.
beats.gist: Katia, shaped as a sixty-five percent Hekla, shows Carl her new Makeup Table.

beats.headline: Already spent
beats.text: Mordecai is back. All they need now, he says, is to wait out the timer and hop down the stairs. Oh, and give him their table upgrade coupons, so he can boost up his alchemy table before they go down a floor. Carl and Katia exchange a look. They have both already spent theirs, and Katia's went into the Makeup Table. Okay, Carl says, they will give him a quick recap. But he has to promise not to smack them again.
beats.gist: Carl and Katia already spent their coupons, hers on the Makeup Table, so Mordecai gets a recap.

beats.headline: Faces still need the table
beats.text: Katia hangs off the corner of the floating house, one arm anchored to the magical brace that holds the balloon, and forms herself into a diving bell, a shape she has never made before, on the fly. Carl remembers when even a small change physically hurt her. Now she can contour herself into just about anything at a moment's notice. She still is not perfect with faces unless she sits in front of her makeup table, but with inanimate things like this, she is an expert.
beats.gist: Katia hangs from the floating house and forms a diving bell, though faces still need her makeup table.

relations.note: the crafting room

recap.text: Carl and Katia tell Mordecai they have already spent their table upgrade coupons, and Katia's went into a Makeup Table. At level three it puts any face she has met on the glass and saves three designs. Her Hekla is only sixty-five percent, short of the ninety that Walk in Their Shoes needs. Carl makes Mordecai promise not to smack them again.

Katia hangs off the corner of the floating house, one arm anchored to the magical brace that holds the balloon, and forms herself into a diving bell, a shape she has never made before. Carl remembers when even a small change hurt her. Now she contours herself into nearly anything at a moment's notice, and though faces still need her makeup table, she is an expert with inanimate things like this.

tagline.text: A bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration comes off the corpse of Gore-Gore, along with an engineer's key and a neighborhood map.
Carl's hair has burned off, eyebrows and all, and he means to grow it back with the Rev-up hair tonic, though he has heard the results are a little overenthusiastic.
The tonic adds length for as long as it stays on, and Carl's head went wrong at the last step: his hair now reaches his waist, grows back when cut, and will keep doing so for about two weeks.
Carl had meant to cut his hair once the tonic wore off, but a hairbrush too good to give up means it stays long.

beats.headline: Off Gore-Gore
beats.text: Down in the channel, one of the two Mongo automatons explodes on the third rail, and the other hauls the Gore-Gore corpse up against the wall. Carl loots him: 498 gold and three items. An Ochre Line Engineer's Key, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, and the neighborhood map, which fills his interface with the whole Ochre line, every stop and the position of every train.
beats.gist: Down on the tracks, Carl loots the Gore-Gore corpse and takes a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration.

beats.headline: No eyebrows
beats.text: Louis puts Carl down, and Carl puts a hand to his head. His skin has healed, but his hair is gone, burned off, and his eyebrows too. Donut says he looks like he is going as one of those crest guys for Halloween, and she will not have a sidekick with no eyebrows. It's okay, Carl says: he has a potion that grows it back, Rev-up hair tonic. The mantaurs dropped them on the fourth floor, but from what he hears the results are a little overenthusiastic.
beats.gist: Carl's burned-off hair and eyebrows can be regrown by Rev-up hair tonic, though the results run overenthusiastic.

beats.headline: Waiting for Katia
beats.text: Carl stares at the bottle. The set comes with little plastic gloves, cotton swabs and a fold-out instruction pamphlet that is really, really long. Donut fusses that the number one crawler simply cannot be without eyebrows. His view counter has spiked, which tells him this has to be some sort of trap. Mordecai insists it works if he follows the instructions to a T, but they are convoluted, full of warnings against letting it touch anywhere you do not want hair, so after a fifth reading Carl waits for Katia.
beats.gist: Carl stares at the hair tonic, reads its long warnings five times, and waits for Katia.

beats.headline: Uh-oh
beats.text: Katia reads the instructions and mixes in little plastic trays, an extra set of hands holding Carl's head still: eyebrows first, then the eyelashes, a mix almost identical to the pubic hair recipe. For the head she mixes in the large tray and sends Louis for Splash Zone; a splotch lands on the table, and its rock-like surface sprouts hair. Then she splotches the cold tonic on and counts down from five. Uh-oh, says Splash Zone: his water spell counts as offensive and will not cast in the saferoom. Carl runs to the shower, because the tonic adds length for as long as it stays on, and comes out with hair to his waist that grows back when cut. About two weeks, Mordecai says.
beats.gist: Katia mixes the tonic, Splash Zone's water spell fails, and Carl runs to the shower with waist-length hair.

beats.headline: Now it stays long
beats.text: Carl's Celestial item from the fight at Club Vanquisher is a hairbrush whose benefits include twenty-five percent to Constitution, and hair that will be shiny and healthy and goddamn glisten. That boost alone makes the brush frustratingly invaluable; like his boxers, it is now too good to give up. Carl had been planning on cutting his hair after the tonic's regrowth effect finally ebbed. Now he will have to keep it long.
beats.gist: Carl keeps his hair long because the brush's twenty-five percent Constitution boost is too good to give up.

recap.text: Down in the channel, one of the two Mongo automatons explodes on the third rail, and the other hauls the Gore-Gore corpse up against the wall. Carl loots the body and takes 498 gold, an Ochre Line Engineer's Key, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, and the neighborhood map. The map fills his interface with the whole Ochre line, every stop and the position of every train.

Louis sets Carl down, and Carl finds his hair burned off, eyebrows included, though his skin has healed. Donut says he looks like a crest guy going as one for Halloween and refuses a sidekick with no eyebrows. Carl answers that he has a potion to grow it back, Rev-up hair tonic, which the mantaurs dropped on the fourth floor, though he hears the results run a little overenthusiastic.

Carl stares at the Rev-up Magic Hair Restoration Tonic and its really, really long pamphlet, and after a fifth reading he waits for Katia. She mixes the eyebrows, eyelashes and head, and Splash Zone's water spell will not cast in the saferoom, so Carl runs to the shower and comes out with hair to his waist. The Celestial hairbrush from Club Vanquisher gives twenty-five percent to Constitution, so he must keep it long.

tagline.text: The Armorer's Table is the crafting table Carl buys with a free table coupon at station 281. Metal shaped at the engineering table is only metal, but picked through the Armorer's Workshop tab it becomes armour the system lets someone equip, Katia included.

beats.headline: A coupon, and a shitty helmet
beats.text: At the saferoom in a glass-fronted donut shop at station 281, Carl asks the bopca, Nodd, for the crafting table menu: a long list, most of it useless, most of it about 25,000 gold a table. He slides one of his two free table coupons forward, and spends both upgrade coupons on taking his sapper's table to level three. His book has confirmed what he suspected: armour shaped at an engineering table never counts as equipped, and if Katia cannot equip it, she cannot add it to her mass. At the new armorer's table he picks his sample's intention from the Armorer's Workshop tab. The only choice is Shitty Helmet. It looks no different, but it resizes itself slightly, and Katia can equip it.
beats.gist: Carl upgrades his sapper's table with coupons, learns engineering-table armour can't be equipped, and picks Shitty Helmet.

beats.headline: An ugly backpack
beats.text: A note from Rosetta in the cookbook's bomb chapter says an equipped backpack keeps unstable satchels from going off, and two more notes under it argue the point. So Carl builds Katia one, a large metal box with reinforced dingo-hide straps, and sets it on a stand he made for it. He tells her he saw backpack listed in the armorer workshop tab, which is true; he searched until he found a way to make it look like a chance find. The system names it Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear. Carl does not care, as long as the word Backpack is in there.
beats.gist: Carl builds Katia a metal backpack with dingo-hide straps and shrugs off its insulting name.

beats.headline: The Scrapheap Breastplate
beats.text: In the temple, Bomo stands covered in spiked armour, and apart from the shoulder pads holding up the launchers almost none of it is joined. Carl sewed the metal pieces one by one onto a fabric undershirt, with dozens of trash-tier daggers in the gaps, and putting it together at his armorer's table turned the whole thing into something called a Scrapheap Breastplate. He did the same for the arms and the legs. Donut casts Laundry Day on Bomo, and the pieces explode off him like a fragmenting grenade, filling the room with metal. Paz is bowled over by a chunk of helmet. A dagger lodges in Carl's arm; he had not realised the armour would fly off like that.
beats.gist: Carl sews armour and daggers onto an undershirt, and Donut's Laundry Day blasts it off Bomo.

relations.note: Armour made here is armour she can equip

recap.text: Carl asks the bopca Nodd for the crafting table menu at a glass-fronted donut shop's saferoom, then spends both upgrade coupons to raise his sapper's table to level three. The armorer's table offers only Shitty Helmet, which resizes itself so Katia can equip it. Carl builds her a large metal backpack with reinforced dingo-hide straps, and the system names it Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear.

Bomo stands in the temple in spiked armour, and apart from the shoulder pads holding up the launchers, almost none of it is joined. Carl sewed the metal pieces onto a fabric undershirt, with dozens of trash-tier daggers in the gaps, and his armorer's table made it a Scrapheap Breastplate. Donut casts Laundry Day on Bomo, and the armour explodes off him like a fragmenting grenade. A chunk of helmet bowls Paz over, and a dagger lodges in Carl's arm.

entities.name: Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear

tagline.text: Carl built Katia a way to carry her own mass: an open-topped metal basket on dingo-hide straps, which the System calls an Ugly Ass Backpack. Loaded with metal poles and equipped, it vanishes into her, and she grows by what is inside it.
Katia has widened the backpack herself on Carl's engineering table, packed more metal into it, and added rubber to layer between the metal and her flesh.

Katia has a better one now, out of a boss box: the same idea, but adjustable, so she can carry even more, and it will not break. It gives her a stability enhancement while she wears it, and retractable stilts make loading much easier.

beats.headline: Backpacks were a thing
beats.text: Notes in the cookbook's margins argue about backpacks. Rosetta found that unstable satchels hold their stability in an equipped backpack, Allister confirmed it, and Forkith, mourning a little sister, says they only slow it now: he found that out the hard way. What Carl takes away is that backpacks are a thing, and he has an idea. He shows Katia the result on a stand he built for it and says he saw backpack listed on the armorer workshop tab, which is true. The System labels it Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear. Carl does not care, as long as the word Backpack is in there.
beats.gist: Carl builds a stand for his backpack, and he doesn't mind the System's absurdly long name for it.

beats.headline: A shell on her back
beats.text: Carl loads it with metal poles and a pour of tiny xistera balls. He has made it open-topped with a slight lip, so that it lists what is in it as contents. Katia is sure she will only get the backpack's own mass. Following a drawing on a gym membership form, she reforms into a slug-like shape with a shelf on her back, the stand clatters away, and the backpack lands on her and disappears, turning the colour of her flesh. The dense mass forms a rounded, shell-like shape. It worked. She tumbles onto her back like an overturned turtle, then reshapes herself round more than a ton of extra metal, closer to a ton and a quarter, Carl says, and stands about eleven feet tall with a strength bonus.
beats.gist: Katia loads the backpack with poles and xistera balls, then reshapes herself around it, eleven feet tall.

beats.headline: Thirty seconds is too long
beats.text: Katia spends the next hour practising with different masses. Taking it off through her inventory is inelegant: unequip more than half her mass at once and her body resets, splotching onto the floor as a quivering blob for a couple of seconds before she is herself again. Putting it on means setting up the redesigned stand, pulling the backpack onto it, backing in, strapping up and turning slug, and then forming whatever she wants from the mass she keeps in it. It takes about thirty seconds, which is still too long. They are working on it.
beats.gist: Katia practises for an hour, but putting the backpack on still takes thirty seconds.

beats.headline: Wider, with rubber
beats.text: Hekla wants Katia stuck to the front of a train as its cowcatcher, and it was Katia's own idea, she tells Carl in chat; it is why the Daughters are here. While he was gone, she altered the backpack on his engineering table and made it wider. There is more metal in it now, so she can make herself even bigger, and she has added rubber to the mix: layered between the metal and her flesh, it absorbs the impacts. What she needs is help with the design for the front of the train. She has to be careful of the third rail.
beats.gist: Katia widens the backpack with more metal and layered rubber so she can grow bigger and absorb impacts.

beats.headline: Bulk up for the saw
beats.text: Carl's missiles have done their job, and the prize lies rumbling on the ground: a still-chugging chainsaw that has to be twenty-five feet long. He did not want to damage it. Get your backpack ready, he tells Katia: they are going to bulk her up so she can lift the thing and stick it into her inventory. She starts to say something about how he is always complaining about the way they portray him, and a mighty rumble fills the world before she can finish. An earthquake.
beats.gist: Katia's backpack is to bulk her up to lift the twenty-five-foot chainsaw, when an earthquake interrupts her.

beats.headline: The house in her inventory
beats.text: Firas, down from the balloon-hung house with water arcing out of it behind him, tells Carl what he missed. It was Louis's idea. With the house floating just off the ground, Katia did that weird thing she does when she puts the backpack on, and it worked: the whole house went into her inventory. That same night, after the recap episode, they patched it, and the whole contraption popped out of her inventory over their heads in a pub called Cuttlefish Point. It almost smooshed them all, and it pretty much blew up the tavern.
beats.gist: Katia's backpack swallows the house; a patch makes it pop out over them.

beats.headline: Out of a boss box
beats.text: Katia gasps as she opens her boss box and a backpack appears. It is pretty much the same backpack Carl designed for her mass storage, she tells him, but it is adjustable, so she can carry even more, and it will not break. It gives her a stability enhancement while she is wearing it, and it has retractable stilts that make loading a lot easier. She can add large amounts of mass much more quickly now. Carl wonders whether they made something new for her or it had already been invented. She shrugs.
beats.gist: Katia opens a boss box and finds an adjustable, unbreakable backpack with retractable stilts.

beats.headline: Voltron, sort of
beats.text: Louis tosses a potion bandolier at Katia, and it equips itself the moment it lands on her. Carl asks what, exactly, the move is. The pitch: she has that new backpack that lets her add a bunch of mass, so let her get really big without a breastplate, drop a giant one on her from the Twister so it equips, let her get bigger, then drop an even bigger helmet. Like the Voltron formation sequence. Sort of. Unless the item misses or does not hit right, Britney points out, and she is crushed. It's a work in progress, says Louis.
beats.gist: Louis's plan is to drop armor on Katia to enlarge her; Britney says a miss crushes her.

relations.note: the margin notes on backpacks and explosives
the plan to drop armour on her from it

recap.text: Carl builds a backpack for Katia, and the System labels it Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear. He loads it with metal poles and tiny xistera balls, and Katia, following a drawing on a gym membership form, reforms into a slug with a shelf on her back. The backpack lands and turns the colour of her flesh, and she stands eleven feet tall around a ton and a quarter of metal.

Katia's missiles-cracked chainsaw prize lies rumbling, twenty-five feet long, and Carl tells her to ready her backpack so they can bulk her up to lift it. An earthquake cuts her off. Firas tells Carl the house went into her inventory, then popped out over their heads in Cuttlefish Point. A boss box gives her an adjustable backpack with retractable stilts.

Louis tosses a potion bandolier at Katia, and it equips itself the moment it lands on her. Carl asks what the move is. Louis pitches it: she uses the new backpack to add mass, a giant breastplate drops on her from the Twister, then an even bigger helmet, like the Voltron formation sequence, sort of. Britney points out that if an item misses, Katia is crushed. Louis calls it a work in progress.

tagline.text: Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #544 is a blue and yellow capsule from a bronze benefactor box stamped with the Valtay Corporation's symbol, and it permanently installs one upgrade in a crawler's interface: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals. Carl has swallowed it. A doorway that is a portal now glows purple for him, and he can read it and see a still picture of the other side.
Portal sight is how Carl reads the gated portals over the abyss: who may pass, which keys count, and a picture of the trainyard waiting on the other side.
Carl's implant still reads portals, but in incompatibility mode since the changes to his body, with limited details and no picture.

description.text: Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #544. Variant 32.c This item is compatible with your Morphology and Interface. Warning: This pill will cause a permanent change to your brain. This item cannot be unequipped or undone once installed. Warning: You do not have a Valtay Corporation Neural Interface installed. While your current wetware system is compatible with this Neural Enhancer, it is recommended you visit a Valtay Corporate Outreach Center to discuss upgrade options. Payment and Legacy plans available. Keeping the Best of You alive. Current wetware: Syndicate Crawl Version 47.002.Human. Taking this pill will install the following upgrade to your interface: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals.

beats.headline: A pill from the worms
beats.text: Donut is sure Princess D'nadia has got her something good, and makes Carl open the bronze benefactor box he has just received, and send a thank-you. Sparks fly as it opens. On its top is a circle with a squiggle through it, and etched underneath, The Valtay Corporation, Keeping the Best of You Alive. Carl shivers, remembering what the Valtay really are. Inside is a single blue and yellow capsule, and for a terrifying moment he thinks it is an actual brain worm. Its description is in a slightly different voice and font than usual, and it offers one upgrade: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals.
beats.gist: Carl opens a bronze benefactor box from Donut's patron and finds a capsule offering one upgrade: portal analysis.

beats.headline: Down with cold coffee
beats.text: Why him, Carl wonders, and why the hurry, and can he trust a description in a different format? He puts it in his inventory first and notes its value, just below the Kimaris figure, and its rarity, common, then pulls it back out, reasonably certain the inventory would have refused a hidden parasite. Then he swallows it with his cold cup of coffee. A new tab appears, Third-Party Upgrades, warning that communication-based upgrades are disabled in the dungeon; the neural enhancer is its only item, and clicking it says only: This upgrade is working properly. He thanks his sponsor in the notes without knowing what it does.
beats.gist: Carl swallows the neural enhancer with cold coffee and finds a Third-Party Upgrades tab.

beats.headline: The door glows purple
beats.text: Carl is about to follow Katia to the training room when his eyes catch the doorway out to the coffee shop. It glows purple now, and a tooltip calls it a Standard Subspace Portal. Analyze? A page of numbers he cannot make sense of, and at the bottom the lines that matter: two-way, gated to user, he can pass, the environment beyond is compatible. Visual Analysis? Yes. A still photo of the coffee shop pops up, empty of customers, with Nodd the Bopca behind the counter picking his nose.
beats.gist: Carl sees the coffee shop doorway glow purple and learns it is a two-way portal he can pass.

beats.headline: A yard full of engines
beats.text: At Abyss Station a driverless train nosedives into the pit, and Carl looks up at the portal over it: an Ultima Corp DungeonWerx Industrial Subspace Portal. The analysis runs much longer than the last one. He is facing the wrong side, and entering from it will do nothing. Passage is gated by conveyance type and to key holders, with compatible keys marked in his inventory. Visual Analysis shows a massive trainyard, thousands of trains spreading out in all directions, only the engine cars, all inside a high fence.
beats.gist: Carl watches a driverless train nosedive, then reads a portal that admits only certain conveyances and key holders.

beats.headline: Half a mile over the pit
beats.text: In station 75's yard Carl reads the portals. The first of four multi-destination light-duty ones, each signed with forty-eight coloured lines, needs a selector to dial and defaults to the Orange Line; its picture is just a stretch of track. The heavy-duty clean-up portal at the front of a rapid-response cart is set to the abyss and carries an environmental warning, and the picture shows why: whatever it catches comes out in the air over the pit, a good half mile above the ground. Elevation is the highlighted problem. He switches the selector to the trainyard, and the warning goes away.
beats.gist: Carl switches the clean-up portal's selector from the abyss to the trainyard, and the warning goes away.

beats.headline: The right one
beats.text: Prepotente explains the portal dial, Carl calls out the numbers Rosetta gives him, and he analyses the door: an Ultima Corp DungeonWerx Municipal, Multi-Destination Doorway-based Subspace Portal. Dial 453! The information changes: two-way, gated by faith, its entrance sequence gated to adherents of the Khepri faith or other entities under the dungeon's ruleset. That's the right one, Carl calls. He holds his breath and asks for the picture. A screenshot appears, and relief floods him.
beats.gist: Carl analyses the door at dial 453 and calls it the right one.

beats.headline: Incompatibility mode
beats.text: Carl examines the portal with his neural implant, and it warns him first: it is working in incompatibility mode due to recent changes to his wetware system, and he should see his Valtay representative for repair. Only limited details are available. Unknown Manufacturer Enhancement Zone Subspace Portal. One-way, open access, and it leads to a stasis chamber. Visual Analysis: unavailable. Carl wags his tail; it is pretty much what he was hoping it would say. Hopefully the implant will go back to working properly when he stops being a damn dog.
beats.gist: Carl's implant, in incompatibility mode, reads the portal as one-way to a stasis chamber.

relations.note: another Valtay neural enhancer

recap.text: Carl swallows a blue and yellow capsule with his cold coffee, and Neural Enhancer #544 lets him analyze subspace portals. The coffee shop doorway glows purple and shows Nodd the Bopca picking his nose behind the counter. In station 75's yard, Carl finds a clean-up portal set to the abyss, which would drop whatever it catches half a mile above the pit. He switches a light-duty portal's selector from the Orange Line to the trainyard.

Prepotente explains the portal dial, and Carl calls out the numbers Rosetta gives him while he analyses the door. At dial 453 the information changes: a two-way Ultima Corp DungeonWerx Municipal portal, gated by faith, its entrance sequence open only to adherents of the Khepri faith or other entities under the dungeon's ruleset. Carl calls it the right one, holds his breath, and asks for the picture. A screenshot appears, and relief floods him.

Carl examines the portal with his neural implant, which warns that it is in incompatibility mode because of recent changes to his wetware and that he should see his Valtay representative. It reports only that this is an Unknown Manufacturer Enhancement Zone Subspace Portal, one-way, open access, leading to a stasis chamber. Carl wags his tail, since this is what he hoped to hear.

tagline.text: A Sheol Brick is what a Lesser Demon's young become: of the thousands born in a litter almost none live, and the rest shrivel and harden into black chunks that burn far hotter and longer than coal. The Nightmare Express runs on them, and Carl has taken a box of about fifty out of its cab.
Mordecai wants as many Sheol Bricks as Carl can get, and Fire Brandy has let him take several hundred, most of them still burning.

description.text: Sheol Brick. If Santa gives coal to the regular naughty kids, he'd probably give this stuff to history's greatest villains, like Hans Gruber and the guy who invented those shoes with the individual toes built in. It burns a lot hotter and a lot longer than regular coal. And when I say "a lot longer," I mean until the end of your lifetime. So like a week or more. To save you distress, I'm not going to tell you where this came from. That was a lie! It's a baby corpse!

beats.headline: Running on dead babies
beats.text: Fire Brandy's own description explains her trade. A Lesser Demon in labour gives birth for about sixty days, fifteen to eighteen thousand babies, one roughly every five minutes, and only one in ten thousand is viable. The rest shrivel and harden into a valuable resource called Sheol Bricks, which burn long and hot when exposed to fire. A stoker who learns water magic seals herself in a boiler, keeps a big engine humming almost by itself, and disposes of her failed young in the same stroke. The train is running on dead babies. Holy crap, thinks Carl, that's fucked up.
beats.gist: Fire Brandy explains that Lesser Demons' shriveled failed babies become Sheol Bricks, which fuel the train.

beats.headline: The box in the cab
beats.text: Fire Brandy points him to a small box at the back of the cab, covered in gore where the driver or the war mage was pushed against it. Carl lifts the lid and pulls out a black chunk. Its description promises not to tell him where it came from, to save him distress, and then admits that was a lie: it's a baby corpse. He drops it in revulsion and wipes his hand on his cloak. There are about fifty bricks in the chest. He takes a deep breath, picks up the entire box and adds it to his inventory. He shudders.
beats.gist: Carl lifts a baby's corpse from a gore-smeared box in the cab, then pockets all fifty bricks.

beats.headline: Several hundred, still burning
beats.text: Carl and Donut find Fire Brandy still aboard the idling Nightmare, still giving birth, refusing a pair of dwarven engineers who want to take the train somewhere: there is nowhere to go, she tells them, and they leave when Carl arrives. Her persona has slipped into something more melancholy. He has shown one of the rocks to Mordecai, who was nearly beside himself and told him to get as many as possible, so Carl asks if she can part with any. She lets him take several hundred still-burning pieces, along with a few dozen that have not yet caught fire. She would give him all of it, she says, but she needs to keep the fire hot and her babies happy.
beats.gist: Carl asks Fire Brandy for Sheol Bricks, and she lets him take several hundred burning ones.

relations.note: its fuel

recap.text: Fire Brandy tells Carl her trade: a Lesser Demon in labour bears fifteen to eighteen thousand babies in about sixty days, and only one in ten thousand lives. The rest shrivel into Sheol Bricks, which fuel the train. Carl lifts a black chunk from the gore-covered box in the cab, learns it is a baby corpse, drops it, and wipes his hand on his cloak. Then he picks up the whole box of about fifty.

entities.name: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles

tagline.text: The Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles are big round sunglasses, a signed gift to Donut from Princess D'Nadia, that seem to be magically fixed to her face. They see in the dark and by heat, guard her eyes, and turn her Magic Missile into a laser she can split four ways.
An empty benefactor box has upgraded Donut's sunglasses instead: they now read the surface and subsurface temperature of anything she looks at, in precise detail.
Donut's sunglasses are locked to her, as Louis found when he tried them on. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack could free them, and nobody they know has one.

description.text: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles. Special High-Fashion Edition. "The Princess Donut." This is a Unique Item. This one-of-a-kind item was a gift from Princess D'Nadia of the Prism Kingdom to Princess Donut of the Blood Sultanate. It was personally signed by Princess D'Nadia. Protects the eyes from a variety of environmental hazards, including magic-based attacks that render the user blind. Enhances all dark vision effects. Allows for heat vision and other visible-light viewing options. In addition, any energy-based spell that originates from the ocular region is caught and focused by these goggles, which allows for multiple combat and targeting options.

beats.headline: Super sunglasses
beats.text: Back on the platform, Carl notices Donut's new look at once: large round sunglasses that make her look like a bug, like the movie-star pair Bea wears on her head in Donut's photograph. The frames have no arms and her nose is too squished to hold them, yet they stay plastered to her face. They are not just couture, she says. Carl reads the description twice. They turn her Magic Missile into a laser, and she can shoot four at once; standing at the back of the Mauve Platform, she has been firing into four train doors at a time. They can even hold one shot's energy and add it to the next.
beats.gist: Donut's sunglasses turn her Magic Missile into a laser, fire four at once, and hold energy.

beats.headline: An empty box, an upgrade
beats.text: Donut's benefactor box arrived empty, and she is still a little salty about it, though a notification followed: her sunglasses have received an update that reads the surface and subsurface temperature of anything she looks at, in precise detail. Mordecai says that is a common tactic. Exceptional items cost a fortune to send, so a benefactor sends an item on one floor and an upgrade for it on the next, and the next, until it would be worth a Legendary box. The intended purpose is rooting out changelings. Carl sees dozens more, weak spots on mobs, traps, secret doors, temperature warnings. Donut has little patience for any of it.
beats.gist: Donut's empty benefactor box brings sunglasses that read temperatures; Carl also sees weak spots, traps, secret doors.

beats.headline: Locked to the princess
beats.text: Most of what the hunters leave behind is restricted to the dead hunter: Florin has two Goriffs' pulse rifles and electric body armour and cannot equip any of it. Donut's sunglasses turn out to carry the same restriction, which they learned when Louis tried to put them on. Mordecai says it is a common addition to benefactor gifts, to keep other players from murdering the recipient for the gear.
