A rare scroll called Cracker Jack could free an item, but nobody they know has one. In the meantime they collect all the gear they can.
beats.gist: Donut's sunglasses are locked to her, so only a rare Cracker Jack scroll could free them.

beats.headline: A magic river under the door
beats.text: Nobody can find the rings on the map. Florin passes on what Lucia worked out: the system counts them as magical gates, so anything that sees magic will spot them. Your sunglasses have a magical-flow setting, Carl tells Donut. They drive off the bed and squeeze under the door into the hallway, and Donut points left, her sunglasses flashing purple. It is that way, under that door, she says; it looks like a magic river flowing toward it. The map says it is a bathroom.
beats.gist: Donut's sunglasses, on magical flow, flash purple and reveal a magic river toward a bathroom.

relations.note: The one scroll that could unlock them

recap.text: Goggles on, Donut shows Carl her new look on the platform: large round sunglasses with no arms that stay plastered to her squished nose. Carl reads the description twice. They turn her Magic Missile into a laser, let her fire four at once, as she has been doing into four train doors from the back of the Mauve Platform, and let her hold one shot's energy for the next.

Donut's benefactor box arrives empty, and she is still a little salty about it. A notification then says her sunglasses now read the surface and subsurface temperature of anything she looks at. Mordecai calls this common: exceptional items cost a fortune, so a benefactor sends an item on one floor and an upgrade on the next, until the total would be worth a Legendary box. Carl sees dozens more uses, and Donut has little patience for any.

Florin holds two Goriffs' pulse rifles and electric body armour he cannot equip, because most of what the hunters leave behind is restricted to the dead hunter. Donut's sunglasses carry the same restriction, which Louis learned when he tried to put them on. Mordecai says benefactor gifts often come this way, so other players cannot murder the recipient for the gear. A rare scroll called Cracker Jack could free an item, but nobody they know has one.

Donut's sunglasses, set to their magical-flow setting at Carl's suggestion, flash purple once she and Carl squeeze under the door into the hallway. Florin has relayed Lucia's finding that the system counts the rings as magical gates, so anything that sees magic will spot them. Donut points left and says a magic river flows toward a door that way. The map calls the room behind it a bathroom.

tagline.text: Seize the Day Toothpaste is a tiny travel tube of cherry-flavored toothpaste, five applications, from a Platinum Big Daddy Box. Brushed with in a safe room, it gives thirty hours of three times damage to bosses, four times against province, country and floor bosses. Carl is keeping it for a day he knows he will meet one.
Its bonus is part of what puts Donut's effective charm over three hundred when she goes to work on Ferdinand.

description.text: Seize the Day Toothpaste – Five Applications. You know that feeling you get when you walk out into the world with minty-fresh breath? It's like you can take on any challenge that is thrown your way. It gives you confidence. It boosts your self-esteem. It makes you feel like you're on top of the damn world. Well, this stuff does none of that. However, if you brush your teeth using this enchanted, cherry-flavored toothpaste, you are imbued with the following buffs for 30 hours: +Three Times Damage to all Boss Monsters. or +Four Times Damage to all Boss Monsters if the Boss is a Province, Country, or Floor Boss. This buff may only be applied in a safe room.

beats.headline: Carpe Diem
beats.text: Killing three bosses with one attack earned Carl a Platinum Big Daddy Box, and it holds a regular, unenchanted toothbrush and a tiny, travel-sized tube of toothpaste: red, with a black skull, and Carpe Diem written on it in what appears to be Comic Sans. Five applications. Brushed in a safe room, it gives thirty hours of three times damage to all boss monsters, four times if the boss is a province, country or floor boss. A fantastic prize, Carl thinks, but only useful if he knows he is going to face a boss that day. He will need to be stingy. He adds it to his stash.
beats.gist: The Carpe Diem toothpaste triples boss damage for thirty hours, across five applications.

beats.headline: Well over three hundred
beats.text: Inside the castle, Donut has to charm Ferdinand. He is a province boss, so her charisma has to beat his constitution plus charisma by a hundred. Her base is 138, and her new benefactor-box tiara doubles it to 276 for thirty hours, before the safe room's buffs: 101 points over. Her effective charm, with all her buffs plus the bonus from the Seize the Day Toothpaste, is well over three hundred. She insists it is not working, but they have already been seeing the effects.
beats.gist: Donut's tiara and toothpaste push her charm past three hundred against Ferdinand.

relations.note: a Platinum Big Daddy Box

recap.text: Carl earns a Platinum Big Daddy Box by killing three bosses with one attack. Inside are a regular toothbrush and a tiny tube of toothpaste, red with a black skull and Carpe Diem in Comic Sans. Brushed in a safe room, each of its five applications gives thirty hours of triple damage to bosses, quadruple against a province, country or floor boss. Carl decides he must be stingy with it and adds it to his stash.

Inside the castle, Donut has to charm Ferdinand, a province boss, and her charisma must beat his constitution plus charisma by a hundred. Her base of 138 doubles to 276 for thirty hours under her benefactor-box tiara, which leaves her 101 points over before the safe room's buffs. With all her buffs and the Seize the Day Toothpaste bonus, her effective charm is well over three hundred. She insists it is not working, though they have already seen the effects.

tagline.text: Banger Spheres are Carl's xistera ammunition: baseball-sized balls of dwarven robot scrap he made by the few hundred at his engineering table. The system gives the name only to the ones made at that size.
Banger Spheres are still Carl's everyday ammunition, plain or spiked, and he has made hollow ones too, with an alarm trap sealed inside.

beats.headline: Baseball-sized, by the hundred
beats.text: The close fighting on the trains has given the xistera little use this floor. On the platform, with babababoons crawling all over the Nightmare, Carl calls one of his new Banger Spheres into the scoop and spins. It hits a babababoon in the neck with an audible splack, and the mob falls; he had been aiming between the eyes. They are nothing but spheres of dwarven robot scrap. He made a few hundred at his engineering table after trying several sizes, and the system only gave the name to the baseball-sized ones. He has ideas for others, spiked balls among them. He throws two more, and the two mobs across the platform die.
beats.gist: Carl throws Banger Spheres, baseball-sized scrap-robot balls, from his xistera and drops mobs of babababoons on the platform.

beats.headline: Bass heavy, for distraction
beats.text: Carl made five of these at his sapper's table, each labelled for a purpose, and because he made them at the table he could pick the songs. This one is a hollow banger sphere with an impact-detonated alarm trap inside, labelled Bass heavy. For distraction. Katia lobs it down the stairs at the ooze, and the announcement comes: Jump Around. Sealed in the metal ball, the music is quieter than usual and still shakes the walls. The ball protects the trap and bounces up and down with the beat, and every time the ooze grabs for it, it slips away. Donut objects to the song in capital letters.
beats.gist: Katia lobs a bass-heavy banger sphere down the stairs, and its bouncing Jump Around distracts the ooze.

beats.headline: Spiked, into a wing
beats.text: Turkeys are piling over one another to reach them, Donut is standing on the passed-out Mongo, and Carl cannot even cast Protective Shell. He pulls a banger sphere, one of his spiked ones, and launches it at the boss turkey up in the rafters. Tom squawks and tries to dodge. The ball smacks into a wing and breaks it with an audible crack. Carl pulls another, but Tom drops from the high rafter and disappears into the mass of turkeys surging toward them.
beats.gist: Carl hurls a spiked banger sphere at boss turkey Tom in the rafters and breaks his wing.

beats.headline: Through their own windshield
beats.text: The plan worked out with Chiyome and the bugbears needs the truck's windshield gone the moment the race starts, so Carl holds a special banger sphere, built to destroy the whole windshield in one hit rather than poke a hole in it. The hail starts light and grows. Hailstones shake the ground, and ice and water cover the glass until he cannot see the lights. Green light. He hurls the sphere through the windshield, which shatters, and the sphere keeps going. Suddenly they can more or less see. In the distance a hailstone the size of a two-story house smashes into the ground.
beats.gist: Carl holds a special banger sphere, hurls it through the hail-covered windshield, and it shatters.

beats.headline: The ball in slot ten
beats.text: An effect from Eris has swapped every nearby crawler's inventory with the crawler closest to them, and Donut is holding Carl's. With ten seconds to Scolopendra's next attack he shouts for her to combine the ball in slot ten of his hotlist with the biscuit in slot twelve. There is no twelve, she shrieks; search and combine, he tells her, and she finds it and drops the ball into his xistera. He puts the motorcycle down, launching them into the air, and throws. The banger sphere with the Nothing Special enriched pet biscuit goes straight into the boss's mouth, and Scolopendra splatters into a quivering puddle the size of a small elephant.
beats.gist: Donut combines sphere and biscuit; Carl's throw into Scolopendra's mouth splatters the boss.

recap.text: With the xistera idle through the close fighting on the trains, Carl loads a new Banger Sphere into the scoop on the platform and spins. It hits a babababoon in the neck with a splack, not between the eyes where he aimed, and the mob falls. The spheres are dwarven robot scrap, a few hundred made at his engineering table, and only the baseball-sized ones got the name. Two more throws kill the two mobs across the platform.

Carl made five banger spheres at his sapper's table so he could pick the songs. This one, labelled Bass heavy. For distraction., holds an impact-detonated alarm trap. Katia lobs it down the stairs at the ooze, and Jump Around plays, quieter inside the metal ball but still shaking the walls. The ball bounces with the beat and slips away each time the ooze grabs, while Donut objects to the song in capital letters.

Tom, the boss turkey, sits in the rafters while turkeys pile over one another toward Carl, Donut stands on the passed-out Mongo, and Carl cannot even cast Protective Shell. He launches a spiked banger sphere at Tom. Tom squawks and tries to dodge, but the ball smacks into a wing and breaks it with an audible crack. Carl pulls another, but Tom drops into the surging mass of turkeys.

Carl holds a special banger sphere built to destroy a truck's whole windshield in one hit. When the green light comes, he hurls it through the glass in the hail, and the windshield shatters. Eris's effect has swapped inventories, so Donut holds his; he shouts for her to combine the ball in slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve, and he throws it into Scolopendra's mouth.

tagline.text: A PVP Coupon is a black ticket with a gold-leaf skull that pays out a stack of boxes and a player level for killing the crawler named on its back. According to Hekla, a crawler in a party who earns a player-killer skull gets them in a Savage box, one for every member, and Katia has found the one with Carl's name on it where Donut hid it under a train track.
Donut says she got rid of both of hers, Carl's under a train track and Katia's in the garbage at a Hotdog on a Stick. The one with Carl's name on it is in Carl's inventory.

description.text: PVP Coupon. Ah, betrayal. Sweet, delicious betrayal. If you have this coupon in your inventory, and you kill the crawler whose name appears on the backside of this coupon, you will receive the following rewards: Gold Savage Box Gold Weapons Box Gold Apparel Box Platinum Adventurer Box (This benefit may only be redeemed a max of 3 times) +1 Player Level (This benefit may only be redeemed a max of 3 times)

beats.headline: Sweet, delicious betrayal
beats.text: Katia hands Carl a slip of paper. While he was gone after the Nightmare hit him, she and Donut went back out to clean the tracks, and practising with her third eye she saw Donut pull this from her inventory and stuff it under the track. She grew a new arm along the rail and grabbed it. It is a black ticket with a gold-leaf skull, and its description is a list of boxes and a player level. On the back: Crawler #4,122. Carl. Hekla says, Katia explains, that a party crawler who earns a skull gets one for every member. This is the only one Donut got rid of.
beats.gist: Katia gives Carl a black PVP coupon Donut hid under the track, the only one Donut discarded.

beats.headline: Imani's book
beats.text: Katia fears Donut still has one with her name on it. Her friend Eva has a skull, she says, for a man she stabbed in the back of the leg, and the coupon book, and told only Hekla. Carl pockets the coupon and asks Imani. She got a Savage box holding only the coupon book, one coupon for every member of the party. She tried to burn them and they would not catch fire, so she left them on the first floor, though Brandon wanted her to keep them. Elle got none with her skull. Donut told Imani about the two she received, and Imani told her to get rid of them.
beats.gist: Imani could not burn her coupons, left them, and told Donut to discard hers.

beats.headline: Buried and binned
beats.text: In the rental trailer, before they leave, Carl starts to raise something, and Donut gets there first: is it about the PVP coupons? Imani is a big gossip, she says, and messaged to apologise. You don't need to worry, Carl. She got rid of them. She did not like having them, so she buried his under a train track and threw Katia's out in the garbage at that Hotdog on a Stick place, and quite frankly it is a subject she would rather not talk about. Carl relaxes. That went much easier than he thought it would.
beats.gist: Imani buried Carl's PVP coupons under a train track and binned Katia's.

relations.note: the one with his own name on it
a book of her own, which she left behind on the first floor
according to Katia

recap.text: Katia hands Carl a black PVP coupon with a gold-leaf skull, marked Crawler #4,122, the only one she saw Donut stuff under the track. Imani's Savage box held only coupons, one per party member, and they would not burn, so she left them on the first floor. In the rental trailer, Donut speaks first: she buried Carl's under a train track and threw Katia's in the garbage at Hotdog on a Stick. Carl relaxes.

tagline.text: A Dirty Little Phased Bolt is ammunition for a crossbow assassin: invisible, hiding its own wound, it drains its victim to a tenth of their health with amnesia and a bleed, and a second takes them to one percent. A death that follows is put down to something else, so the shooter gets no credit and no skull. Two of them were in Katia, and Donut says she saw Hekla shoot them.
Carl keeps a broken one in his inventory. Dipped in blood it shows its shape for a moment, and it is his proof of what Hekla did.

description.text: Dirty Little Phased Bolt. This item is broken. It must be repaired before you may use it. This is a Phased item. It is invisible. It will hide its entry point and will only be discovered if it is physically touched. The perfect ammunition for the discerning crossbow assassin. This item will cast both Temporary Amnesia and Suffering Bleed onto its victim, draining them of health until they are at 10%. A second bolt will lower the victim's health to 1%. Victims who subsequently perish will be listed as dying from an alternate source. You will not get credit or experience for the kill. …

beats.headline: Mixed in with her arrows
beats.text: Katia is the train's scoop, and Donut, watching through her sunglasses, messages Carl in capitals: Hekla has shot Katia with an invisible arrow. She did it earlier too and Donut took it for a mistake. It was mixed in with her regular arrows, it went into the scoop, and the arrows are still stuck in her. Katia comes off the front of the train with her health plummeting and falls unconscious. There is no wound on her shoulder. Carl scrabbles until his hand finds something invisible and yanks, and only then does the hole in her leather appear. Donut heals her.
beats.gist: Hekla's invisible arrow hits Katia, the train's scoop; Carl yanks it out and Donut heals her.

beats.headline: No credit for the kill
beats.text: Carl pulls the invisible bolt into his inventory, finds the second one, its shaft splintered, and yanks it out too. He examines it. It is broken, phased and invisible, it hides its entry point until it is touched, and it is the perfect ammunition for the discerning crossbow assassin. Temporary Amnesia and Suffering Bleed drain the victim to ten percent, a second bolt to one, and a victim who then perishes is listed as dying from something else, with no credit, no experience and no skull. What the actual fuck? Why was she trying to kill Katia?
beats.gist: Carl pulls out a second broken bolt that hides its wound and makes victims die uncredited.

beats.headline: Bolts, Donut
beats.text: You tried to kill Katia, Donut yells at Hekla in the cab; I saw it; you used invisible arrows. Bolts, Hekla says. They're called bolts when they're from a crossbow, Donut. Katia, awake now, wants everyone to take it down a notch, and cannot understand why she does not remember. Because Hekla shot you with a scary arrow, Donut tells her. Hekla laughs, and it sounds unhinged. Bolt, Donut. It was a bolt. No, says Katia: they were both shooting, and Donut hit her with a magic missile aimed at the ghouls. She remembers.
beats.gist: Donut accuses Hekla of shooting Katia with invisible bolts, but Katia remembers Donut's magic missile hit her.

beats.headline: Dipped in blood
beats.text: Silfa insists Hekla would never have let Carl hurt her. Just like she wouldn't deliberately shoot Katia with two of those invisible bolts from her crossbow? Carl pulls the broken bolt from his inventory. It stays invisible in his hand, so he dips it in blood and holds it up, and its shape appears for a moment before everything flows off it. He hands it up to the fairy. She hesitates, grasps it, and her eyes go big as she examines its properties. He takes it back. This means nothing, she says.
beats.gist: Carl dips Hekla's invisible bolt in blood so Silfa can examine its shape.

relations.note: the broken one

recap.text: Katia, the train's scoop, falls unconscious off the front of the train with her health plummeting after Hekla's invisible bolt, mixed in with her regular arrows, goes into her. Carl scrabbles until his hand finds the bolt, yanks it out, then pulls a second, splintered one. Donut heals Katia. Carl dips the broken bolt in blood so its shape shows, and Silfa, holding it, goes wide-eyed but says it means nothing.

entities.name: Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers
aka: Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers

tagline.text: The Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers was Hekla's, and Katia, who killed her, looted it. It never runs out of basic bolts, only a woman may wield it, and its damage and speed climb with every woman in the party.
Katia's crossbow rides on Donut's back now, clipped to the Scorpion's Bite weapon mount and bigger than the cat herself. Donut admits it is weaker than it could be, with no women in her party.

description.text: Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers. This is a unique item. This is a repeating, ranged weapon. It has the buffet enchantment, meaning it will not run out of basic ammunition. […] This crossbow is rumored to have been given to Nekhebit's last warrior guardian as a gift for remaining true to her faith. This item may only be wielded by a female. For every female in your party, up to thirty, this item's damage and firing speed is increased by 25 percent. […] +15 Dexterity when wielded +10 Strength when wielded Casts Birth Defect on monster types who generate or birth additional monsters.

beats.headline: Off Hekla's back
beats.text: Carl tries to pull the crossbow off the undead Hekla's back and it will not come; it has to be Katia, who killed her, and he tells her to grab the key first and then everything she can. In the escape the body is torn in half, and the half with the crossbow is left on the far side of the wall. It's too bad about that crossbow, Carl says. Oh, you mean this, says Katia, and it forms in her hands. It looks like gold, feels almost like plastic, and is inlaid with carvings of a vulture creature. The moment Carl touches it, the system warns him: You have a dick.
beats.gist: The crossbow left behind on Hekla's torn body re-forms in Katia's hands, since she killed her.

beats.headline: Two a second, not Hekla's speed
beats.text: Katia rolls into her sentinel-gun form, three spider-like legs and a flesh-coloured shield, and the crossbow appears out of her inventory and locks into place behind it, a firing slit opening like a mouth. It loads, cocks and fires itself while she holds the prod down: about two bolts a second, magical, razor-tipped, about twenty inches long, gone on their own a minute after firing. That is fast, but nowhere near as fast as it was for Hekla, and the fire and lightning on Hekla's bolts went with the rest of her gear. Against the tentacled thing that used to be a Razor Fox, each hit takes only a tiny bit of health.
beats.gist: Katia's crossbow fires itself twice a second, slower than for Hekla, and barely dents the tentacled thing.

beats.headline: On Donut's back, Mordecai's bolt
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx is trapped in a circle of words of power, and a weapon mount from the Apothecary's gold benefactor box appears on Donut's back: the Scorpion's Bite. Katia's crossbow forms on it with an ominous click, bigger than Donut and not loaded. It is not as strong as it could be, Donut says, with no women in her party. Mordecai walks into the tent holding a plain bolt with some of his mother's ashes in its tip, a funeral rite of his culture. He says goodbye to Katia, loads the bolt into the crossbow on Donut's back and walks out. The crossbow fires. The bolt slams between the alien's eyes, and she slides to Victory's feet, dead.
beats.gist: Katia's crossbow forms on Donut's back, and Mordecai's ash-tipped bolt kills the alien.

beats.headline: Into the god's eyes
beats.text: Donut swaps into the room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps, the Scorpion's Bite on her back with the crossbow cocked and ready, and loaded into it is Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus. She aims and fires true, straight into Emberus's smouldering eye socket. A second shot takes the other eye: one of her ten Danforth bolts, made to hold the god in place. His yellow invulnerability glow winks off. For fifteen seconds Emberus is vulnerable, and he cannot move.
beats.gist: Donut's bolts hit both of Emberus's eyes, leaving him vulnerable and immobile for fifteen seconds.

relations.note: The goddess its description is named for

recap.text: Carl cannot pull the crossbow off the undead Hekla's back; only Katia, who killed her, can. The escape tears the body in half and leaves the crossbow's half beyond the wall, yet it forms in Katia's hands, almost plastic to the touch. Carl touches it and the system warns him: You have a dick. Behind Katia's sentinel-gun form it fires about two bolts a second, each taking only a tiny bit of health from the tentacled former Razor Fox.

Katia's crossbow forms with an ominous click on the Scorpion's Bite, a weapon mount that has appeared on Donut's back while Huanxin Jinx stands trapped in a circle of words of power. Mordecai walks in with a plain bolt holding some of his mother's ashes in its tip, says goodbye to Katia, loads the crossbow and walks out. The bolt slams between the alien's eyes, and she slides dead to Victory's feet.

Donut swaps into the room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps with the Scorpion's Bite on her back and the crossbow cocked, Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus loaded. She fires it straight into Emberus's smouldering eye socket, then puts a second shot, one of her ten Danforth bolts, into the other eye. His yellow invulnerability glow winks off, and for fifteen seconds he is vulnerable and cannot move.

entities.name: Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo
aka: Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo

tagline.text: The Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo is a gold champion's belt from Katia's Platinum Slam Master box. It adds strength and constitution, and when her whole body is moving, whatever she hits takes the force of twice the mass.

description.text: Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo. While you'll never be as amazing as the greatest, most beautiful wrestler of all time—Christopher Alan Pallies—you will look pretty snazzy when you wrap this bad boy around your waist. This enchanted belt offers the following benefits: +5% Strength +5% Constitution +The Avalanche benefit.

beats.headline: Platinum Slam Master
beats.text: After the bounty, Katia's boxes bring a Find Crawler skill potion and half a million gold, and one more: a Platinum Slam Master box, for killing a certain number of mobs with her momentum. Out comes a gold wrestling belt like any heavyweight champion's. Who is Christopher Pallies, she asks; Carl does not know. Five percent strength, five percent constitution, and the Avalanche benefit: hit a living creature with her body while all of it is moving, and the force is as if they were hit by twice the mass. It does not carry to weapons. We need to stick you to the front of another train, Carl says. He does not say aloud that her Rush just got stronger too.
beats.gist: Katia's Platinum Slam Master box gives her a gold belt: five percent strength and constitution, double-mass hits.

beats.headline: Like a monster truck
beats.text: Katia's new riot shield upgrades her Rush to Crowd Blast. It is still the battering ram she killed Hekla with, but now everything in a wide cone ahead of her takes ten to twenty percent of the damage. With her wrestling belt bonus on top, Carl reckons, it would be the equivalent of hitting someone with a monster truck. More important, she can now use it every five minutes instead of once a day.
beats.gist: Katia's riot shield upgrades Rush to Crowd Blast, hitting a wide cone and usable every five minutes.

relations.note: Its Crowd Blast plus the belt's Avalanche

recap.text: Katia's boxes bring a Find Crawler skill potion, half a million gold, and a Platinum Slam Master box that opens on a gold wrestling belt like any heavyweight champion's. The belt gives five percent strength, five percent constitution, and Avalanche: a body hitting a living creature while moving lands as if twice the mass. Her riot shield turns Rush into Crowd Blast, a wide cone usable every five minutes.

entities.name: Growler Gary's left hands
entities.role: The keys to the rapid-response carts

tagline.text: The rapid-response carts start only with a gnoll's left hand on each of two key consoles, so Carl collects fourteen left hands from Growler Gary, who regenerates every time. Take a hand off, and the cart shuts down.
Carl took one spare pair of Gary's hands, and he is still a pair short.

beats.headline: Left hand only
beats.text: Some NPCs regenerate in minutes, says Carl's book, and Growler Gary once woke in a pile of his own blood. While he sleeps, Mongo kills him and chomps off both arms at the elbow. Sorry, Gary, says Carl, and takes them. On the first rapid-response cart he puts one arm on the hand-shaped key console and it glows green; he weighs it down with a rock and crosses to the second, eight feet away, too far for one gnoll to reach both. Warning: You must use your left hand to activate the key. Back to the bar, says Donut. Gary, resurrected, is sober now, and Mongo kills him again. Within five minutes the first cart is running, and with its portal tuned Carl lifts a hand away to start the next one. The cart shuts off. Back to the bar.
beats.gist: Carl has Mongo kill Gary twice and takes his arms, but one hand cannot hold both carts.

beats.headline: Fourteen left hands
beats.text: Altogether they collect fourteen left hands from Growler Gary: twelve would have done, but Carl wants an extra pair in case they need to drive a seventh cart. Gary, sober now, because resurrection does that, fights back only the first few times. They are too strong for him. He hides in the back of the bar, huddled into the corner with his spear, whimpering like an injured dog. If you're sorry, he says on the fifth, why are you doing it? The floor of the back room is slick with blood.
beats.gist: They take fourteen left hands from Growler Gary, though twelve would do, and he whimpers.

beats.headline: One pair short
beats.text: With the tunnel sealed, the ghouls being generated at 72 stop heading for 36 and turn this way. Carl thinks once again of Growler Gary. They collected one extra pair of hands from the poor gnoll, but they are actually one pair short. He can't use the portal carts to protect the others, but he can use one to protect themselves. Help me position one of the carts on the track, he says. Then we gotta go talk to Gary again.
beats.gist: Carl sees the ghouls turn toward them and asks for help setting a portal cart on the track.

beats.headline: Still in place
beats.text: The interdiction cart hangs vertically from the crane like a prize fish on display, its front facing down, the scoop at the bottom of its portal scraping the marble floor. With chains anchoring it so it won't swing, Carl climbs his handmade ladder to the cockpit. He pats the two Growler Gary left hands to make sure they are still firmly in place, then turns on the portal and tunes it to the abyss.
beats.gist: Carl climbs a ladder, pats Growler Gary's two left hands, and tunes the portal to the abyss.

relations.note: he chomps off the first two arms
the hand-shaped key consoles

recap.text: Mongo kills Growler Gary over and over and chomps off his arms, since the key console on each rapid-response cart answers only to a left hand. They collect fourteen left hands, one extra pair, and still come up one pair short once the ghouls turn their way. Carl climbs into the cockpit of the interdiction cart hanging from the crane, pats the two Gary hands to check they hold, and tunes the portal to the abyss.

entities.name: Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart
entities.role: Railway cart with a mobile portal

tagline.text: The Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart is the hobgoblins' wreck-clearing vehicle, with a mobile portal across its front that sends everything on the track to a trainyard or into the abyss. It runs on batteries, and only a pair of gnolls can start it.
One interdiction cart hangs nose-down from a crane over the hole in the station, its portal facing the floor and tuned to the abyss, swallowing whatever comes up.

description.text: Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Cart. Contraption. Main Passenger-Line Gauged. The main workhorse vehicle of the Hobgoblin Interdiction Team. Includes battery power or powered track selection option. Includes portal track selector. Includes dual-destination, selectable debris scoop. […] The debris scoop will safely transport any active and running trains and their passengers back to the railyard. Once the wreck is reached, the debris scoop is switched to abyss mode, clearing the line of the damage. […] Unfortunately, the corporation running the Iron Tangle has little trust for the hobgoblins and requires security to escort these vehicles at all times. As such, this cart may only be started by a pair of gnolls.

beats.headline: A blade that is a portal
beats.text: Growler Gary tells them to take an interdiction team cart: dial in a line and it goes, on batteries even with the power out, and take a lead car, with the front portal. The yard holds unpowered trailers too heavy to lift, flatbed auxiliary carts with an outboard engine, and ten rapid-response carts that have never been used, each with a wide, flat blade across the front like a squeegee. The blade is a mobile portal. It fills the tunnel ahead and throws everything on the track, trains included, to a trainyard or into the abyss. Only a pair of gnoll hands on two sensor plates will start one. Mongo kills the sleeping Gary and bites off both his arms at the elbow.
beats.gist: Mongo kills sleeping Gary and bites off his arms to start the portal cart.

beats.headline: Two carts down each line
beats.text: Three groups of crawlers are stranded at the abyss at the ends of different lines, and Carl's plan is not to drive at all: start a cart, set it on the right track, and let it run to the end. The first draft scoops everything to a trainyard, the crawlers too. Katia and Bautista point out what else is on those tracks, crashed trains and possibly thousands of ghouls, and what the crawlers would be thrown into. So each line gets two carts. The first has its portal tuned to the abyss, to clear the way. Fifteen minutes behind it comes a second, its portal tuned to the train station, for the crawlers to stand in front of.
beats.gist: Two carts run down each line: one clears the abyss, the other follows fifteen minutes behind.

beats.headline: Six carts, six alarms
beats.text: Each portal is a two-way switch, abyss or trainyard, and each cart's trainyard is different, painted on the edge of each cart; only one is tuned to trainyard E, where they came in, so that cart stays. The carts make almost no noise, so Carl fixes an alarm trap to all six, to let the stranded crawlers hear the portal coming. He engages the first engine, checks that the portal is set to the abyss and the cart dialled to the right portal, and watches it shoot down the track, hit the portal and disappear. Katia and Donut send the last three while he wires explosives to the back of the vermillion train.
beats.gist: Katia and Donut send three carts through the portals while Carl alarms all six.

beats.headline: A crane over the hole
beats.text: Crawlers build a five-legged crane over the station's five stairwells, two train wheels on top for the pulley, and Imani's magical chain lifts the back of an interdiction cart until it hangs vertically, front down, like a prize fish. Carl climbs his handmade ladder to the cockpit, pats the two Growler Gary left hands still in place, and turns the portal on, tuned to the abyss. Facing down, it is almost exactly the size of the marble circle in the centre of the room. At one day left, across the Tangle the centres of the stations fall away and Krakaren monsters pour in. Back in their station, the monsters are falling into the portal headfirst, feet first and sideways. Thousands of them, and they keep coming.
beats.gist: Crawlers hang an interdiction cart from a crane, and Carl turns on its portal; Krakaren monsters fall in.

beats.headline: Grull, thrown away
beats.text: Grull is loose in Trainyard E, melting through its far side with his heat breath, when the portal cart comes barrelling in with Zhang at the controls. Li Na has kept the second mantaur alive as nothing but a torso and a head, which makes him easier to throw. Five punches start the summoning, and Grull turns and gallops at them. They toss the mumbling mantaur up at the oncoming cart, and with one second left, the body enters the portal and disappears. Grull, readying some massive, body-glowing attack, whiffs away, leaving only a smoke outline in the air. The music stops.
beats.gist: Zhang drives the portal cart in, and Grull whiffs into the thrown mantaur's portal.

beats.headline: The Nightmare into the abyss
beats.text: With five hours to the collapse, they carry the portal cart, turn it and set it on the employee track, its wheels just inside the wider rails. The Nightmare is loaded with explosive satchels, meant to blow up in the abyss and take loads of Krakaren monsters with it, maybe the province boss too. Fire Brandy and Tizquick have chosen to stay aboard; Carl says goodbye to them and steps off. The train backs up to the edge of the trainyard, whistles twice, speeds toward the portal and disappears. Zhang climbs back into the cart and turns the portal off.
beats.gist: Carl says goodbye to Fire Brandy and Tizquick, who stay aboard the explosive-laden Nightmare.

relations.note: His idea, and his hands on the plates

recap.text: Mongo kills the sleeping Growler Gary and bites off his arms at the elbow, since only gnoll hands on two sensor plates will start a cart whose blade is a portal. Carl sends two carts down each line to the stranded crawlers, the first tuned to the abyss, the second fifteen minutes behind it tuned to the train station. Crawlers hang a cart from a crane over the stairwells, and thousands of monsters fall in.

entities.name: Teleport Trap
entities.role: Two-part trap and a way to travel

tagline.text: In a note by Crawler Milk in the Cookbook's chapter on portals, teleport traps are simply the worst.

A teleport trap can be set inside a saferoom, because the real trap module sits outside, at the destination. Lucia Mar has set at least two, one just inside a saferoom door and one just outside the guildhall's.

A two-part teleport trap needs both halves set by the same trapper, but nothing says the anchor has to stay put. Carl mounts anchors on the backs of little spider automatons and sends them where he wants to go.

beats.headline: The worst of the portals
beats.text: Carl slips off to the personal space and opens the Cookbook's chapter on portals. A note by Crawler Milk, from the sixth edition, finds them hard to understand: dozens of types that work in different ways. Some are like doors you never notice, some work at a touch, some drag you in if you go slack, though you can still break free. Sometimes you must be big enough to fit, and sometimes a portal the size of a button tosses you into a monster den. Teleport traps are the worst. Carl adds a note about the different brands of portals, but has no time to write more.
beats.gist: Carl reads Crawler Milk's note calling teleport traps the worst of dozens of confusing portals.

beats.headline: Lucia's two traps
beats.text: Lucia Mar has set at least two teleport traps, one just inside the saferoom door and one just outside the guildhall's. According to some kid at the panel, the system allows them in saferooms because the real trap module is set outside, at the destination: a loophole that has been around for years. Carl's plan uses it. Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on the Sledge and sends the two automatons in one after the other. The first triggers the trap and appears right outside among the hunters. The second rushes at Lucia with what looks like Donut on its shoulder, but is one of Bautista's beanie babies, a black cat thing in a crown and sunglasses.
beats.gist: Lucia Mar's saferoom trap sends Donut's two automatons out; the second charges her carrying a beanie baby.

beats.headline: Traps for summoned guards
beats.text: Astrid can call one to three club guards to her with every casting, no cooldown, so the ambush needs a contingency, and Carl takes a page from Lucia Mar's playbook. Down the hallway to the monster door he sets his two-part teleport traps, to send any NPC who trips them to a locked closet on the top floor. Astrid flies everywhere and will not trip them, but he calls out fairies specifically, in case she slams into one on purpose. The second halves, the beacons, still have to go upstairs into the hidden utility closet.
beats.gist: Carl sets teleport traps down the hallway to send tripped NPCs to a locked top-floor closet.

beats.headline: Anchors on spider automatons
beats.text: Samantha asks why Carl does not do what the scary lady does, and he could kiss her. He has four sets of two-part teleport traps; the market has one more. Into Samantha's neck hole go three fist-sized spider automatons, each with an anchor half fixed to its flat top, and a red one carrying a trap Donut set. Mordecai objects that one trapper must set both halves, or crawlers would trade anchors through the guild rooms. That is the point, says Carl: the anchor rides the automaton, and the automaton can go anywhere. He arms the triggers in the clearing, slips his last anchor into Samantha, and throws her. She lands across the street and lets the spiders out.
beats.gist: Carl throws Samantha across the street after loading her with three anchor-carrying spider automatons.

beats.headline: Totems through the traps
beats.text: Carl teleports onto the spider automaton across the street from the capitol building and crushes it under his weight. The other three, two regular and the red one, scatter; the fourth stays inside Samantha. In the room where the floor began, Ren and Quan are fighting. Donut is far away in her own fight with the duendes, with her deck, so she can summon totems, and through the teleport traps Carl can bring them to him. With luck Quan cannot snare them, and they can attack him without first getting past his own totems. It is an exploit, and a chickenshit one. Jola fills the left of the room and Lazarus appears on the right, the spider automaton under him crunching in a shower of sparks.
beats.gist: Carl teleports onto a spider automaton, crushes it, and brings Donut's totems to him through the traps.

beats.headline: Both halves on one robot
beats.text: On the roof of a block of penthouses, a demon stands in the shell of the snake city boss. Carl sets his last automaton down in front of the door. This one carries both halves of a teleport trap. It will walk up and bump the snake, setting it off, and because the anchor rides on the same robot, the snake will go nowhere, though it still technically teleports. That should break the demon out of the shell, and out of Sister Ines's control; done properly, the nun has to die first.
beats.gist: Carl sets his last automaton, carrying both trap halves, before the door to teleport the snake nowhere.

beats.headline: Into Samantha
beats.text: Forty-five seconds. Carl tells Samantha not to let him out until the fire flares, and she wants to know why he is yelling; she is having a tussle. Behind him Raul groans while Alpha Carl berates him. Carl pulls the teleport trap's trigger out of his inventory and steps into it, and he arrives at the trap he left inside Samantha.
beats.gist: Carl steps into the teleport trap's trigger and arrives at the trap he left inside Samantha.

beats.headline: Four automatons out
beats.text: The ground before the castle glitters with thousands of traps, far thicker than Carl expected, and he means to collect any summon traps on the way. From his inventory he pulls the teleport automatons, each carrying the second half of a trap, then puts most of them away: the traps here are too thick for a larger force. He keeps out only Katia's, Imani's, Holger's and Splash Zone's, and messages those four to come in. Katia, Imani and Splash Zone appear. The trap meant for Holger brings Dong Quixote instead, mounted on Gonk, the swamp yak that once belonged to King Rust: Holger gave Dong his half of the trap.
beats.gist: Carl calls four teleport automatons in, but Holger's trap brings Dong Quixote on Gonk instead.

relations.note: Carl's note on portals
her note on portals in the Cookbook

recap.text: Carl slips off to the personal space and opens the Cookbook's chapter on portals. A note by Crawler Milk, from the sixth edition, finds them hard to understand: dozens of types, some that drag you in if you go slack. A portal the size of a button can toss you into a monster den, and teleport traps are the worst. Carl adds a note about brands of portals.

Lucia Mar has set one teleport trap just inside the saferoom door and another just outside the guildhall's. Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on the Sledge and sends the two automatons in one after the other, using the loophole that the real trap module sits outside, at the destination. The first triggers the trap and appears among the hunters. The second rushes at Lucia with a beanie baby on its shoulder, a black cat thing in a crown and sunglasses.

Astrid can call one to three club guards with every casting, so Carl sets two-part teleport traps down the hallway to send any NPC who trips them to a locked closet. He fixes anchors to three fist-sized spider automatons and throws Samantha across the street to release them. He teleports onto one and crushes it, then brings Donut's totems to him through the traps.

Carl pulls out the teleport automatons, each holding the second half of a trap, then puts most away because the traps glittering before the castle are too thick for a larger force. He keeps out Katia's, Imani's, Holger's and Splash Zone's, and messages those four to come in. Katia, Imani and Splash Zone appear. Holger's trap brings Dong Quixote, mounted on Gonk, the swamp yak that once belonged to King Rust, because Holger gave Dong his half.

entities.name: The Left Fang of the Green Sultan

tagline.text: The Left Fang of the Green Sultan is one of Eva's two sabers, dropped in a train's engine car and picked out of the gore by Carl. It is half of a set and only magical with its brother, so on its own it gives nothing, and Eva has lost her main weapon.
Carl has given the saber to Katia as she prepares to go her own way, and told her to return it to its rightful owner.
Katia has returned the saber to Eva. She cut off Eva's escape-ring hand with it, then drove it through her breastplate.

beats.headline: Found in the gore
beats.text: His train bomb built, Carl is about to jump out of the front window of the vermillion engine when he spots something on the floor. It is one of Eva's two sabers, dropped when Donut raised Hekla from the dead, fallen into the gore and forgotten. He pulls it into his inventory and goes out the window. In the hours of grinding that follow, Katia practises with it in her smaller form. The description says it is part of a set, only magical when the two are together; alone, the enchanted saber gives no buffs at all. Good, thinks Carl. Eva has lost her main weapon.
beats.gist: Carl finds one of Eva's sabers in the gore and pockets it; alone, it gives no buffs.

beats.headline: Back to its rightful owner
beats.text: Katia is going to separate from them, with a pretty big party of helpers, Louis and Firas, Gwen and her team, Daniel Bautista and a few of his friends, and Florin, and Donut is about to cry. Carl wants to argue, and does not. He pulls the Left Fang from his inventory, half of Eva's main weapon, and tells Katia to make sure she returns it to its rightful owner. The saber glints with a green, venomous light. Katia nods, and it disappears into her inventory. She will make sure of it.
beats.gist: Katia leaves with a large party, and Carl gives her the Left Fang to return to its owner.

beats.headline: Through the breastplate
beats.text: Katia and Li Na pull dead bugs off the unconscious Eva, who has almost no health and ten seconds before she wakes. Li Na casts Preserve Injury so she cannot heal, and points at the ring on Eva's top right hand, the one that would let her disappear. Katia draws Eva's old sword and cuts the hand off with it, then the poisonous rapier from the top left stub. Eva wakes, spits defiance, then begs. Katia plunges the sword into her chest, punching right through the metal of her magical breastplate. Die, Eva.
beats.gist: Katia and Li Na stop Eva healing, cut off her ring hand and rapier, and Katia stabs her.

relations.note: one of her pair, dropped on the train

recap.text: Carl, his train bomb built, spots one of Eva's two sabers in the gore, dropped when Donut raised Hekla from the dead. He pulls it into his inventory and jumps out the front window of the vermillion engine. Its description says the pair is magical only together, so alone it gives no buffs. Good, thinks Carl: Eva has lost her main weapon.

Katia leaves the others with a large party of helpers: Louis and Firas, Gwen and her team, Daniel Bautista and a few of his friends, and Florin. Donut is about to cry, and Carl wants to argue but does not. He takes the Left Fang, half of Eva's main weapon, from his inventory and tells Katia to return it to its rightful owner. The saber glints green and venomous, and Katia nods and stows it in her inventory.

Katia and Li Na pull dead bugs off the unconscious Eva, who has ten seconds before she wakes. Li Na casts Preserve Injury so Eva cannot heal and points at the ring on her top right hand, the one that would let her disappear. Katia cuts that hand off with Eva's old sword, then the poisonous rapier from the top left stub. Eva wakes, spits defiance, begs, and Katia punches the sword through her breastplate into her chest.

entities.name: Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit
aka: Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit

tagline.text: The Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit is a wrist bracer that pops a small metal shield into place with a twist. Katia gives it to Carl once her new riot shield will not let her wear both, and a hit on it has a small chance to disarm the attacker.
Carl has swapped the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit for a better shield bracer, and it has gone onto the pile of gear for the Faction Wars team.

description.text: Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit. Forms a metallic buckler on command. May be triggered via hotlist or by shaking your wrist like you're thinking of your hot Aunt Lydia. This item is enchanted with Shatter. Any attack that lands upon this shield has a 1.5% chance to disarm the opponent. If the opponent is disarmed, there is a 90% chance the item will drop to the ground, a 5% chance the weapon will break, and a 5% chance the weapon will be immediately transferred to your own inventory.

beats.headline: Much better than a litterbox
beats.text: Katia's fan box gives her a riot shield, and when she tries to equip it the system will not let her wear both. So she takes a bracer off her left wrist and tells Carl to have it; he needs a shield anyway. He had forgotten she owned it. She mostly used it to add to her mass. It looks like the bracer on his right wrist, the one that forms his gauntlet. He slides it on over the arm of his jacket and experiments: a twist of the wrist and a small shield pops into place, a shake and it disappears. Much better than a litterbox, says Donut.
beats.gist: Katia gives Carl her spare bracer, a shield that pops out with a wrist twist.

beats.headline: A gerbil, caught
beats.text: The gerbils will not stop coming, the town's defenders are falling, and Carl is sure this is a punishment. He tosses a smoke curtain and a pair of hob-lobbers, steps over the barricade and wades out toward the street while Donut yells after him, and extends his left-arm shield. He catches a flying gerbil with the auto-buckler. It falls hard to the ground, blinded and dazed. Too tired to fight it any more, he steps on it.
beats.gist: Carl, sure the gerbils are a punishment, catches one with his auto-buckler and stomps it.

beats.headline: Swapped for a pushier shield
beats.text: A short black forearm bracer covered in little buckles comes out of Carl's boxes: the Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield, an overly enthusiastic auto buckler that catches physical and magical bolt attacks and can throw them back. He already wears two bracers, and the Peach Pit's disarm chance has never once worked for him. Mordecai calls the new one much better, and it matches his other bracer. Carl pulls the Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit off his left arm and tosses it onto their growing pile of weapons and armour for the Faction Wars team.
beats.gist: Carl swaps his Peach Pit buckler for the Right Back Atcha shield and discards the old one.

relations.note: Katia could not wear both

recap.text: Katia's fan box gives her a riot shield, but the system will not let her wear it alongside the bracer on her left wrist. She hands the bracer to Carl, who had forgotten she owned it. It looks like the bracer on his right wrist, and he slides it on over his jacket sleeve. A twist pops out a small shield, a shake makes it vanish, and Donut calls it much better than a litterbox.

Carl is sure the gerbils are a punishment, since they keep coming while the town's defenders fall. He tosses a smoke curtain and a pair of hob-lobbers, steps over the barricade, and wades toward the street while Donut yells after him. He extends his left-arm shield and the auto-buckler catches a flying gerbil, which falls hard, blinded and dazed. Too tired to fight it, he steps on it.

Carl pulls a short black forearm bracer covered in little buckles from his boxes: the Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield, an overly enthusiastic auto buckler that catches bolt attacks and can throw them back. The Peach Pit's disarm chance has never once worked for him, and Mordecai calls the new bracer much better. Carl tosses the old one onto the pile for the Faction Wars team.

entities.name: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield

tagline.text: Katia's fan box gave her a riot shield of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces: tall, curved and absurdly light, with Get Back on the front. It adds constitution and Rooted in Place, and it upgrades her Rush to Crowd Blast, which hits a whole cone in front of her and can be used every five minutes instead of once a day.

description.text: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield. Sometimes the galaxy isn't a happy place. Sometimes the unwashed masses forget their place in the machine. And sometimes these dregs bubble up to the surface, causing a phenomenon widely known as "Civil Unrest." And when that happens, the powers that be don't want to become the powers that were. So they hire backup. An outside force to come down and kick everything back into order, and maybe commit a few war crimes in the process just so the filth knows their place. One such outfit, trained specifically for this sort of situation, is the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces. …

beats.headline: Get Back
beats.text: In the Soda saferoom at station 59, Katia opens her fan box first, before Mordecai gets back. Out pop a goddamned baseball bat and a shield: about six feet tall, curved like a half cylinder, with loops to hold with both hands or slide one arm through, a small plastic-like window at the top, and Get Back on the front in white, blocky letters. It's a riot shield, Carl says, and it is absurdly light. It gives five percent to constitution and five to Rooted in Place, and it upgrades Rush to Crowd Blast. Only a crawler with Rush can equip it.
beats.gist: Katia's riot shield, Get Back, is light, curved, and six feet tall, and upgrades Rush to Crowd Blast.

beats.headline: An electric litterbox
beats.text: Crowd Blast is the battering-ram skill Katia killed Hekla with, upgraded. She still rushes forward, but everything in a wide cone in front of her takes ten to twenty percent of the damage, and she can use it every five minutes, not once a day. Rooted in Place makes her much harder to knock over, which, its description warns, is not necessarily a good thing. Katia cannot tell if people were trolling her: they know she hates using Rush. Donut compares it to getting an electric litterbox for your birthday. Useful, indeed. But a litterbox.
beats.gist: Katia's upgraded riot shield blasts a wide cone every five minutes; Donut calls it an electric litterbox.

beats.headline: Like a wrecking ball
beats.text: Katia, in her she-hulk form, about eight feet tall and wide, wears the riot shield on her left arm in its original form, and it makes her look especially imposing. When the hallway ahead fills with Krakaren monsters and ghouls, crammed tight and rushing at them, she widens, rotates the shield ninety degrees and pushes it forward like a battering ram. Go, says Carl. She activates Crowd Blast and explodes into the crowd like a wrecking ball, and the monsters rocket back like bowling pins. Acid mists into the air and she cries out, but she goes all the way to the first intersection.
beats.gist: Katia, as an eight-foot she-hulk, rams her riot shield into a Krakaren crowd and scatters it.

beats.headline: Hulking out
beats.text: Leaving town for the Bactrian town, about three miles off on the other side of the dunes, Katia adds extra mass, rising up and hulking out, and pulls her riot shield onto her left arm. It still freaks him out when she changes, Carl admits. That's because you're used to being the biggest guy in the room, she says.
beats.gist: Katia hulks up and takes her riot shield on her left arm; Carl admits it still unnerves him.

recap.text: Katia opens her fan box in the Soda saferoom and pulls out a baseball bat and a six-foot riot shield marked Get Back. The shield upgrades her Rush to Crowd Blast, and Donut compares it to an electric litterbox for your birthday. In the hallway, Katia turns the shield sideways, explodes into the Krakaren monsters like a wrecking ball, and sends them flying like bowling pins. Acid mists her, but she reaches the first intersection.

Katia leaves town for the Bactrian town, about three miles off on the other side of the dunes. She adds extra mass, rises up and hulks out, then pulls her riot shield onto her left arm. Carl admits it still freaks him out when she changes. She tells him that is because he is used to being the biggest guy in the room.

entities.name: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Telescoping Crowd Control Baton

tagline.text: The baseball bat in Katia's fan box is a police baton, faintly glowing with enchantment, that telescopes from twenty-five centimetres to three metres and casts a Cone of Knockback when swung at a group of ten or more.

description.text: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Telescoping Crowd Control Baton. This enchanted truncheon is designed to crack skulls and to teach those ungrateful bastards to show some got-damned respect. This item's length is adjustable, from 25 centimeters to 3 meters. Automatically casts Level-five Cone of Knockback if swung at a group of 10 or more like mobs. This triggers only once every five minutes.

beats.headline: Not a baseball bat
beats.text: The other thing out of Katia's fan box looks like a baseball bat, and it is actually a police baton. At first glance there is nothing special about it, but as Katia rolls it over in her hands, eyes wide and lips tight, Carl sees the slight glow of enchantment. Its length adjusts from twenty-five centimetres to three metres, and swung at a group of ten or more like mobs it automatically casts a level-five Cone of Knockback, once every five minutes. Those are both pretty awesome, Carl says. Especially the shield.
beats.gist: Katia's baton telescopes from twenty-five centimetres to three metres and knocks back groups of ten.

beats.headline: Swung one way
beats.text: Crowd Blast has carried Katia into the hallway full of Krakaren monsters and ghouls, all the way to the first intersection, a T with short stairwells going down on either side. Dazed but still on her feet, she pulls her crowd-control baton and swings it in one direction while the crossbow flips upside-down and fires in the other. Carl comes running up behind her with a second boom jug in his hand.
beats.gist: Katia swings her baton one way while the crossbow flips and fires the other, Carl running up behind.

recap.text: Katia pulls a baseball-bat-shaped object from her fan box and finds a police baton, faintly glowing with enchantment. It extends from twenty-five centimetres to three metres, and swung at ten or more mobs it casts a level-five Cone of Knockback once every five minutes. Crowd Blast carries her to a T intersection in the hallway of Krakaren monsters and ghouls, where she swings the baton one way while her crossbow flips upside-down and fires the other.

tagline.text: The Stuffed Grulke Infantry Figure is a beanbag toad in a spiked helmet, the commonest of its line, one of more than a thousand stuffed monsters from Miss Quill's apartment. Pull the tag and throw it, and a real grulke fights for fifteen to thirty seconds.

description.text: Stuffed Grulke Infantry Figure. (With tags) This is the most common variation of the Grulke line of collectible figures. In terms of rarity, these things clock in just below frat boys with early-onset liver disease. It's literally not possible to enter a waystation kinder shop and not find one of these for sale on the shelf. You'll be hard-pressed to find a collector who will buy this off you. It sure is cute, though.

beats.headline: A beanbag with its tag on
beats.text: Bautista's quest to kill Miss Quill failed when Carl's party killed her by accident, blowing a hole in the ceiling of the magistrate's office, and when he got into her apartment it was empty except for stuffed monsters, more than a thousand of them. He tosses Carl one: a brown frog in a spiked helmet, tag still on, the same creature Mordecai is shape-shifted into. The paper tag says only Grulke Infantry, Jaxbrin Amusements, Ltd. Pull the tag like a grenade, Bautista explains, throw it, and in about ten seconds it fights for you, or attacks you. The common ones last fifteen to thirty seconds. He has four more like it.
beats.gist: Bautista gives Carl a beanbag frog in a spiked helmet; pulling its tag summons a fighter for seconds.

beats.headline: The frog con
beats.text: With smoke billowing out of Donut's hole in the wall and camels everywhere, Carl rips the tag off the stuffed grulke and tosses it into the alley. A mighty croak, and a level-15 toad stands there with a 25-second timer, asking what he is doing here. Carl asks him to hop out onto the street and over the city wall. You summoned me just to make me run, the grulke complains, and goes anyway, landing in front of two surprised camels and bounding out of sight. Soon a camel is telling Donut that frog creatures attacked the town hall.
beats.gist: A toad summoned from the stuffed grulke hops over the city wall, and camels blame frog creatures.

beats.headline: Questions at the gate
beats.text: The storm ends, and the town survives. The camels do not retract the sails as usual; Langley says there are guards at the main gate now, and anti-air defences going up all around the city. Everyone is still allowed to come and go, but everyone is interrogated about grulke toads and gnomes. The laid-back town has become a city under siege.
beats.gist: The storm ends, and guards, anti-air defences and questions about grulke toads and gnomes fill the town.

relations.note: One of more than a thousand in her apartment

recap.text: Bautista's quest to kill Miss Quill failed when Carl's party killed her by accident and blew a hole in the ceiling of the magistrate's office. Her apartment held nothing but more than a thousand stuffed monsters, and Bautista tosses Carl one: a brown frog in a spiked helmet, tag still on. He says to pull the tag like a grenade and throw it, and in about ten seconds it fights for Carl, or attacks him.

Carl rips the tag off the stuffed grulke and tosses it into the alley. A level-15 toad with a 25-second timer appears and asks what he is doing here. Carl asks him to hop over the city wall, and the grulke complains that he was summoned just to run, then bounds past two surprised camels. When the storm ends, guards stand at the main gate, and everyone is interrogated about grulke toads and gnomes.

tagline.text: Astral Paw is the spellbook Donut pulls from the mailbox as her spellbook-of-the-floor club prize, and she reads it before anyone can talk her out of it. Mordecai calls it a good utility spell: a paw that handles things at a distance as if she were touching them, with more force than Astral Hand and claws to come at level five.
Donut picks Astral Paw as one of the two spells her War Crime combines, and over the hole of Larracos it becomes a glowing paw big enough to pin an army under it.
A gift from the gods has pushed Donut's Claw skill to 17, and Mordecai tells her that her Astral Paw spell can now cut through almost anything. She stiffens at the name.

beats.headline: A paw with no thumb
beats.text: On the way to the personal space, Donut bounces over to the mailbox and grabs her spellbook-of-the-floor club prize, and she is glowing as she reads it before Carl can remind her that they talk about spellbooks first. Unwad your panties, Carl. Mordecai names it: Astral Paw, a utility spell like Hole. Not as good as Astral Hand, with no thumb to hold things, but more force, and it can be a weapon: claws at level five, a much bigger paw at ten, her own skills carried into it at fifteen. About ten meters at level one. Back home, Carl laughs, she could finally have knocked that vase off the high shelf.
beats.gist: Donut grabs her Astral Paw spellbook from the mailbox, and Mordecai explains the spell.

beats.headline: Elmer goes down the slope
beats.text: Elmer the mayor charges a customary execution fee of a hundred gold, and offers both at once for a hundred and fifty. Let's do it, says Carl, and pulls out a few more coins. The moment Elmer steps closer to take the money, Donut casts Astral Paw and pushes him from behind toward the slope. He tumbles off the edge of town and rolls down, flipping like a ragdoll and bouncing off a rock. Carl whirls with a banger sphere and never gets the chance to throw it.
beats.gist: Donut casts Astral Paw and pushes Elmer off the edge of town as he reaches for coins.

beats.headline: The paw over Larracos
beats.text: Donut has been named Champion, her health draining, frozen, and Carl cannot tell what the second spell she picked for War Crime was. Then he sees it, hovering above the hole of Larracos: the massive, glowing outline of a cat's paw. The frozen soldiers and the god Meatus float slowly up out of the hole as music blasts across the world, and the claw grows big enough to catch thousands. They wake and scream, bunched against its underside, swarmed by fleshers that dissolve them. When Li Na's chains spread for the finisher, Donut stretches her arm over empty air. I shouldn't have picked Astral Paw. I have to do it myself.
beats.gist: Donut's giant glowing paw lifts the frozen soldiers and Meatus, and fleshers dissolve them.

beats.headline: Cannibals off the bridge
beats.text: Cannibals drop onto the truck and explode against its barrier, and Olga taps a gauge: they are overheating the shield. Donut's claw caps disappear, blue light fills the cab, and she swipes at open air. Her Astral Paw sweeps through the woods ahead, clearing the cannibals off the bridge like pieces off a chessboard; most fly screaming into the jungle. It is nowhere near the size of her War Crime, which she cannot cast again until the twelfth floor, but it is still huge. Whatever was holding the arched tree down snaps, and it catapults the rest the other way.
beats.gist: Donut's Astral Paw sweeps most cannibals off the bridge, and a snapped tree flings the rest away.

beats.headline: A Cadillac crushed flat
beats.text: The Russian crawlers' Cadillac bursts forward to the middle of the lobby and flips up at a right angle, like a rocket about to launch: they are making a run for the exit. The APV and Chris's truck fire spells at it, its shield sparks and flickers, and Prepotente hurls something that knocks it out. In that moment Donut casts Astral Paw and smashes the car where it stands, crushing it like a tin can. Less than a second passes from her shout to the crush. Three new player-killer skulls form over her.
beats.gist: Donut's Astral Paw flattens the Russian crawlers' escaping Cadillac like a tin can, earning three player-killer skulls.

recap.text: Donut bounces to the mailbox, grabs her spellbook prize, and reads it glowing before Carl can remind her that spellbooks get discussed first. Mordecai names it Astral Paw, a utility spell like Hole: not as good as Astral Hand, since a paw has no thumb, but with more force and a reach of about ten meters at level one. It grows claws at level five, a much bigger paw at ten, and carries her own skills at fifteen.

Elmer the mayor charges a hundred gold for the customary execution and a hundred and fifty for both, and Carl says let's do it and pulls out a few more coins. As Elmer steps closer for the money, Donut casts Astral Paw and pushes him from behind toward the slope. He tumbles off the edge of town, flipping like a ragdoll and bouncing off a rock, and Carl whirls with a banger sphere he never throws.

Donut, named Champion with her health draining and her body frozen, casts a massive, glowing outline of a cat's paw above the hole of Larracos. The frozen soldiers and the god Meatus float up, and the claw grows big enough to catch thousands, who wake and scream as fleshers dissolve them. When Li Na's chains spread for the finisher, Donut stretches her arm over empty air. She has to do it herself.

Donut's claw caps vanish and blue light fills the truck's cab as she swipes at open air, and her Astral Paw sweeps the cannibals off the bridge like chessmen, most flying screaming into the jungle. In the lobby, she casts it again on the Russian crawlers' Cadillac, which has reared up to run for the exit, and crushes it like a tin can. Three new player-killer skulls form over her.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Gnome FarSeerer is a dirigible gnome bomb sight, a white telescope covered in pipes and gears, that lets its user inspect things at a distance. Skarn keeps one to watch the patrols, and every gnome it targets is told they are being watched.
Donut has stolen the FarSeerer off Skarn's roof in ten seconds flat, and she says she forgot the thirty gold she was told to leave for it.

description.text: Enchanted Gnome FarSeerer. Used to sight long-range targets for their bomb runs, the FarSeerer is credited as one of the key inventions that allowed the Dirigible Gnomes to obtain air superiority. When properly installed on a Gnomish Dreadnaught, this device increases the accuracy of gravity-based bombs by 75%. Allows for inspection and information on objects at a distance. It's pretty good for spying on your neighbors, too. You don't need porn when you got this thing hanging off the edge of your airship. Warning: All gnomes targeted with this device are given a notice that they are being watched.

beats.headline: Skarn watches the patrol
beats.text: Skarn moves to the telescope, which points toward the desert. He likes to watch the patrol to make sure they are okay; Flint says if he grows up big and strong, maybe they will let him stay and he can join it one day. The telescope is a white tube covered in pipes and gears, made of something odd, maybe ceramic. Carl examines it: a dirigible gnome bomb sight that lets its user inspect things at a distance, and tells every gnome it targets that they are being watched. Flint found it in the dunes, Skarn says, among lots of crashed stuff from the last war. There! There it is!
beats.gist: Carl examines the telescope Skarn watches the patrol through: a gnome bomb sight that alerts every target.

beats.headline: Ten seconds flat
beats.text: Part of Carl feels bad about stealing from little Skarn and his burgeoning charge-people-to-look-through-his-telescope business, but there is no time to debate it. He knocks, checks that Flint is out, and tells the boy to run to the Toe if the bombs start, and to tell all his friends. While they talk, Donut scales the wall, leaps to the roof and steals the gnomish farseer telescope in ten seconds flat. Carl told her to leave thirty gold pieces on the roof as payment. She tells him she forgot.
beats.gist: Donut steals Skarn's telescope in ten seconds and forgets Carl's thirty gold pieces of payment.

beats.headline: Letting the gnomes know
beats.text: Wynne the dirigible gnome is duct-taped to the raised back seat of the ATV as Carl heads out across the desert, the farseer in his hand, staring up at the flying fortress. The damn thing is huge. He focuses on several different gnomes long enough that each receives a notification that they are being watched. That is the point: they want the gnomes to know they are here. The Wasteland does not bomb them. It keeps moving south, toward Hump Town.
beats.gist: Carl watches gnomes through the farseer so each gets notified, while the fortress keeps moving south.

recap.text: Skarn lets Carl look through the white tube of pipes and gears that Flint found in the dunes. Carl sees it is a dirigible gnome bomb sight that tells every gnome it targets they are being watched. Donut steals it in ten seconds flat and forgets the thirty gold pieces Carl told her to leave. Carl aims it at gnomes from the ATV, and the flying fortress keeps moving south.

entities.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit
aka: Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit

tagline.text: The Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit, on Carl's left foot, carries two benefits. Sticky Feet lets him walk on walls and ceilings barefoot once every six hours, and Super Spreader passes his active debuffs to a target once an hour.

description.text: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit. This is a unique item. Most children in the universe know the exciting tale of the Leprous Bandit, the infamous human thief whose people were starving to death because of a planet-wide quarantine. … To this day, the Leprous Bandit remains an inspiration. This toe ring imbues the following: The Sticky Feet Benefit. The Super Spreader Benefit.

beats.headline: Smushed for Daddy
beats.text: Being stepped upon by a deity and surviving earns Carl the Smushed for Daddy achievement and a platinum Spicy Box, which he got, as he puts it, because the system AI is a goddamned pervert. Inside is a toe ring with a long tale of a human thief who broke into a floating garden. Two benefits in one item, says Mordecai; that is almost legendary tier. Sticky Feet: once every six hours, for his dexterity times two seconds, Carl may walk on a wall or ceiling, bare feet only. Super Spreader passes his active debuffs to a target once an hour. Gross, he says, and slides it onto his left pinky.
beats.gist: Carl survives a deity's stomp and wins a toe ring that spreads debuffs and walks walls.

beats.headline: Upside down over an ooze
beats.text: They go with Carl's least favorite idea, the last resort, which Donut suggests out loud: he will walk on the ceiling over the ooze. Sticky Feet gives him his dexterity times two seconds, once every six hours, and his dexterity sits at thirty-two. He has practised a few times, but not yet in combat. Oozes hunt by vibration and sound, Mordecai warns, so his clomping on the ceiling will draw it unless he distracts it with one of the things he built. He lowers himself, places a bare foot on the ceiling, and readies Sticky Feet.
beats.gist: Carl plans to walk the ceiling over the ooze using Sticky Feet, which lasts only thirty-two seconds.

beats.headline: Stuck to the wing
beats.text: Carl is clutching the wing brace when the plane pulls sharply upward and whips around like a haywire carnival ride. He activates Sticky Feet at once, which for a moment saves him from flying right off the wing. Donut is in the cockpit, screaming, all the way on her back against the small seat with a death grip on the yoke. The plane does a complete loop, and loops again, rolling starboard.
beats.gist: Carl clutches the wing brace, uses Sticky Feet, and stays on as the plane loops with Donut screaming.

beats.headline: Left to Fester, shared
beats.text: Carl has used Sticky Feet a lot; the ring's second ability he has never tried. Super Spreader reaches anyone close enough for him to see their name, and Ping has made that range far greater. He scrolls the list to Hunter Xindy, a level 61 mantis of the Dark Hive, and clicks Activate. She stops dead in the air, then retreats fast as she realises she has a debuff: she now has his Left to Fester too, and it will not go away until Chin'Dua is dead.
beats.gist: Carl uses Super Spreader on Hunter Xindy, a level 61 mantis, and she retreats, now afflicted too.

beats.headline: Quan Ch, leaking slugs
beats.text: Quan Ch has both sets of keys and is heading for one of the two exits. Carl makes a new chat group for Imani and Tserendolgor. Be careful: he is really good, but he is not going to be feeling well. Carl cast Super Spreader on him at the last second, and he is going to be leaking slugs. They will fight for him, but every one that comes out damages him more, and it gets worse with each passing minute. Delay him as long as possible.
beats.gist: Quan Ch heads for an exit with both key sets, leaking slugs that hurt him.

recap.text: A deity steps on Carl, he survives, and the platinum Spicy Box he earns holds a toe ring, which he slides onto his left pinky. Sticky Feet lets him walk on walls or ceilings, bare feet only, for his dexterity times two seconds every six hours. He readies it to cross a ceiling over an ooze, then uses it on a plane's wing, where it keeps him from flying off for a moment as Donut screams and loops the plane.

Carl has never tried the second ability of his Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit, Super Spreader, which reaches anyone close enough for him to see their name. Ping has stretched that range far wider. He scrolls to Hunter Xindy, a level 61 mantis of the Dark Hive, and clicks Activate. She stops dead in the air, then flees once she realises she now carries his Left to Fester, which stays until Chin'Dua is dead.

Carl sees Quan Ch carrying both sets of keys toward one of the two exits. He starts a new chat group for Imani and Tserendolgor and warns them that Quan Ch is really good but feels sick, because Carl cast Super Spreader on him and he leaks slugs. Carl tells them to delay him as long as possible.

tagline.text: The Gnomish Knock-Knock is a refrigerator-sized fuel-air bomb, barely stable, slung under the gnomes' patrol ships. Only a few are left, and they are kept now as a standoff weapon.

The last few Knock-Knocks hang under the Wasteland itself on the morning it comes to bomb Hump Town. Carl's second volley of missiles goes at its gun battery and three bombs on its underside, and the sky to the north goes up in white fire.
Carl counts the Knock-Knocks under the Wasteland as one quadrant's "cheat", a quick way to kill everything, like the drain hidden in the side of the sandcastle.

description.text: Gnomish Knock-Knock. Type: Fuel-air bomb. Effect: Thermobaric Explosion. Status: 40. Barely stable. I wouldn't be tapping on the thing. Ever seen a hundred Dromedarians die because their lungs imploded, followed by their skin getting melted off their body just before they all shatter into mist? Well now's your chance! Fun for the whole family, this was the main weapon of the Gnomish Bombardier Squads. There are only a few of these things left, and they're usually strapped to the failing air force's most reliable patrol ships. The fuel-air Knock-Knocks were once used to devastating effect in the early days of the last conflict. The remaining munitions are instead used as a mutual-standoff weapon. …
