beats.headline: Under a rowboat-sized airship
beats.text: Through a telescope, Carl looks the Wasteland over: a jagged island held aloft by colossal balloons, its edges dotted with ballistae and trebuchets. A rowboat-sized gnomish airship drifts into view on four propellers, and dangling under it is a refrigerator-sized bomb. Zoomed in, the telescope gives him the item, status 40, barely stable, with an adjustable pressure fuse that sets the height it bursts at. Carl asks Skarn whether they dropped one of those on his old village. Yep, says the kid. It was a long time ago, though, and he does not remember it.
beats.gist: Carl spots a gnomish airship carrying a bomb; Skarn says gnomes bombed his village.

beats.headline: Three miles of range
beats.text: To hit one of the Knock-Knocks parked under the gnomes' castle from the surface, the missiles need a range of about three miles. The missiles now burn a propellant Mordecai improved, with a second stage that lights when the first burns out, and recycling a few impact hob-lobbers showed Carl a simpler trigger, which leaves room for a full stick of hobgoblin dynamite in each warhead. The test shot chases Ruckus as the boss climbs. The second stage sparks, and the missile blows a few hundred feet short.
beats.gist: The missiles now reach three miles, but the test shot blows a few hundred feet short of Ruckus.

beats.headline: Four missiles, then three bombs
beats.text: The Wasteland has come down to about two and a half kilometres, and its underside crawls with harnessed gnomes arming bombs: dozens of small round ones, and the few Knock-Knocks left. They drop them by cutting the chains. From the hijacked balloon, at the very edge of his missiles' range, Carl fires the four guided missiles he has assigned to the Knock-Knocks he spied after sunrise, just as the airship's gun battery fires at the balloon, and all four detonate early as they cross its volley. He aims the second launcher at the battery and three bombs on the underside. The three of them leap from the basket, and the whole world to the north explodes in a ball of white, hot fire.
beats.gist: Carl fires four missiles at the gnomes' Knock-Knocks, and they detonate early against the airship's volley.

relations.note: the last few hang on chains under its belly

recap.text: Through a telescope Carl sees a gnomish airship with a refrigerator-sized bomb dangling beneath it. Skarn says they dropped one on his old village, but he does not remember it. Carl's test missile, with Mordecai's propellant and a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, blows a few hundred feet short. From the hijacked balloon, his four missiles detonate early in the airship battery's volley, and the three of them leap as the north explodes in white fire.

tagline.text: Pawna's Tears is the potion in Carl's Legendary Deity's Box, named for Pawna, the goddess of peace and Grull's sister and arch enemy. It adds five to any spell or skill its drinker chooses and can be saved, and Mordecai calls it the single best item of loot Carl has had.
Carl has spent Pawna's Tears on Donut, to bring her Laundry Day to fifteen against Circe Took. His sponsor says he will replace it.

description.text: Pawna's Tears. This potion adds plus five to any spell or skill of your choosing.

beats.headline: From the deity's box
beats.text: Surviving a physical attack by a god earns Carl the Indomitable achievement and a Legendary Deity's Box. In it is a potion in a rounded, ornate bottle, like expensive perfume, smoke rising from the glass. Mordecai's talon shakes as he holds it. Pawna, he explains, is the goddess of peace, Grull's sister and arch enemy. Don't take it now. Save it. It is valued above the Kimaris figure, and it can be saved, unlike a Cheat Code: Carl can train a skill to fifteen and take it to twenty.
beats.gist: Carl survives a god's attack, wins a potion raising a skill to twenty.

beats.headline: Or the other Pawna potion
beats.text: A benefactor box brings Pawna's Cries, plus three to a spell or skill, to be drunk before the floor ends. Carl still has Pawna's Tears, plus five with no time limit, and they are saving it. Then his Escape Plan reveals more words on the note: Circe sponsored Diwata, give the potion to Donut, fifteen is needed and should be kept secret, with a temporary boost from Prepotente, Imani and Samantha together. Or use the other Pawna potion if they have to. The sender will replace it.
beats.gist: Give Pawna's Tears to Donut, the note says; use Pawna's Cries only if forced.

beats.headline: Laundry Day at fifteen
beats.text: Diwata has manifested, and she looks exactly like her true identity, Circe Took, wearing the god as armor. Donut casts Laundry Day. She trained it every day for weeks, to nine, and Pawna's Cries made it twelve, but it needed fifteen, and Samantha could not be coaxed into a boost. So they used the backup: Carl's Pawna's Tears, a bit of a waste of the stronger potion, though his sponsor claims he will replace it. Circe Took stands stripped of her protection, sopping wet and covered in bubbles. She dies shrieking Carl's name.
beats.gist: Donut casts Laundry Day, boosted by Carl's Pawna's Tears, and Circe Took dies wet and shrieking.

recap.text: Carl survives a physical attack by a god and receives the Indomitable achievement and a Legendary Deity's Box. In it sits a potion in a rounded, ornate bottle like expensive perfume, smoke rising from the glass. Mordecai's talon shakes as he explains that Pawna is the goddess of peace, Grull's sister and arch enemy, and tells Carl to save it. Unlike a Cheat Code, it keeps: Carl can train a skill to fifteen and take it to twenty.

Carl holds Pawna's Tears, a plus-five potion with no time limit, when a box brings Pawna's Cries, a plus-three potion to drink before the floor ends. His Escape Plan reveals more words on the note: Circe sponsored Diwata, and Donut needs fifteen. Diwata manifests looking exactly like Circe Took. Donut casts Laundry Day at twelve, so Carl's Pawna's Tears covers the rest, and Circe Took dies sopping wet, covered in bubbles, shrieking his name.

entities.name: Scroll of Water Breathing
entities.role: Breathing underwater, a scroll at a time

tagline.text: A Scroll of Water Breathing lets a crawler breathe underwater for three seconds per point of intelligence. They turn up in box after box on this floor, which Mordecai reads as a hint about what the floor holds, and Donut announces that cats do not swim.
Water-breathing scrolls have to be chained one after another, and when one runs out, the water in a crawler's lungs comes back up.
A Water Breathing scroll grows gills, and in surgery Mordecai uses one to give Louis gills that stay.

description.text: Scroll of Water Breathing. Allows you to breathe underwater. Lasts as many seconds as your intelligence stat times three. It does not protect you from swimmer’s ear or being eaten by an undead barracuda. I hope you know how to swim.

beats.headline: Cats do not swim
beats.text: Among Donut's boss boxes is a scroll that fills Carl with dread: a Scroll of Water Breathing. I am a cat, Donut announces the moment she gets it; cats do not swim, cats do not go in water. Katia receives several more of the scrolls along with antidote potions, making them this floor's version of the torch and the bandage, and Carl gets a handful. Sometimes things like these scrolls are a not-so-subtle hint about what is on a level, Mordecai says.
beats.gist: Carl dreads the Scroll of Water Breathing in Donut's boss boxes, while Donut insists cats do not swim.

beats.headline: Eight scrolls
beats.text: With Donut afraid of being buried alive, Carl asks how many water-breathing scrolls she has. They're called water breathing, not sand breathing, she tells him. Eight. Then the water hits, and they are sinking in the water quadrant, Donut unconscious and bleeding. Thankfully she had taken the scroll: with her intelligence it lasts over two and a half minutes. Carl's lasts 54 seconds, and he is already close to needing another.
beats.gist: Carl's water-breathing scroll lasts 54 seconds; Donut's, thanks to her intelligence, lasts over two and a half minutes.

beats.headline: Brown water
beats.text: Carl pops a kayak from the flying house's garage onto the surface, lifts Donut in and paddles. His water-breathing scroll runs out, and he vomits dark, brown water he had not known was in his lungs; it feels like being kicked in the stomach while breathing fire. A moment after, Donut vomits too, far more water than seems possible. A bronze I'm Wet box, for more than sixty seconds fully submerged, brings ten more scrolls for each of them.
beats.gist: Carl paddles Donut in a kayak, vomits brown water when his scroll expires, and earns ten more scrolls.

beats.headline: Everyone take a scroll
beats.text: Lusca's babies are dead, but oxygen is running low and the AI complains they are just sitting there being boring. They have to go out there. Everyone take a scroll, Carl says, and takes theirs before he turns the portal and water flows in around the seal. When the boss lies dead on the ocean floor, he clicks another. Ashore, though out of the water, he takes one more to stave off the vomiting that would incapacitate him.
beats.gist: Carl has everyone take Water Breathing scrolls underwater, then takes more after the boss dies and ashore.

beats.headline: Gills that stay
beats.text: Louis's ribcage is held open while new organs go in, taken from the body of a full naiad, which has Carl worried she breathes only water. Mordecai sews a rebreather into the bronchial, then casts a Water Breathing scroll on Louis, the scroll version because Katia's potion cooldown is too long now. As the gills form, he connects tubes from the new organs to them, and Bucket Boy jams stops into the slits to keep them there after the water breathing ends. Louis coughs water from his neck. Bucket Boy pulls the stops out. The gills remain.
beats.gist: Louis gets gills: Mordecai sews in a rebreather, casts Water Breathing, and Bucket Boy props the slits open.

recap.text: Donut pulls a Scroll of Water Breathing from her boss boxes and announces that cats do not swim. When the water hits, she sinks unconscious and bleeding, and her scroll lasts over two and a half minutes to Carl's 54 seconds. Carl paddles her out in a kayak, vomits brown water when his scroll runs out, and a bronze I'm Wet box brings ten more scrolls each. Against Lusca, he takes a scroll before turning the portal.

Louis's ribcage is held open while new organs from a full naiad's body go in, and Carl worries she breathes only water. Mordecai sews a rebreather into the bronchial, then casts a Water Breathing scroll on Louis, since Katia's potion cooldown is too long now. He connects tubes from the organs to the forming gills, and Bucket Boy jams stops into the slits. Louis coughs water from his neck; Bucket Boy pulls the stops out, and the gills remain.

tagline.text: A Surefire is a crafting part the size of a bottle cap that gives any projectile the Guided status: an arrow, a bolt or a rocket seeks the target it is given. Carl has a case of twenty-five.
Surefires are what turn Carl's rockets into guided missiles. He had used ten when Ruckus's boss box sent a case of twenty-five more.
A launcher of twenty-five surefire missiles brings down a fleeing hunter, and Carl has used the last of the parts.
Out of the seeking-missile attachments for some time, Carl gets a group of surefires from a gold box and can build more missiles.

description.text: Surefire. Crafting item. A Surefire adds the “Guided” status to any projectile, powered or not. It may be utilized on a vast array of crafting tables. If added to an arrow or bolt, you must choose a target prior to unleashing the weapon, and the projectile will seek that target. If added to a trap, additional options become available. Such as “Target any healers within range” or “Target anyone who thinks it’s okay to put mayonnaise on hotdogs.” If added to a powered weapon, such as an explosive-based rocket, targets may be assigned during the crafting process or upon firing, but not both. Note: this upgrade alone does not add range to the projectile.

beats.headline: Twenty-five bottle caps
beats.text: Carl's gold sniper's box holds a crafting item: a case of twenty-five small black items, each about the size of a bottle cap. A Surefire adds the Guided status to any projectile, powered or not. On an arrow or a bolt, the target is chosen before the shot; on a trap, new options open up; on a rocket, targets are set while crafting or on firing, but not both. It adds no range. Cool, Carl says, and moves on to his platinum boxes.
beats.gist: Carl's gold box holds twenty-five bottle-cap-sized Surefires, which make any projectile guided, and he moves on.

beats.headline: Twenty-five more
beats.text: Alone with Donut in the crafting room, Carl opens the silver boss box from killing Ruckus. First comes a case of twenty-five more surefires, which is a relief. He has already used ten of the first ones to give his missiles the guided upgrade, and he was about to use the rest. This gives them some wiggle room, and he can alter the plan.
beats.gist: Carl finds twenty-five more surefires in the boss box, giving him room to change plans.

beats.headline: Locked on the escorts
beats.text: While the gnomes' balloon sat on the ground, Langley handed out targets, and the six archers plus Louis and Firas used the surefire aiming system to lock their missiles onto the circling escort planes and balloons. On Carl's order, eight rockets corkscrew up from the surface, each launcher tube carrying two, and four more blast into the air at the remaining planes before the first salvo even hits.
beats.gist: Langley hands out targets, and eight shooters lock surefire missiles onto the escort planes and balloons.

beats.headline: Five by five
beats.text: Carl sets a multi-launcher the size of a poker table against a hedge: twenty-five single-stage surefire missiles in a five-by-five grid, targets already programmed, on a remote trigger. When he clicks it, the first five streak after the fleeing hunter Xindy. The fourth is shot down early; the fifth hits as her shield fails, and she explodes. The rest spread off in different directions. His second rocket box holds only ten rockets, because he ran out of surefires, and is pre-set to kill the closest hunter-class mobs.
beats.gist: Carl fires twenty-five surefire missiles from one launcher; the fifth kills Xindy.

recap.text: Carl's gold box holds twenty-five black surefires, each the size of a bottle cap, and each adds the Guided status to any projectile. The silver box from killing Ruckus holds twenty-five more, which gives Carl room to alter his plan after he has already used ten on his missiles. Langley hands out targets, and on Carl's order eight rockets corkscrew up at the escort planes while four more blast into the air before the first salvo hits.

Xindy flees while Carl sets a multi-launcher the size of a poker table against a hedge, loaded with twenty-five surefire missiles in a five-by-five grid, targets programmed. He clicks the remote trigger. The first five streak after her; the fourth is shot down early, and the fifth hits as her shield fails, and she explodes. His second rocket box holds only ten rockets, because he ran out of surefires.

tagline.text: The Wall of Fire tome, from Donut's platinum box, teaches a fifteen-mana escape spell: a wall of flame ten metres wide and two high, for fifteen seconds at first level. Mordecai warns that fire spreads. Donut wanted Fireball.
Donut's Wall of Fire crackles bigger than ever, thanks to her new nipple ring.
Wall of Fire is one of the spells Donut's new cloak is raising to level 15 over the coming week, and Mordecai expects her to be a terror on the battlefield.
Powered up to level 16, Donut's Wall of Fire runs a mile along the road and a hundred feet into the air.

beats.headline: Another magic book
beats.text: Donut's final box, a platinum one, contains another magic book: a fifteen-mana spell called Wall of Fire. That's an escape spell, Mordecai says, a wall about ten metres wide and two metres high that lasts fifteen seconds at level one. It is common, and it grows powerful, but it is fire, and fire spreads: cast on something flammable, it stays on fire when the magic goes away. He has seen it a hundred times: fire gets out of control very easily. It's not Fireball, Donut grumbles. She glows as she reads the book.
beats.gist: Donut's last box holds Wall of Fire, a fifteen-mana escape spell Mordecai says spreads fire easily.

beats.headline: Burning gerbils
beats.text: After ten solid minutes of fighting, the gerbils keep coming, and Donut casts Wall of Fire just as the next wave shoots at the defensive line. That is a mistake. The little bastards launch themselves through the air, and passing through the magical fire they ignite, turning into miniature, gnashing fireballs. The fire kills them, but not before they attach to the chests of the camel defenders and set them alight. By now they have been pushed all the way back to the entrance of Weird Shit Alley.
beats.gist: Donut's Wall of Fire backfires: burning gerbils leap through it and set the camel defenders alight.

beats.headline: Inside Ghazi's room
beats.text: Katia cries Shell, and Carl flies back from the door and slams against the stairs. He hits Protective Shell just as Donut's Wall of Fire bursts up inside the room, and the door explodes. The fire catches the piles of books and tables at once. Ghazi runs into view, shouting, straight through the wall of the shell, trapped on their side of the flames. His dot is still white.
beats.gist: Katia's Protective Shell catches Carl as Donut's Wall of Fire blows out the door, trapping Ghazi.

beats.headline: Bigger than ever
beats.text: There are too many mobs, Anton cries, his crossbow making little monkey noises with every shot, while Sister Ines lobs her white balls one after another. Donut casts Wall of Fire, which crackles bigger than ever thanks to her new nipple ring, and a pair of clockwork Mongos appear and tear through the mobs. Carl tosses two infused smoke curtains, and a holy gooper clears the way to the saferoom.
beats.gist: Donut's bigger Wall of Fire summons clockwork Mongos, and Carl's smoke curtains clear the way.

beats.headline: A mile of flame
beats.text: Skulls are flooding the streets ahead of the truck, leaving a narrower and narrower path to the finish line. Donut leans forward and casts her level 15 Wall of Fire, powered up to level 16. A line of flames appears on the passenger's side, running parallel with the truck about thirty feet away, and races ahead far into the distance. The flames go straight up, easily a hundred feet into the air. The line has to be a mile long.
beats.gist: Donut casts Wall of Fire, and a mile-long line of flame rises beside the truck.

recap.text: Donut opens a platinum box and finds Wall of Fire, a fifteen-mana book that Mordecai warns keeps burning on anything flammable. She casts it against the gerbils, who fly through the wall, ignite, and set the camel defenders' chests alight. In Ghazi's room, her wall bursts up as Katia cries Shell, the door explodes, and the books catch, while Ghazi runs through the shell, trapped on their side of the flames, his dot still white.

Anton cries that there are too many mobs, his crossbow making little monkey noises with every shot, while Sister Ines lobs her white balls one after another. Donut casts Wall of Fire, which crackles bigger than ever thanks to her new nipple ring, and a pair of clockwork Mongos appear and tear through the mobs. Carl tosses two infused smoke curtains, and a holy gooper clears the way to the saferoom.

Donut leans forward and casts her level 15 Wall of Fire, powered up to level 16, as skulls flood the streets ahead of the truck and narrow the path to the finish line. A line of flames rises on the passenger's side, thirty feet away and parallel to the truck, then races far ahead. The flames climb straight up, easily a hundred feet, along a line that has to be a mile long.

tagline.text: The Gnomish Drop Bear is one of the dirigible gnomes' earliest fast-attack planes, an open-air, twin-engine biplane with famously underpowered engines and a quick-escape balloon. It does not drop bombs; its payload is something the System calls much more entertaining.
Carl now has a Drop Bear of his own, an abandoned biplane named Death Trap, which he sprays over and renames Nightmare II.

description.text: Gnomish Drop Bear. Contraption. This is one of the Dirigible Gnome's earliest fast-attack planes. There are only a handful of these still in service. While able to quickly reach most targets when drop-launched from home base, the twin engines of these early models were famously underpowered. Damaged Drop Bears oftentimes had difficulty obtaining enough altitude to reach home, even after ditching their payload. This is why most of these planes carry rapid-deploying, quick-escape balloons, making them sitting targets for enemy aircraft and flak. … Don't worry, these guys don't drop bombs. Their standard payload is something much more entertaining.

beats.headline: A buzzsaw overhead
beats.text: A plane rockets by a hundred feet over their heads, whining like a flying buzzsaw. It must have dropped from the Wasteland: an open-air biplane, an engine nestled between the wings on each side, a red-hatted gnome pilot and a second gnome facing backward. A screaming grey animal like a jacked-up rabid koala is painted on its nose, and two egg-shaped objects hang under it in small nets. Carl's smoke curtains do not hide them. As it lines up thirty feet off the ground, Donut teleports them away, and the object it drops where they stood clangs, bounces once, and does nothing.
beats.gist: Donut teleports them away from a gnome biplane's dropped egg-shaped object, which clangs, bounces once, and does nothing.

beats.headline: Smoke from one engine
beats.text: Carl's full-strength hob-lobber goes off in mid-air, much too low and behind the fast plane, but the biplane shudders and smoke trails from one of its two engines. It banks away and climbs, fleeing the fight. The metallic egg it dropped is the size of a garbage can, and nothing moves. Katia, watching the plane, sees it turning into a balloon; it has dropped the second bomb way over there, and that did not go off either. Their engine went out, says Carl; they are deploying their escape balloon.
beats.gist: Carl's hob-lobber misses low, but the biplane smokes, drops duds, and flees by balloon.

beats.headline: Death Trap, renamed
beats.text: Louis, Firas and Langley have secured an intact Drop Bear, its pilot nowhere to be found, and covered it with a tarp at the edge of the other town. It runs on actual gasoline, and Carl fills the tank only a quarter of the way to keep it light; there are no bombs left under the wings. It looks like something a drunk built in his backyard out of scrap metal. Wiping the dust off the nose shows the rabid koala and, stencilled in Syndicate standard, the plane's name: Death Trap, with four bombs painted after it. Carl sprays over it and writes Nightmare II on the side.
beats.gist: Louis, Firas and Langley secure an intact Drop Bear; Carl part-fills its tank and renames it Nightmare II.

recap.text: Katia, Carl and Donut watch a biplane rocket past a hundred feet overhead, a screaming rabid koala painted on its nose and two egg-shaped bombs slung beneath it. Donut teleports them away as it lines up, and the bomb clangs, bounces once and does nothing. Carl's hob-lobber goes off too low, but one engine smokes, and the plane climbs away under an escape balloon.

tagline.text: Rapid Detox clears its drinker of alcohol and most drugs, and for a single floor makes them violently ill if they drink. Mordecai gives it to Louis and Firas disguised, so neither can read what it is.

beats.headline: Sobered by force
beats.text: Mordecai hands each of the two men a white potion with a blank description. Louis downs his and is soon not drunk anymore, though he still feels sick. Firas is suspicious and asks why there is no description, but drinks. Soon both are on their hands and knees, scream-vomiting for minutes. It's called Rapid Detox, Mordecai tells Carl: it clears alcohol and most drugs, used to treat alcoholism and to torture prisoners. Sage beetle ichor hid the description. Louis gets a notification that he can't drink anymore.
beats.gist: Louis and Firas drink Mordecai's blank-label Rapid Detox potion, scream-vomit for minutes, and Louis can no longer drink.

relations.note: disguised with sage beetle ichor

recap.text: Mordecai hands Louis and Firas each a white potion with a blank description. Louis drinks his and sobers up, though he still feels sick, while Firas asks why there is no description before he drinks. Both drop to their hands and knees, scream-vomiting for minutes. Mordecai tells Carl the potion is Rapid Detox, which clears alcohol and most drugs and is used to treat alcoholism and to torture prisoners.

aka.name: Veriluxx RealPet Dungeon Crawl Special Edition Exclusive

tagline.text: Veriluxx RealPet Companions is Donut's new sponsor, and its first benefactor box is a product sample she is to play with on camera before she, Carl and Mongo go on a program about it.
The product is a toy robot Donut, three-quarters her size, with fur like rat hair, bootleg Garfield lines and a creepy streak. Donut is thrilled to have merch. Mongo bites its head off.
The newest robot Donut is three times heavier and survives Mongo, but a cheap tab holds shut a panel at the back of its head, and opening it starts a five-second self-destruct warning.
Loita is dead, blown up by the last robot Donut, and Carl had made sure its panel would fall off.

description.text: Veriluxx RealPet Dungeon Crawl Special Edition Exclusive. “Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk.” Dungeon Crawler World: Earth. The ultimate play toy, Veriluxx RealPet Companions are budget-friendly, nearly indestructible collectibles that will give your child hours and hours of fun. Because these interactive toys do not require an implant certificate to play with and enjoy, parents needn’t worry about how many hours their children are spending with their new best friends! Mix and match! They fight! They love! They will share your deepest, darkest secrets! Each Veriluxx RealPet Companion is a fully licensed depiction of your favorite personality or creature. …

beats.headline: A product sample
beats.text: Donut hops up and down on Mongo: she has a new sponsor, Veriluxx RealPet Companions, and wonders who that is. Loita explains that Donut will soon receive a benefactor box from them that is really a product sample, part of the sponsorship contract. She is to take it out and interact with it a few times. Carl may make some of his famous comments, but should not disparage it too much if Donut wants a real box. In six or seven days, the two of them and Mongo go on a program to discuss the product.
beats.gist: Donut gets a new sponsor, Veriluxx RealPet Companions, whose box is a product sample.

beats.headline: It is Donut
beats.text: The box opens, and it is Donut: a toy robot Donut, about three-quarters her size, fur like rat hair, licking its paw in a stilted, mechanical way. I sure do like lasagna, it says. I hate Mondays, Carl. A 1980s commercial voice reads its description. It asks for Ferdinand, sends Ruby running, and tells Carl the void is wet and hungry. Donut is overjoyed: she has merch. Then the toy asks Mongo if he is a cocker spaniel and hisses, and Mongo decapitates it. It catches fire, and the cleaner bot foams it.
beats.gist: The box opens on a toy robot Donut that quotes lasagna until Mongo decapitates it and it burns.

beats.headline: Three more, all broken
beats.text: The toy company has sent three more robot Donuts, and Mongo has promptly destroyed two. The third, supposedly more durable, has survived one attack. It jumps onto Carl's shoulder, wondering how long the babies will continue to cry in the dark, until he pushes it off and Mongo shakes it by the neck. The head rips, a countdown appears, and it explodes in sparks and smoke, scorching the front of the Spit and Swallow. Its marble-sized controller core has popped like popcorn. Loita says the sponsor now has to make the doll self-destruct if it is sufficiently broken, to keep Carl out of its parts.
beats.gist: Mongo destroys the third and sturdier robot Donut by shaking it by the neck, and it explodes.

beats.headline: Three times the weight
beats.text: The newest version weighs about three times as much as the last and is slightly bigger. Mongo attacks it at once and does no obvious damage. It still throws out bootleg Garfield quotes. A small panel on the back of its head is held shut by a cheap little tab, like a battery compartment; when Carl clicks it open, a warning gives five seconds until self-destruct, and he shoves it back. Patted on the head, it moans. Mordecai says the logo on the box suggests Veriluxx is associated with Veritan Linkage, a lending fund that advocates enslaving those who can't pay their taxes.
beats.gist: Donut's sponsor's newest Veriluxx toy is heavier and bigger, and Carl nearly sets off its self-destruct.

beats.headline: Left beside Loita
beats.text: Carl sets robot Donut on the green-room couch next to Loita and tells it to stay by her. It asks her if she has ever felt true cold. On the set of the Veriluxx New Toys Showcase, holo dolls of Donut and Mongo bounce on the table, and Carl goes off script: he likes how compliant the toy is, and isn't compliance the thing of their parent company, Veritan Linkage? Then the lights flicker and the studio goes red. In the green room the couch is obliterated, and Loita lies blackened, missing her left arm and both bottom legs, still alive.
beats.gist: Carl leaves robot Donut beside Loita, then the studio goes red and Loita is blackened.

beats.headline: The panel falls off
beats.text: Orren lays it out. Loita jumped down off the couch, the toy jumped after her, the panel on the back of its head dislodged, and a few seconds after that it exploded, killing her. Sitting on Carl's sapper's bench had raised its yield. Carl calls the panel a cheap piece of crap. What he does not say is that he shimmed the tab with a cut-down thumbnail as he set the toy beside her, knowing the heavy robot would jump the moment she stood up.
beats.gist: Orren explains that the toy jumped after Loita, its panel came loose, and it exploded, killing her.

relations.note: the explosion that killed her

recap.text: Veriluxx sends Donut a toy robot Donut, and Mongo decapitates it after it asks if he is a cocker spaniel. The third replacement explodes and scorches the Spit and Swallow, so the sponsor makes the dolls self-destruct. Carl shims the panel tab on the heavier model's head with a cut-down thumbnail and sets it beside Loita on the couch. It jumps after her when she stands, the panel falls off, and the blast kills her.

entities.name: Mairmei Mushroom
entities.role: An alchemy material, and a drug

tagline.text: Mairmei Mushroom is an alchemy material, and all its description says is that these little guys are quite the trip. Carl took a batch from the town hall in Hump Town, and Mordecai has never seen the strain before.
The camels have been feeding a mushroom to their gnome prisoner to keep him compliant, and eaten raw, Mordecai says, the mushrooms help get people to do what you want, if not reliably.

description.text: Mairmei Mushroom – Alchemy Material. These little guys are quite the trip.

beats.headline: Quite the trip
beats.text: Back at base, Carl hands Mordecai the batch of mushrooms he took from the desk in the basement. Mordecai frowns. The system calls them Mairmei Mushroom, alchemy material, and all the description says is that these little guys are quite the trip. Carl assumes a psychedelic; the cookbook has very little on mushrooms. Mordecai is intrigued, because he has never seen this strain, and Carl gives him the batch to study before they open the benefactor boxes.
beats.gist: Carl gives Mordecai the basement mushrooms, a strain he has never seen, to study.

beats.headline: A tolerance for the mushroom
beats.text: The camel who calls himself Henrik explains the collateral that keeps the gnomes from bombing Hump Town: Wynne cooperated for years, until he was moved to the chamber below the town hall and understood his situation had changed. Since then they have had to drug him to force compliance, and it is getting harder. He has grown a tolerance for the mushroom, and they must feed him more every day. Mordecai has not yet worked out what the mushrooms do, but eaten raw they apparently help get people to do what you want. The mind control is not very reliable, but it has worked well enough here.
beats.gist: The camel Henrik says the gnomes drug Wynne with the mushroom, and he now needs more daily.

relations.note: Carl gives him the batch to study
the camels drug him with the mushroom

recap.text: Back at base, Carl hands Mordecai the mushrooms he took from the desk in the basement. The system calls them Mairmei Mushroom, an alchemy material that is quite the trip, and Mordecai, who has never seen the strain, takes the batch to study. The camel Henrik says the gnomes drug Wynne, who has grown a tolerance and must be fed more every day. Raw, the mushrooms apparently make people do what you want, unreliably.

tagline.text: The Toraline Root Vegetable is a rare tuber that grows only in dirt once covered by lava, and by the System's account it tastes like dogshit. It came in a silver benefactor box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, and nobody, Mordecai included, knows what it is for.

Mordecai, with Samantha's help, has worked out the toraline's uses: a special ink for scrolls, or lava-themed potions at about an eighth of the yam each. One of them, a phase potion, has got Maggie out of Chris's head.
More than half of the toraline is gone, and the sponsors who sent it have sent a note: Save the toraline.
A sliver of the toraline, brewed in a beaker by Shi Maria with Carl's own hands, has become the black ink of a tattoo on his chest. Mordecai still has the biggest piece.
Toraline ink mixed with Carl's blood makes a permanent tattoo that lends a spell to someone else, and the yam potion renews it. There is barely any of the vegetable left.
With some ink tips from Milk, Rosetta says, they no longer need the toraline to do what they need.

description.text: Toraline Root Vegetable. Alchemy Material. This rare tuber only grows in dirt that has been covered by lava. They are very rare. Nobody ever goes digging them up, either. You know why? Because they taste like dogshit, that's why. They're pretty much useless. In fact, fuck you for wasting my time with this.

beats.headline: Thanks for the yam
beats.text: Carl hands Mordecai a batch of Mairmei Mushroom from a desk in the basement. Then the boxes. After the Valtay pill comes the silver box from the anti-crawl group, a spiral galaxy symbol on it, and inside is what looks like a sweet potato. Mordecai has never seen one. He has seen potions that need something similar, mostly salves for scaled creatures, or it might be a traditional marriage proposal. Carl tosses it into his inventory. Thanks for the yam, mystery aliens.
beats.gist: Carl hands Mordecai mushrooms, then opens a silver box holding a sweet potato-like yam that Mordecai cannot identify.

beats.headline: An eighth a potion
beats.text: Thanks to Samantha's help, Mordecai has figured out the yam thing, and he wants Carl back at the saferoom: he has a potion for him. While the rest of the plan waits, Mordecai is in the crafting room working on the second potion made from it. Each one takes only about an eighth of the vegetable, and Carl tells him they had better have at least three, one each for him, Katia and Donut.
beats.gist: Mordecai brews yam potions, an eighth of the yam each, and Carl wants three.

beats.headline: Grown in lava
beats.text: Carl tells the hidden Chris, and Maggie inside him, what the yam is. It grows in lava or magma, and it makes either a special ink for scrolls or a few lava-themed potions: a healing scroll for lava rock monsters like Chris, or a phase potion to pass through lava rock. Mordecai made the phase potion. When Chris erupts from the sand beside the winding box, Carl drinks it, and as Chris hurls the box away, Carl reaches into his head for the worm lodged in his brain.
beats.gist: Carl tells Chris the yam grows in lava, then drinks Mordecai's phase potion and reaches into Chris's head.

beats.headline: Wasted half of it
beats.text: A woman asks Dr. Hu how much they have spent, and he says it is best she does not know. She lists the dangers: Carl is unstable, he could die at any moment, and he is not nearly as clever as Hu thinks. You should have included instructions with the yam, she says. They wasted half of it on saving that other crawler. He knows what it's really for, says Dr. Hu. Does he? She is not so sure.
beats.gist: A woman tells Dr. Hu the yam's cost, Carl's instability, and the half they wasted saving another crawler.

beats.headline: Save the toraline
beats.text: A benefactor box brings a Pawna's Cries potion and, unusually, a note. It says simply: Save the toraline. More than half of it is already gone, into the potion that let Carl pull Maggie out of Chris's brain. Save it for what, Carl asks, and why won't they just spit it out? Notes are expensive, says Mordecai: they are paid by the character, and the rules force the sender to be cryptic. Then Carl's Escape Plan skill buzzes, and more words appear on the page.
beats.gist: A benefactor's note says to save the toraline, but over half is already gone.

beats.headline: Potatoes and milk
beats.text: On Shadow Boxer, a photo on the roundabout shows Carl chopping potatoes beside a jug marked Milk, a photo that cannot exist: they never let him near that kitchen except to clean it, the jug is shaped like a two-litre soda bottle, and the camera would be standing in a wall. His stew was milk and potatoes, he says. Potatoes are very versatile. Very, Rosetta agrees, and vanishes mid-sentence: Harbinger has stopped the interview. Carl remembers a rant of Milk's in the cookbook, and a reply he is fairly sure was Rosetta's. Just like all root vegetables. The toraline.
beats.gist: Carl finds an impossible photo of himself chopping potatoes, and Rosetta vanishes when Harbinger stops the interview.

beats.headline: Ink in a beaker
beats.text: Shi Maria has Carl's body. Going through his inventory she finds a potion and wants to know what he made it with, and then an empty beaker he looted on the first floor is in his hands, a small sliver of the toraline inside it. Mordecai still has the biggest piece. She casts Self-Immolation, which burns through the floor beneath him, and once he has dropped into the apartment below, the hot beaker holds a little bubbling black ink. She unequips his shirt and takes out the stick-and-poke tattoo kit, jabs its stick into Li Jun's eye when he comes close, then dips it in the beaker and pokes the ink rapidly into Carl's chest.
beats.gist: Shi Maria, in Carl's body, burns through the floor and turns toraline into ink for a chest tattoo.

beats.headline: A finger-sized slice
beats.text: Rosetta, in person, puts an icy hand on the Bedlam Bride tattoo and asks how much Carl has left. Of what? The toraline, she says, and the ink the spider used to make that tattoo. Over chat she warns him to say nothing out loud. He hands over all he has, a finger-sized slice, and the still-hot glass of the ink Shi Maria brewed, a few thimblefuls left. Mordecai has more of the toraline, he says, but not much. Give me access to your saferoom, she says, and we will get to work.
beats.gist: Rosetta takes Carl's last toraline and the ink left from Shi Maria's brew.

recap.text: Carl tosses the yam from the anti-crawl group's silver box into his inventory. Mordecai, with Samantha's help, works out that it grows in lava and yields potions at an eighth of the vegetable apiece. Carl drinks Mordecai's phase potion as Chris erupts from the sand, then reaches into Chris's head for the worm in his brain. A woman tells Dr. Hu that half the yam was wasted on saving that other crawler.

A benefactor box brings a Pawna's Cries potion and a note: Save the toraline. More than half of it is already gone, into the potion that let Carl pull Maggie out of Chris's brain. Carl asks save it for what, and why the sender won't say; Mordecai answers that notes are paid by the character, and the rules force the sender to be cryptic. Then Carl's Escape Plan skill buzzes, and more words appear on the page.

Carl watches a photo on Shadow Boxer's roundabout show him chopping potatoes beside a jug marked Milk, though no one let him near that kitchen except to clean it. Shi Maria, in Carl's body, burns through the floor with Self-Immolation, then jabs the tattoo kit's stick into Li Jun's eye. She dips it in the beaker holding a sliver of toraline, now black ink, and pokes it rapidly into Carl's chest.

Rosetta lays an icy hand on Carl's Bedlam Bride tattoo and asks how much toraline and spider ink he has left. Over chat she warns him to say nothing aloud. He hands over a finger-sized slice and a few thimblefuls of the still-hot ink Shi Maria brewed. Mordecai has more toraline, he says, but not much. Rosetta asks for access to his saferoom so they can get to work.

tagline.text: The Valtay Corporation's Neural Enhancer #275 is the second pill the brain-parasite corporation has sent Carl. Swallowed, it adds his current elevation and airspeed to his interface, permanently.

description.text: Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #275. Variant 35.j This item is compatible with your Morphology and Interface. Warning: This pill will cause a permanent change to your brain. This item cannot be unequipped or undone once installed. Warning: You do not have a Valtay Corporation Neural Interface installed. While your current wetware system is compatible with this Neural Enhancer, it is recommended you visit a Valtay Corporate Outreach Center to discuss upgrade options. Payment and Legacy plans available. Keeping the Best of You alive. Current wetware: Syndicate Crawl Version 47.002b.Human. Taking this pill will install the following upgrade to your interface: Current elevation and airspeed.

beats.headline: Thanks, brain worm dudes
beats.text: The bronze Valtay box whirls open with great fanfare on another pill, identical to the last. This one installs a single upgrade: current elevation and airspeed. That's it? Carl thinks, and does not dare say it, then remembers how damn useful the last upgrade was. He pops it and thanks the brain worm dudes. The settings are a mess of velocities until he finds Relative Surface Speed, and the elevation display fills his screen with numbers until he picks kilometres and meters. Trying Planetary Sea-level Only is a mistake.
beats.gist: Carl pops a Valtay pill that installs an elevation and airspeed display.

beats.headline: Eyes on the indicators
beats.text: In the gnomes' balloon basket Carl keeps his eye on the altitude indicator: almost three hundred meters, close to a thousand feet up, the escorts well below. When the three of them leap from the basket and the world to the north explodes, he tumbles with no point of reference, ignores the spinning world outside and fixes on the altitude and speed indicators in his vision. Donut cannot remember when to drink her potion. Now, he tells her. The potion is Dolores Doesn't Splat, and it only works if they are falling faster than two hundred kilometres an hour when they drink it.
beats.gist: Carl fixes on his altitude and speed indicators while tumbling, then tells Donut when to drink.

recap.text: A bronze Valtay box opens on a pill that adds an altitude and speed display, and Carl pops it, thanking the brain worm dudes. He picks Relative Surface Speed and kilometres and meters; Planetary Sea-level Only is a mistake. Leaping from the gnomes' balloon basket almost three hundred meters up, he tumbles, ignores the spinning world, and watches the indicators until he tells Donut to drink Dolores Doesn't Splat, which works only above two hundred kilometres an hour.

tagline.text: Ruckus, the giant cyborg buzz-ard, carries a twenty-five-foot stick of ten spinning buzzsaws, each blade the size of a truck tire, hung under her on a pair of thick cables.
Ruckus is dead and her buzzsaw is in Katia's inventory. It runs on the same dwarfish battery as the Chariot, seems to work without the bird, and is lighter than it looks.
The buzzsaw is gone, broken apart on the ocean floor after it cut through Lusca's head.

beats.headline: Ten blades on a stick
beats.text: Through the telescope, Ruckus is a colossal hawk in steampunk armour, and her weapon sits on the ground beside her: not the chainsaw-like device the regular buzz-ards carry, but a twenty-five-foot stick with ten spinning buzzsaws, attached by a pair of thick cables she can lengthen and retract. In the fight it swings under her like a pendulum. When three rockets blow her wing off, she spins and wraps herself in its cable; the saw pinwheels after her, bounces free and sticks itself sideways into the rock of the tomb, still cutting.
beats.gist: Ruckus swings a ten-saw stick on cables until rockets blow off her wing.

beats.headline: Into Katia's inventory
beats.text: They loot everything they can from the wreckage, almost a ton of dwarfish aluminum included. The giant buzzsaw is powered by the same type of dwarfish battery that runs the Chariot; Carl pulls the battery, and the whole thing shuts off. A cable joined the saw to the bird, but the weapon seems to work whether it is attached or not. It is lighter than it looks, and Katia manages to pull it all into her inventory.
beats.gist: Katia pulls the battery from the giant buzzsaw, shutting it off, and stores the weapon in her inventory.

beats.headline: Leatherface
beats.text: Inside Lusca's mouth, Carl calls the plan they made for the flying house: Leatherface, the saw dropped on a chain and swung as a melee weapon. His Protective Shell stops the boss dead. Katia fires the rocket and pulls the activated buzzsaw from her inventory, holding onto its back. They pinwheel out of the mouth and back, and the screaming saw cuts through Lusca's upturned snout like a hot knife through calamari, until a tentacle slams them down and it buries itself in the ocean floor. They have cleaved her brain.
beats.gist: Katia and Carl swing the buzzsaw out of Lusca's mouth and cleave her brain.

beats.headline: Broken on the seabed
beats.text: Lusca floats on her side on the ocean floor, a jagged red line along the top of her. Behind Carl, the buzzsaw is buried all the way into the seabed. It makes a strangled noise, and the whole thing breaks apart, pieces flying every which way. One of the round blades dislodges and shoots off through the water, spinning into the darkness like a tire off a crashed car.
beats.gist: Ruckus's buzzsaw, buried in the seabed behind Carl, shatters, and one blade spins away into the dark.

recap.text: Ruckus, a colossal hawk in steampunk armour, swings a twenty-five-foot stick of ten spinning buzzsaws on two cables until three rockets blow her wing off and the saw sticks in the tomb rock. Carl pulls its dwarfish battery, and Katia pulls it into her inventory. Inside Lusca's mouth, they swing it as Leatherface and cleave her brain, then it buries itself in the seabed and breaks apart, one blade spinning off like a tire.

tagline.text: Carl wants a parachute in a hurry, and Feather Fall is a potion for it, but Mordecai has none of the materials: the seed pods it needs, he says, are scarce until the sixth floor.
Carl buys a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions at the Masquerade's prize counter, because Eva's thievery has left the group seven fall-protection potions short.
Carl hands out Feather Fall potions once the escape plan is live, and when the last five seconds come he drinks one himself rather than trust his nipple ring.

beats.headline: No seed pods
beats.text: Carl asks Mordecai what his options are if he needs a parachute quickly. One of a few dozen potions, a flight ability or a fall shield buff, says Mordecai, or turn Katia into a hang glider. He checks his stock. He does not have the Feather Fall materials: the seed pods he needs are scarce until the sixth floor, and the same goes for Bubble Boy. He has enough for one other kind of potion, maybe two of them, and Carl will not like it.
beats.gist: Mordecai lacks the seed pods for Feather Fall, so Carl's parachute options shrink to potions he won't like.

beats.headline: Not the real thing
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia each receive the same Silver Skydiver's Box, and each holds the same thing: three potions of Half Splat. Mordecai tells them to keep those in their hotlists until they can get a real Feather Fall. Half Splat keeps you from dying of falling damage, but you hit the ground at five percent health. Carl grumbles that they are still better than that Dolores Doesn't Splat potion.
beats.gist: Carl, Donut and Katia each get three Half Splat potions, which leave you at five percent health.

beats.headline: Twenty-four for the castle
beats.text: Katia has done a full circuit of the group and worked out that they are seven fall-protection potions short, thanks to Eva's thievery. Nobody is certain the potions will even be necessary. At the prize counter Carl wanted a skill upgrade for himself, but he is one hand short if he also refills the potion supply. So he takes a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions, with the shrink wand, the lore book, the Skedaddle sheet music and a case of healing potions.
beats.gist: Short seven potions, Carl takes a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions.

beats.headline: Still in a prize box
beats.text: The talent show is under way. Carl tells Donut not to wait for them: get out the moment the seal is broken, and they will try to jump on stage and follow; if that does not work, Escape Plan D. He bought Feather Fall potions, and he will hand them out. Donut points out that he does not have them: they are in a prize box, and there will be no time. Others need them, says Carl. He will hand them out as soon as Samantha turns off the inventory and magic block.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut to escape once the seal breaks; he will hand out Feather Fall potions.

beats.headline: Five seconds, then potions
beats.text: The Recital quest completes, and the Sledge sends his last message: five seconds, good-bye. All around them is blood and carnage and death. Potions, Carl shouts. He has his nipple ring's fall ability, but he does not trust it, and drinks a Feather Fall potion. He got the potions out of their prize box, along with a bunch of other things, standing on Prepotente's personal saferoom cube, the last zap of the goat's wand, in exchange for letting Prepotente take over the party for a day or so.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a Feather Fall potion rather than trust his nipple ring's fall ability.

recap.text: Asked for a quick parachute, Mordecai offers a flight ability, a fall shield buff or turning Katia into a hang glider, but he has no seed pods for Feather Fall, which are scarce until the sixth floor. Carl, Donut and Katia each open a Silver Skydiver's Box holding three potions of Half Splat. Half Splat stops a fall from killing you but leaves you at five percent health. Carl grumbles that it still beats Dolores Doesn't Splat.

Katia counts the group seven fall-protection potions short, thanks to Eva's thievery, so Carl takes a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions at the prize counter, one hand short of the skill upgrade he wanted. Donut points out the potions sit in a prize box. After the Sledge's five-second message, Carl shouts for potions and drinks one, distrusting his nipple ring's fall ability.

entities.name: Enchanted Roll of Never-ending Duct Tape

tagline.text: Carl asked the viewers for duct tape, and a silver fan box has sent him the universe's greatest: fifty metres of extra-durable fabric tape that grows back at a metre an hour until the roll is full again.
The duct tape has bound a gnome prisoner, sealed a bomb into a submarine's minifridge and patched a flying house's net of ropes, and Louis has just used up the whole roll.

description.text: Enchanted Roll of Never-ending Duct Tape. Fifty meters. Odds are good you know who Ted Bundy is. Odds are even better you don't know who Vesta Stoudt is. And while this problem is not exclusive to you hairless monkeys and your pollution-ridden world, those first two statements are part of the reason why you have received this prize. Will you use it to tie people up? Will you use it to save the lives of those you love? Will you wrap your ankles together and sensuously rub your supple feet up and down a dungeon wall while you run your hands through your hair? Who knows! …

beats.headline: Finally, the tape
beats.text: Alone with Donut in the crafting room before the raid, Carl opens his two new boxes. The silver boss box for killing Ruckus holds twenty-five more surefires and a bottle of Jellyfish Salve. Then the silver fan box from the end of the last floor. Yes, he says. Finally. Thanks, guys. It is a thick, enchanted roll of duct tape, fifty metres that grow back, and he already has a use in mind. He takes it to his sapper's table.
beats.gist: Carl opens his silver fan box and finds a never-ending roll of enchanted duct tape.

beats.headline: Better than rope
beats.text: With about forty-five minutes left, the raid leaves Hump Town by the main gate, and on the Chariot's raised back seat sits the struggling form of Wynne the dirigible gnome. Carl had planned to tie him with rope, but duct tape works much better. In front of the landed gnomes Carl pours a vial of Mountain Dew down "Wynne's" throat, then throws the duct-taped form over his shoulder and trudges toward their wicker basket, praying none of the gnomes notice that the back seat of the Chariot is gone, or that Wynne is about two feet longer than he should be.
beats.gist: Carl duct-tapes Wynne, pours Mountain Dew down his throat, and carries him past the gnomes.

beats.headline: Katia under the tape
beats.text: Under the duct tape, "Wynne" is mostly Katia. She is shaped as the whole back seat of the Chariot, which Carl had to remove for this to work, and as the body of the gnome sitting on it, her real eyes in among the tape for a wide, raised view of the situation. She is Henrik's body in the cart behind as well. The bulk of the plan rests, once again, on Donut's charm bonus and Katia's shapeshifting.
beats.gist: Under the tape, "Wynne" is mostly Katia, shaped as the Chariot's back seat and two bodies.

beats.headline: Taped into the minifridge
beats.text: On the submarine's bridge the commentators expect the rest of the depth charges to be duds, and the display window looks about to break. Carl yanks the fuse from a hob-lobber, replaces it with hobgoblin pus, and tapes a potion bottle to the bomb with his duct tape, a crude cousin of something more elegant in the cookbook. He has no idea whether it will work. He looks for a place safe from the first rush of water, puts the bomb in the bolted-down minifridge beside the captain's chair, and duct-tapes the door closed.
beats.gist: Carl tapes a potion bottle to a hob-lobber rigged with hobgoblin pus and seals it in a minifridge.

beats.headline: Mending the net
beats.text: On the roof of the flying house, with the wind picking up, Louis is desperately mending the net of ropes, and the patch is not going to hold for long. He tosses the empty roll of magical duct tape back down to Carl, so high that Carl has to jump for it. He catches it. Barely. He would have throttled Louis if it had gone over the edge, and he puts the roll back in his inventory to regenerate.
beats.gist: Louis tosses the empty duct tape roll to Carl, who barely catches it and stores it to regenerate.

beats.headline: A rocket on Samantha's head
beats.text: Samantha's head sits on the ground with her jaw held all the way open, like she is getting a root canal, and a rocket tied to the side of it with duct tape wrapped round her forehead and her neck. This is one of the few things Carl could not test in his workshop. He pulls out his xistera extension and tells her not to close her mouth until she sees them or the catapult. Okay, says Samantha. Click. The missile launches her into the air like a bottle rocket.
beats.gist: Samantha's head lies with her jaw held open while a duct-taped rocket launches her upward.

recap.text: Carl opens the silver fan box and finds a thick roll of enchanted duct tape, fifty metres that grow back. He wraps it over Katia, who is shaped as Wynne the gnome and the Chariot's missing back seat, then tapes a potion bottle to a hob-lobber bomb and duct-tapes it inside the submarine's minifridge. On the flying house's roof, Louis tosses the empty roll down, and Carl jumps and catches it, barely.

Samantha's head sits on the ground with her jaw held wide open, like she is at a root canal, and a rocket is tied to it with duct tape wrapped round her forehead and her neck. Carl could not test this in his workshop. He pulls out his xistera extension and tells her not to close her mouth until she sees them or the catapult. She says okay, he clicks, and the missile launches her like a bottle rocket.

entities.name: Jellyfish Salve
entities.role: For a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting

tagline.text: Jellyfish Salve comes in what Donut calls a lotion bottle, five applications, and takes the pain out of a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting, though not the minute of blocked healing. It came out of Carl's silver boss box for killing Ruckus.
Carl has given Katia some of the Jellyfish Salve, and he tells her to keep it in her hotlist outside the Akula.

description.text: Jellyfish Salve (5 applications) If you can’t talk someone into peeing on you after you get stung by a Pain Amplifier Jelly, then this will do the trick. Effect: removes the pain portion of the Kill Me Now It Hurts debuff. Warning: It does not remove the one-minute healing block effect associated with the Jelly’s sting.

beats.headline: A lotion bottle
beats.text: Alone with Donut in the crafting room, Carl opens his two new boxes. The silver boss box for killing Ruckus the chicken hawk holds a case of twenty-five more surefires and a second, more worrying item. It's a lotion bottle, says Donut, who got the same prize, just like the one he used to keep hidden by the bed. Jellyfish Salve, five applications, for the pain of a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting, though not its one-minute healing block. Carl really hopes they won't have to deal with the water quadrant.
beats.gist: Carl's boss box holds Jellyfish Salve: five applications for a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting.

beats.headline: Keep it on the hotlist
beats.text: Over the Akula, Katia sees big blue jellyfish near the entrance. Vadim tells her to watch for the white ones, the pain amplifiers, which are smaller; the big blue ones only wrap round you if you get close. She lands, and Carl puts his hand on her now-silver edge. We're going in, he says. Be safe. Keep that salve I gave you in your hotlist. In and out, she answers.
beats.gist: Katia lands; Carl touches her silver edge and tells her to keep his salve in her hotlist.

relations.note: her box held the same prize
Carl gave her some

recap.text: Carl opens the silver boss box for killing Ruckus the chicken hawk and finds twenty-five more surefires and a lotion bottle. Donut, who got the same prize, says it looks like the one Carl used to hide by the bed. The Jellyfish Salve, five applications, eases a Pain Amplifier Jelly's sting but not its one-minute healing block. Over the Akula, Carl tells Katia to keep it in her hotlist.

tagline.text: The Vahana is a Gnomish Legate Balloon, perhaps the oldest vehicle left aboard the Wasteland, black and gold striped from the days when such balloons meant ambassadors and perhaps peace. It brings the gnomes' negotiator down to the sand.
Carl hijacks the Vahana with Donut and Katia and fires his missiles at the Wasteland from its basket. All three jump as the airship's gun battery smashes into it.

description.text: Gnomish Legate Balloon. The Vahana. Contraption. Of all the vehicles left aboard the dreadnaught Wasteland, the Vahana is perhaps the oldest. Once, long ago, the gnomes believed they could avoid war. And while they could not leave this conflict-infested world, they could take to the skies, out of reach of everyone else. They hoped they could set themselves up as neutral peacekeepers. Everyone knew that the black and gold-striped balloons were off limits. The balloons were a symbol of hope. The sight of a Gnomish Legate on the horizon heralded the arrival of ambassadors, and perhaps peace. But when new visitors came to their world, coming via a mysterious portal, everything changed. …

beats.headline: Black and gold stripes
beats.text: Thirteen vehicles drop from the Wasteland and circle downward, bombs and rockets on their undersides. In the middle of the formation, a single traditional hot-air balloon keeps descending, black and gold striped and covered in ribbons and small flags, decorated for a parade rather than a war, a shield shimmering round it. Three gnomes look over the edge of its basket: an aerostat pilot, a negotiator and a sniper captain. It crunches into the sand, and Carl reads its properties. The Vahana, a Gnomish Legate Balloon.
beats.gist: Black-and-gold parade balloon descends among thirteen bomb-laden vehicles, carrying three gnomes, and crunches into the sand.

beats.headline: A hole in the basket
beats.text: Carl climbs into the Vahana's wicker basket with Katia, shaped as the stricken gnome Wynne, and Donut, and watches the pilot to memorise the controls as it rises toward the Wasteland. When Langley's rockets go up at the escorts, the sniper Crixus turns them all red. Katia anchors herself with two spikes through the wicker, and Donut casts Hole under the floor. All three gnomes drop through it; Leon catches the edge of the hole and is knocked off by a magical cat paw. After a fight with three rising balloons, Carl moves to the controls.
beats.gist: Carl, Katia and Donut climb into the Vahana, and Donut's Hole spell drops them through its floor.

beats.headline: Abandoned under fire
beats.text: Carl yanks the pull for the fire source and they jerk upward, pushing 500 metres; a farseer is already fixed to the fire controls. A battery on the Wasteland rotates toward the hijacked balloon. He rests a multi-launcher on the basket's edge and fires four missiles, spins the sidewheel, and catches the round balls on Protective Shell. Then he launches the second four and yells jump. All three leap from the wicker basket just as dozens of round balls smash into it.
beats.gist: Carl hijacks the Vahana, fires missiles at a battery's round balls, and all three jump.

recap.text: Carl climbs into the black and gold striped Vahana with Katia, shaped as the gnome Wynne, and Donut, and watches the pilot to memorise the controls. Donut casts Hole under the floor, and all three gnomes drop through it. Carl yanks the fire pull, fires eight missiles from a multi-launcher, and catches the round balls on Protective Shell. He yells jump, and all three leap before dozens of round balls smash the basket.

tagline.text: Dolores Doesn't Splat is a potion for anyone falling faster than two hundred kilometers an hour. It speeds the fall, softens the ground at impact, and slams the drinker into it five times in a row.
Dolores Doesn't Splat is no pleasure, but Mordecai calls it genius: Carl's health was still at a hundred percent when he landed.

beats.headline: Five landings in a row
beats.text: Carl, Katia and Donut leap from the wicker basket as the Wasteland's guns smash into it, and as Carl tumbles through the air, Donut cannot remember when to drink it. Now! Mordecai, who brewed the three doses, had warned they would not like it. A crocodilian crawler alchemist devised it long ago while falling down a pit; it combines a potion from the breeding of rock buffalos with one like Katia's Crowd Blast, and it only works above two hundred kilometers an hour. Five seconds to impact become two, the ground softens, and they slam it like meteors, rise fifteen feet and slam it again. Five times. Then Carl is walking on air: he has broken through the necropolis roof.
beats.gist: Carl, Katia and Donut leap from the basket, drink Mordecai's potion, and crash through the necropolis roof.

beats.headline: Better than Half Splat
beats.text: Each of their Silver Skydiver's boxes holds three potions of Half Splat. Mordecai tells them to keep those in the hotlist until they can get a real Featherfall: they keep a crawler from dying of falling damage, but leave them at five percent health. They're still better than that Dolores Doesn't Splat potion, Carl grumbles. Hey now, says Mordecai. That potion is genius. It may not be pleasant, but his health was still at a hundred percent when he landed.
beats.gist: Mordecai's Half Splat potions leave five percent health; Dolores Doesn't Splat leaves a hundred.

recap.text: Carl, Katia and Donut leap from the wicker basket as the Wasteland's guns smash it. Past two hundred kilometers an hour, the ground softens under Mordecai's potion, and they slam it like meteors, rise fifteen feet and slam it again, five times, until Carl breaks through the necropolis roof. Mordecai says the Half Splat potions in the Silver Skydiver's boxes leave a crawler at five percent health, while Carl landed at a hundred.

tagline.text: The Coffee Shop Author Kit is a magical sheet of paper with a quill and a jar of ink. Whatever Carl writes in a new tab of his scratchpad appears on the paper, and whatever is written on the paper appears in the scratchpad.
Clipped to the wall of the bathroom stall in the personal space, the Coffee Shop Author Kit is how Carl and Katia trade messages nobody else can see.

description.text: Coffee Shop Author Kit. Alcoholism and crippling self-doubt not included. So you want to be a writer. It started with sappy poetry in middle school. You soon graduated to Naruto fanfiction. … Anyway, this is a magical sheet of paper. You will find you now have a second tab on your scratchpad in your interface. You can write something on this paper, and it will appear in the scratchpad and vice versa. If the proper spell and glyphs are accurately copied onto this paper, you can present the sheet at a market kiosk, and a scroll will appear for sale. …

beats.headline: Paper from a strange box
beats.text: Carl's Gold Makeup Sex is the Best Sex box holds a sheet of paper, a quill pen and a little capped jar of black ink. Odd, says Mordecai: pricey, used by scholar and arcanist classes for scroll production, and Carl's best bet is to sell the set. The description gives Carl a second scratchpad tab, which panics him, because the cookbook already hides one, but he simply has three now. He writes Does this work? and the pen rises, dips and copies it, then copies his rudimentary cat portrait. Am I a joke to you, Carl? Cool and completely useless, says Carl.
beats.gist: Carl's paper, quill and ink hold a pen that copies his writing and his cat portrait.

beats.headline: A haunted bathroom
beats.text: The stall in the personal space bathroom is the only place the crew can trade messages without anybody seeing. A dry-erase marker on the metal kept getting wiped by the cleaner bot, so Carl clipped the magical paper to the wall with a magnet from the Juicer's boss room; Katia writes with the pen, it appears in his scratchpad, and he answers at once. Donut tried it once, writing with her mouth: I AM NOT USING THIS, CARL. Katia took it all down when the refugees arrived, but has just put the quill and paper back to pass on coordinates when Louis barges in. You didn't tell me your bathroom was haunted!
beats.gist: Carl clips magical paper in the stall so Katia's writing appears in his scratchpad.

beats.headline: The plan, written down
beats.text: Carl adds a note to the Cookbook, 25th edition. He is starting something he does not think will succeed, and as Drakea asked of future authors, he means to document every step. The crew has a way of talking that prying eyes cannot see, and he points readers to his earlier post on the coffee shop author's kit to see how it works. Then he pastes in page one of their notes. The party is a trap. Queen Imogen is a country boss. Goal one is to survive.
beats.gist: Carl adds a Cookbook note: the party is a trap, Imogen a country boss, survival goal one.

recap.text: Carl's Gold Makeup Sex is the Best Sex box holds a sheet of paper, a quill pen and a jar of black ink, and Mordecai tells him to sell the set. The pen copies Carl's Does this work? and his rudimentary cat portrait. Carl then clips the paper to the bathroom stall wall with a magnet from the Juicer's boss room. Katia has just put the quill back to pass on coordinates when Louis barges in.

Carl adds a note to the Cookbook, 25th edition, saying he is starting something he does not think will succeed and, as Drakea asked of future authors, means to document every step. He points readers to his earlier post on the coffee shop author's kit, where the crew's hidden way of talking is explained. He pastes in page one: the party is a trap, Queen Imogen is a country boss, goal one is to survive.

tagline.text: Half Splat is a potion against falling: with it the ground cannot kill you, but you land at five percent of your health. Carl, Donut and Katia each have three, from the same Silver Skydiver's box.
At the Butcher's Masquerade Carl has half-splat potions to spare, and he leaves a bathroom counter covered with them, and a note, for the crawlers who come in after him.

beats.headline: Three skydiver's boxes
beats.text: After the Wasteland falls, Carl, Donut and Katia each open the same Silver Skydiver's box, and all three hold the same thing: three potions of Half Splat. Mordecai grunts. Keep them in the hotlist until you can get a real Featherfall, he says, but they are not that great: falling will not kill you, and you will be at five percent health when you hit the ground. Still better than that Dolores Doesn't Splat potion, Carl grumbles. Hey now, says Mordecai. That one is genius. Unpleasant, maybe, but Carl's health was at a hundred percent when he landed.
beats.gist: Carl, Donut and Katia each open a Silver Skydiver's box and find three Half Splat potions.

beats.headline: Off the top wing
beats.text: The biplane is spiralling down like water down a drain, and Quan Ch is closing in with his hands glowing. Carl chooses to worship Emberus, starts to glow, and tells Donut to get on his back, hold on with her claws if she has to, and take the half-splat potion. From the top wing he throws the celestial grenade at Quan and leaps. The god appears, and the plane flies into his nose and explodes. When they slam into the ground, Carl, invulnerable for sixty seconds, takes no damage. Donut bounces off his back and lies unconscious at five percent health, her skin smouldering and her hair singed.
beats.gist: Carl takes the half-splat potion's cue, worships Emberus, and survives the fall invulnerable while Donut lies unconscious.

beats.headline: Into the lacuna fog
beats.text: Phase two is over and the five gods have wandered off, so Carl and Donut set out across the lacuna for bubble 543. Getting out of their bubble is the hard part. Donut clings to Carl while he walks his feet down its almost invisible underside like Spider-Man, and at the lip both of them drink a half-splat and drop into the dark fog. The ground down there is completely flat.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut each drink a half-splat and drop from their bubble's lip into the fog.

beats.headline: The last one, in midair
beats.text: Sierra tosses Carl straight up into the sky like a rag doll, and he drops face-first toward her as she writhes on the treetops with her head on fire. He slams down his last half-splat potion. It will keep him from dying, though it will drop his health to five percent, but the boss is not on the ground, and he has no idea whether the potion even works like this. His gauntlet forms, he tears straight through her like paper, and he keeps falling through the branches. His ribs crunch and his legs break in the mud. He hits Heal.
beats.gist: Carl slams his last half-splat potion mid-fall, tears through Sierra, and crashes into the mud.

beats.headline: A counter full of potions
beats.text: In the boudoir off the ballroom, a glorified locker room where nobody actually changes, Carl covers the bathroom counter with dinosaur repellent and half-splat potions, with a note for everyone who finds them: store the half-splat in the inventory in a ready position, and drink the dinosaur one now if they have not already. They may have to flee fast, and there will be loose, prey-driven dinosaurs everywhere. Carl wants them attacking the hunters, not the crawlers.
beats.gist: Carl leaves half-splat potions and repellent on a bathroom counter, with a note to keep the potions ready.

recap.text: Carl, Donut and Katia each open a Silver Skydiver's box and find three potions of Half Splat. Mordecai says a fall will not kill you but leaves you at five percent health. Off the top wing, Carl throws the celestial grenade at Quan and leaps, glowing as a worshipper of Emberus, with Donut on his back. The plane flies into the god's nose; Carl, invulnerable for sixty seconds, takes no damage, and Donut lies unconscious, her skin smouldering.

Carl drops his last half-splat potion as Sierra tosses him straight up like a rag doll, and he falls face-first toward her while she writhes on the treetops with her head on fire. The potion will hold him at five percent health, and he does not know whether it works in midair. His gauntlet forms, he tears through her like paper, and he breaks his legs in the mud before he hits Heal.

tagline.text: A Live Ammo Ball is a dirigible gnome grenade: a fist-sized clamshell sphere holding a living creature in stasis, which bursts out when the ball hits. The five on a dead sniper's bandolier each hold a level-11 frenzied gerbil, and the many more that fell with the Wasteland loose thousands of gerbils on Hump Town.

A big, broken live ammo ball is the casing of the largest bomb Carl has built on purpose: filled with explosives and Nitro Sludge, welded shut, and named by the System Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.

description.text: Live Ammo Ball. Live ammo balls are a common and versatile ranged weapon of the Dirigible Gnomes. These round, clamshell spheres are designed to be fired great distances using a gnomish Tickle Stick, or they may be manually lobbed like a grenade. They are also fired in large clusters from anti-aircraft point defense batteries. Just be glad you're not in charge of cleaning up that mess. A living, usually angry, creature is placed inside the ball, and the ball opens upon impact with the target. The stasis field keeps the creature within safe from injury until the ball is opened. These balls are similar in technology to pet carriers. …

beats.headline: A five-pack of gerbils
beats.text: Of three dead gnomish snipers, one has landed on his back with his bandolier unbroken: five fist-sized grenade balls. Donut loots it, announces that she believes Carl has given the System AI a case of blue balls, and drops it at his feet. Every ball contains the same thing, a frenzied gerbil, level 11. Carl remembers Crixus's throw, another sniper's shot and the Wasteland's volley of a hundred, all flying over their mark, and Ralph, the gerbil boss on the second floor. The AI wanted him to stomp one.
beats.gist: Donut loots a sniper's bandolier of five grenade balls, and each holds a level 11 frenzied gerbil.

beats.headline: Thousands of red dots
beats.text: Carl is in the middle of refusing Donut's idea that he sacrifice a squish-sized creature to the AI every morning when the map fills with thousands of red dots. They are gerbils. With snipers and chunks of the Wasteland raining from the sky, he realises, there were hundreds if not thousands of those balls up there, built to survive heavy impacts. Ten minutes into the fight the level-11 gerbils are launching themselves at Hump Town's defenders and burrowing into flesh, and Donut's Wall of Fire only turns them into miniature, gnashing fireballs.
beats.gist: Donut's Wall of Fire turns the level-11 gerbils into gnashing fireballs that still burrow into defenders.

beats.headline: Welded into a bomb
beats.text: Carl has a large, egg-shaped, clamshell bomb casing from the previous floor, a live ammo ball too broken to hold a living creature again. He fills it with explosives and a few blocks of Mordecai's Nitro Sludge, welds it closed, builds a little cart for Bomo to pull it on and, for good measure, imbues it with Fear. If it works properly, the simulator says, it will flatten everything within a third of a mile. The System names it on its own: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.
beats.gist: Carl welds explosives and Nitro Sludge inside a broken live ammo ball casing.

recap.text: Carl finds a dead gnomish sniper with a bandolier of five fist-sized grenade balls unbroken. Donut loots it, announces that Carl has given the System AI a case of blue balls, and drops it at his feet. Each ball holds a frenzied level 11 gerbil, and Carl realises the AI wanted him to stomp one. The map fills with thousands of red dots, and gerbils burrow into Hump Town's defenders, while Donut's Wall of Fire turns them into fireballs.

Carl takes a large, egg-shaped clamshell casing, a live ammo ball too broken to hold a living creature again, and packs it with explosives and a few blocks of Mordecai's Nitro Sludge. He welds it shut, builds a little cart for Bomo to pull it on, and imbues it with Fear. The simulator says it will flatten everything within a third of a mile. The System names it Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home.

entities.name: Mongo's speed and strength fang caps

tagline.text: Mongo's second pair of fang caps came out of Donut's platinum quest box, like the first, and adds fifteen percent to the dinosaur's movement speed and fifteen percent to his strength.

beats.headline: Same box, new caps
beats.text: Donut's platinum quest box holds what her last one did: a skill potion and a pair of fang caps. She drinks the potion, three more points of Animal Wrangling, up to eight. The last caps gave Mongo a damage buff and poison and paralysis that seldom fire, because whatever he chomps is usually dead already. These add fifteen percent movement speed and fifteen percent strength to the level-29 dinosaur. Once again Donut makes Carl fit them to his teeth, and first he has to fish out a little piece of robot Donut.
beats.gist: Donut's quest box holds another skill potion and fang caps, adding fifteen percent speed and strength to Mongo.

recap.text: Donut's platinum quest box holds a skill potion and a pair of fang caps, as her last one did. She drinks the potion, raising Animal Wrangling by three points to eight. The caps add fifteen percent movement speed and fifteen percent strength to Mongo, the level-29 dinosaur; his last pair gave poison and paralysis that seldom fire, since whatever he chomps is usually dead already. Carl fits them to his teeth, after fishing out a little piece of robot Donut.
