tagline.text: The Platinum Sharpening Stone is a little black rock from the quest box for saving Hump Town, made for any spiked weapon and too short-lived to keep. Carl rubs it along his gauntlet's spikes at once, and they grow a little longer.

description.text: Platinum Sharpening Stone. Warning: This item has a short shelf life. Apply this to any spiked offensive weapon to receive the following buffs. Plus (2 x current level)% damage to all attacks. Plus 1 to all current stat buffs. Does not add new buffs if they do not exist. It also makes the weapon look extra oily and mean looking. In other words, the weapon’s appearance may change. But only a little.

beats.headline: The last box
beats.text: The last of Carl's boxes is the platinum quest box from saving Hump Town, and he needs something good: everything lately has been weird or not yet usable. It holds 5,000 gold coins, twenty healing scrolls and a little black rock. Mordecai is pleased. This is what he was talking about: Carl is starting to get items that enhance the ones he already has. It is for the gauntlet, he says, and Carl has to use it now.
beats.gist: Carl opens his last box and finds a little black rock meant for his gauntlet.

beats.headline: Rubbed into the spikes
beats.text: The stone has a short shelf life, so it cannot wait. Carl forms his gauntlet and rubs the rock along the spikes. The whole thing glows, and the spikes themselves grow a little longer. With the gauntlet formed, he gets an extra point of dexterity and another of strength. Then he turns to the paper and inkwell from his other box while Katia opens her platinum one.
beats.gist: Carl rubs the Platinum Sharpening Stone along his gauntlet's spikes, lengthening them and raising his dexterity and strength.

recap.text: Carl's last box, the platinum quest box from saving Hump Town, holds 5,000 gold coins, twenty healing scrolls and a little black rock. Mordecai is pleased and says the rock is for the gauntlet and must be used now. Carl forms the gauntlet and rubs the stone along its spikes. The whole gauntlet glows, the spikes grow a little longer, and Carl gets one point of dexterity and one of strength.

tagline.text: Princess Formidable's emergency box gives Katia a set of ten crossbow bolts of Petrify Rock Class. Each one leaves its target Petrified, conscious but unable to move, for sixty seconds, and Mordecai says they cost more than regular bolts.

beats.headline: Ten bolts from a princess
beats.text: Katia has received an emergency benefactor box, a silver one from Princess Formidable, and Mordecai says she needs to open it now: it probably cost the princess a sizeable chunk of her net worth. Then Carl realises the igneous in front of him is not Chris but Maggie. She pulls a round, spiked ball, and a crossbow bolt slams into her head. The rock creature crashes to the street, Petrified, a sixty-second timer overhead. Katia jogs up: her box held a set of ten bolts of Petrify Rock Class. The creature's eyes still move; she is conscious but cannot move. Why, Katia asks, give her bolts to petrify Maggie instead of kill her?
beats.gist: Katia's silver box holds ten Petrify Rock Class bolts, and one turns Maggie to stone.

beats.headline: Seven minutes left
beats.text: Imani stops them: Chris has messaged her. He is petrified, and he is being controlled. Juice Box says there is an Infiltrator in him, and she is the one to kill. At ten seconds Mordecai says shoot him again; Katia fires into his chest, the bolt whiffs away in a puff of smoke, and the timer resets. An Infiltrator takes full control of a living body, Mordecai explains, and getting her out without killing him is next to impossible. Katia fires her third of ten. Seven more minutes. When Katia is down to three bolts, three minutes is not enough to get him to the stairwell.
beats.gist: Katia fires bolt after bolt into petrified, controlled Chris, resetting the timer each time.

recap.text: Katia opens a silver box from Princess Formidable and finds ten bolts of Petrify Rock Class. Carl realises the igneous is Maggie, and a crossbow bolt to the head leaves her Petrified on the street under a sixty-second timer. Imani says Chris is petrified too, with an Infiltrator controlling him. Katia fires into his chest, the bolt whiffs away in smoke, and the timer resets; with three bolts left, three minutes is not enough to reach the stairwell.

tagline.text: The Nightmare II is a gnomish Drop Bear biplane the other crawlers found intact, renamed by Carl over its stencilled Death Trap. It runs on gasoline, has a rear-facing gun, and carries an emergency balloon that lifts it to the top of the bubble.
The Nightmare II came down slowly on its emergency balloon after the boss fight, and it lives in the flying house's garage.
Carl has flown the Nightmare II once, against Quan Ch over Orthrus, and it went spiralling into the nose of Emberus and exploded.

beats.headline: Death Trap, painted over
beats.text: The others secured an intact Drop Bear, its pilot nowhere to be found, and Langley had it covered with a tarp before the storm. It runs on actual gasoline. Carl fills the tank only a quarter of the way to keep it light, and there are no bombs left under the wings. On the nose, over a frothing, rabid koala, the stencilled name reads Death Trap, with four bombs painted after it. Carl sprays over it and writes Nightmare II on the side. Donut objects, but only half-heartedly. He has to rip off both armrests to fit in the pilot's seat.
beats.gist: Carl sprays over the name Death Trap on the Drop Bear and writes Nightmare II.

beats.headline: Up on the emergency balloons
beats.text: There is no runway. Donut takes the rear-facing gunner's chair and makes shooting noises. Carl yanks the lever beside his seat like a car's emergency brake, the twin emergency balloons hiss full, and the plane jerks upward tail first; on the way up Donut finds there are still bullets in the gun, and don't you dare, says Carl. At the ceiling of the bubble, about five kilometres above the bowl, the plane, still tied to its balloons, skitters along on its engines like a bicycle on training wheels toward the glowing balloon of the flying house. Donut jumps from her seat onto its net, and Carl follows from the nose.
beats.gist: Carl yanks the lever, the balloons hiss full, and the plane jerks up tail first.

beats.headline: Back down on its own
beats.text: Marching back to Hump Town, Donut spots the airplane slowly descending from the sky. It is the Nightmare II. It came loose from the main balloon during the boss fight, and its emergency balloon has finally lost its juice and is letting it down. Carl sends Louis and Firas out to secure it and drag it back to the house. It should fit in the large garage, safe from the next storm, and it will give them something to do.
beats.gist: Louis and Firas go out to drag the fallen Nightmare II back to the house garage.

beats.headline: Off the edge of the yard
beats.text: Louis and Firas lashed the biplane down in the garage, the only part of the flying house that still has a roof. Now they all pull it out of the garage facing the wind, and Donut sits at the gun behind Carl, sticking her Torch spell under the top wing to light both cockpits. Carl barely knows what he is doing: yoke, pedals, a fuel gauge, a gyroscope he does not understand, twin throttles. He pushes the throttle, and the little biplane rolls off the edge of the yard and drops like a rock until flying into the wind lets him pull up over the ocean. His Biplane Pilot skill rises to three.
beats.gist: Carl pilots the biplane off the yard's edge, drops, then pulls up over the ocean.

beats.headline: Into the nose of a god
beats.text: Quan has knocked Orthrus unconscious at two percent and is moving in to finish him. Carl dives the Nightmare II at the dog, tells Donut to grab the stick, and from the wing throws a potion ball of Mordecai's Special Brew that tops the puppy's health back up. Donut, paws locked on the yoke, loops the plane twice; something falls off the back, and the pedals break. Carl gets it out of its roll but not its spiral. He chooses to worship Emberus, and from the top wing he throws the celestial grenade at Quan and jumps. Emberus appears above them, a city-sized floating head, and the spiralling Drop Bear hits him right in the nose and explodes.
beats.gist: Quan nearly kills Orthrus; Carl heals him, then jumps, and the spiralling Drop Bear explodes on Emberus's nose.

relations.note: the rear-facing gunner
batch b4a wrote it as gnomish-drop-bear

recap.text: Carl sprays over the name Death Trap on the captured Drop Bear, writes Nightmare II on its side, and rips off both armrests to fit the pilot's seat. Louis and Firas lash the plane down in the garage, and Carl flies it off the edge of the yard, his Biplane Pilot skill rising to three. He throws a celestial grenade at Quan and jumps, and the spiralling plane hits Emberus in the nose and explodes.

tagline.text: Bonnie's necklace looks like a walnut and holds a little purple soul crystal, the power for the balloon that keeps her house afloat. How far its clamshell is open decides how much power the balloon gets, and Carl keeps it open just a fraction.
Katia says that if Carl had not left the controller with Louis, they never could have flown the house to the land quadrant. Louis and Firas have turned into quite the pilots.

description.text: Soul Crystal. F-Quality. Used to power the balloon that keeps this house afloat. Nothing too exciting. You probably want to avoid breaking it, though. Charge: 89% Kill something to charge it up.

beats.headline: A walnut on a string
beats.text: The suburban house has come down cockeyed on a dune half a mile east of Hump Town, and since Denise died its magical balloon has been slowly refilling. The ropes are like steel cables. Carl tells Bonnie they have to leave; she pulls a walnut-like necklace from her shirt, fiddles with it, and the house settles. Her dad gave it to her with the potion, she says, and told her to give it to an adult. Inside a sliding clamshell is a little purple-hued gem, a soul crystal. It stopped feeding the balloon under the goose's anti-magic aura. Carl keeps it, the shell open just a fraction: enough, he hopes, to keep the balloon off the ground but not to lift the house.
beats.gist: Bonnie's walnut necklace holds a soul crystal, and Carl keeps its shell open a crack.

beats.headline: The controller left with Louis
beats.text: In the personal space, Katia catches Carl up. Once she learned they would not know his fate for a few days, she took matters into her own hands and tried flying the house to the land quadrant. It would not let them at first, until they worked out what was wrong. If Carl had not left the controller with Louis, she says, they never could have flown the thing. Louis and Firas have turned into quite the pilots, and they are already on the way back to pick him up.
beats.gist: Katia says the house would not fly until fixed; Carl's controller, left with Louis, made it possible.

recap.text: Carl tells Bonnie the house has to leave, and she pulls a walnut-like necklace from her shirt, fiddles with it, and the house settles. Inside its sliding clamshell is a purple-hued soul crystal, which stopped feeding the balloon under the goose's anti-magic aura. Katia says they could never have flown the house without the controller Carl left with Louis.

tagline.text: A Hobgoblin Disco Ball is a hobgoblin smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion. Its rainbow smoke hides everything inside it, bounces to the beat and blinds whoever threw it as well, and Carl's first one goes off on his crafting-room floor.

Orren credits the dust a disco ball leaves behind with Administrator Loita's death, and calls it one of the most brilliant assassinations he has seen a crawler execute. Carl had only wanted the toy too filthy to take into the studio.
Carl throws disco balls in fights now: from the wing of a biplane at Quan Ch, and by hand at Queen Imogen, whose goop-covered face, by Donut's account, never saw Prepotente coming.

description.text: Hobgoblin Disco Ball. Type: Magically-infused Deflagrating Tossable. Effect: It's a real trip. Status: 25. Unstable. Molly not included. Take a Hobgoblin smoke curtain, soak it in an invisibility potion, and what do you get? You get a party, that's what you get! Produces heavy, multi-hued billows of smoke that are both photosensitive and frequency responsive. And in case you don't know what that means, just set one off and find out. The smoke will conceal all movement within, and the plumes will bounce to the beat. Warning: Unlike a regular smoke curtain, the caster of this tossable is not immune to its effects. In other words, you'll be just as blind as the monsters. …

beats.headline: Rainbow in the crafting room
beats.text: Carl has been infusing smoke curtains since he read about the idea in the cookbook, mostly into duds. This one he stole the recipe for and has to pretend he stumbled on: a red smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion, now shining with a multi-coloured opalescence. His Infusion skill rises to level 3. Robot Donut, watching from the table, hops up and down to cheer, the ball goes flying to the floor, and Carl steps back right onto it. Rainbow smoke fills the room, Mordecai curses over his alchemy table, and it leaves a sandy, technicolor residue on everything. The common area smells of burnt cotton candy.
beats.gist: Carl steps on a dropped ball, and his invisibility-infused smoke curtain bursts into rainbow smoke.

beats.headline: The dust did the job
beats.text: Administrator Loita is dead, killed when the Donut toy that followed her off the couch exploded, and Orren lays out how. The disco ball's residue slowly ate at the panel on the back of the toy's head, the moisture of the admin's rebreather ran it along the edges, and the jump dislodged the panel and set off the self-destruct. One of the most brilliant assassinations he has ever seen a crawler execute, he says. Carl knows better. He only wanted the dust all over the toy so nobody would want it in the studio, and had not realised the dust was already doing the job for him.
beats.gist: Orren credits Loita's death to a brilliant assassination, but Carl's disco ball dust did the work by accident.

beats.headline: From the lower wing
beats.text: Quan Ch hangs in the air ahead with his shield still up. Carl locks the biplane's trajectory, climbs out onto the lower wing beside the starboard propeller, and tells Donut to switch her glasses to heat. He loads the hobgoblin disco ball into the xistera and throws, missing the propeller by inches. It bursts over Quan's chest anyway, knocking him back, its sticky sand clinging to his shield like mud. As they pass, Donut empties the gun and a double magic missile into the rainbow cloud. Carl's fused hob-lobber goes off twenty feet short, close enough, and the pulsing smoke plummets out of the sky with its sticky remnants following Quan down like a comet.
beats.gist: Carl throws the disco ball from the wing, and it bursts over Quan, knocking him from the sky.

beats.headline: Against the queen's lightning
beats.text: Imogen's health is almost gone, a black nimbus round her and her hands crackling red: a lightning attack. Britney is screaming on the ground, and Louis and Firas lie unconscious side by side. Carl has had no time to reinstall the xistera, so he throws a hobgoblin disco ball by hand, shouting at Britney about her jacket. It splatters multi-coloured goo across the side of Imogen's head, and she barely notices. Her lightning comes out as a single bolt, drawn into the clump of spreading butterflies. It is not what Carl intended, but it works too.
beats.gist: Carl hurls a hobgoblin disco ball by hand at Imogen, and her lightning strikes the butterflies instead.

beats.headline: Out of the truck's roof
beats.text: Racing along an apartment ceiling to make sure Imani and Elle reach their gate, Carl climbs out of his seat with Sticky Feet on and hurls Biscuit Packs at the beetles. One crashes into the truck's electrified shield and comes back for more, and he drops a hobgoblin disco ball out of the hole in the roof. It goes off as it falls, flashing colourful lights and thick smoke everywhere. Elle reports they have already hit the gate. Then the truck drops from the ceiling into the smoke-filled living room.
beats.gist: Carl drops a hobgoblin disco ball out of the truck's roof, filling the room with lights and smoke.

relations.note: Orren blames its residue for the toy that killed her
robot Donut, dusted in the crafting room

recap.text: Carl soaks a red smoke curtain in an invisibility potion, and his Infusion skill rises to level 3. Robot Donut cheers, the ball hits the floor, Carl steps on it, and rainbow smoke leaves sandy residue on everything. The residue eats the panel on a Donut toy's head, so the toy explodes and kills Administrator Loita. Carl throws the ball from the biplane's lower wing, and it bursts over Quan Ch's chest, its sticky sand clinging to his shield.

Imogen's health is nearly gone, a black nimbus around her and her hands crackling red, while Britney screams on the ground and Louis and Firas lie unconscious side by side. With no time to reinstall the xistera, Carl throws a hobgoblin disco ball by hand, shouting at Britney about her jacket. Multi-coloured goo splatters across the side of Imogen's head, and she barely notices. Her lightning leaves as a single bolt, drawn into the spreading butterflies.

Racing along an apartment ceiling, Carl climbs out of his seat with Sticky Feet on and hurls Biscuit Packs at the beetles. One crashes into the truck's electrified shield and comes back for more, so he drops a hobgoblin disco ball out of the hole in the roof. It goes off as it falls, flashing colourful lights and thick smoke everywhere. Elle reports they have already hit the gate, and the truck drops into the smoke-filled living room.

tagline.text: The Belt of Buoyancy is a simple belt that wraps around Donut's stomach and keeps her from sinking, though it only works in the water. She spends a good three minutes complaining about it.

beats.headline: One more thing for Donut
beats.text: More than sixty seconds fully submerged without dying earns the I was in the pool achievement, an honorary mudskipper, and a Bronze I'm Wet Box, which holds another ten scrolls of water breathing for each of them. Donut's box, for some unfathomable reason, is silver instead of bronze, and she gets an additional item: a Belt of Buoyancy. It is a simple belt that wraps around her stomach and keeps her from sinking, and it only works in the water. She spends a good three minutes complaining about it, and about how she is never going back there again.
beats.gist: Donut earns a silver box and a Belt of Buoyancy, which only works in water.

recap.text: Donut stays fully submerged for over sixty seconds without dying. That earns the I was in the pool achievement, an honorary mudskipper, and a Bronze I'm Wet Box holding ten more scrolls of water breathing for each of them. Her box is silver, for no reason anyone can explain, and it also holds a Belt of Buoyancy, which wraps around her stomach and keeps her from sinking in water. She complains for three minutes.

tagline.text: A Potion of Bloodlust doubles its drinker's strength and speed for as many seconds as their constitution, and leaves them not knowing where they are or why they are fighting. Carl has two, and Mordecai tells him not to use them.
Carl does not drink his Potions of Bloodlust. One, taped to a hob-lobber and set off on the flooding bridge of a submarine, spreads through the water and drives Lusca's babies into a feeding frenzy.
Carl's last Potion of Bloodlust goes into a potion ball. Beamed at a flying mantis warrior, it enrages her, and she pulls the head off her own sister.

description.text: Potion of Bloodlust It’s like giving yourself a PCP enema after spending the day riding the Night Train Express. Drinking this potion gives the following effects for (Constitution) seconds. Strength times two. Movement speed times two. Dexterity times .5 The Where the Fuck Am I? Who the Fuck Are You? Debuff Constitution times .5 For every crawler, NPC, or mob killed by you while this potion is active, your movement speed increases by an additional 25%.

beats.headline: Two potions, one warning
beats.text: Carl's silver Pacifist's Box, for winning a boss battle without killing the boss, holds two potions that give Mordecai pause. Don't use those, he says: the last time he saw someone drink that potion, they accidentally killed half of their party. It is a berserking potion, and its debuff means the drinker does not remember where they are or why they are fighting. Carl puts both away. He will look in the cookbook for advice that might make the potion more useful.
beats.gist: Mordecai warns Carl against the two berserking potions, which wipe the drinker's memory, so Carl pockets them.

beats.headline: In the minifridge
beats.text: The sub is already inside Lusca, and the bridge window is about to break. Carl swaps a hob-lobber's fuse for hobgoblin pus and duct-tapes a potion bottle to it; the cookbook has a more elegant version with a different potion, and he has no idea if this will work. He tapes the bomb inside the bolted minifridge by the captain's chair. The window breaks and the babies flood the bridge; holding the stateroom door's turning wheel with one hand, he slams the detonator. Xs bloom on the map. It was the potion of bloodlust: spread through the water, it started a feeding frenzy.
beats.gist: Carl's bloodlust bomb detonates, and the water turns into a feeding frenzy.

beats.headline: The last one, thrown
beats.text: Running up a temple wall on Sticky Feet, Carl pulls a potion ball filled with his last potion of Bloodlust. Ping returns only an error, as if the map is blocked in this town. He stows the ball and throws a full-strength hob-lobber into the bunched mantises and nebular priests instead. Then two more mantis warriors swoop in, and he beams the berserking potion at the closer one. It slams into her back. Enraged, she yanks the head off her own sister, dives on the group below and cleaves a human priest in half.
beats.gist: Carl throws a hob-lobber at the mantises, then beams a berserking potion at one, who kills her sister.

relations.note: on her babies, through the water

recap.text: Carl seals away two potions from his silver Pacifist's Box after Mordecai warns that the last drinker of the berserking potion accidentally killed half of their party. With the sub inside Lusca, he swaps a hob-lobber's fuse for hobgoblin pus, duct-tapes a potion bottle to it, and tapes the bomb inside the bolted minifridge. The window breaks, the babies flood the bridge, and he slams the detonator. The potion of bloodlust spreads through the water and starts a feeding frenzy.

Running up a temple wall on Sticky Feet, Carl pulls a potion ball holding his last Potion of Bloodlust, but Ping returns only an error, as if the map is blocked in this town. He throws a full-strength hob-lobber into the bunched mantises and nebular priests instead. Two more mantis warriors swoop in, and he beams the berserking potion at the closer one. Enraged, she yanks the head off her own sister and cleaves a human priest in half.

tagline.text: Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder looks like an ordinary black bandana with a white paisley pattern. It gives Carl +5 to Detect Traps, a level-15 Tripper spell once every five hours, and the Remote Detonator benefit.

Carl's black paisley bandana still gives him a level-15 Tripper. Neither Imani nor Elle can wear it, so Imani carries its Tripper spell as a tattoo from Katia, and Carl feels a jolt in his chest when she casts it.

description.text: Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder. This handy-dandy, versatile garment can be worn around the neck, in the hair, or on your face if you want to cosplay as a cowboy robbing a bank. Can also be tied around your arms or legs, but only if you want to look like a moron. Don't tie it around your leg. This simple, square piece of fabric is a reminder that looks can be deceiving. The wearer of this item receives the following benefits: +5 to the Detect Traps skill. Wearer may cast a level-15 Tripper spell once every five hours. The Remote Detonator benefit.

beats.headline: A name from the cookbook
beats.text: The gold boss box peels open like a banana on a black bandana with a white paisley pattern, like the one Carl wore at work against the stench of the docks. The name makes his pulse quicken: Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder. Tripper at level fifteen sets off every trap in a wide radius, though it does not disarm them. The real prize is Remote Detonator, which sets off any explosive Carl has designated. He ties it round his head, and Donut does not like the vibe. Mordecai remembers Drakea, a famous crawler with a class like Carl's, partly responsible for what happened to the nagas.
beats.gist: Carl ties a bomb-triggering bandana, Drakea's Kerchief of Disorder, round his head, and Donut dislikes the vibe.

beats.headline: The first remote detonation
beats.text: Donut shrieks with joy at the gun, and a double-shot magic missile slams into a growing plume of pulsing rainbow smoke. Carl loads a fused hob-lobber, designates it with his new remote detonator skill and throws it. Even able to throw twice as far now, he has waited a hair too long, so he sets it off just as the ball starts to dip, twenty feet short of the plume. That is plenty close. The crackling circle of rainbow smoke plummets out of the sky, and its sticky disco-ball remnants follow Quan Ch down like a comet.
beats.gist: Carl detonates a fused hob-lobber twenty feet short of the rainbow smoke, and the plume falls.

beats.headline: Every trap at once
beats.text: Carl sets a launcher box of twenty-five surefire missiles against a hedge and marks its timed trigger with Remote Detonator, then marks a bomb with a second one. One mental click on the first trigger in his hotlist, and the rockets corkscrew into the air one by one. Then, on the run, he steps on two traps at once: a cheap spike trap and an alarm that starts blasting Kickstart My Heart. He casts Tripper, and every trap in a wide radius goes off around them, songs and small explosions. He pulls the alarm into his inventory to shut it up.
beats.gist: Carl sets off a missile launcher and a bomb, then triggers two traps; Tripper detonates every trap nearby.

beats.headline: Tripper on loan to Imani
beats.text: Elle reports that they are inside the stronghold, searching for traps, and a searing pain hits Carl's chest. Crawler Imani C has used your Tripper spell. Lots of traps just went off. The plan had been to lend her or Elle the bandana, but neither can wear it: fairy-class and other magical races are extremely limited in the magical gear they can wear. Taking it off, Carl learned his own Tripper had risen to level seven by itself. He could not give Imani the item, but she could borrow the spell as a tattoo, and when Katia drew the blood he lost six levels of it. That does not matter: the bandana brings it to fifteen either way.
beats.gist: Imani borrows Carl's Tripper spell as a tattoo, since neither she nor Elle can wear the bandana.

relations.note: its Tripper spell, lent by tattoo

recap.text: Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder opens from a gold boss box as a black paisley bandana. Its Tripper skill sets off every trap in a wide radius, and Remote Detonator sets off any explosive Carl has designated. Carl ties it round his head, and Donut does not like the vibe. He designates a fused hob-lobber and throws it, and it goes off twenty feet short of a rainbow smoke plume, which plummets out of the sky.

Carl sets a launcher box of twenty-five surefire missiles against a hedge and marks its timed trigger and a bomb with Remote Detonator. One mental click on the first trigger in his hotlist sends the rockets corkscrewing up. On the run, he steps on a cheap spike trap and an alarm blasting Kickstart My Heart, then casts Tripper, which sets off every trap around them. He pulls the alarm into his inventory.

A searing pain hits Carl's chest as Imani C uses his Tripper spell inside the stronghold, and lots of traps go off. Neither she nor Elle can wear his bandana, because fairy-class and other magical races are limited in their gear. Carl takes it off and finds his Tripper has risen to level seven; Katia draws his blood so Imani can borrow the spell as a tattoo, and he loses six levels, but the bandana brings it to fifteen.

tagline.text: The earth patch is a tiny round patch, the size of a half-dollar, depicting the planet Earth. Sewn onto an eligible garment it gives +5% Strength and immunity from cloud-based attacks, and Donut dismisses it as a screen print.
The earth patch was the first patch on Carl's jacket, sewn on by Katia, and a patch of flaming arrows now sits beside it on his shoulder.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Small. This patch depicts the planet Earth, which is currently under the regency of the Borant System. Ahh, the planet earth. A whole lot of culture. A whole lot of spunk. So many dumbasses. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: +5% to Strength. Immunity from cloud-based attacks. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: A screen-printed planet Earth
beats.text: Three things pop out of the platinum Spicy Box: a black sleeveless jacket, a tiny round patch depicting the planet earth, and a small unenchanted sewing kit with white and red thread. The patch is the size of a half-dollar, not attached to the jacket but clearly meant to be sewn on. Donut jumps to the table to inspect it and pushes it aside with a strange amount of disgust. This is just a screen print. Amateur hour. Carl has several immunities already, says Mordecai, but this is another layer of protection: sew it on right away, and mind the space.
beats.gist: Mordecai tells Carl to sew on a tiny Earth patch right away; Donut sniffs at it.

beats.headline: Immune by patch already
beats.text: On the sixth floor the specialties for Carl's class play out on his screen, and he cannot click anything; he just has to watch. Revolutionary means the front of the line, a tear gas canister to the chest, the first to start swinging. It gives an extra point of strength at every level, two to Unarmed Combat, faster melee training, the Blend into the Crowd benefit, and immunity to cloud-based attacks, which the menu marks as already obtained via upgrade patch.
beats.gist: Carl's class specialties play out on his screen, and cloud-attack immunity is already marked obtained.

beats.headline: Arrows on the shoulder
beats.text: The gold ranged weapon box holds a small square patch, about the size of Carl's first, the planet earth: a dozen flaming arrows clutched in an eagle claw, drawn Sailor Jerry style. Each new patch adds a point to all his stats plus its own benefit. Katia, who affixed the first one, has already grabbed the sewing kit. She takes the jacket, maps out the best places, and sews the arrow patch next to the planet earth on the shoulder.
beats.gist: Katia sews the new arrow patch beside the planet earth patch on Carl's jacket shoulder.

relations.note: she sewed it on

recap.text: Carl's platinum Spicy Box gives up a black sleeveless jacket, a small unenchanted sewing kit with white and red thread, and a round patch of planet Earth the size of a half-dollar, made to be sewn on. Donut hops onto the table, shoves the patch aside in disgust, and calls it a screen print, amateur hour. Mordecai says Carl has some immunities already, but the patch adds another layer of protection, so he should sew it on right away.

Carl watches the class specialties on his screen and cannot click anything. Revolutionary puts him first in line, takes a tear gas canister to the chest, and swings first. It grants immunity to cloud-based attacks, which the menu marks as already obtained by upgrade patch. Katia sews the gold box's flaming-arrow patch beside the planet earth on his jacket.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle is a black, sleeveless canvas jacket that gives +1 to all Carl's base stats, a point more for every patch sewn onto it, double that with a back patch. It also adds half again to the range and accuracy of every explosive he throws.
Carl's Battle Rattle now carries three patches, the planet earth, a fistful of flaming arrows and a hand-stitched bomb, and each one adds a point to all his stats.
Carl's Battle Rattle carries five patches now, and on its back the Scavenger's Daughter, a divine back patch that doubles the stat boost they give him.

description.text: Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle. This sleeveless jacket in its current form only offers meager protections compared to some other items of this caliber. However, its ability to host as many upgrade patches as you can fit makes this one of the best, most upgradeable protection items in the game. The plain, unadorned version of this jacket imbues the following effects: +1 to all base stats. This base stat upgrade increases by +1 for every compatible patch that is added to this jacket. If an eligible Back Patch is added, this benefit is doubled. Access to the Desperado Club (already obtained) Access to the Naughty Boys Employment Agency (already obtained) +50% range and accuracy for all thrown explosives.

beats.headline: A jacket of upgrade slots
beats.text: Carl's hands are shaking as the last box opens, the platinum Spicy Box. First out is a black, sleeveless jacket of thick canvas, glowing with a very subtle, almost purple light. You got really good loot this time, says Mordecai: the dungeon is starting to solidify your look for you. That's a patch jacket, with lots of upgrade slots, and they will need more patches as soon as possible. Carl is glad to be rid of his old leather jacket, burned, holed, one arm gone, its zipper broken two floors ago. He reads the new one's description. Hell yeah: the range benefit alone makes it one of his most valuable items.
beats.gist: Carl opens the platinum Spicy Box and finds a black canvas patch jacket with many upgrade slots.

beats.headline: Katia sews on two
beats.text: Two patches in one sitting. The gold ranged weapon box gives a small square of flaming arrows in an eagle claw, and the Gold Spicy Box a bigger white rectangle with a bomb hand-stitched in fine black thread, which Donut calls classic Spanish blackwork. Each patch adds a point to all Carl's stats on top of its own benefit; bigger ones take more room for the same. Katia, who affixed his first one, has already grabbed the sewing kit. Carl pulls off the jacket and hands it to her, and she maps out the best places and sews the arrows next to the planet earth on the shoulder, then moves to the bomb, placing it at the bottom left of the front along the hemline.
beats.gist: Carl hands Katia his jacket, and she sews on flaming arrows and a hand-stitched bomb.

beats.headline: A back patch of skulls
beats.text: The celestial predator box explodes into fireflies and leaves only a full-sized back patch: thick black fabric embroidered with a white pyramid of skulls, covered in clear stitching like fiberoptic wire. Carl has five patches already, the earth, the arrows, the bomb, the anti-vampire Midnight Epicure patch and a new peace symbol, and a back patch doubles the boost they give. What it does itself stays hidden until it is affixed and worn. He sews it on himself, Donut on his shoulder disapproving of every stitch. The angle of entry is crucial!
beats.gist: Carl sews a skull-pyramid back patch onto his jacket while Donut disapproves, doubling his five patches' boost.

beats.headline: A four-leaf clover patch
beats.text: Carl removes his jacket, grabs the sewing kit and sews on a small patch of a foot crushing down a set of four-leaf clovers, placing it above the Midnight Epicure patch. It gives the Lucky Shot benefit: once per floor, a fatal blow is deflected into the body of a party member instead. Then Donut wants to show him an upgrade for Mongo's saddle, and notices what he is doing: it is not straight. It is, says Carl, and he is taking the patch off the second he has used it.
beats.gist: Carl sews a lucky-clover patch onto his jacket, and Donut says it is crooked.

recap.text: Carl opens the last box, the platinum Spicy Box, with shaking hands. Out comes a black, sleeveless jacket of thick canvas, glowing with a very subtle, almost purple light. Mordecai says the dungeon is starting to solidify his look and that the patch jacket needs more patches as soon as possible. Carl, glad to be rid of his burned leather jacket, reads the description and decides the range benefit alone makes it one of his most valuable items.

Katia sews two patches onto Carl's Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle: flaming arrows in an eagle claw from the gold ranged weapon box, and a bomb hand-stitched in fine black thread from the Gold Spicy Box, which Donut calls classic Spanish blackwork. Each patch adds a point to all Carl's stats. She puts the arrows beside the planet earth on the shoulder and the bomb along the front hemline.

Carl opens the celestial predator box, which explodes into fireflies and leaves a full-sized back patch: thick black fabric embroidered with a white pyramid of skulls, covered in clear stitching like fiberoptic wire. A back patch doubles the boost of his five patches, and its own effect stays hidden until it is sewn on and worn. He sews it on himself, Donut on his shoulder disapproving of every stitch.

Carl sews a small patch of a foot crushing down four-leaf clovers above the Midnight Epicure patch on his jacket. It gives the Lucky Shot benefit: once per floor, a fatal blow is deflected into a party member's body instead. Donut comes to show him an upgrade for Mongo's saddle and says the patch is not straight. Carl says it is, and he is taking it off the second he has used it.

tagline.text: A Potion of Dinosaur Repellent promises that a pack of dinosaurs will eat its drinker last, for a full thirty hours. Mordecai's "uh-oh" when Carl draws one does not help.
Carl has received ten of these potions and drunk one, though the description is vague about what it actually does. Donut refuses hers, afraid it will make Mongo shy away from her.
Carl leaves a counter covered in these potions for the crawlers on their way into the ballroom, so that loose dinosaurs will go for the hunters and not for them.

description.text: Potion of Dinosaur Repellent. Drink this if your party is attacked by a pack of dinosaurs, and they’ll eat you last. Effect lasts a full 30 hours.

beats.headline: Mordecai says uh-oh
beats.text: Carl works through his loot. It is mostly the regular stuff: junk clothing and weapons, healing potions and mana restorations, a single invisibility potion, hobgoblin dynamite, and the first Good Healing Potions, which Mordecai calls a sign he is progressing nicely. Then comes something a little concerning, and Mordecai's uh-oh when it appears does not help. A Potion of Dinosaur Repellent: drink it if your party is attacked by a pack of dinosaurs, and they'll eat you last.
beats.gist: Carl's loot holds a Potion of Dinosaur Repellent, which makes dinosaurs eat the drinker last.

beats.headline: Forty pairs of eyes
beats.text: Mongo rushes out of the gate into the jungle with Donut on his back, and the shrieks that follow are not his. Carl has received ten dinosaur repellent potions since the end of the previous floor, and the description is vague about what the potion actually does. He took one earlier. Donut refused, afraid it would make her pet shy away from her, and he regrets not making her take it. In the clearing ahead, forty velociraptors surround Donut and Mongo, every one of them watching Mongo.
beats.gist: Donut and Mongo rush into the jungle, where forty velociraptors surround them, all watching Mongo.

beats.headline: On the bathroom counter
beats.text: Past the security checks, the crawlers are ushered into the boudoir, a glorified locker room with cubicles and bathrooms on the way into the ballroom. Carl covers a bathroom counter with dinosaur repellent potions and half-splat potions, with a note: store the half-splat ready in your inventory and, if you have not already, drink the dinosaur one now. They may have to flee quickly, he warns, with loose, prey-driven dinosaurs everywhere. They want those attacking the hunters, not them.
beats.gist: Carl leaves dinosaur repellent and half-splat potions on a bathroom counter for the crawlers.

beats.headline: Stolen and not taken
beats.text: After the boss fight, Carl lies hurt and asks after Lucia and Eva. Lucia teleported away before it started, Donut tells him. Katia says Eva was bitten by a dinosaur and is buried over there, not dead yet, and Katia is looking for her. Eva stole all those dinosaur repellent potions, Donut adds, and she did not even take one.
beats.gist: Eva stole the dinosaur repellent potions, Donut says, but she took none herself and lies bitten and buried.

recap.text: Carl sorts through his loot and finds mostly the usual: junk clothing and weapons, healing and mana restoration potions, a single invisibility potion, hobgoblin dynamite, and his first Good Healing Potions, which Mordecai calls a sign he is progressing nicely. Then he reaches a Potion of Dinosaur Repellent, and Mordecai's uh-oh does not help. Drunk when a pack of dinosaurs attacks, it makes them eat the drinker last.

Mongo rushes out of the gate into the jungle with Donut on his back, and forty velociraptors in the clearing all watch him. Carl took one of his ten dinosaur repellent potions, but Donut refused hers, and he regrets not making her. After the boss fight, Donut says Eva stole all the repellent potions and did not take one, and Katia says a dinosaur bit Eva and she lies buried, not yet dead.

tagline.text: A Ring of Water Breathing is a glowing blue ring that lets its wearer breathe underwater as well as on land, for a point of charisma. Carl, Katia and Tran each get one, and Mordecai warns that it grows gills and makes the skin slimy.
Carl slips the ring on to go into the water after Samantha, and the gills form on his neck at once. Donut is appalled that it costs him only one point of charisma.

description.text: Ring of Water Breathing. If you wear this ring, you can breathe underwater. You can still breathe on land, too. That makes you an amphibian. Did you know that all amphibians swallow their prey whole? That’s such an interesting fact. -1 Charisma

beats.headline: The prize he needed
beats.text: Carl's gold I'm Wet box opens on a prize he wishes he had had all along: a glowing blue ring that twinkles with little sparkles. Katia and Tran received the exact same prize. A Ring of Water Breathing lets you breathe underwater, and on land too, which makes you an amphibian, for a point of charisma. Don't wear that unless you are actually going into water, Mordecai warns as it disappears into the inventory. It makes you grow gills, and it makes your skin slimy.
beats.gist: Carl opens a Ring of Water Breathing, and Mordecai warns him not to wear it on land.

beats.headline: Hit with the ugly stick
beats.text: Samantha thinks it was a trap and says she has just wriggled free. Carl tells Donut to stay where she is; he is going in. He slips the water-breathing ring on his finger and feels the gills form on his neck, and a notice says he has been hit with the ugly stick. Donut is appalled that it only lowered his charisma by one: he is all slimy, and Signet told them to wait. A new explosion rocks the river, bloody water showering from the castle window.
beats.gist: Carl slips on the water-breathing ring, grows gills, and is hit with the ugly stick.

recap.text: Carl's gold I'm Wet box opens on a glowing blue Ring of Water Breathing, a prize he wishes he had had all along. Katia and Tran receive the exact same ring. It lets the wearer breathe underwater and on land, which makes the wearer an amphibian, for a point of charisma. Mordecai warns Carl not to wear it unless he is going into water, because it grows gills and makes the skin slimy.

Carl tells Donut to stay put and slips the water-breathing ring on his finger, and gills form on his neck. A notice says he has been hit with the ugly stick. Donut is appalled that it lowered his charisma by only one, since he is all slimy and Signet told them to wait. A new explosion rocks the river, and bloody water showers from the castle window.

tagline.text: Each of Carl's seven silver Summary Judgement boxes holds a gold piece, a photograph and a Stock Certificate for one share in a company from the home system of one of the plaintiffs who sued him. They are worth about ten credits each, and Mordecai says crawlers should not be getting anything with credit value at all.

King Rust tells Carl that the stock certificate he owns is losing significant value by the moment, now that his daughter has told the whole galaxy the Skull Empire builds backdoors into everything it makes.

description.text: Stock Certificate. The bearer of this instrument now holds one share of common stock in the Sigmund Textiles Foundry, a publicly-traded company based in the Gun-ya system within the Skull Empire and traded via the I.R.F. Last recorded value per share: 10.422 credits.

beats.headline: Seven shares, seven mothers
beats.text: All seven of Carl's silver Summary Judgement boxes open on the same three things: one gold piece, a stock certificate equal to one share, and a photograph. No two certificates look alike. Some are paper, one is an egg covered in writing, another is printed on glass. The first photograph is an ordinary eight by ten of a young orc in an overly flowery dress and a gaudy crown: the mother of Plaintiff #1, Prince Stalwart of the Skull Empire. Mordecai sits there with his beak open. The AI, he thinks, has just given Carl photographs of the mothers of everyone in that lawsuit.
beats.gist: Carl's seven silver boxes each hold a gold piece, a share certificate and a photograph of a mother.

beats.headline: About ten credits each
beats.text: Carl examines one: a share of common stock in the Sigmund Textiles Foundry of the Gun-ya system, within the Skull Empire, last valued at 10.422 credits. Odd, agrees Mordecai. He cannot remember what the I.R.F. stands for, only that it is about the biggest stock exchange in the universe, and crawlers are not even allowed to gamble at the Desperado Club's credit tables. Each certificate is from a company based in a plaintiff's system, as if the AI is needling them. The photographs are valuable too: Carl now knows the seven factions who tried to take the gate from him.
beats.gist: Carl examines seven stock certificates, odd ones from plaintiffs' home systems, and the photographs name seven factions.

beats.headline: Losing value by the moment
beats.text: Donut cannot believe that anyone can scoot onto a satellite circling Venus, press a button and blow up the solar system. Its security is impenetrable, King Rust says, and it will explode if anyone unauthorized tries to break in. But the Skull Empire manufactures the satellites, and builds backdoors into everything it makes so none of it can be used against it. That was a secret until his daughter announced it to the whole galaxy. I'm afraid that stock certificate you own, Carl, is losing significant value by the moment. Carl laughs again.
beats.gist: King Rust says the Skull Empire built backdoors into its satellites, so Donut's stock certificate loses value.

recap.text: Carl opens all seven silver Summary Judgement boxes, and each holds one gold piece, a stock certificate worth one share, and a photograph. No two certificates look alike: some are paper, one is an egg covered in writing, one is printed on glass. The first photograph shows the mother of Prince Stalwart of the Skull Empire, a young orc in a flowery dress and gaudy crown.

Carl laughs again as Donut cannot believe that anyone can scoot onto a satellite circling Venus, press a button and blow up the solar system. King Rust says its security is impenetrable and it will explode if anyone unauthorized tries to break in, but the Skull Empire builds backdoors into everything it makes, a secret his daughter announced to the whole galaxy. He tells Carl that the stock certificate he owns is losing significant value by the moment.

tagline.text: The Twister is the flying house: a beige suburban house from Texas, cut down to its ground floor, hanging in a net under a huge glowing balloon. Louis and Firas fly it on the air currents and named it; Louis wanted Tiddy Twister II, after his van.
The Twister has gone through the portal to the sixth floor with the changeling refugees. Louis and Firas cannot pass that way, and mean to recover it once they have taken the stairs.
Louis and Firas have the Twister back, with a ballista Bonnie built on the side of its yard. The ceiling on this floor is too low for the balloon to clear the trees.
The Twister is gone. With the mantises aboard, the Sledge, who still has its controller, crashes it into the last two guard turrets still firing.

beats.headline: The house gets a name
beats.text: The world rumbles while Mordecai goes to check on something, and Louis says he hopes the Twister is okay. That's what they named the house, Firas explains, and it's parked right outside of town. Louis wanted to call it the Tiddy Twister II, but Firas told him they're trying to be more mature, and Katia wouldn't let them. The original Tiddy Twister was Louis's van. Carl says he thought it was Louis's mom's van.
beats.gist: Louis hopes the Twister is okay, and Firas says that is the house's name.

beats.headline: Riding the storm
beats.text: Donut's Heal Critter says she is too far away from Orthrus, so Carl sends Louis and Firas out to the Twister in the storm and tells Donut to meet them there. Up in the house she casts it, and it works. The house is breaking up, Louis reports; the balloon is slamming back and forth like a bull. It lands with its net ripped to pieces, holes in the yard and water arcing from a severed main. It will fall out of the sky if they don't fix it, Louis calls. Carl looks at the garage.
beats.gist: Donut's Heal Critter works, but the house lands wrecked and Louis says it will fall unless fixed.

beats.headline: Off the edge of the yard
beats.text: With nowhere to take off, Carl talks Louis and Firas into flying the house out over the ocean near the edge of the bubble, so the plane can drop off the edge of the Twister. They pull the drop bear out of the large garage and face it into the wind. Louis lowers the balloon onto the breeze from outside the bubble, and it speeds up. The little biplane rolls off the edge of the yard and drops like a rock until Carl pulls up. The Twister descends back toward the pazuzu village.
beats.gist: Carl talks Louis and Firas into flying the house out, and the plane drops off the edge.

beats.headline: Through the portal
beats.text: Carl doesn't want Louis and Firas leaving bubble 543 and risking the Twister before they have to; if anything happens to the balloon, it screws everything up. When it goes, the journey to Imani and Elle's world is uneventful, changelings coasting alongside as geese. Mordecai insists the portal will not let crawlers pass from floor to floor, so the Twister goes through with the changelings to the sixth floor, without Louis and Firas, who will take the regular stairwell and hope to recover the flying house. Louis frets on chat: Skarn is a good pilot but a little shit, and Bonnie wants to install some upgrades.
beats.gist: Carl keeps Louis and Firas off the Twister, which crosses to the sixth floor with changelings.

beats.headline: A ballista in the yard
beats.text: Louis and Firas have recovered the Twister from the changeling refugees, and Bonnie went with the refugees. Before she did, Firas says, she built a giant crossbow, a ballista, out of the mechanism for the garage door opener and fixed it to the side of the yard. Katia test-fired it, and it blew up a tree. But the ceiling on this floor is low: the balloon is too big to get over the trees, so the house is not very useful.
beats.gist: Louis and Firas recover the Twister, and Firas reports Bonnie's garage-door ballista blew up a tree.

beats.headline: Weedkiller from the deck
beats.text: Louis's Extermination Professional class has an ability called Tent the House, which delivers a potion over a wide area, wider still cast from the deck of the Twister, once every six hours. Loaded with Mordecai's weedkiller, Katia and the others move in on an Odious Creeper using the Twister, and the kill is credited to Crawler Louis Santiago 2, who is not sure he can stomach that again. By the time fifteen more creepers have fallen, Louis has killed three.
beats.gist: Louis's Tent the House ability, cast from the Twister, poisons an Odious Creeper; Louis takes the kill.

beats.headline: Taken by the mantises
beats.text: The ground rumbles with one of Carl's bombs dropped from the Twister; a spotlight finds the airship, and the bomb meant for the mounted elves misses. Then Louis comes running: the mantises have taken the Twister, the changelings have turned to birds and left, and the Sledge had to jump. Sledge has the controller, and Bonnie, the bear cubs and Prudence are okay. Bombs still dangling, he says he can crash the Twister into the other turrets, like a helicopter in GTA. Don't crash the Twister, Louis begs. Carl tells him to do it.
beats.gist: Louis reports the mantises have taken the Twister, and Carl tells him to crash it into the turrets.

beats.headline: Got both
beats.text: In the queen's chamber, the whole palace shakes with one explosion, then a second, louder one, and acorns fall from the inverted tree like hail. Sledge reports in: guard turrets get good, Twister house blow up, got both. Louis wails. Surviving is winning, Louis, Sledge tells him. Everything else is bullshit.
beats.gist: Sledge reports the guard turrets and the Twister house both blown up, and tells Louis surviving is winning.

relations.note: all that was left in the sky when the Wasteland crashed
built a ballista on its yard
at the controls at the end

recap.text: Carl sends Louis and Firas to the Twister in the storm, and Donut's Heal Critter works from up in the house. The house lands with its net ripped to pieces, so Carl talks the pair into flying it out over the ocean, and the little biplane rolls off the yard and drops like a rock until he pulls up. Mordecai insists the portal will not pass crawlers, so the Twister goes through without Louis and Firas.

Louis and Firas get the Twister back from the changeling refugees. Bonnie, who left with them, had built a ballista from the garage door opener's mechanism, and Katia's test shot blew up a tree. Loaded with Mordecai's weedkiller, the Twister carries Katia against an Odious Creeper, and the kill goes to Louis. Then the mantises take the Twister, and Sledge jumps.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Handcuffs are novelty cuffs in red, fuzzy velvet, magically reinforced so that only a strength of 200 can break them. There is no key: Carl locks and unlocks them himself, and can set a safe word.

description.text: Enchanted Handcuffs. My safe word is, "Harder, Daddy." You know what these are. Your mom had a pair in her drawer, and your dad was probably no stranger to these things, either. Used to lock a person's arms together at the wrist. This set of novelty handcuffs is magically reinforced. Requires a strength of at least 200 to break. There's no key. These are locked and unlocked magically by you. You may also institute an optional safe word or phrase that disengages.

beats.headline: The first savage box
beats.text: Carl's first Silver Savage Box is meant for player killers, and he is not looking forward to whatever this is; he wants to avoid getting a skull if he can. He cringes as it opens. A pair of handcuffs pops out, encased in red, fuzzy velvet. They are magically reinforced and need a strength of at least 200 to break, and there is no key: he locks and unlocks them himself, with an optional safe word. Oh for fuck's sake, says Carl, putting the fuzzy handcuffs away.
beats.gist: Carl's first Silver Savage Box holds fuzzy red velvet handcuffs, and he pockets them in disgust.

beats.headline: Cuffed to a pole
beats.text: The elf hunter is going to wake up in seconds. Hunter Killer, asks Donut? No, says Carl: heal him, but I want to talk to him first. He slips a ring on and pulls the enchanted handcuffs from his inventory. Akland comes round handcuffed to a pole, Donut behind him with a magic missile ready. It's not supposed to be like this, he pleads. He is just an accountant who did well at fantasy hunter camp, and they offered him money. Carl tells him about the world he had. Then the system tells Carl he has marked Akland.
beats.gist: Carl heals the elf hunter Akland, cuffs him to a pole, and tells him about his lost world.

beats.headline: Wrists too thick
beats.text: D'Nadia sent her three guards out as the explosive spiders came. Two are splattered over the wall. The third, an enormous samurai rhinoceros she somehow hired, cast a shield, but the concussions knocked him out for ten minutes. Carl's first instinct is to kill him, but he holds off. He tries to handcuff him, but the rhino's wrists are too thick, so he duct-tapes his wrists and ankles instead and tells Rend to guard him. Don't eat him.
beats.gist: Carl cuffs nothing: the rhino's wrists are too thick, so he duct-tapes him and leaves Rend guarding.

beats.headline: A prisoner for a bounty
beats.text: Mork, a lisping ram cleric of Hellik, jabs a shaking finger at Prepotente: there is a Holy Crusade Bounty on him, and he dares enter this club? Carl raises a hand in peace and points to Prepotente's wrists, shackled in fuzzy handcuffs that are not locked. He has captured him and is here to collect the bounty. Prepotente throws himself to the floor with an exaggerated flourish. The handcuffs jingle ominously, and Carl fears they will fly off his wrists. I have been caught! My goose has been cooked!
beats.gist: Carl presents Prepotente in unlocked fuzzy handcuffs as a captive, and Prepotente flops dramatically to the floor.

recap.text: Carl dreads his first Silver Savage Box, which is meant for player killers, and he hopes to avoid a skull. He cringes as it opens and a pair of handcuffs in red, fuzzy velvet pops out. They are magically reinforced and need a strength of at least 200 to break. They have no key, so he locks and unlocks them himself, with an optional safe word. Oh for fuck's sake, says Carl, and puts them away.

Carl slips on a ring, pulls the enchanted handcuffs from his inventory, and has Donut heal the elf hunter, because he wants to talk to him first. Akland wakes cuffed to a pole, Donut behind him with a magic missile ready. He pleads that he is only an accountant who did well at fantasy hunter camp, and they offered him money. Carl tells him about the world he had, and the system tells Carl he has marked Akland.

Carl finds the last of D'Nadia's three guards, an enormous samurai rhinoceros, knocked out for ten minutes by the concussions that splattered the other two. He wants to kill him, holds off, finds the rhino's wrists too thick for the handcuffs, and duct-tapes his wrists and ankles instead. Rend is told not to eat him.

entities.name: Ping tome
entities.role: Carl's spell book from a quest box

tagline.text: The platinum quest box for saving a puppy held a magical tome, a black leather hardback warm to the touch with a skull on the cover. Opened, it taught Carl Ping.

beats.headline: On the same wavelength
beats.text: Everyone else has opened their platinum quest boxes, mostly spell books. After his first savage box spits out a pair of fuzzy handcuffs, Carl opens his. It holds a magical tome. He turns it over in his hands: a black leather hardback, warm to the touch, with a skull on the cover. He looks up at the ceiling and grins. It's nice to see they're on the same wavelength for once. Opening the book makes it glow, and the spell adds itself to his list: Ping, five mana. It won't find mobs or crawlers, which is disappointing, but it will find NPCs, and more importantly elites and hunters.
beats.gist: Carl's tome adds Ping, a five-mana spell that finds NPCs, elites and hunters.

recap.text: Carl opens his platinum quest box after his first savage box spat out a pair of fuzzy handcuffs. Inside is a tome in black leather with a skull on the cover, warm to the touch, and he grins at the ceiling at being on the same wavelength for once. The tome glows when opened and adds Ping to his list for five mana. Ping finds no mobs or crawlers, but it finds NPCs, elites and hunters.

tagline.text: Rockard's Ring of Sniping is an amber-stoned ring that marks on the map every creature under half health and every one wearing magical gear, which makes stealing kills simple. Carl pulls it off the arm he tore from Quan Ch and puts it on.

description.text: Rockard’s Ring of Sniping. This amber-stoned ring is named after Rockard, one of the dungeon’s most infamous crawlers. This orcish warrior was known for his uncanny ability to swoop in at the last moment and steal glory from other crawlers, gaining the best loot and experience. Everybody hated him. It was great! Fun fact. This guy led his season’s top 10 list until he was knifed in his sleep by his own mother. Luckily for you, crawlers can’t be killed by other crawlers in saferooms anymore. A shame, really. Wearing this ring imbues the following benefits: The Ripe benefit. The Loaded benefit.

beats.headline: Off Quan's arm
beats.text: Carl is still holding the arm he ripped off Quan Ch, and it has three rings on its fingers. The first is a simple plus-two ring of strength, which becomes his fifth ring. The second is Rockard's Ring of Sniping. Ripe marks every creature under half health on the map; no wonder Quan had his reputation. Loaded marks every non-hidden creature wearing magical gear. Carl adds it to his finger. The last, a gold band carved For Daddy inside, he pushes back onto the finger.
beats.gist: Carl takes Rockard's Ring of Sniping from the arm he ripped off Quan Ch.

relations.note: on the arm Carl tore off

recap.text: Carl is still holding the arm he tore off Quan Ch, and three rings sit on its fingers. He takes the plus-two ring of strength as his fifth ring. He puts on Rockard's Ring of Sniping, whose Ripe marks every creature under half health on the map and whose Loaded marks every non-hidden creature wearing magical gear, which explains Quan's reputation. He pushes the last ring, a gold band carved For Daddy inside, back onto the finger.

tagline.text: The Tome of Twinkle Toes, from Donut's platinum quest box, teaches a cheap spell that makes Mongo, or any other minion, run really fast for as many seconds as her intelligence.
Twinkle Toes lets Mongo outrun the dune buggy, and Donut practices it to level it up. Mongo screeches with joy whenever she casts it.
Hedy the gremlin says pet spells do not work on special mounts, so Twinkle Toes will be no help to a biological vehicle on this floor.

beats.headline: Platinum spell books
beats.text: Carl has been putting off his boxes to have a distraction. Everyone else has already opened their platinum quest boxes, and most of what they got was spell books. Donut's holds a tome of Twinkle Toes, a cheap spell that makes Mongo, or any other minion, run really fast for as many seconds as her intelligence level. She is pretty excited about it. Katia gets a spell called Hanzo, Louis and Firas get spellbooks too, and Gwen gets a new spear.
beats.gist: Donut opens a tome of Twinkle Toes, a spell that makes Mongo run fast.

beats.headline: Faster than the buggy
beats.text: Carl drives the chariot down the main road while Donut rides Mongo alongside. Her Twinkle Toes spell lets Mongo run faster even than the dune buggy, and she has been practicing it, trying to level it up. Mongo loves going fast and screeches with joy whenever she casts the spell. Carl stops a few times to plant claymore-like mines that only hunters will trigger.
beats.gist: Donut casts Twinkle Toes, and Mongo outruns the dune buggy, screeching with joy.

beats.headline: Two riders, two spells
beats.text: Bautista drives the carriage, with Carl, Imani, Katia and others aboard. Donut rushes alongside to the left astride Mongo with Twinkle Toes active, Mongo decidedly more buff with the Muscle Mommy benefit. On the other side Dong rides Gonk, his own Twinkle Toes active, making the swamp yak run astonishingly fast, while Bigs whoops on the yak's head. Jamal holds up the rear on his spider legs, spurting little bursts of flame.
beats.gist: Donut and Dong ride Mongo and Gonk, each with Twinkle Toes active, while Bautista's carriage and Jamal follow.

beats.headline: Not for special mounts
beats.text: The party leader must choose a vehicle, mechanical or biological. Donut thinks the animal is the best choice: she has the Twinkle Toes spell and a level 15 Heal Critter, though Mongo won't like another animal in the party. Pet spells don't work on special mounts, Hedy the gremlin gasps from the garage floor, and clocks the other gremlin with a mallet. Neither Twinkle Toes nor Heal Critter will work on them.
beats.gist: Donut wants Twinkle Toes and Heal Critter on an animal mount, but Hedy says they fail.

relations.note: he has the spell too

recap.text: Carl puts off opening his boxes to have a distraction, while everyone else has already opened their platinum quest boxes, mostly spells. Donut's holds a tome of Twinkle Toes, a cheap spell that makes Mongo, or any other minion, run really fast for as many seconds as her intelligence level, and she is pretty excited. Katia gets a spell called Hanzo, Louis and Firas get spells too, and Gwen gets a new spear.

Carl drives the chariot down the main road while Donut rides Mongo alongside. Her Twinkle Toes spell makes Mongo run faster than the dune buggy, and she has been practicing it to level it up. Mongo screeches with joy each time she casts it. Carl stops a few times to plant claymore-like mines that only hunters will trigger.

Donut rides Mongo to the left of Bautista's carriage, her Twinkle Toes active and Mongo more buff with the Muscle Mommy benefit. On the other side Dong rides Gonk, the swamp yak, which runs astonishingly fast under his own Twinkle Toes while Bigs whoops on its head. Jamal holds up the rear on his spider legs, spurting little bursts of flame.

Donut, who has the Twinkle Toes spell and a level 15 Heal Critter, argues that the animal is the best choice when the party leader must pick a vehicle, mechanical or biological, though Mongo won't like another animal in the party. Hedy the gremlin gasps from the garage floor that pet spells don't work on special mounts, then clocks the other gremlin with a mallet. Neither Twinkle Toes nor Heal Critter will work on them.

tagline.text: The Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot is a head-throwing attachment made for Carl by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network and sent in an emergency platinum benefactor box. On the end of his xistera it throws Samantha five hundred metres for every point of his strength, and taking it off brings her back.
The extension recalls Samantha the moment it comes off Carl's hand, so he does not wear it all day, and she roams free instead.
Dropping the extension brings Samantha back, and what she holds can come with her: once it brought Sister Ines, the sea snake she rode and thousands of seals, crabs and fish, living and undead.

description.text: Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot. Head-throwing attachment. This is a unique item! This item was created especially for Crawler Carl by The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, Intergalactic NFC. Attaches to the end of a xistera. Allows for the tossing of a head. This special edition head tosser is custom made to fit decapitated love doll heads. When tossing a head of a withering spirit, the distance traveled will be greatly enhanced. (500 meters x Strength.) Tossed head will be magically returned once the extension slot is removed from xistera.

beats.headline: Fifty kilometres of Samantha
beats.text: An Emergency Platinum Benefactor Box arrives from the Pacifist Action Network as a feral demon, Slit, comes for Samantha with a crackling whip. Carl shoves Samantha face-first into the extension's round slot. She fits perfectly. He turns ninety degrees and chucks her with all his might, well over a hundred strength with his gear: over fifty kilometres. Slit turns to follow. Once Slit is gone, he pulls the extension off and into his inventory, and Samantha pops into existence at his feet, screaming that it was her kill. Taking it out again, he runs a finger over the wicker-like stuff and its tiny inscription: made for Crawler Carl, with design approval by the network's president of Outreach Operations.
beats.gist: Carl shoves Samantha into the extension slot and chucks her fifty kilometres; Slit follows.

beats.headline: Two rockets and a ping
beats.text: Two missiles duct-taped to her head, Samantha lies face down in the installed extension. Carl drinks a levitation potion, then Major Charlie for thirty seconds of extra intelligence, rises up through the green cloud and pings: two hunters in a clearing a kilometre and a half northeast of town. Go get 'em. He lobs her at them, the rockets flare over the clearing, and she disappears into the trees to a distant detonation. Bring me back, she messages. He drops the extension and she pops up at his feet, hair on fire, with the ankle of the second, unconscious elf clamped in her teeth.
beats.gist: Samantha rides the head-tosser, and Carl lobs her at two hunters, who fall to her rockets and teeth.

beats.headline: Recalled from the river
beats.text: Carl loaded Samantha into the extension with an alarm ball taped to her head and threw her upstream, to shout when it went off and aim for the castle. The extension has stayed on his arm since. Now Miss Nadine breaks for the water, and he has to take it off before he dives in. Samantha, I gotta teleport you back. No, she messages, I almost have him. He pulls the extension into his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl pockets the extension to dive after Miss Nadine, while Samantha protests.

beats.headline: Everything comes back
beats.text: The plan was for Samantha to roll up to Sister Ines and bite onto her; Carl would drop the extension and summon them both, and a card battle would follow. That is not what happens. When he drops the xistera extension, everything lands around him and Donut in about a quarter of a mile each way: Samantha, Sister Ines, the massive snake she rides, around a thousand zombie baby seals, five thousand zombie crabs, five hundred zombie adult seals, a great many living ones, what seems like every fish in the world, and an alarming number of corpses.
beats.gist: Samantha's plan to bite Sister Ines fails; dropping the extension lands everyone and everything around Carl and Donut.

beats.headline: A few feet
beats.text: Entering Havana, Carl teleports onto a spider automaton and crushes it; the other three scatter. Samantha kept her word, for once, and the fourth spider is still inside her. He unsummons the xistera extension still at the end of his hand, and she blinks and reappears right next to him, teleported only a few feet. A bolt of lightning crashes out through the capitol's front door.
beats.gist: Carl unsummons the xistera extension, and Samantha reappears right beside him, teleported only a few feet.

beats.headline: Back from the volcano
beats.text: Carl fired Samantha up and out of Larracos to Emberus in the volcano, telling her he cannot bring her back while the god is touching her. Now she messages: he's not touching me anymore, bring me back. Carl drops the xistera, and Samantha clunks to the ground, heavy and smoking. If he thought she had been burned before, this is ten times worse. He barely recognizes her.
beats.gist: Carl drops the xistera, and Samantha, back from the volcano, hits the ground heavy and smoking, barely recognizable.

relations.note: recalled along with Samantha

recap.text: Samantha arrives in an Emergency Platinum Benefactor Box from the Pacifist Action Network just as a feral demon, Slit, comes at her with a crackling whip. Carl shoves her face-first into the extension's round slot, where she fits perfectly, then turns ninety degrees and throws her over fifty kilometres. Slit turns to follow. Carl pulls the extension into his inventory, and Samantha pops out at his feet, screaming that the kill was hers.

Carl tapes two missiles to Samantha's head, drinks a levitation potion and Major Charlie, and rises through the green cloud to ping two hunters. He lobs her at them, and she vanishes into the trees to a distant detonation. She reappears at his feet, hair on fire, an unconscious elf's ankle in her teeth. When Miss Nadine breaks for the water, Carl pulls the extension into his inventory.

Carl drops the xistera extension to summon Samantha and Sister Ines for a card battle, and everything within a quarter of a mile lands around him and Donut: the massive snake, five thousand zombie crabs, alarmingly many corpses. In Havana he teleports onto a spider automaton and crushes it, and the other three scatter. He unsummons the extension, and Samantha reappears a few feet away. A bolt of lightning crashes out of the capitol's front door.

Carl fires Samantha up and out of Larracos to Emberus in the volcano, telling her he cannot bring her back while the god is touching her. Now she messages that the god is not touching her anymore and asks to be brought back. Carl drops the xistera, and Samantha clunks to the ground, heavy and smoking. He thought she had been burned before, but this is ten times worse, and he barely recognizes her.

tagline.text: The Phase Lava Rock potion is one of Mordecai's brews from the toraline yam. For one minute its drinker can move through lava and lava rock, and a creature made of lava rock cannot touch him.

beats.headline: One minute through rock
beats.text: With under an hour to collapse and the saferooms closed, Carl calls to the camouflaged lava rock crawler hiding somewhere in the sand: he knows Maggie is in there. They told her about the potion, she answers from under the dune. He explains the yam from the sponsor box, which Mordecai worked out with Samantha's help, and what Mordecai made from it, a Phase Lava Rock potion. Once he takes it, Chris's arms will go right through him. It only lasts a minute, so he edges along the sand toward the winding box and waits. They only need to move it five feet.
beats.gist: Carl tells hidden Maggie that Mordecai's potion will let Chris's arms pass through him for one minute.

beats.headline: A hand into Chris's head
beats.text: Chris erupts from the ground beside the winding box. Carl slams the phase potion and rushes him as he hurls the box away, its two watches flying in different directions. Carl reaches into Chris's head, through the rock, to the one solid thing in it, a palm-sized worm lodged in his brain, and pulls. It bites his palm and burrows into his arm. He waits out the last two seconds of his potion countdown and drinks the double-healing potion that cured his parasites on the third floor. The worm bursts out of his neck, and Mongo grabs it.
beats.gist: Carl yanks the worm from Chris's brain, then a potion forces it out of him.

relations.note: Maggie, the worm in Chris's brain

recap.text: Carl tells Maggie, the lava rock crawler hiding in the sand, about the Phase Lava Rock potion Mordecai made from the sponsor-box yam. When Chris erupts beside the winding box, Carl slams the potion, reaches through the rock into his head, and pulls out a palm-sized worm. It bites his palm and burrows into his arm, so he drinks the double-healing potion, and the worm bursts from his neck into Mongo's grasp.

tagline.text: A gold Hunter-Killer Box is the reward for The Hand that Claws the Master, an achievement for permanently killing a non-crawler biological. The achievement may be awarded more than once, but the boxes come only on the sixth floor, and Carl's first batch is thirty-four.
Each Hunter-Killer Box holds gold and the severed hand of a hunter; Carl's thirty-four open one after another, every one with a thousand gold more than the last.

beats.headline: A red dagger, then thirty-four
beats.text: Donut has a new symbol after her name, a single red dagger with its point up, like the Desperado Club's logo: Hunter Killer X 1, for a magic missile fired while they were running away. Carl dives into his notifications. The Hand that Claws the Master (x35): he has permanently killed a non-crawler biological, and the AI admits it may have slipped an extra one in. The reward is a Gold Hunter-Killer Box (x34), with a note that the achievement may be awarded more than once, but the boxes only on the sixth floor. He has killed thirty-four.
beats.gist: Donut earns a Hunter Killer mark for a magic missile, and Carl is awarded thirty-four Gold Boxes.

beats.headline: A row down to the wall
beats.text: Donut has a Hunter-Killer box of her own but wants Carl to open his first, because thirty-four will be more dramatic. They line up in a row floating all the way to the wall, and everybody stops to watch. The first holds 1,000 gold and the mangled claw of Xindy, the mantis he blew out of the sky; the second, 2,000 and the hand of Chin'dua; the third, 3,000 and an orc's hand. Each adds a thousand, 595,000 gold in all, and the Emberus fountain chimes: Carl owes it 29,750. Donut's own box gives her a gray hand and, to her outrage, only 1,000 gold.
beats.gist: Carl opens his Hunter-Killer box first, and each box adds a thousand gold; Donut's holds only 1,000.

beats.headline: Fourteen more than expected
beats.text: Most of Carl's new prize boxes are low-tier adventurer boxes, but fourteen are Hunter Killer boxes, including the one from Future Hunter the orc, several more than he expected. He seems to have been credited for three nebs and three mantises killed by another mantis while she was enraged, though not for her own death at the hands of her people. Those six earn boxes and no experience. He now has 52 hunting trophies and 637,000 gold from those boxes alone.
beats.gist: Carl receives fourteen Hunter Killer boxes, including six for kills by others that earn no experience.

relations.note: his fountain takes its share of the gold

recap.text: Donut has a red dagger after her name for a magic missile fired while they were running away. Carl opens his Hunter-Killer boxes in a floating row to the wall, from Xindy's mangled claw and 1,000 gold to 595,000 gold in all, and owes the Emberus fountain 29,750. Donut's own box gives her a gray hand and only 1,000 gold, to her outrage. Fourteen more Hunter Killer boxes leave him 52 hunting trophies.

tagline.text: A Hunting Trophy is a hunter's severed hand, and one comes in every Hunter Killer box Carl earns for a kill. The hand is a prize ticket for a counter that opens at the Butcher's Masquerade.
At Chaco's prize counter, hunters' hands are the currency. One buys a 25-pack of potions, thirty buy a future floor boon, and Carl arrives with sixty-six.

description.text: Hunting Trophy. It's the hand of a hunter. Gross. You own 34 of these items. You ever go to one of those arcade pizza joints as a child?
