You're usually there because it's some other kid's birthday, or worse, because your parent hates raising you so much they'd do anything just to keep you distracted for ten minutes in exchange for a pitcher of watered-down beer. The whole place is chaos. …

beats.headline: Thirty-four boxes of hands
beats.text: Thirty-four Hunter Killer boxes line up in a row that floats all the way to the wall, and each holds gold and a hand. The first is the mangled claw of Xindy, the mantis Carl blew out of the sky with his rockets. The second is the hand of Chin'dua, the drunk draconian. The third is an orc's. None of them wear rings. All that, Donut says, and it's a bunch of horrible hands. At least it's not tongues: Lucia Mar collects tongues.
beats.gist: Thirty-four Hunter Killer boxes hold gold and a hand each, and Donut calls them horrible hands.

beats.headline: A prize ticket
beats.text: Carl pulls the mantis claw from his inventory and examines it while Donut opens her own box, and a gray hand pops out. The description wanders through arcade pizza joints and a prize counter where forty dollars of tickets buy five cents of bubble gum, then gets to the point: the hand is the ticket. The prize counter where it may be exchanged opens at the Butcher's Masquerade, near the end of this floor. The cheapest award costs a single hand. Transfer or sell one, and it reverts to some dude's appendage.
beats.gist: A Hunting Trophy, a hunter's hand, works as a prize ticket, and the cheapest award costs one hand.

beats.headline: JayGee's hand, held high
beats.text: A trap Carl left kills a hunter, and the gold Hunter Killer box holds 35,000 gold and the fat, mottled gray hand of a hunter named JayGee. Carl holds the trophy up to the ceiling and waves it: if JayGee's family or friends are watching, they can go fuck themselves. You shouldn't do that, Mordecai says. People out there have long memories. Good, Carl says. He doesn't want them to ever forget.
beats.gist: JayGee's trap-killed hunter yields 35,000 gold and a hand; Carl waves it, defying warnings of long memories.

beats.headline: Fifty-two trophies now
beats.text: Most of Carl's new boxes are low-tier adventurer boxes, but fourteen are Hunter Killer boxes, including the one from Future Hunter the orc. He now has fifty-two hunting trophies.
beats.gist: Fifty-two hunting trophies sit in Carl's inventory after new boxes, fourteen of them Hunter Killer boxes.

beats.headline: Sixty-six hands to spend
beats.text: Chaco the Bard stands behind the prize counter in the ballroom. You currently have 66 hunter hands, he tells Carl. Wow. Every purchase arrives as a prize box, and upgrades are installed at once. The items turn on a vertical carousel as miniature holograms. A single hand buys a 25-pack of good healing or mana potions; two buy one upgrade from a row, plus ten percent to a lowest stat, plus five percent to a highest, or plus two to a random combat skill or spell; three and five buy potions and scrolls by the dozen; thirty buy a future floor boon; fifty, full sets of armor. One prize costs a hundred hands.
beats.gist: Chaco the Bard's prize counter sells items for hunter hands, and Carl has 66 to spend.

recap.text: Carl pulls the mantis claw of Xindy from his inventory while Donut opens a box of her own, and a gray hand pops out. Its description says the hand is a ticket for the prize counter at the Butcher's Masquerade, where the cheapest award costs one hand. A trap Carl left kills a hunter, and he holds up JayGee's hand and tells JayGee's friends to go fuck themselves. Chaco the Bard says Carl has 66 hands to spend.

entities.name: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home

tagline.text: Carl's biggest bomb yet: a broken live ammo ball about five feet tall, filled with explosive and Mordecai's Nitro Sludge, welded shut, imbued with Fear and set in a cart for Bomo to pull. The simulator says it flattens everything within a third of a mile.
Kicked out of a saferoom door at Vrah's mantises, the wheeled bomb kills the last three of her mantis warriors, explosion protection and all. Vrah gets away.

description.text: Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home – Wheeled Bomb. Type: High Yield Thermobaric Explosive. Also imbues Fear within blast radius. Effect: I hope you're paid up on your homeowner's insurance. Status: 250. Fortified. Boom.

beats.headline: A bomb for Bomo
beats.text: The plan: send Bomo out of the personal space into the Zockau saferoom with a very large bomb, step outside, and level the town with half an hour on the timer. The bomb starts from blocks of Nitro Sludge Mordecai left on the sapper's table, a by-product of a shield potion that look like squares of uncooked ramen: inert, but each the equivalent of several hundred pounds of ammonium nitrate when vaporized hot enough. Carl finds the mix by trial and error and packs it into a broken live ammo ball, an egg-shaped clamshell, welded shut. It stands about five feet tall, so he builds a cart Bomo can pull, and adds Fear, because why not.
beats.gist: Carl packs Nitro Sludge into a welded clamshell and builds Bomo a cart.

beats.headline: A knife in the door
beats.text: Minutes before the hunters are loosed, Carl pulls the cart from the bomber's studio to the door. Bomo will open it, Donut will cast Clockwork Triplicate so a clockwork Bomo appears in the space outside, and the clockwork one will roll the bomb out. Bomo opens the door, and a note is stuck to the outside with a knife. Vrah: every hunter is now protected from further explosions, so he would only be killing his precious NPCs, and she has ordered the town guards to worship Emberus. Sorry, Bomo, Carl says. They will save him and the bomb for another time. He writes come and get it on the note and tosses it out.
beats.gist: Carl plans a clockwork Bomo decoy to roll out the bomb, but finds a knifed note and replies.

beats.headline: Out the saferoom door
beats.text: Carl rams a gonorrhea arrow into Vrah's neck just before her shield pops up, and he and Donut vault into the saferoom. The wheeled bomb is right there at the door, the one he wanted to use to level Zockau, with the Sledge peering out at two mantises rushing toward them. Cover your ears, Carl shouts, kicks it out the door and slams it. Donut has been over this: she can't cover her... Bam. The saferoom rocks and everyone rolls like billiard balls. The blast kills the three remaining mantises despite their protection against explosions, an ursine guy and a bunch of mobs in the woods. Lucia has got away, and so has Vrah, rocketing into the air.
beats.gist: Carl kicks a wheeled bomb out the saferoom door; it kills three mantises and mobs, but Vrah escapes.

beats.headline: Now the size of a thermos
beats.text: In a very narrow room, against three guards moving as if fast-forwarded, Carl drops his second-largest bomb. Its first version was Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home, used on the sixth floor. This one packs about the same punch without the Fear, self-contained in a device the size of a thermos instead of one so big it needed wheels, a thermobaric blast that incinerates anything within a hundred meters. Louis has fifty of them on Party Planner, no more because the explosive dust is a pain to make. The AI has helpfully named it The Waffle Maker.
beats.gist: Carl drops his second-largest bomb, a thermos-sized thermobaric device, on three fast-moving guards in a narrow room.

relations.note: meant to pull it
her last mantis warriors

recap.text: Carl plans to send Bomo out with a five-foot egg-shaped bomb of Nitro Sludge, but a knife pins a note to the door: Vrah has protected every hunter from explosions. Carl writes come and get it on the note and tosses it out. Then he kicks the same bomb out the saferoom door at two rushing mantises and slams it. The blast kills the three remaining mantises, an ursine guy and a bunch of mobs.

Carl drops his second-largest bomb in a very narrow room, against three guards moving as if fast-forwarded. It is the thermos-sized version of Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home, the wheeled bomb used on the sixth floor, with about the same punch and no Fear. Its thermobaric blast incinerates anything within a hundred meters. Louis keeps fifty on Party Planner, and the AI has named it The Waffle Maker.

entities.name: Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie
aka: Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie

tagline.text: With the ursine town she renames Point Mongo comes a collar charm Donut must wear to order its guards: one tiny turquoise gem for the town, plus eight dexterity, plus four intelligence, the Snitch skill and 3,592 gold every ten days. She hates it, because it replaces her butterfly charm.
A second, red gem hangs on Donut's leadership charm now, for a small settlement: a little intelligence and dexterity, a spear skill she can never use, and only 403 gold every ten days.

description.text: Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie The middle size of the chains of leadership, this pendant signifies you as a member of the elite. Each jewel encrusted upon this charm represents a settlement owned and controlled by the bearer. If one still maintains a settlement's jewel upon the collapse of the level, the holder of this necklace will permanently receive a tax stipend every ten days from that settlement based on size and population. In addition, each gem will impart additional benefits based on the town. In order to upgrade this necklace, one must first conquer an Extra-Large-sized Settlement. Upgraded necklaces will also upgrade all existing gems. …

beats.headline: The gem is turquoise
beats.text: Donut likes her butterfly charm. It makes fairies like her, it is part of her fit, and stupid Angel the cocker spaniel had four or five tags on her collar. The system only lets a crawler wear so many magical items, Carl says, and the new one is better. It's ugly, says Donut, and the gem is turquoise: does she look like an elderly woman in a bingo hall? She does not need it to rename the Large Ursine Settlement Point Mongo, but to order the guards about she must wear it. One gem, Plain Turquoise, Point Mongo: plus eight dexterity, plus four intelligence, Snitch at level ten, and 3,592 gold in taxes every ten days.
beats.gist: Donut keeps her butterfly charm but must wear the ugly turquoise mayoral charm to order Point Mongo's guards.

beats.headline: Nobody likes a snitch
beats.text: The charm's gem comes with Snitch, a skill rather than a spell. Inside any settlement it alerts all the town's guards, who start moving to her. At level five one guard is teleported to her at once, at level ten it is five, and at ten they can also be summoned up to a kilometer outside a town she owns. There is no cooldown, but the System warns her not to abuse it: these guard guys get really cranky. Donut huffs, mumbles, and changes out the charms.
beats.gist: Donut's charm gem carries Snitch, which summons town guards to her, and the System warns against abuse.

beats.headline: Patted down by gnolls
beats.text: Two gnoll security guards with diver's flippers tied at their waists search Carl and Donut, then leave through a hatch in the ceiling. The one bent over Donut clutches her collar charm and examines it closely. It used to be a butterfly, Donut tells him, but now it's this ugly thing. Ghastly, she knows. He lets it go, declares them clear, and appears to scratch her under the chin on his way out.
beats.gist: Donut's collar charm, once a butterfly, is examined by a gnoll guard before he clears them.

beats.headline: A red gem, and 403 gold
beats.text: A red gem has been added to Donut's leadership charm, for a small-sized settlement. It gives plus two to intelligence, plus one to dexterity and a few points in some spear-throwing skill she will never be able to use, which annoys her, especially since its tax stipend is only 403 gold every ten days.
beats.gist: Donut's charm gets a red gem: small stat bonuses, a useless spear skill, and a 403-gold stipend.

relations.note: Carl's own leadership charm, a necklace

recap.text: Donut swaps her butterfly charm for the Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie, which she calls ugly because its gem is turquoise, and which she must wear to order the guards about. The gem, Plain Turquoise for Point Mongo, gives plus eight dexterity, plus four intelligence, the Snitch skill and 3,592 gold in taxes every ten days. A gnoll guard examines the charm and lets it go.

tagline.text: A pack of twenty trap add-ons called Fail Safes, the prize in a Trapmaster box Carl earns when one of his roadside traps kills a hunter. Each one tells him if its trap is ever disabled or set off.

beats.headline: A trap-leaving reward
beats.text: A sudden group of notifications: a trap Carl left has killed a hunter, a gold Hunter Killer Box, and the achievement Insurgent, for an explosive device left along a well-travelled path that killed its intended target. Too bad he didn't get to see it, because he is a trap-leaving bitch. The reward is a Gold Trapmaster Box. He cannot believe it worked; he placed that one after the bugbear settlement. The hunter-killer box holds 35,000 gold and a hand. The Trapmaster box holds a very useful mod, a pack of twenty trap add-ons called Fail Safes, which will send him a notification if a trap is ever disabled or set off.
beats.gist: Carl's trap kills a hunter, earning the Insurgent achievement and a Gold Trapmaster Box of twenty Fail Safes.

recap.text: A trap Carl left after the bugbear settlement has killed a hunter. The explosive device, set on a well-travelled path, earns him the achievement Insurgent, a gold Hunter Killer Box and a Gold Trapmaster Box. The first holds 35,000 gold and a hand. The second holds twenty trap add-ons called Fail Safes, which notify him when a trap is disabled or set off.

tagline.text: Carl takes nine potions of Levitation off a dead hunter. They raise the drinker into the air for twice their intelligence in seconds, though nobody says how high one can go or what happens if it runs out on the way down.

A Levitation potion moves its drinker up and down on a slider and nothing more. Mordecai calls them dangerous: they will not stop a fall that already has momentum, so treat it like standing on thin ice.
Carl drinks his last Levitation potion at a railing in Larracos and goes straight up out of Larracos.

beats.headline: Nine off a dead hunter
beats.text: The hunter Bravvo was using one of these to scout Point Mongo when he caught a missile to the face. Hunters carry slots, not bottomless inventories, so his loot is thin: thirty good health potions, thirty good mana refills, a longsword for the sell pile, clothes, and his naked corpse. The only real prize is a set of nine potions of Levitation. Not as good as flying potions, they let the drinker rise into the air for intelligence times two seconds. It is not clear how high one can go, or what happens if the potion runs out before you have lowered yourself.
beats.gist: Carl finds nine Levitation potions on the dead hunter Bravvo, each lifting the drinker briefly.

beats.headline: Up and down on a slider
beats.text: Two or three elf hunters have set up a catapult and are walking gas-filled rocks across the town, and Carl has Samantha loaded face down in the xistera. He drinks the first potion. A slider appears in his interface, up and down only, with a sixty-second countdown, and he realises he has done this in the wrong order. His feet rise a foot, and tapping the air feels like standing on glass. Mordecai has stressed how dangerous these are: momentum will still drop you, so they are no substitute for feather fall unless taken before the jump. Treat it like thin ice. Carl hovers, waiting out his potion timer.
beats.gist: Carl drinks the potion, rises a foot, and hovers through its sixty-second countdown.

beats.headline: Knocked out of the sky
beats.text: In a freezing downpour, Carl needs to see the sparks Miriam Dom is shooting into the air. He downs one of the potions of Levitation and pushes the slider up through the trees, his cloak billowing. Far behind him the night glows with a big fire, and he reckons Donut has set the whole forest aflame. The sparks show two kilometres south. Then a screeching, frothing form slams into him from the side, the levitation snaps off at once, and he pinwheels down out of the sky until he freezes in midair to pounding EDM music.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a Levitation potion to find Miriam Dom's sparks, but something slams him from the side.

beats.headline: A look over the fog
beats.text: The park ahead is several blocks wide and full of red dots, and Sister Ines says every one of them is undead. Carl uses one of his dwindling supply of levitate potions to get a better view from above. The roiling fog hides everything, but from that height he can see the dots wandering aimlessly, which lends weight to Donut's zombie theory, and the spire at the centre of the square is a familiar one: a Club Vanquisher.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a levitation potion to see over the fog and spots a Club Vanquisher spire.

beats.headline: The last one
beats.text: The final messages from Toyotomi and Bomo come in, and Carl does not think. He runs past Juice Box and the Semeru dwarves, punches a zarogoth out of the way at the railing, and drinks the final Levitation potion in his inventory as dozens of arms reach for him. He shoots straight up, pushing it to the limit, and its apex carries him up and out of Larracos, still a good hundred metres short of the edge of Shanty Town. Instead of aiming, he drops an entire inventory folder of bombs toward the Piccadilly.
beats.gist: Carl drinks his last Levitation potion and rockets up out of Larracos, short of Shanty Town's edge.

recap.text: Carl drinks the first of Bravvo's nine Levitation potions with Samantha loaded face down in the xistera and elf hunters walking gas-filled rocks across the town. A slider appears, his feet rise a foot, and he realises he has drunk it in the wrong order. In a freezing downpour, he drinks another and pushes the slider up through the trees to see Miriam Dom's sparks. Something screeching slams him, the levitation snaps off, and he pinwheels down.

Carl, facing a park several blocks wide and full of red dots that Sister Ines says are all undead, drinks one of his dwindling levitate potions to see it from above. The fog hides everything below, but he can see the dots wandering aimlessly, which lends support to Donut's zombie theory. The spire at the centre of the square is a Club Vanquisher.

Carl hears the last messages from Toyotomi and Bomo and stops thinking. He runs past Juice Box and the Semeru dwarves, punches a zarogoth away at the railing, and drinks the final Levitation potion while dozens of arms reach for him. It carries him straight up and out of Larracos, still a good hundred metres short of the edge of Shanty Town, and he drops a whole folder of bombs toward the Piccadilly.

tagline.text: Carl's fan box holds a postcard-sized plastic badge on a red lanyard, SPECIAL GUEST flashing round its edge. His fans have put him on the CrawlCon roster for three events, attending virtually, and Zev advises him to cooperate.
Worn round his neck at the production facility, the badge lets Carl see the names over people's heads while his menus are switched off.

description.text: Congratulations, Crawler! You've received a free fan booth at CrawlCon! With thousands of physical attendees and billions of virtual visitors, Dungeon Crawler World fans from all corners of the galaxy gather once every other season to geek out together over all things Crawl! With special guests, panels, vendors, cosplay, and so much more, CrawlCon is the event of the galaxy! Thanks to your fans, you've been added to the CrawlCon roster! You will attend three events! Your presence at the con will be virtual. Please see your outreach associate for details on your schedule.

beats.headline: Fan box time
beats.text: Carl opens a fan box with Katia watching. A plastic rectangle pops out on a red lanyard printed Titan Entertainment in Syndicate standard. The badge is the size of a postcard. Its back scrolls with advertisements; its front shows a moving image of a horned demon shooting fire from its mouth, SPECIAL GUEST exploding along the edge, and a spinning logo reading Carl, Dungeon Crawler World: Earth. A timer appears at twenty-two hours. Carl reads the description: what the ever-loving fuck? Yeah, thanks, assholes, he tells the ceiling. Katia reads it and barks with laughter. He tells Zev to send Donut instead. It's in your best interests to be cooperative, Zev answers, just this once.
beats.gist: Carl opens a fan box and finds a CrawlCon badge naming him special guest, which Katia finds funny.

beats.headline: Around his neck
beats.text: Zev opens Carl's inventory for a moment: pull out the CrawlCon badge from the fan box and put it around your neck, take nothing else out, and lose the bandana. The red demon on the front roars silently, shooting fire, and the back scrolls an ad for a real estate venture on what looks like a swamp planet. A new tab appears in his interface, CrawlCon schedule, and he cannot open it. This vessel has its own containment zone, Zev explains, and his crawler wetware blocks him out.
beats.gist: Zev has Carl wear the CrawlCon badge, but its schedule tab stays locked.

beats.headline: Names without menus
beats.text: Zev makes Carl put the badge on again before he is transported down to the production facility for his next appearance. He lands hard in the green room in front of a two-headed ogre trying to play cards against itself. His menus are gone, but thanks to the badge he can still see the names floating over their heads: Dmitri on the right side, Maxim on the left, the Popov brothers, number five in the dungeon. They wear the badge too, around both their necks.
beats.gist: Carl, badge on again, lands in a green room and still reads the Popov brothers' names.

recap.text: Carl opens a fan box with Katia watching and pulls out a postcard-sized badge on a red lanyard, its front showing a horned demon shooting fire. Zev has him put it around his neck and lose the bandana, and a CrawlCon schedule tab appears that Carl cannot open. In the green room, the badge lets him read the names floating over a two-headed ogre's heads: Dmitri and Maxim, the Popov brothers.

tagline.text: Major Charlie is a potion Mordecai brews for Carl, usually called Brain Juice, though not even Mordecai can explain the name. It adds ten points of intelligence for thirty seconds, then takes ten away for five minutes.

beats.headline: Three kilometres of Ping
beats.text: Elf hunters with a catapult are shelling the town with gas-filled rocks from somewhere out in the forest. Carl's intelligence sits just over thirty with his daily buffs, and his Ping reaches a kilometre plus five hundred metres for every ten points, so Mordecai has made him a potion: ten more points for thirty seconds, then ten fewer for five minutes. Carl drinks it hovering on Levitation. Boy, are you smart! He zooms up through the green cloud, casts Ping, filters the map down to purple hunters and finds two of them, a kilometre and a half northeast. Then he hurls Samantha at them.
beats.gist: Mordecai's potion lifts Carl's Ping past three kilometres, and he finds two Elf hunters shelling the town.

recap.text: Elf hunters out in the forest shell the town with gas-filled rocks from a catapult. Mordecai has made Carl a potion that adds ten intelligence for thirty seconds, then takes ten away for five minutes. Carl drinks it while hovering on Levitation, zooms up through the green cloud, and casts Ping, filtering the map down to purple hunters. He finds two, a kilometre and a half northeast, and hurls Samantha at them.

entities.name: Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser
aka: Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser

tagline.text: The black bracelet Carl took off the moon elf Akland is the Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser: ten constitution, five dexterity, fifteen percent fire resistance and a level-10 Fireball once every twenty minutes. Donut wears it on a front leg.
Donut has cast her bracelet's Fireball indoors now, into Lucia Mar in a wooden pub, and set its back wall alight.

description.text: Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser. This item has been upgraded three times. Warning: this item has a 50% chance to permanently break if it's upgraded again. This murky bracelet is light and kinda stylish if you're one of those sad sacks who always wears black and complains about how nobody ever understands you. It's made of obsidian glass, which is actually a type of rock that only forms under extreme, lava-based circumstances. And interestingly enough, this is what you'll turn into if you don't treat this item with the respect it deserves. This bracelet imbues the following effects. +10 to Constitution. +5 to Dexterity. +15% Fire Resistance. Wearer may cast a level-10 Fireball spell once every twenty minutes.

beats.headline: Give it to me now
beats.text: Akland, the moon elf Samantha dragged back by the ankle, had a black bracelet on his arm, and Carl pulled it off before killing him. He offers it to Donut and asks whether she still has a couple of slots left. Black, glass, a plain bangle, she says, not as ugly as that wood anklet, and then she reads the description and gasps. Give it to me now, Carl. It appears on her front right leg, suddenly much smaller; she snorts and moves it to the front left. Don't use a fireball in a tight space, says Carl. I know how fire works, Carl.
beats.gist: Donut puts on a black bracelet Carl pulled off Akland, after reading its description and gasping.

beats.headline: A beachball of fire
beats.text: Carl's Protective Shell goes up too close to the boss and launches it straight into the night sky, with the ogre Areson, Carl assumes, still riding it. Donut gallops into the shell on Mongo. Shoot it, Carl shouts. Fireball! A beachball-sized ball of fire rises slowly, almost reluctantly, and blasts into the pink stomach of the flailing beast. It bursts into flames end to end, lands on top of the shield with a vicious splat, and slides off into the trees, stuck face down. Fireball is awesome, Donut cries.
beats.gist: Donut's bracelet fires a beachball-sized fireball from Mongo that bursts the flailing beast's pink stomach into flames.

beats.headline: An outdoor spell
beats.text: On the screen, Carl watches the fight in the treehouse pub. Donut is rooted by a snare, one paw stuck to the floorboards for ninety seconds. She fires a full-powered magic missile into Lucia Mar, and as Lucia starts to recover, Donut casts a Fireball into her chest. Lucia slams into the back wall, and the far wall of the wooden pub bursts into flames. Donut has already opened a platinum Did-You-Really-Just-Cast-Fireball-in-a-Room-This-Small box. Fireball is an outdoor spell, Donut, says Mordecai.
beats.gist: Snared Donut casts Fireball in a wooden pub, and Mordecai says it is an outdoor spell.

beats.headline: A bracelet on every leg
beats.text: Donut's own gold box holds a sparkling silver bracelet with little purple gems, and she equips it at once. She moves the obsidian bracelet that lets her cast Fireball to her right forward leg and puts the new one on the left. With the fallen oak anklet on one back leg and her plus-two dexterity bracelet on the other, she has a bracelet on all four legs and cannot add any more.
beats.gist: Donut equips a silver bracelet with purple gems, moves her Fireball bracelet, and wears one on every leg.

recap.text: Carl pulls a black bracelet off the moon elf Akland before killing him, and Donut demands it the moment she reads its description. Its Fireball sends a beachball of flame into the flailing beast's pink stomach, then into Lucia Mar's chest inside the wooden pub, where the far wall bursts into flames and Mordecai tells her Fireball is an outdoor spell. A silver bracelet from her gold box puts one on every leg, and she can add no more.

tagline.text: A light-duty trebuchet the size of a windsurfing board, built from glowing, poisonous bamboo by the Dream's raiders and left spiked to the ground in a clearing. It hurls three hundred kilos and infuses whatever it throws with Poison Cloud. Carl takes it.

A little cup on the sling changes the poison: pour a potion in and the rock carries that instead. Loaded with Mordecai's weedkiller, Carl's rock chucker kills an Odious Creeper, and Donut, as spotter, gets the credit.

description.text: Enchanted Venomous Elven Rock Chucker – Contraption. The mounted, fast-attack artillery specialists of the Dream don't bring siege engines with them when they go raiding. That's why they're so annoyingly deadly. Using a combination of knowledge, druid magic, and a little something-something extra—wink—they're able to rapidly construct their war machines on the fly. These can't-take-a-joke beanpoles can conjure up a whole regiment of wall-breaching contraptions in a matter of hours. Translation: you don't want these pale fuckers on your doorstep. This particular light-duty rock thrower is made by casting Bamboozeled on a patch of land and then assembling the device from the resulting poisonous bamboo stalks. …

beats.headline: The real prize
beats.text: The dead hunter's hand is already gone, sent to Carl in a hunter killer box; his loot runs to an unenchanted bow, a gonorrhea arrow and a photograph of Louis with a dog filter. The real prize is the trebuchet, abandoned in the clearing and spiked to the ground, oddly small for the rocks it has been lobbing: the size and height of a windsurfing board, made of a weird, hollow wood, light enough to carry easily, and glowing green. There is no counterweight. Two plates want to come together like magnets; ratchet the arm, attach the rock to the sling, pull the lever. Carl suspects the postage-stamp plates are high tech, not magic. These assholes are still cheating.
beats.gist: The trebuchet is the real prize: a small, light, glowing green, magnet-plated, counterweightless elven cheat.

beats.headline: The cup on the sling
beats.text: Carl's poison delivery system was over-engineered. The rock chucker's Poison Cloud is not self-contained after all: pour a potion into the little cup on the side of the sling and it changes the delivery poison. There still has to be a projectile, and he has plenty of three-hundred-pound rocks. In the rain and mud, a mile short of the nearest Odious Creeper, he spikes the trebuchet into the grass while Donut climbs so high up a tree that he cannot see her. He has no idea how to aim it, so the first rock goes without the potion: she can tell him if it is close.
beats.gist: Carl spikes the rock chucker into the grass while Donut climbs a tree; the first rock flies plain.

beats.headline: The spotter takes the credit
beats.text: Next attack will contain the poison, Carl writes, and if it works he can keep his garbage can poison bombs for something else. He adds Mordecai's weedkiller to the trebuchet and hits the lever. You hit it perfectly, Donut reports; the green stuff is getting messed up by the rain. A few seconds after the shot, the System announces that an Odious Creeper has fallen and Crawler Princess Donut has been given credit for the kill. Thirty remain, and she is up two levels to 47. Mordecai says he forgot to mention that the spotter usually gets the lion's share of credit with siege equipment. Forgot my ass, Carl thinks.
beats.gist: Carl adds weedkiller to the trebuchet, and Donut gets the Odious Creeper kill credit.

relations.note: as spotter

recap.text: Carl takes the dead hunter's gonorrhea arrow and the green-glowing trebuchet, light enough to carry. A mile from the nearest Odious Creeper, he spikes it into the grass, sends Donut up a tree, pours Mordecai's weedkiller into the cup on the sling, and hits the lever. The System credits Donut with the kill, and she rises two levels to 47.

tagline.text: A card Donut finds on a dead Skull Empire hunter when she loots everything at once. It has no description and looks like a credit card, and she wants to spend it before they cancel it.
Credit chits are, as far as Carl can tell, the intergalactic equivalent of credit cards. He takes a second one off a dead dreadnought hunter.
With the right card machine, King Rust's eyeball, his family ring and a password, King Rust's money moves onto a credit chit and out of everyone's reach.

beats.headline: Something extra from loot-all
beats.text: The Skull Empire hunter called The Talent has zapped himself with his own Lightning scroll. Carl tells Donut to loot him, so he will not pay that much in tithe taxes, and she gasps: almost 75,000 gold and three scrolls of Lightning. When she hits loot all she gets something extra that was not listed: a credit chit. It looks like a credit card and has no description. They need to go buy something with it before they cancel it, she says. Hold onto it for now, Carl tells her; they will ask Mordecai. And from now on, loot hunters one item at a time.
beats.gist: The Talent's loot-all produces a nameless credit chit, and Carl tells Donut to hold it for Mordecai.

beats.headline: Credit chit and all
beats.text: An unaffiliated hunter, a level-50 dreadnought merchant, opens his mouth to scream, and Carl kicks him in the nuts. He lands on the man's chest and breaks his neck by the twin horn stubs, out of sight of the guards. Into the inventory goes the body. It doesn't have much, but it does have one of those weird credit chits, like the one taken off the orc several days earlier. From what Carl gathers, they are the equivalent of intergalactic credit cards.
beats.gist: A hunter's credit chit comes off a merchant Carl kills with a neck-break, a kick, and the inventory.

beats.headline: From the dead pig
beats.text: Rosetta has her hand on the eye tattoo on Carl's chest and is demanding his toraline out loud. In chat, where they cannot hear, she asks something else: does he still have the credit chit he got from the dead pig? It is the card they looted off the orc hunter on the sixth floor, and Donut has it in her inventory. Good, Rosetta writes. She will get it from her.
beats.gist: Rosetta asks in chat about the orc hunter's credit chit; Donut has it, and Rosetta will collect it.

beats.headline: Robbing a king
beats.text: Carl brings King Rust's dripping head to Rosetta in the smoke, and she presses it to a pad on a device like a hand-held credit card machine. Something beeps. She tosses the head back to him and tells him to take the corpse too. Then she pulls a long, plastic-like card from the device, tosses it to the ground, slams in a similar one and presses a button. A happy little beep. Is that the credit chit? Donut asks. Are you robbing him? You said we needed a password!
beats.gist: Carl brings King Rust's head to Rosetta, who scans it, and Donut asks about the credit chit.

beats.headline: Not on the chit anymore
beats.text: In the liaisons' room, Orren bounces his ball off the wall and talks to someone Carl cannot see or hear. They are trying to claw it back, but she has already transferred it to a credit chit and sent it off. Monetary transactions are not covered by the communications blackout. It required the family ring, his eyeball and a password, and she seems to have used Colloid, the only bank the orcs use. No, sir. It is not on the chit anymore. Either way, it is too late.
beats.gist: Orren's call is too late: she already sent the money to a credit chit through Colloid.

recap.text: Carl kicks the level-50 dreadnought merchant in the nuts before he can scream, then breaks his neck by the twin horn stubs, out of sight of the guards. The body goes into the inventory with a credit chit, one of those weird cards like the one taken off the orc several days earlier. Carl gathers they work as intergalactic credit cards.

Rosetta presses her hand to the eye tattoo on Carl's chest and demands his toraline aloud, while in chat she asks if Donut still holds the credit chit looted from the orc hunter. Carl brings her King Rust's dripping head, and she presses it to a pad on her card machine. Orren learns the money went by family ring, eyeball and password to Colloid, so it is not on the chit anymore.

tagline.text: Summoning traps cover the slope below Fort Freedom alongside the alarms, and bush elves are quietly disarming a path through them to the water.

A recycled summoning trap calls two guards or minions to wherever it is set off, and it misfires if you have no minions or control no town. Carl collects ten; if they ever use one, Donut will have to set it.

description.text: Summoning Trap. This is a Recycled Trap. Effect: Once triggered, will summon two town guards or minions to the location of the trap. Will summon two random guards or minions from this floor only. If you do not have minions or if you do not control a town, this trap will misfire. Specific guards or minions may be programmed at a Sapper's Table. Delay: two seconds. Target: Programmable. Duration: one time use.

beats.headline: Lights on the slope
beats.text: From the edge of the forest above Fort Freedom, a long, muddy slope runs down to the river, cleared of foliage by the naiads so they can see anything coming. As Carl watches, lights pop up all over it. Traps, lots of them: alarms and summoning traps, and silent alarms all along the stone walkway. A group of bush elves crawls over the mud, quietly disarming the ones inside the protection spell, then creeps out of it to start on one Carl had not even noticed. They are carving a path to the water.
beats.gist: Carl watches bush elves disarm lit traps on the muddy slope, carving a path to the river.

beats.headline: Two dead guards
beats.text: Knocked off course by a sizzling saddle, Carl scrambles back up the hill toward the rampaging boss, and his foot hits a summoning trap nobody disarmed. A pair of naiad guards suddenly appear in front of him, already dead, splat onto the hill and roll down toward him. He has to hurdle one to keep going.
beats.gist: Carl hits an undisarmed summoning trap, and two dead naiad guards splat onto the hill; he hurdles one.

beats.headline: Ten for the inventory
beats.text: While Samantha makes her own way to the shore, Carl works the slope for untriggered traps to train his stalled Find Traps skill. The summoning traps are hard to spot. He trips two by accident, and both times they bring a pair of naiad guards, every one of them already killed by were-castors. After the third or fourth, Find Traps reaches ten, and the slope lights up like a Christmas display. He collects everything, ten summoning traps among it. He has no towns on this floor and no minions; that is a Donut thing. If they ever use one, she will have to set it.
beats.gist: Carl trips two summoning traps while training Find Traps to ten, then collects ten of them.

relations.note: where its guards can be programmed

recap.text: Carl watches lights pop up across the muddy slope above Fort Freedom, where bush elves crawl through alarms and summoning traps to carve a path to the water. His foot hits an undisarmed summoning trap, and two dead naiad guards splat on the hill and roll at him; he hurdles one. While Samantha makes her own way to the shore, he trips two by accident, brings Find Traps to ten, and collects ten summoning traps.

tagline.text: Slippery Slope is a trap on the south shore of the river, across from Fort Freedom, that would have made Carl slip and fall into the water. He disarms it and keeps it.

beats.headline: Into the inventory
beats.text: Across the river on the south shore, the ursine are big dead, chomped in half by something huge, and pink boa feathers litter the ground. Carl ties the sleeping Samantha to his back by her hair and loots armour, enchanted daggers and swords, worth over a thousand gold in all. Most of the traps here have already been disarmed or triggered, but at the edges of the area he finds and disarms a few more, among them a new one called Slippery Slope, which would have caused him to slip and fall into the water. The traps all go into his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl disarms the new Slippery Slope trap, among others, and loots the dead ursine's gear.

recap.text: Across the river, Carl finds the ursine dead, chomped in half by something huge, and pink boa feathers on the ground. He ties the sleeping Samantha to his back by her hair and loots armour, enchanted daggers and swords worth over a thousand gold. At the edges he disarms the remaining traps, including a new one called Slippery Slope, which would have dropped him into the water, and pockets them all.

tagline.text: The Automaton Table is a level-five crafting table left alone in an empty studio at the production facility after Carl's CrawlCon panel, with Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit lying on it. Carl takes both.
The Automaton Table builds from the recipes in Dr. Ratchet's manual, and its first build is the Spider Stalker.
Carl has given Katia access to the Automaton Table, and she is building something for Tran on it, with vehicles to follow.

beats.headline: Left behind after the panel
beats.text: On the way to his CrawlCon panel, Carl was walked through a studio where an older dwarf with a CrawlCon badge, Dr. Ratchet, was preparing a demonstration at a workbench beside a quarter-sized dwarven automaton. He needed the room's juice, so Carl would have to go upstairs; then he called after him: good luck, and keep your head down. After the panel, the studio is empty except for one table. Automaton Table. Level 5. On it lies Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit. Carl takes the table and the guide into his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl takes Dr. Ratchet's abandoned Automaton Table and his automaton-building guide into his inventory after the panel.

beats.headline: Ask the lawyer first
beats.text: Carl's legal question for his attorney is still unanswered, and Mordecai does not know either. Ask your lawyer, Mordecai says, and if he doesn't respond, wait until after the next recap episode. If they don't take it away from you, install it in the crafting studio and start working.
beats.gist: Mordecai can't answer Carl's workbench question and tells him to ask his lawyer.

beats.headline: Not much use yet
beats.text: The level-five table is not much use yet, despite a manual full of recipes. Carl has been terrified they would take the table or the recipes back, since he basically stole them from the production facility, but nobody has said a word. The trouble is parts. Then he finally finds the materials for something called Spider Stalkers.
beats.gist: Carl's level-five automaton table is little use without parts, until he finds the materials for Spider Stalkers.

beats.headline: Much too close
beats.text: The hunters come running straight at the party, leading two of the explosive spiders right into their laps, and Carl scrambles into his interface to disable them. Before he can, Kiwi and Mongo fly over him and pounce on the pair, two tentacle-faced Saccathians with mechanical enhancements on their legs, who die screaming. The spider automatons stop dead, turn back around, and go looking for new targets.
beats.gist: Kiwi and Mongo kill the two Saccathians before Carl can disable the spiders, which turn for new targets.

beats.headline: Parts for a fabricator
beats.text: A platinum, dog-shaped Tserendolgor box opens with more supplies for the automaton table, and this one is an XL box, so the chest is bigger than last time. Carl knows from the instruction manual that the XL boxes contain parts for a fabricator, something he has been hoping to build for a while. He pulls it all into his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl opens a platinum, dog-shaped XL box and pulls the fabricator parts into his inventory.

beats.headline: Katia at the table
beats.text: Responsibilities are finally being shared out, Florin falling right into the position of general. Carl has given Katia access to his automaton table, and she is working at it right now, building something for Tran to use now that his wheelchair is gone. She has bigger plans than that. They are going to need vehicles, and she is getting the ball rolling.
beats.gist: Katia is building something for Tran at Carl's automaton table and starting on vehicles.

relations.note: Carl copies Dr. Ratchet's recipes into it

recap.text: Carl takes the level-five Automaton Table and Dr. Ratchet's guide from an empty studio, then waits on his lawyer's answer, since he basically stole both. The table is not much use without parts until he finds the materials for Spider Stalkers. Hunters run two explosive spiders into the party, and Kiwi and Mongo pounce on the Saccathians, who die screaming. The spiders stop dead, turn back around, and go looking for new targets.

Carl opens a platinum, dog-shaped Tserendolgor box, an XL one, and the chest is bigger than last time. The instruction manual says XL boxes hold parts for a fabricator, which he has hoped to build for a while, so he pulls it all into his inventory. Florin falls right into the position of general. Katia, given access to the automaton table, builds something for Tran, whose wheelchair is gone, and starts the ball rolling on vehicles.

entities.name: Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit

tagline.text: An autographed paperback left lying on an Automaton Table in an empty studio after Carl's CrawlCon panel. Carl takes the guide and the table into his inventory.
The guide is an instruction manual full of automaton recipes, and Carl has copied every one into his scratchpad and into the Cookbook in case it is taken back.
Katia builds from the manual too: she has repurposed one of its recipes into Tran's two-part wheelchair.

beats.headline: Autographed and left behind
beats.text: On his way to the panel, Carl passed through a studio where an older dwarf with a CrawlCon badge, Dr. Ratchet, was preparing a demonstration at a workbench beside a quarter-sized automaton. Now the studio is empty except for a table: Automaton Table, Level 5. On it lies a regular paperback with a familiar smiling dwarf riding on the back of a mechanical horse thing, Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit. Carl opens it to the first page. It is autographed. He takes the guide and the table into his inventory.
beats.gist: In the empty studio, Carl takes the autographed guide and the Automaton Table.

beats.headline: Copy out the automaton book
beats.text: Carl's question for his attorney is a legal one, and he has not heard back; Mordecai, asked first, does not know. Ask your lawyer, Mordecai says, and if he doesn't respond, wait until after the next recap episode. If they don't take it away from you, install it into the crafting studio and start working. In the meantime, transcribe everything you can from that automaton book into your scratchpad.
beats.gist: Carl asks Mordecai about the manual; Mordecai doesn't know and says to ask the lawyer.

beats.headline: Recipes, but no parts
beats.text: Carl's level-five Automaton Table is not much use yet, despite an instruction manual filled with recipes. He has been terrified they would take the table or the recipe book back, since he basically stole them from the production facility, but so far nobody has said anything. Just in case, he has copied every recipe into his scratchpad and then into the Cookbook. The problem is supplies: he has some of the parts for several recipes and every part for none, until he finds the materials for something called Spider Stalkers.
beats.gist: Carl's level-five Automaton Table has recipes but no complete parts list, until he finds Spider Stalkers materials.

beats.headline: A kit with the right parts
beats.text: Carl picks up a large steampunk chest, ridiculously heavy, and lifts the lid. The description comes in a different voice, like a television commercial: Doctor Ratchet's Automaton Build-It Kit, enough items for over fifteen automatons, fun for the whole family, from personal servants to flame-throwing sentinel droids. It lists dozens of parts, and Carl recognises several of them as things he needs for recipes in the instructional book he stole from the production facility. Excellent, he says.
beats.gist: Carl opens a heavy steampunk chest holding Doctor Ratchet's Build-It Kit, parts he needs for his stolen recipes.

beats.headline: What an XL box holds
beats.text: Among Carl's boxes is a platinum, dog-shaped one from Tserendolgor, holding more supplies for his automaton table, and it is an XL box, so the chest is bigger than last time. Carl knows from the automaton instruction manual that the XL boxes contain parts for a fabricator, something he has been hoping to build for a while.
beats.gist: Carl finds a platinum, dog-shaped XL box from Tserendolgor; his manual says XL boxes hold fabricator parts.

beats.headline: Katia repurposes a recipe
beats.text: Katia has finished building Tran's two-part wheelchair, much like what she means to build next for Jamal, from a recipe she took out of Carl's automaton manual and repurposed. Walking around, Tran is a small mechanical crab body that can climb walls and run, for short distances, at incredible speed. Then there is the battle armour version he wears now: a second exoskeleton over the crab legs that encases him in full plate and a helmet.
beats.gist: Katia builds Tran a two-part wheelchair from Carl's automaton manual recipe: crab body, plus armour.

relations.note: Carl copies its recipes into it
the recipe Carl first builds
his wheelchair is built from one of its recipes

recap.text: Carl passes through a studio where an older dwarf named Dr. Ratchet, wearing a CrawlCon badge, sets up a demonstration beside a quarter-sized automaton. When Carl returns, the studio is empty except for an Automaton Table, Level 5, and an autographed paperback of Dr. Ratchet's Guide. He takes both into his inventory, and copies every recipe into his scratchpad and then the Cookbook, afraid they will be taken back.

Carl lifts the lid of a ridiculously heavy steampunk chest, and its description arrives in the voice of a television commercial: Doctor Ratchet's Automaton Build-It Kit, with enough items for over fifteen automatons, from personal servants to flame-throwing sentinel droids, fun for the whole family. The kit lists dozens of parts, and Carl recognises some of them as things he needs for recipes in the instructional book he stole from the production facility. He says, "Excellent.

Carl opens a platinum, dog-shaped box from Tserendolgor. It is an XL box, so the chest is bigger than last time, and Dr. Ratchet's Guide tells him XL boxes hold fabricator parts. Katia finishes Tran's two-part wheelchair from a recipe she took out of that manual: a small mechanical crab body that climbs walls, and a second exoskeleton over the crab legs that encases him in full plate and a helmet.

tagline.text: A Gold Spicy Box gives Carl a white patch with a little bomb hand-stitched on it in Spider Reaper Minion silk. It adds constitution, damage for every explosive and two levels of explosives handling, and a discount from the traveling Spider Reaper Minion merchants.
Carl's white bomb patch, in Spider Reaper Minion silk, adds constitution, explosive damage and explosives handling. An identical bomb is embroidered over the crotch of the Royal Court's capture flag.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Medium. This patch is finely made from Spider Reaper Minion thread silk. It's a bomb. You blow shit up all the time. It's appropriate you have a patch depicting it. This patch is finely made, which means all below upgrades are enhanced. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: +11% to Constitution. +6% damage to all explosives. +2 to the Dangerous Explosives Handling Skill. +15% Discount from traveling Spider Reaper Minion merchants. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: Classic Spanish blackwork
beats.text: Carl expected a toe ring or foot lotion from the Gold Spicy Box. Instead he gets a second patch, a little bigger than the first: white, rectangular, with a little circular bomb hand-stitched in fine black thread, almost like a pencil drawing. Donut gasps and pulls it over to look. Exquisite, she says, classic Spanish blackwork. How would she know? Then it clicks: the useless hobby potion she got on the third floor, Scutelliphily, must be about patches, and Britney supplies the Latin, the love of small shields. The silk is Spider Reaper Minion thread. Carl hands Katia his jacket, and she starts mapping out where to sew the patches.
beats.gist: Carl expects a toe ring or foot lotion but gets a second patch: a hand-stitched black bomb.

beats.headline: On the court's flag
beats.text: The Royal Court's capture flag is a little bigger than Carl's hand, and it is a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways, as if off a clothesline. The court's name is embroidered top and bottom in motorcycle-club style, and centred over the crotch is a bomb patch identical to the one on Carl's jacket. It really is tacky. Imani's squad got a butterfly, Donut complains, and the stitching looks as if Carl sewed it.
beats.gist: The Royal Court's capture flag is a tiny pair of heart-covered boxers bearing a bomb patch.

relations.note: Scutelliphily, the love of small shields

recap.text: Carl expects a toe ring or foot lotion from the Gold Spicy Box and pulls out a second patch, a little bigger than the first: white, rectangular, a small bomb hand-stitched in fine black thread. Donut gasps and calls it classic Spanish blackwork. Then it clicks that her useless third-floor hobby potion, Scutelliphily, is about patches, and Britney supplies the Latin, love of small shields. Carl hands Katia his jacket, and she starts mapping where to sew.

Carl finds the Royal Court's capture flag a little bigger than his hand: a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways, as if off a clothesline. The court's name is embroidered top and bottom in motorcycle-club style, and over the crotch sits a bomb patch identical to the one on Carl's jacket. Donut complains that Imani's squad got a butterfly, and that the stitching looks as if Carl sewed it.

tagline.text: A small square patch from a gold ranged-weapon box: a dozen flaming arrows in an eagle's claw, drawn Sailor Jerry style. Katia sews it onto Carl's jacket beside the planet earth, for five percent more dexterity and five percent more damage from every ranged projectile.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Small. This patch depicts the twelve flaming arrows the great Skyfowl hero Radiant Star shot into his grandfather in order to end the frozen time that plagued their world. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: +5% to Dexterity. +5% damage to all ranged projectiles. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: Sailor Jerry style
beats.text: Fifty-two hunting trophies in, Carl works through his boxes. The gold ranged-weapon box holds a patch for his jacket, the first he has got on this floor. Every patch he can fit adds plus one to all his stats on top of its own benefit. This one is small and square like his first, the planet earth, and shows about a dozen flaming arrows clutched in an eagle's claw, drawn in an old-school Sailor Jerry style. He thinks it looks kind of cool. Plus five percent dexterity and five percent damage to all ranged projectiles. Hell yeah. Katia, who sewed on his first one, grabs the kit and sews the arrows next to the planet earth on his jacket's shoulder.
beats.gist: Carl finds a flaming-arrows eagle-claw patch in a gold box, and Katia sews it beside his planet earth.

relations.note: the hero Radiant Star's arrows

recap.text: Carl works through his boxes after fifty-two hunting trophies, and the gold ranged-weapon box holds a patch for his jacket, the first he has got on this floor. It shows about a dozen flaming arrows clutched in an eagle's claw, drawn in old-school Sailor Jerry style, and adds five percent dexterity and five percent damage to all ranged projectiles. Katia sews it next to the planet earth on his jacket's shoulder.

tagline.text: A recipe Mordecai has been chasing for fifty cycles, sent by the Apothecary with a drawing of Mongo. The potion must be brewed for a specific animal, and its special ingredient is a liter of that animal's blood, per potion.
Brewed from Mongo's blood, the potion is named Charm Mongoliensis now: it makes the closest eligible monster Donut's minion for the rest of the floor, and the one they want is the pack leader Kiwi.
A second charm potion, brewed with cat blood and drunk by Donut on stage at the masquerade, makes Sir Ferdinand her minion.

beats.headline: Fifty cycles of chasing
beats.text: Carl's silver box from the Apothecary holds two pieces of paper: a potion recipe and a drawing of Mongo. Mordecai squeaks. He has been chasing this one for fifty cycles. You don't chill it, you put it in the centrifuge and then flash-freeze it. So simple. He has the ingredients, too: the thorn sap tips Carl has collected by the dozen, and the hard one. They both turn to look at Mongo. The recipe is for Charm Animal, which has to be brewed for a specific animal. Absolutely not, says Donut. It's just blood, Carl says: a liter of it, collected outside a saferoom. Per potion, Mordecai adds.
beats.gist: Carl's recipe for Charm Animal needs Mongo's blood, a liter per potion, taken outside a saferoom.

beats.headline: A liter in the rain
beats.text: With the knockout potion in him, Mongo is asleep in a dryad town, and Donut has to collect the blood herself. Most of it goes all over the place, but a few wet monkeys help her hold the flask, which is really hard without thumbs, and there is no time for another liter. Mordecai only has time to make one charm potion. In the next town, Prepotente Number Seven, Carl rushes into the saferoom, grabs the finished green potion, and they bounce.
beats.gist: Wet monkeys help Donut collect Mongo's blood, and Carl grabs the finished green potion.

beats.headline: Donut glows, then Kiwi
beats.text: The raptors have the party surrounded in a clearing, and Mongo stays in his carrier in case his presence negates the spell. Donut needs to be close: the potion lasts a minute, and she must not charm the wrong one. It is named Charm Mongoliensis now, and it tames the closest eligible monster as Donut's minion for the duration of the floor. She walks to within ten feet of the pink dinosaur, telling Kiwi she is forgiven but not forgotten. Donut glows, and about three seconds after her, Kiwi glows. Her dot turns white with the green mark of a minion, and every raptor in the pack turns white with her.
beats.gist: Donut charms Kiwi with Charm Mongoliensis, and every raptor in the pack turns white with her.

beats.headline: A liter of cat blood
beats.text: Carl's planning notes, added to the cookbook: there is a difference between Donut enchanting someone, as she does the Bopcas, and magically charming them, as she did Kiwi. Enchanted, Ferdinand would fall over himself to please her but could still object. Charmed, he would be her official minion and do what she says almost without question. Mordecai can make a charm animal potion. All they need is a liter of cat blood, and they have a ready source. The spell is line of sight, so if Ferdinand is in the audience, Donut can down it the moment she goes on stage.
beats.gist: Carl plans to have Mordecai brew a charm potion from cat blood so Donut can charm Ferdinand.

beats.headline: Sir Ferdinand joins up
beats.text: Up on stage, the curtains pull back on Donut alone. Ferdinand sits on the center table among the three judges in his ridiculous hat, eyes on her, tail wagging. Carl hands a Feather Fall potion to a crawler as Donut's message comes in: she took the charm potion, and it worked. Come on, baby, Ferdinand calls, and tells Empress D'nadia that is his bird up there. Carl's interface blinks. Sir Ferdinand, minion of Princess Donut, has joined the party.
beats.gist: Donut's charm potion works on Ferdinand, and he joins Carl's party as her minion.

relations.note: the recipe
a liter of his blood

recap.text: Mordecai squeaks that he has chased the Charm Animal recipe for fifty cycles, and Donut collects a liter of Mongo's blood herself, spilling most of it. She drinks the green potion near Kiwi, who glows, and every raptor in the pack turns white with her. Carl plans a second batch from a liter of cat blood, and Sir Ferdinand, tail wagging in his ridiculous hat, joins the party as Donut's minion.

entities.name: Enchanted Silver Bracelet of the Ab-solar

tagline.text: A silver bracelet set with little purple gems shaped like bulbs of garlic, from Donut's gold Apothecary box. Under a rant about vampire novels, it protects her against vampirism and lycanthropy and adds a quarter to her magic damage against sapient undead.

description.text: Enchanted Silver Bracelet of the Ab-solar. "AnD SO The lioN fEll iN lOVe WiTh The LaMB." I'm actually quite fond of the Twilight novels. Plus, I would never stoop so low as to disparage the work of an over-imaginative and obviously undersexed artist who managed to become a brazilianaire from barely-disguised erotica targeted at adolescent girls. However, I would like to take this opportunity to point out that your culture's obsession with fictional, underaged heroes was absolutely misguided. …

beats.headline: Purple, like garlic
beats.text: Carl's gold box from the Plenty gives a patch; Donut's gold box from the Apothecary gives a sparkling bracelet, and she equips it at once. The obsidian Fireball bracelet moves to her right foreleg, this one goes on the left, and with the fallen oak anklet and her plus-two dexterity bracelet on the back legs, all four legs are full. She loves it, though the description sounds like the AI is having a stroke. Its purple gems are shaped like bulbs of garlic. It protects against vampirism and lycanthropy, with plus 25 percent magical damage against sapient undead. Carl's patch gives the exact same benefits. Mordecai grunts: the two sponsors really are working together.
beats.gist: Donut equips a sparkling bracelet with garlic-shaped purple gems, and Carl's patch gives the same vampire protection.

beats.headline: A vampire, by coincidence
beats.text: Miriam Dom is trapped and asking for help as the sun sets. Mordecai suggests letting her die and collecting her gear in the morning. Two different sponsors who know more than they do just spent a huge amount of money to protect them from vampirism, he says, and by coincidence a vampire shows up asking for help. She saved my life, Carl says, grabbing the sewing kit. If it's a trap to turn them into vampires, they will be protected.
beats.gist: Miriam Dom begs for help at sunset; Mordecai suspects a trap, but Carl takes the sewing kit anyway.

relations.note: the same three benefits, from the Plenty

recap.text: Donut equips the sparkling bracelet from her Apothecary gold box, its purple gems shaped like garlic bulbs, and all four of her legs are full. Carl's patch from the Plenty gives the same protection, and Mordecai grunts that the two sponsors are working together. Miriam Dom calls for help at sunset; Mordecai says to let her die and take her gear in the morning, but Carl grabs the sewing kit, since she saved his life.

tagline.text: A gold box from the Plenty holds a patch for Carl's jacket: a gray goat head on black, denim-like cloth, the symbol of the Midnight Epicure, a children's bogeyman grown into a ward against all night evils. It protects against vampirism and lycanthropy and adds a quarter more magical damage against sapient undead.
The goat on Carl's patch is the Midnight Epicure, the god Prepotente worships: a tale made to scare non-caprid children that grew into a symbol of hope and comfort for his kind.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Medium. Ah, yes. The Midnight Epicure. The Caprid Who Devours the Sky. This scary-ass fable is used to terrify children across the universe. […] Over the cycles, the rather disturbing symbol of the Midnight Epicure, which is really just a racist caricature of an adult Caprid, developed into a ward against all night evils. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: Protection against Vampirism. Protection against Lycanthropy. +25% Magical damage against all sapient undead. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: The Plenty's goat
beats.text: Carl's gold box from the Plenty hisses, spins and opens like a flower on a patch for his jacket, the same size as his white bomb patch: black, denim-like material with a gray goat head screen-printed on it. Donut mutters about screen printing. Read the description, says Mordecai, and sew it on right away. Carl has seen the satanic goat before, on the back of Prepotente's hand, and sketched it into the cookbook, assuming it was a deity's mark. The description calls it a fable. Its benefits are exactly those of the silver bracelet Donut has just pulled from her own box.
beats.gist: Carl's gold box opens into a goat-head jacket patch, matching the bracelet Donut pulled from hers.

beats.headline: Sewn on, not straight
beats.text: Mordecai suggests letting Miriam Dom die and collecting her gear in the morning: two sponsors who know more than Carl have just spent a fortune protecting him from vampirism, and a vampire is asking for help the moment the sun sets. She saved my life, says Carl, grabbing the sewing kit; if it is a trap, they will be protected. He sews the patch on beside the bomb patch, his wide stitches covering Katia's careful threading, and Donut gasps that it is not straight. It is good enough. An achievement, a few levels in sewing, and the patch glows as it is officially affixed.
beats.gist: Carl sews the Midnight Epicure patch on over Katia's stitches, ignoring Mordecai's advice.

beats.headline: Protected by the jacket
beats.text: Carl stabs the loose heart of the boss in the rain, and the monster explodes, showering gore over all of them and spilling the rest of itself from the ruined trees. When Mongo leans down to bite at the remains, Carl tells him not to dare. Vampirism is contagious, and Carl knows that if his jacket did not protect him he would likely be infected: he would die, then wake up overcome with hunger. Half the dinosaurs in the forest are infected already.
beats.gist: Carl stabs the boss's heart, then forbids Mongo to bite the remains; his jacket alone prevents infection.

beats.headline: She can see the glow
beats.text: Carl is still cautious with Miriam Dom, and she understands why. The two of them are in no danger from her, she tells him. She can see the glow on them: Carl and Donut are both protected from vampirism, and she could not feed on them even if she wanted to.
beats.gist: Miriam Dom tells a wary Carl that the glow on him and Donut protects them from vampirism.

beats.headline: The goat is a god
beats.text: Carl asks Prepotente about his god; all he knows of it is what the patch on his jacket says, the one that protects him from vampires and werewolves. The Midnight Epicure, says Prepotente, protects all prey animals by destroying all existence after unleashing all the consumed back into the galaxy: they who were eaten become the devourers. It began as a xenophobic tale to scare non-caprid children and grew into a symbol of hope and comfort for his kind. His sponsors gave him the ability to worship it in a benefactor box.
beats.gist: Prepotente learns his god, the Midnight Epicure, destroys all existence and frees the eaten to devour.

relations.note: the same three benefits

recap.text: Carl's gold box from the Plenty opens on a black patch with a gray goat head, and he sews it beside his bomb patch, his wide stitches covering Katia's careful threading, though Mordecai urges letting Miriam Dom die. Donut gasps that it is not straight. When the boss explodes in the rain and showers him with gore, the jacket keeps the vampirism off him. Miriam Dom sees the glow and says she could not feed on him or Donut.

Carl asks Prepotente about his god, the goat on the patch that protects Carl's jacket from vampires and werewolves. Prepotente says the Midnight Epicure protects all prey animals by destroying all existence after unleashing the consumed back into the galaxy, so the eaten become the devourers. The tale began as a xenophobic story to scare non-caprid children. His sponsors gave him a benefactor box to worship it in.

tagline.text: Mordecai's holy water grenades: potion balls of a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant, dipped in the blood water of Carl's Emberus shrine. Against vampires, he says, they act like napalm.

beats.headline: Napalm to vampires
beats.text: As Carl heads out to Miriam Dom, Mordecai calls wait, hops sideways into the crafting room and comes back with two potion balls in his small arms. He dips them in the red water of the Emberus shrine at the back of the room and hands them over. The system labels them Holy Goopers. Blessed water mixed with a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant, Mordecai explains: Emberus is a light-based god, and the shrine's blood water with a healing potion and the coagulant acts like napalm to vampires. Hit them with this, then have Donut max out her Torch spell. So they're holy water grenades, Carl says. Cool. Exactly.
beats.gist: Mordecai dips two potion balls in shrine water and hands Carl the Holy Goopers.

beats.headline: Against Sierra's talons
beats.text: Sierra has Carl in her twin talons, one round his legs and one round his chest, trying to pull him apart like a hot mozzarella stick. A magic missile hits her wing. Carl casts Heal and pulls the Holy Gooper into his free hand, smashing the sticky holy water against the talon on his chest. The foot sizzles, and she only crushes harder. He pulls his second and last as the new sun comes up and Donut emerges from the canopy. The throw misses when the boss rears back from the light, but her head bursts into flames anyway, and she tosses him straight up into the sky.
beats.gist: Carl smashes a Holy Gooper on Sierra's talon; her head bursts into flames and she tosses him skyward.

beats.headline: Clearing the way
beats.text: Before the cemetery, Carl moves a few of Mordecai's holy gooper grenades to the ready position, though he has only six of them, along with healing potion smoke curtains he has not yet tested. The mobs swarm. The saferoom is that way, Donut cries, pointing through a mass of creatures, and Carl tosses a holy gooper and clears the way, then another curtain to keep the path open. None of her psionic attacks work on these things, she shouts.
beats.gist: Carl throws a holy gooper grenade and a smoke curtain to reach the saferoom.

relations.note: dipped in his shrine's water

recap.text: Mordecai calls Carl back before Miriam Dom and dips two potion balls in the red water of the Emberus shrine. The system labels them Holy Goopers: blessed water, healing potion and coagulant, which Mordecai says acts like napalm on vampires. Held in Sierra's twin talons, Carl smashes one against the talon on his chest; the foot sizzles and she crushes harder. His second throw misses, but her head bursts into flames anyway.

Before the cemetery, Carl moves a few of Mordecai's holy gooper grenades to the ready position, though he has only six, along with healing potion smoke curtains he has not yet tested. The mobs swarm, and Donut points through a mass of creatures to the saferoom. Carl tosses a holy gooper and clears the way, then a curtain to keep the path open, while Donut shouts that her psionic attacks do nothing to these things.

tagline.text: Miriam Dom left over forty scrolls of something called Size Up in the pile of everything she owned, and Carl takes two where Prepotente cannot see.
Prepotente knows Carl took Size Up scrolls from his mother's pile, and he asks for five fine healing potions as payment.
Donut drinks a Size Up potion before the race and reads off Osvaldo's dexterity with all his buffs, his abilities and the levels of his skills.

beats.headline: Two of forty
beats.text: Miriam Dom is a pile of dust, and beside it stands a stack of everything she owned, dumped from her inventory because she feared turning to dust would make her body unlootable. She was right. She told Carl he could take a few items for helping her, and he promised it would all go to Prepotente. He intends to keep that promise. Mostly. Among the potions and plants are over forty scrolls of something called Size Up. He walks out of Prepotente's sight and takes two. As the second goes into his inventory, his interface flickers, and the number 50 slams into place.
beats.gist: Carl takes two Size Up scrolls from Miriam Dom's pile, and his interface flickers to 50.

beats.headline: Payment for the scrolls
beats.text: Prepotente needs at least five more fine healing potions for the recipe his benefactor box just sent him. Carl has about fifty and says he has a few. Give them to me, says the goat: consider it payment for the Size Up scrolls you stole from my mother. Carl pauses, then asks to hear what is on the paper first, and once he has, hands over five potions without further complaint.
beats.gist: Carl pays Prepotente five fine healing potions for the stolen scrolls, once he has heard the recipe.

beats.headline: A look at Osvaldo
beats.text: While they wait, Donut downs a Size Up potion and watches the back of Osvaldo's head. Then she reports. His dexterity is really high, 285 with all his buffs. He has a Deflector ability, and his Jump skill is level fifteen. Carl asks about Puddle Jump or Phase: he has Puddle Jump, but only at level eight, which means a ten-second countdown.
beats.gist: Donut reads Osvaldo's stats: dexterity 285, Deflector, Jump fifteen, Puddle Jump only level eight.

beats.headline: Protected from examination
beats.text: In the Desperado Club's casino the croupier is level 120 and an Enforcer, his examination full of redactions, a much higher level than Carl expected. Carl tells Donut to take a Size Up and asks anyone else with examination skills to let him know what they see. Donut reports back that he is protected from the examination.
beats.gist: Carl has Donut Size Up the level 120 Enforcer croupier, who is protected from examination.

recap.text: Carl finds Miriam Dom dead as dust, her whole inventory stacked beside the pile. Out of Prepotente's sight, he takes two of her forty-odd Size Up scrolls, and his interface flickers as the number 50 slams into place. Prepotente then demands five fine healing potions as payment for the scrolls stolen from his mother. Carl asks to hear the paper first, then hands them over.

Donut downs a Size Up potion and reads the back of Osvaldo's head: dexterity 285 with all his buffs, a Deflector ability, Jump at level fifteen. Carl asks about Puddle Jump or Phase, and she says he has Puddle Jump only at level eight, a ten-second countdown. In the Desperado Club's casino, Carl sends Donut to take a Size Up and examine the level 120 Enforcer croupier, and she reports he is protected from the examination.

tagline.text: A legendary benefactor box gives Prepotente a vintage-style spray applicator and a recipe for a herbicide. The mix of fine healing, blessed water and weedkiller only works when his new magical canister turns it into a very fine mist.

beats.headline: A pump and a tin can
beats.text: Prepotente spends his wand's tiny three-minute safe space opening his loot boxes, which Carl thinks is a waste. Ten seconds before it closes, his legendary benefactor box gives up two items. One looks like a handheld bicycle pump with a tin can welded under the nozzle; Donut says it is like one of Bea's perfume bottles, and Carl recognises a sprayer for putting herbicide on a garden. The other is a piece of paper. Prepotente wants five fine healing potions from Carl, payment for the Size Up scrolls Carl stole from his mother, and Carl makes him tell what is on the paper first: fine healing, blessed water and a weedkiller, applied as a very fine mist through the new canister.
beats.gist: Prepotente's legendary box yields a pump sprayer and a paper describing a healing-water weedkiller mist.

beats.headline: Mordecai builds on it
beats.text: A System message: another Odious Creeper has fallen, credit to Crawler Prepotente, forty remain. That is his third, says Carl. On the counter, Mordecai has four moonshine jugs of his own weedkiller, built on what Prepotente said and what he received: a weedkiller designed to take out an odious bloom, with several anti-undead boosts added, like the holy grenade he once made for Carl.
beats.gist: Mordecai builds four jugs of moonshine weedkiller, shaped for the Odious Creeper, after Prepotente's third kill.

recap.text: Prepotente spends his wand's three-minute safe space opening loot boxes, which Carl thinks is a waste, and ten seconds before it closes his legendary benefactor box gives up a handheld bicycle pump with a tin can welded under the nozzle, plus a paper. Carl makes him say what is on it before paying: fine healing, blessed water and a weedkiller, applied as a fine mist. Mordecai sets four moonshine jugs of his own weedkiller on the counter.

entities.name: Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill and Undead Repellant, Extra-Strength Edition

tagline.text: Uncle Morty's is Mordecai's weedkiller for the Odious Creepers, an existing weedkiller for an odious bloom with anti-undead boosts added: four moonshine jugs of it, each enough for two or three creepers. It is very flammable, and if it burns before the monster absorbs it, it does not work.
Poured into the little cup on the elven rock chucker's sling, Uncle Morty's goes out with a three-hundred-pound rock and brings a creeper down in seconds.

beats.headline: Four jugs on the counter
beats.text: Katia asks whether Mordecai made the stuff. Four moonshine jugs of bubbling yellow liquid sit on the counter, one almost as big as he is, labelled Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill and Undead Repellant, Extra-Strength Edition. He took a weedkiller designed to take out an odious bloom and added anti-undead boosts. Each jug has enough for two or three, maybe four. Louis's Tent the House ability spreads a potion over a wide area, but he must use it at maximum distance: the stuff is very flammable, and if it catches fire before it is absorbed, it will not work. Carl takes two jugs, Louis the other two.
beats.gist: Katia asks if Mordecai made the jugs of weedkiller, and Carl and Louis each take two.

beats.headline: Into the sling cup
beats.text: Carl's delivery system was over-engineered. The venomous elven rock chucker taken from the Dream hunters has a Poison Cloud enhancement, and a potion poured into the little cup on the side of the sling changes the poison. A mile short of the creeper, in the mud and rain, Donut climbs a tree to watch. Carl adds the poison, hits the lever, and a rock flies. You hit it perfectly, says Donut; the green stuff is getting all messed up by the rain. Mordecai said that would help. A few seconds after that, the notice comes: a creeper has fallen, credit to Crawler Princess Donut. Thirty remain.
beats.gist: Carl poisons a sling rock, and Donut, up a tree, earns the creeper kill.
