beats.text: The spell reanimates weapons and armour with undead spirits plucked from the river of falling souls, and most of the gear disintegrates when it ends. Mordecai sees the combination at once: with Laundry Day at level fifteen, Donut can strip a group of mobs of their armour and turn it on them, full of wailing spirits. Carl slides the tome back to her. She glows as she applies it, and it lets out a little scream as it disappears in a puff of purple smoke.
beats.gist: Donut applies the summoning tome, and it screams and vanishes in purple smoke.

beats.headline: The Phantasm move
beats.text: Donut casts Laundry Day on Bomo, and the armour Carl made for him at his armourer's table, dozens of metal pieces and trash-tier daggers sewn one by one onto a fabric undershirt, explodes off him like a fragmenting grenade. Then she casts part two, her new spell. A purple rent opens above the temple, dozens of wispy white ghosts pour down screaming into the scattered armour on the floor, and every piece starts to shake. It is working.
beats.gist: Donut casts Laundry Day on Bomo, his armour explodes off, and her new spell sends ghosts into it.

recap.text: Donut's De-Sleeving box holds 100,000 gold and a chained tome that bounces, smokes purple, and wriggles like a puppy in Carl's hands. Its spell fills armour with undead spirits, and Mordecai sees that Laundry Day at level fifteen lets Donut strip mobs and turn their gear on them. She applies it, and the tome screams a little and vanishes in purple smoke. She blasts Bomo's armour off him like a grenade, and ghosts pour screaming into the pieces.

entities.name: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Defiler

tagline.text: The Nipple Ring of the Defiler is a silver ring with an eyeball hanging from it, wearable only by a crawler a god has marked for death, which Carl is. It reads the religion of everyone nearby, lets him break shrines without divine fallout, adds a quarter to his damage against clerics and casts Black Nimbus once an hour.
Black Nimbus strips a worshipper of their god's blessing for a while. It takes away the god's protection, not the god's wrath.

description.text: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Defiler This may only be equipped on a crawler who has been Marked for Death by a god. Hey, that’s you! All nipple rings must be manually affixed the first time they are equipped. Wearing this ring imbues the following effects: Instantly know the religious affiliation of all nearby mobs and crawlers. Allows the destruction of church shrines without further ill effects from deities. +25% damage against all clerics. The ability to cast Black Nimbus once an hour.

beats.headline: The apostate's box
beats.text: The platinum apostate box, earned for not getting killed by Diwata, holds a ring. A nipple ring. Donut is triumphant: now that his nipples are full, there are other places he is not pierced yet. It is silver, with an eyeball hanging from it, and only a crawler marked for death by a god may wear it. Li Na could already do everything it does. Its spell, Black Nimbus, pulls a target out of their deity's blessing and keeps them out of church. Lots of divinity-themed items, says Mordecai, and that is never good.
beats.gist: Carl's platinum apostate box holds a ring only a god-marked crawler may wear.

beats.headline: Black Nimbus on Anton
beats.text: Ogun has come for his two worshippers, Paz and Anton, and has eyes only for them. Carl's new ring came with Black Nimbus, which removes the benefits of worshipping a god, and maybe it would save them from a smite, but it reaches only one. He steps forward and casts it on Anton, then reads a Heal scroll on each man. A black crown forms over Anton's head, and the shunned mark disappears. The god turns, more curious than angry. A good attempt, he says: it has removed the man from his protection and his mercy, not from his wrath. He steps back onto Anton's head and crushes him.
beats.gist: Carl casts Black Nimbus on Anton and heals both men, but Ogun still crushes Anton underfoot.

recap.text: Carl wins a silver nipple ring with an eyeball hanging from it, a platinum apostate box prize for not getting killed by Diwata. When Ogun comes for his worshippers Paz and Anton, Carl casts its spell, Black Nimbus, on Anton and reads a Heal scroll on each man. A black crown forms over Anton's head, but Ogun says it removed only protection and mercy, not wrath, and crushes him.

tagline.text: The Prison Tattoo Kit is the same stick-and-poke gear Edgar the tortoise used on Tsarina Signet. Tattoos can carry all sorts of magical buffs and upgrades, and everything depends on the artist.
Katia has used the kit to tap a Desperado Club pass onto Samantha's neck, and the ink is already starting to fade.
Shi Maria has used the kit through Carl's own hands: its stick took Li Jun's eye, then tattooed an eye into Carl's chest.
With the right ink, the kit can put a skill into a crawler's skin. Katia is using it to tattoo a skill from Li Na's blood onto Carl's right arm.

description.text: Enchanted Prison Tattoo Kit. So, you’re doing time. Hey, I’m not one to judge. You wonder, how did I get here? How did I mess my life up so much? You figure, now is the day I’m going to turn everything around. Now is the day I’m going to make certain I get on the right path. I’m gonna get out of here and get a job and make my family proud. Let me commemorate this important occasion by letting SkullFuck from the next cell come over and etch a poorly-drawn dragon on the side of my face. This kit allows an artist to create a tattoo of their choosing upon the skin of a willing or unwilling target. …

beats.headline: Stick and poke
beats.text: The Gold Quest Box for the Vengeance of the Daughter opens, and Carl recognises what comes out at once. Donut asks, with disgust, whether it is what she thinks. It is: a stick and poke tattoo kit, the same items Edgar the tortoise used to put magical tattoos on Tsarina Signet. A long, sharp needle, some ink, a few stick things, and something that looks like sandpaper. He has no idea how any of it works, and the description, about doing time, is no help. What is he supposed to do with this?
beats.gist: Carl opens the Gold Quest Box and finds a stick and poke tattoo kit he cannot use.

beats.headline: A pass on her neck
beats.text: At the Desperado's door, Clarabelle glares at Samantha: she has seen her on the recap plenty of times and never noticed the pass on her neck. Samantha hisses, snaps her teeth, and announces that she is going to kill Clarabelle's mother. Carl clamps her jaw shut with his arm and tells Clarabelle they just finished a quest where she killed someone, and they put the tattoo on her neck. It is disgusting, says Samantha, who hates tattoos more than she hates sushi. A gold coin, and Clarabelle waves them through.
beats.gist: Carl clamps Samantha's jaw and shows Clarabelle her neck pass, and a coin gets them in.

beats.headline: The ink is fading
beats.text: Carl picks Samantha up in both hands and looks her in the eyes. She is covered in sand and gore, heavier than usual, with a slight vibration to her. The Desperado Club logo is still on her neck, where Katia tapped it with the poke and stick tattoo kit, but the ink is starting to fade. This is important, he tells her, so pay attention.
beats.gist: Carl holds Samantha and tells her to listen as the tattoo on her neck fades.

beats.headline: Through Carl's hands
beats.text: Combined with Shi Maria, Carl is a torso on a spider's body, and she is in control. She pulls the stick and poke kit from his inventory into his hands. When Li Jun slides down Li Na's chain to help, she has warned him: Carl jabs the stick into Li Jun's eye, licks the eye off and eats it. If he will not take her card to the next floor, she tells him, she will attach herself to something he cannot discard so easily. She dips the stick into the beaker and rapidly pokes a small tattoo into his bare chest, just above the sternum: an eye, which blinks, closes and disappears against his skin.
beats.gist: Combined with Shi Maria, Carl stabs Li Jun's eye with a stick, eats it, tattoos an eye.

beats.headline: The right sleeve
beats.text: Katia sets a vial of ready-mixed ink on the table, and Carl puts the poke and stick kit beside it. Li Na is not mad at him, Katia says, only at herself for not protecting her brother. Her blood was freely given, so she lost five levels only for a while and can still use the skill; the tattoo itself is permanent. Carl has several tattoos on his left arm and none on his right, so the right sleeve it is. A level-13 skill needs a big one and almost all the ink. Rosetta says a properly themed tattoo lasts longer.
beats.gist: Katia mixes the ink, and Carl chooses his right arm for a big, permanent tattoo.

relations.note: the same tools he used on Signet

recap.text: A Gold Quest Box gives Carl a stick and poke tattoo kit: a long, sharp needle, ink, a few stick things, and something like sandpaper. Clarabelle waves him and Samantha past the Desperado door for a gold coin, because of the logo tattooed on Samantha's neck, where the ink starts to fade. Joined with Shi Maria, Carl jabs the stick into Li Jun's eye, eats the eye, and pokes a blinking eye onto his own chest.

Katia sets a vial of ready-mixed ink on the table, and Carl puts the poke and stick kit beside it. Li Na is not mad at him, Katia says, only at herself for not protecting her brother. Her blood was freely given, so she lost five levels only for a while. Carl has tattoos on his left arm and none on his right, so he takes the right sleeve.

entities.name: Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield

tagline.text: The Right Back Atcha Personal Shield is a short black forearm bracer covered in little buckles that throws out an overeager small buckler. It catches physical attacks on Carl's dexterity and magic bolts on his intelligence, and sends three in four of them back at the attacker, sometimes doubled.

description.text: Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield. You ever meet one of those dudes who is always super quick to take offense to everything? You gotta walk on eggshells around him. Has some job where he wears a shirt and tie even though he looks like he just woke up in an alley somewhere. He’s always saying, “What the hell is that supposed to mean?” He hits on anything with a pulse. He wants people to call him T-Bone or Bulldog or something. He dies of a heart attack in his mid-forties. You get my drift. Well, this little auto buckler is the armor version of that. …

beats.headline: Swapped for the Peach Pit
beats.text: Among the box prizes is a forearm bracer, black, short and covered with little buckles. Carl already has two: the one that forms his Grull gauntlet, and the one on his left arm that forms a buckler meant to disarm opponents 1.5 percent of the time, which he has never got to work. This one auto-deploys a small buckler that catches physical attacks and magic bolts, with a 75 percent chance to reflect them and a 25 percent chance to double the reflection. Mordecai says it is much better, and it matches the other bracer. Off comes the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit, onto the pile for the Faction Wars team.
beats.gist: Carl swaps his Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit for a black bracer that auto-deploys a reflecting buckler.

recap.text: Carl finds a short black bracer covered in little buckles among the box prizes. It auto-deploys a buckler that catches physical attacks and magic bolts, with a 75 percent chance to reflect them and a 25 percent chance to double the reflection. Mordecai says it is much better than the Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit, which Carl takes off and puts on the pile for the Faction Wars team.

tagline.text: The peace symbol patch is a small upgrade patch from Carl's gold pacifist's box. It makes neutral mobs less likely to aggro and adds ten per cent to his Dexterity and to his skill at the bongos, and it is sewn to the bottom of his jacket, beside the bomb symbol.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Small. This patch depicts a peace symbol. Ahh, isn't that cute? Buzz off, dirty hippie. Go be smelly somewhere else. The Grateful Dead sucked. And so does Phish. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: Neutral mobs are less likely to fall into aggro. +10% to Dexterity. +10% skill in playing the bongos. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: Buzz off, dirty hippie
beats.text: In the line of boxes from the last floor, the gold pacifist's box holds a small upgrade patch for Carl's jacket, a round peace symbol, and Donut scoffs at the quality. It is almost the size of his earth patch, black with a white, screen-printed peace symbol. The description tells him to buzz off, dirty hippie, and says the Grateful Dead sucked, and so does Phish. Carl calls that unnecessarily rude. Donut does not like Phish either: Angel the cocker spaniel's owner was always listening to them.
beats.gist: Carl's jacket gets a black, screen-printed peace symbol patch that tells hippies to buzz off, and Donut scoffs.

beats.headline: Sewn on first
beats.text: Before the celestial back patch goes on, Carl sews the peace symbol onto the bottom of his jacket next to the bomb symbol. He does the small one first, to be doubly certain the back patch's effect catches every regular patch. It is his fifth, after the earth symbol, the arrows, the bomb symbol and the anti-vampire Midnight Epicure patch, and every patch on the jacket adds one point to all his stats.
beats.gist: Carl sews the peace symbol onto his jacket first, his fifth patch, so the back patch counts it.

beats.headline: A meatball that is not red
beats.text: Carl zaps a level-1 tummy acher onto the table: half the size of his fist, a spattering of black hairs on its head, Garret's underbite and single round tooth. The first of these things Carl ever saw was red-tagged. This one is not, and he does not know whether that is because it used to be Ren's pet or because of his peace symbol patch plus his higher charisma.
beats.gist: Carl zaps a tummy acher onto the table; this one is not red-tagged.

recap.text: Carl sews a round, black-and-white screen-printed peace symbol onto the bottom of his jacket, next to the bomb symbol, before he attaches the celestial back patch. He does the small patch first to be doubly certain the back patch's effect catches every regular patch. It is his fifth, after the earth symbol, the arrows, the bomb symbol and the anti-vampire Midnight Epicure patch, and each patch adds one point to all his stats.

Carl zaps a level-1 tummy acher onto the table, half the size of his fist, with a spattering of black hairs on its head, Garret's underbite and a single round tooth. The first one Carl ever saw wore a red tag, and this one does not. He cannot tell whether that is because it used to be Ren's pet or because of his peace symbol patch and his higher charisma.

tagline.text: The Combo card is a very rare, consumable T'Ghee utility card. It fuses two monster cards into one creature for the shorter of their two summoning times, and afterwards both are out for the rest of the combat.
Donut has spent the Combo card, fusing two problem totems into one, and the Glow-Up card has made the result permanent.

description.text: T’Ghee Card. Very Rare. Utility Card. Combo. Consumable. You ever mix two completely incompatible foods together to see how they taste? Sometimes it’s great. Like chicken and waffles! Sometimes it’s... a bad idea. Like tuna and haggis. Temporarily combines two monster cards into a single creature. Summoning length is equal to the shorter of the two summoning phases. Post summoning, both monsters are tagged out for the remainder of combat, even if they still have health. Warning: This is a consumable card. It will be destroyed upon use.

beats.headline: In a mob's inventory
beats.text: The Experience is dead, and Donut finds a card thing in its inventory, though she thought cards only came from flagging monsters. It is the size of a postcard, rigid but papery, the Syndicate's logo moving on its back and a red stylised plus floating in a field of stars on its face. Very rare, utility, consumable: chicken and waffles, or tuna and haggis. It fuses two monster cards into one. Carl wonders how rare these really are and tries to put it in his inventory. Cards may only be held by the Squad Leader.
beats.gist: Donut finds a fusing card in a dead mob's inventory, but only the Squad Leader may hold cards.

beats.headline: Discarded, the first time
beats.text: Five cards in the deck, and the totem is not among the four Donut draws: two Time Extends, the Combo card and Stout. A hand without a totem leaves her vulnerable, so Carl tells her to discard or play at once, and with no snare or mystic cards yet, the Combo goes. She flicks her paw downward and it disappears in a puff of smoke, a ten-second timer counting down in the empty space.
beats.gist: Donut discards the Combo card, which vanishes in smoke with a ten-second timer counting down.

beats.headline: Kept in for realism
beats.text: Building the ready deck for the practice arena, Donut does not want the Combo card in it, since it will not be used in practice. Carl thinks it best to keep it in, to make the practice as realistic as possible. A fight can start without warning, so the ready deck has to hold everything they would really carry.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut build the practice arena's ready deck, and Carl keeps the Combo card in.

beats.headline: Two problem cards, one totem
beats.text: From the practice arena Donut reports that they were pretty mad, and Shi Maria too: she wanted the Glow-Up used on her. Before they went into the club, Katia gave Donut one of her excess totems, a mythic creature from Iceland named Jola, and Donut wants him in the active deck, which puts her one totem over. Rather than drop a card, she has used the consumable Combo card to combine two of the problem cards, spent all the utility buffs on them, and made the change permanent with the consumable Glow-Up.
beats.gist: Donut combines two problem cards to fit Jola, then makes the change permanent.

beats.headline: What the Combo made
beats.text: Church organ music, fat digital cherubs and a herd of digital street dogs herald the card Donut made with the Combo: Uzi Jesus and Asojano in one, the most over-the-top reveal of all their cards. What rises from the smoke is a dirty, sandalled, robed figure, hunched and sickly, a green-tinted nimbus round his head and his weapon used as a walking stick. Level 140, like Uzi Jesus. The card names him Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, created via Combo.
beats.gist: Donut's Combo card reveals Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, a sickly, sandalled level 140 blend of Uzi Jesus and Asojano.

recap.text: With The Experience dead, Donut finds a postcard-sized Combo card in its inventory, but Carl cannot hold it, since only the Squad Leader may. Drawn in a hand with no totem, it vanishes in a puff of smoke when she flicks her paw. Katia's gift of a totem, Jola, leaves her one over, so Donut spends the card fusing Uzi Jesus and Asojano into Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, a sickly, sandalled, level 140 figure leaning on his weapon.

tagline.text: The red beret came off the head of the Experience, a mob with an angry bearded face like Che Guevara's. It glows because it is magical, and Donut gasped when she read its stats.
The red beret gives Donut only a small boost to all her stats, but she wears it now and then because it is appropriate for the location.

beats.headline: Dibs on the hat
beats.text: Combat starts in a voice Carl has never heard before, and the Experience lopes at them: a wolf-sized thing on stiff legs with a comically large human head, an angry bearded guy in a glowing red beret, suspiciously like Che Guevara, barking like a man through a megaphone. Donut's missiles and fireball do most of the work. If he joins the squad, she says, he will have to shave, and she gets to keep his hat. Too late: he dies. Dibs on the hat. Looting him, she gasps at the beret's stats, puts it on, and wonders about embracing the revolutionary look.
beats.gist: Donut's missiles and fireball kill a bearded, Che Guevara-like Experience, and she takes its red beret.

beats.headline: Appropriate for the location
beats.text: Donut usually wears her white Tiara of Mana Genita, which raises her intelligence. She also has the red beret she took from a mob earlier on the floor. It gives only a small boost to all of her stats, but she puts it on from time to time because it is appropriate for the location. She keeps literally hundreds of hats in her inventory, and sometimes lines several up in front of the mirror, or tries one on Mongo, who sits patiently while she clucks over it.
beats.gist: Donut sometimes wears a red beret, which gives a small boost to all her stats.

recap.text: Donut's red beret comes off a dead mob: a wolf-sized thing on stiff legs with a comically large human head, an angry bearded guy suspiciously like Che Guevara. Her missiles and fireball kill him, she calls dibs, and she puts the beret on. It gives only a small boost to all her stats, so she wears it from time to time, because it is appropriate for the location.

tagline.text: The Flee card is an uncommon, one-use T'Ghee special card that teleports a whole squad out of combat, without saying how far or where to.
In the final phase a Flee card has a price: a keyholder who flees loses a key to the opponent. It is also the only way to hand a key to someone else.

beats.headline: Team Sister Ines's draw
beats.text: After the fight, Carl and Donut collect three common utility cards, two Time Extends and a Stout, none of them one-time consumables like their Combo card. Team Sister Ines gets three cards too: the same two Time Extends and an uncommon special card titled Flee. That one can be used only once, and it teleports the whole squad away from combat. It does not say how far, or where to.
beats.gist: Team Sister Ines draws two Time Extends and a one-use Flee card that teleports the squad away.

beats.headline: Two from Katia
beats.text: Katia's deck is still thin: no mystics, no snares, only a couple of specials, and she is going totem hunting in a few hours. She pushes a pair of Flee Cards across to Carl. Take two, she says; they're consumable, so be careful. He also takes another Stout and two utilities he has not seen before, Blue Stuff for a totem's mana and Greased Lightning for a mob's speed.
beats.gist: Carl takes two Flee Cards from Katia, plus a Stout and two utilities.

beats.headline: A key for a key
beats.text: The final announcement changes one rule. Without a key, a Flee card works as it always has, teleporting the user out of a losing battle to a random place nearby, which is no help to someone guarding a door. A keyholder who flees automatically loses a key, one at random, to the opponent. That is also the only way to give a key away: start a battle and flee. Donut asks what they will do if Imani does not get a key, and Carl has been thinking on it: they will force her to fight them, Donut will use the Flee card and give her their key, and the bone key benefit on his jacket will open the door for him.
beats.gist: A fleeing keyholder loses a key, so Donut will flee a fight with Imani.

beats.headline: Three for three
beats.text: Quan plays Force Play, a mystic card Carl always assumed was dumb: pick a card in an opponent's hand, and it plays itself. Sister Ines has a Flee card in her hand. Team Quiteria flees and loses its key. Carl yells to Donut not to keep a Flee card in her hand; she has already discarded it. Then Quan swoops back and switches hands with her, three for three, all Flee cards, and casts another Force Play. Their squad flees, and its key and Team Quiteria's both go to Team Quan.
beats.gist: Quan's Force Play makes both other squads flee, and Team Quan takes their keys.

beats.headline: Jurgen flees
beats.text: The fighting has mostly calmed. Osvaldo and some guy named Jurgen got into a card battle, and Jurgen had to use a Flee card. He had really made good on his promise to break the stairwell, and now the two of them, somewhere in Brazil, are working together to clear the rubble away.
beats.gist: Jurgen uses a Flee card against Osvaldo, then the two work together clearing the stairwell rubble Jurgen made.

beats.headline: Too easy to flee
beats.text: Almost five thousand have died, and Carl knows more will before the collapse. Still, the number is shockingly low, and he sees the shape of it. They made it too easy to flee fights because they wanted these last few days to be the real slaughter, and the crawlers found a way out of it. They are hitting the ninth floor not scattered, not broken and not afraid, and in unprecedented numbers.
beats.gist: Almost five thousand have died, a low toll, because fleeing was too easy.

relations.note: forced on his opponents with Force Play

recap.text: Carl and Donut draw three common utility cards, while Team Sister Ines draws an uncommon special card titled Flee, which teleports the whole squad away once. Katia pushes two Flee Cards across to Carl, warning they are consumable. The final announcement makes a fleeing keyholder lose one key at random. Quan plays Force Play, switches hands with Donut, and sends three Flee cards for three, taking two keys.

tagline.text: Stout is a common T'Ghee utility card that adds 25% to a mob's health for the length of a combat. It is not a one-time consumable, and Carl and Donut collect one after a fight with the duendes.
Carl and Donut hold two Stout cards now. Carl takes the second from a pile of spare cards Katia's team brings over.

beats.headline: Three common cards
beats.text: When the fight is done, Carl and Donut have collected three common utility cards. Two are Time Extend cards, which double how long a summoned totem lasts, and the third is a Stout card, which adds 25% to a mob's health for the duration of combat. Unlike their combo card, these are not one-time consumables. Team Sister Ines gets three cards too. Nobody is sure yet how deck combat works.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut collect three common utility cards: two Time Extend cards and a Stout card, all reusable.

beats.headline: Spinning like a ninja star
beats.text: Geraldo the monk seal is summoned, the enemy is on its way, and Donut tries the utility cards on him. She puts her paw on the Stout card and flips it upward. It spins through the air like a ninja star and slams into the seal with a loud trumpet fanfare, and Geraldo glows as his health bar grows longer. The word Buffed appears over him in a comic-book explosion. This is quite festive, Donut says; why can't all the fights be like this?
beats.gist: Donut flips the Stout card at Geraldo the seal, and his health bar grows longer.

beats.headline: A second one from Katia
beats.text: Katia comes over to check on Carl and offers utility cards. Her team has little trolls everywhere, called the Lads, that drop a lot of cards, and Louis has mass killed about two hundred of them with a cloud attack. She plops a deck onto the counter, full of Time Extend and Buff cards and others Carl has not seen, and pushes over a pair of consumable Flee cards. Carl grabs another Stout card and two new utility cards, Blue Stuff and Greased Lightning.
beats.gist: Katia offers Carl utility cards, and he takes another Stout card plus Blue Stuff and Greased Lightning.

beats.headline: Into the practice deck
beats.text: Carl and Donut build an eighteen-card deck, and one of its six utility cards is a single Stout, which Carl lists as strength-increasing. In the practice room's 1980s shopping mall, Donut's first four cards are Greased Lightning, Stout, Shi Maria and Uzi Jesus. Carl tells her to save the utility cards and play the two totems: summon Jesus, talk to him for a second, then summon Shi Maria. He wants to see how the two work together.
beats.gist: Donut plays Jesus and Shi Maria together while Carl watches how the two totems work.

beats.headline: Onto the stolen warrior
beats.text: Donut's active deck for the turkey barn holds two Stout cards. Late in the fight, with zombie turkeys rising, she is distracted, slicing at one that moves to chomp onto the unconscious Mongo. She tosses a new card, but it is a Stout, and she tosses it onto her stolen lizard temple warrior, who keeps screaming about his mother. Then Carl runs at the turkey deckmaster, and his kick obliterates it.
beats.gist: Donut tosses a Stout card onto her stolen lizard temple warrior while Carl kicks the turkey deckmaster apart.

relations.note: the second Stout card, from her team's spares

recap.text: Donut tries the Stout card on Geraldo the monk seal, flipping it with her paw. It spins like a ninja star, slams into him with a trumpet fanfare, and lengthens his health bar, and Buffed bursts over him in comic-book letters. Katia then gives Carl a second Stout, Blue Stuff, Greased Lightning and two consumable Flee cards. In the turkey barn, Donut tosses a Stout onto her stolen lizard temple warrior while a zombie turkey goes for the unconscious Mongo.

tagline.text: Time Extend is a common T'Ghee utility card that doubles how long a summoned totem lasts. It is not consumable, and Carl and Donut have two.
Time Extend can be made permanent: a totem buffed with one and then hit with a Glow-Up card keeps the doubled summoning time in future battles.

beats.headline: Not consumable
beats.text: After the fight, Carl and Donut collect three common utility cards: two Time Extends, which double the time a summoned totem lasts, and a Stout card. Unlike their combo card, these are not one-time consumables. Team Sister Ines receives three cards as well: two more Time Extends, and an uncommon special card called Flee.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut collect three common utility cards, including two Time Extends, which are not one-time consumables.

beats.headline: Two buffs, no more
beats.text: With Geraldo the monk seal summoned and the enemy on its way, Donut tries the utility cards on him. After a Stout card has buffed his health, she activates the first Time Extend, and it lands on the seal with a comic-book explosion: sixty more seconds on his timer. The second will not go: uncommon totems can only hold two utility cards.
beats.gist: Donut summons Geraldo the seal, buffs him with a Stout card, and adds one Time Extend.

beats.headline: Made permanent
beats.text: A consumable special card called Glow-Up changes a card so it permanently reflects its current state, and Carl works out what that means for Time Extend. A totem with a summoning time of 120 seconds, buffed with a time extend and then given the Glow-Up, would summon for 240 seconds in every battle after. Glow-Up can only be used once, so the buffs will have to be stacked with care.
beats.gist: Carl learns Glow-Up makes a buffed card permanent, so a 120-second totem could summon for 240, once.

beats.headline: Onto the crab
beats.text: Deckmaster for three minutes on a beach of dead seals, Carl holds Golden Combo, a Time Extend and the card he came for, Raul the crab. He flips Raul into the water, and when the crab has finally been told what he is there to do, Carl tosses the time extend onto him just as the Midnight Express timer ends.
beats.gist: Carl flips Raul the crab into the water, then tosses a Time Extend onto him.

recap.text: Carl and Donut collect three common utility cards after the fight: two Time Extends and a Stout card. Donut buffs Geraldo the monk seal with Stout, then lands a Time Extend for sixty more seconds, but the second will not go, since uncommon totems hold only two utility cards. Carl works out that a Glow-Up would make a Time Extend permanent. As the Midnight Express timer ends, he tosses a Time Extend onto Raul the crab.

tagline.text: A Spirit Box is a set trap that roots whoever steps on it for sixty seconds, lowers their spirit resistance and summons a random non-corporeal entity to possess them. A haunted town in the fog is littered with them.

description.text: Spirit Box. Set Trap. Effect: Roots target in place. Lowers spirit resistance, and a random non-corporeal entity from the area is summoned to the location and will attempt to possess you. Or eat you. Or just melt your face off and put the goo on a spirit corndog or something. Target: Corporeal dumbasses who step on it. That means you. Duration: You will be rooted in place for sixty seconds. If you end up possessed, that's pretty damn permanent.

beats.headline: Dozens in the fog
beats.text: Traps, Anton says. Through the fog dozens of lights flash, all the same kind, a pair straight ahead side by side, while red dots drift toward the party, drawn by Paz. Carl kneels and examines the closest: a Spirit Box, a set trap that roots its target for sixty seconds, lowers spirit resistance and summons a random non-corporeal entity to try to possess it. Possession is pretty damn permanent. He disarms it and takes it into his inventory. There is no time for the second before three monsters shuffle out of the fog.
beats.gist: Carl disarms a Spirit Box, a trap that roots and possesses, and pockets it before three monsters arrive.

beats.headline: Tripper sets them all off
beats.text: Dozens more ghommids come out of the fog, all summoned by Paz's presence, and Carl calls for the saferoom. He casts Tripper, setting off every Spirit Box trap in town. He would rather farm them, but it is too risky to run with them everywhere; Mongo would set one off at any moment. Thousands of wails rise into the night as ghommids are summoned to traps all over. One, an owl the size of a man, pops into existence right in front of Carl above the second trap.
beats.gist: Carl casts Tripper, setting off every Spirit Box trap in town, and an owl ghommid appears.

recap.text: Carl kneels in the fog and examines the nearest of dozens of flashing lights: a Spirit Box, a set trap that roots its target for sixty seconds and summons a non-corporeal entity to possess it. He disarms it and pockets it, but three monsters shuffle out of the fog. Carl casts Tripper, setting off every Spirit Box in town, and thousands of wails rise as an owl the size of a man appears above the second trap.

tagline.text: Greased Lightning is a T'Ghee utility card that increases a mob's speed by 25%. Carl takes one from the spare cards Katia's team brings over, and thinks it would make Geraldo ridiculously fast.
Greased Lightning is a speed card Donut plays on her totems fight after fight, and her active deck now holds two of them.

beats.headline: From Katia's spare pile
beats.text: Katia's team has more cards than they know what to do with, dropped by little trolls called the Lads, and she plops a deck of them onto the counter. Carl sifts through it, grabs another Stout card and two utility cards he has not seen before: Blue Stuff, which increases a totem's supply of mana points, and Greased Lightning, which increases a mob's speed by 25%. Added to Geraldo, Carl thinks, it would make him ridiculously fast.
beats.gist: Carl takes Greased Lightning from Katia's spare pile; it speeds a mob by 25%.

beats.headline: Four spiders, one fast
beats.text: In the practice room's 1980s shopping mall, with Skylar Spinach split in two and fighting a reindeer herd, Donut's hand holds three cards and no totems. Play Greased Lightning on Shi Maria, Carl says. Donut flips it out toward the injured spider; it somersaults through the air like a boomerang and slaps onto her back. A giant lightning graphic appears with a crack, at the same moment Shi Maria casts an illusion and splits into four. One of the four is suddenly moving much more quickly than before.
beats.gist: Donut flips Greased Lightning onto Shi Maria, who splits into four; one copy speeds up.

beats.headline: Against the mud balls
beats.text: Carl and Donut lose the second of three deck-on-deck fights to a muddy blob guy whose deck is all tanks and snare cards. The blob hits Shi Maria with a Damnation card, and she wastes her time fighting a rolling mud ball with a high dodge. She only kills it after Donut hits her with Greased Lightning, and the blob simply summons another of the same monsters.
beats.gist: Donut's Greased Lightning kills a rolling mud ball, but the blob summons another.

beats.headline: To build his self-confidence
beats.text: Raul the crab is chasing a screeching ghost, a Reef Explorer, through the dark trees, and Lazarus wants to end it himself: that pansy is taking too long. Donut discards a card and tosses a Greased Lightning at Raul. It spins off like a ninja star, dodges a tree and hits the crab in a sparkle of digital confetti. Lazarus is to stay and protect her; Raul needs the experience. Raul snaps at the ghost, and when it tries to run behind a tree the speed-enhanced crab snaps again and cuts its leg off. It drops dead.
beats.gist: Donut tosses a Greased Lightning at Raul, and the sped-up crab snaps off the fleeing ghost's leg.

beats.headline: Onto Skylar Spinach
beats.text: Donut's active deck for the turkey barn holds two Greased Lightning cards. Her first totem is Skylar Spinach, who floats up toward the middle of the battlefield, and at the same moment she casts The Thief at the ogre, pulling a card out of the ogre's hand into her own deck. Weren't expecting that, were ya, she calls with autotuned glee, as she tosses a Greased Lightning onto Skylar.
beats.gist: Donut casts The Thief at the ogre and tosses a Greased Lightning onto her first totem, Skylar Spinach.

relations.note: from her team's spare cards

recap.text: Katia's team has more cards than they know what to do with, so she plops a deck of them onto the counter, and Carl sifts out Greased Lightning, which raises a mob's speed by 25%. Donut then flings it onto Shi Maria, who splits into four, one of them suddenly fast. She uses it again to finish a mud ball, and again on Raul the crab, who cuts a ghost's leg off.

tagline.text: Hobbled is a very rare, consumable snare card, the first snare card Carl and Donut own, out of Donut's gold T'Ghee box. Played on an enemy totem, it cuts the monster's summoning time by ninety per cent, and the cut stays with it for the rest of the combat.

beats.headline: The first snare card
beats.text: Back in the personal space, Donut opens three boxes. The bronze Stranger Danger box holds an expired tube of mace for a keychain, a joke prize with no magic at all. The gold T'Ghee box, earned for using the practice room, holds a single card: their first snare card, a very rare consumable called Hobbled, its face a pair of legs tied together. It cuts a totem's summoning time by ninety per cent, and if the totem times out and is pulled again, the cut persists through combat. A minute becomes six seconds. Too bad the card is consumable.
beats.gist: Donut opens three boxes and finds Hobbled, a card that cuts a totem's summoning time ninety per cent.

beats.headline: Into the practice deck
beats.text: Carl and Donut put together their first eighteen-card deck: six totems, six utility cards, three snares, two mystics and a single Flee card. The snares are pointless in a practice simulation, because they only work against an opponent carrying cards, but Carl wants a realistic deck, since a fight does not always give warning. Hobble, consumable, goes in with the mana-draining Hole in the Bag and the new Damnation card.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut build an eighteen-card practice deck, adding Hobble, a snare, for realism despite its uselessness.

recap.text: Donut opens three boxes in the personal space. The bronze one holds an expired tube of mace for a keychain. The gold one holds their first snare card, a very rare consumable called Hobbled, its face a pair of legs tied together. It cuts a totem's summoning time by ninety per cent, so a minute becomes six seconds. Carl puts it in their first eighteen-card deck anyway, for realism.

tagline.text: The Bard's Golden Throat is a golden, amethyst-encrusted headset microphone, voted to Princess Donut by her Princess Posse. It keeps her songs within a step and a half of the note, helps her form bard songs and spells, amplifies her voice two to five times, and adds five per cent to her Charisma.

description.text: The Bard's Golden Throat – Enchanted Headset Microphone. Nuclear power. The airplane. Transistors. Antibiotics. Important inventions and discoveries of the 1900's that changed the world. But those were nothing, absolutely nothing, compared to the greatest invention of the century. It happened in September of 1997. That was the day it all changed. That was the day a company called Antares Audio Technologies released into the wild a piece of software that finally cured a horrific disability that'd been plaguing young men and women for a millennia. The disability? Tone deafness. The cure? It was called AutoTune. …

beats.headline: A real one this time
beats.text: Donut's platinum fan box opens and she bounces with excitement: her Princess Posse voted on it, and it is a real one, not the prop she used at the party, with a purple jewel on it. She will look just like Britney, the real one. It is the Bard's Golden Throat, carrying the Golden Throat enchantment, the dungeon's autotune, which Mordecai went looking for on the sixth floor and never found. It tunes songs within a step and a half of the note, assists bard songs and spells, amplifies speech and song two to five times, and adds five per cent Charisma. Equipped, it makes her sound like she is talking through a fan.
beats.gist: Donut opens her platinum fan box and finds a headset microphone that autotunes and amplifies her voice.

beats.headline: A secret weapon
beats.text: Donut discovers she can make her voice even louder, and Mongo screeches. Carl looks up at the ceiling and suggests they keep it as a secret weapon. She supposes he is right. The headset goes into her inventory, on her hotlist, to put on when she needs a little extra oomph, or when he is not paying attention to her properly.
beats.gist: Donut tests her louder voice through the headset, Mongo screeches, and Carl suggests keeping it secret.

beats.headline: Limbered
beats.text: Among the ghommids, with Carl's back patch fed again, Donut sings from his shoulder, her voice electronic with autotune: she will protect her pretties, with her voice of an angel and her expertly sung ditties. It works. The party is limbered, its dexterity up by half. Still amplified and autotuned, Donut tells Carl to be quiet, because she needs to sing another verse to stack it. The second verse loses its rhyme, the boost is cancelled because the bard cannot hold a tune, and she is muted from singing for five minutes. She pulls the headset away.
beats.gist: Donut sings through her headset and limbers the party, but her rhymeless second verse cancels it.

beats.headline: Orders from a distance
beats.text: At the door of the turkey barn Carl tells Donut to get Clockwork Triplicate ready and pull out her microphone, and the headset poofs onto her head. She cannot cast while her deck is summoned, and her bard songs will not work either, because they must be activated from her interface. But they have found that with the headset on she can still amplify her voice and give orders from a distance.
beats.gist: Donut's headset lets her amplify her voice and give orders while her deck is summoned.

beats.headline: Full setting
beats.text: Amayon has Carl and Samantha in his hand, and Carl knows that any spell he casts will make the demon drop him or squeeze harder. Then Donut bellows at the demon at the top of her lungs, headset microphone at the full setting, autotune on. He orders her to turn off her spell or be obliterated. She will, she shouts back, if he lets her friends go.
beats.gist: Donut shouts through her headset at Amayon, who demands she stop; she agrees if he frees her friends.

beats.headline: Auto-Tune to the max
beats.text: Carl and Donut are to sing one of the guild-entrance songs, one listed with two singers, so that each of them has a performance bar. Carl takes the lead, because Donut has only a few lines and her chances are higher. She will use her headset with the Auto-Tune turned to the max, and Carl has to read a scroll, Gelded Choirboy, to hit the notes at all. Before they start, she raises the headset's volume and asks the crowd to encourage Carl: this is his first time singing ever, she tells them.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut sing a two-singer entrance song; Donut wears her Auto-Tune headset while Carl reads Gelded Choirboy.

beats.headline: Take on me
beats.text: When the chorus comes, Donut echoes Carl's line, her Auto-Tuned voice high and, thankfully, in key, piercing the chaos of the brawl in the bar like a knife. At the same moment she shoots a low-powered magic missile that blows an axe out of the hand of a Draconian about to sink it into the back of Dong's head.
beats.gist: Donut echoes Carl's chorus in key and blasts an axe from a Draconian's hand.

beats.headline: Borrowed, Auto-Tune off
beats.text: When Prepotente's song ends and it is Carl's turn, he taps the headset microphone he has borrowed from Donut, its Auto-Tune turned off for this. His voice reverberates over the stands as Hedy's truck passes, and he tells them what he told Donut about the difference between revenge and vengeance.
beats.gist: Carl borrows Donut's headset microphone, Auto-Tune off, and tells the stands about revenge versus vengeance.

recap.text: Donut opens her platinum fan box and finds the Bard's Golden Throat, a headset microphone with a purple jewel, the dungeon's autotune. Amplified, her voice makes Mongo screech, so Carl suggests she keep it as a secret weapon. Among the ghommids she sings the party limbered, but a second verse loses its rhyme and mutes her for five minutes. At full setting, she bellows at Amayon to let her friends go.

Carl sings lead on a guild-entrance song, reading the scroll Gelded Choirboy to hit the notes, while Donut tells the crowd it is his first time singing ever. At the chorus her Auto-Tuned voice pierces the brawl as she shoots a low-powered magic missile that blows an axe from the hand of a Draconian about to sink it into Dong's head. After Prepotente's song, Carl taps the borrowed headset microphone, Auto-Tune off, and tells the stands about revenge and vengeance.

tagline.text: The Thief is a mythic mystic card, black-bordered, that steals a card from an opponent. It is not consumable. The goddess Yemaya gave it to Princess Donut, and it gives her all five kinds of card.

beats.headline: A gift from a river goddess
beats.text: In her temple, Yemaya thanks Bomo for repairing her shrine and hands out tokens of her gratitude, one for brave Sister Ines and one for beautiful Princess Donut. Donut takes hers out of the air before Carl can examine it. It has the black border of mythical rareness, second only to the orange uniques. It is a mystic card, she shout-whispers, so they have all five kinds now; it lets them steal a card from someone else, it is not even consumable, and it is called The Thief.
beats.gist: Donut receives The Thief from Yemaya, a black-bordered mythical mystic card that steals another's card.

beats.headline: Out of the ogre's hand
beats.text: Donut opens the turkey-barn fight with Skylar Spinach and, at the same moment, casts her mystic card, The Thief, at the ogre, who is in the middle of summoning a card of her own. The card poofs out of the ogre's hand and appears in Donut's deck. Weren't expecting that, were ya, Donut calls with autotuned glee, as she tosses a Greased Lightning onto Skylar.
beats.gist: Donut casts The Thief at the ogre mid-summon, takes her card, and tosses Greased Lightning onto Skylar.

beats.headline: A protection, stolen
beats.text: As the giant Christmas cat starts to form, Donut plays her Thief card on the hydra, stealing a card from its hand, and scoffs loudly at whatever she has taken. It is a protection utility. When Shi Maria comes out, Donut hurls it onto the forming spider, and the card Lucian throws at Shi Maria disappears, ineffective, as the protection sputters out. He just wasted it, Donut crows: she used his own card against him.
beats.gist: Donut steals a protection card from the hydra, then hurls it at the forming spider, wasting Lucian's card.

beats.headline: Banjo, from a demon lord
beats.text: Donut's first move against Amayon is The Thief, cast just as the demon lord sweeps out his first totem. A card, not the one he is summoning, flicks up out of his deck, resizes itself and lands in her hand. Holy wow, she calls, look at that card. It is Banjo, a level-120 Hell Scrub, a gorilla-sized cloud of black tentacles, and it is what drags a succubus off Carl as his shield sparks out.
beats.gist: Donut casts The Thief on Amayon and takes Banjo, a level-120 Hell Scrub, from him.

recap.text: Donut opens the turkey-barn fight by casting her mystic card, The Thief, at an ogre mid-summon, and the ogre's card poofs out of her hand into Donut's deck. Against the hydra, she steals a protection utility and hurls it onto the forming spider, so Lucian's card against Shi Maria fizzles. Against Amayon, she steals Banjo, a level-120 Hell Scrub that drags a succubus off Carl.

tagline.text: Force Discard is a rare T'Ghee mystic card. It picks a random card from the opponent's hand and tosses it onto the discard pile.

beats.headline: Found while grinding
beats.text: Carl reaches level 65 and Donut 57, and he maxes out and drains his Scavenger's Daughter bar three times. They collect several more cards along the way, among them another snare that drains a totem's mana, and a rare mystic card called Force Discard, which picks a random card from the opponent's hand and tosses it onto the discard pile.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut hit levels 65 and 57, then collect more cards, including the rare mystic Force Discard.

beats.headline: Out of the judge's hand
beats.text: Against the keymaster, Judge Lucian snatches Donut's new staff totem with a steal-totem snare. She answers with Shi Maria and throws the utility she stole at the start of the fight onto the forming spider, a protection. Lucian looks ready to throw another totem, and Donut flips her Force Discard onto him: the card vanishes from his hand in a puff of smoke. His next card at Shi Maria disappears too, ineffective, and the protection sputters out. Ha, says Donut.
beats.gist: Donut flips Force Discard onto Judge Lucian, vanishing his totem card and fizzling his next throw.

beats.headline: Amayon's last card
beats.text: Amayon's row is down to two cards: the rock monster still active, and one in his hand he is struggling to play, growling as his claw refuses to move. Carl realises it is Ysalte holding him back: she knows that once he is out of cards he is free to cast his spells. Carl calls to Donut. She is on it. She tosses out Force Discard, and Amayon's last card disappears with a Poof. Suck it, Donut shrieks, and the kaiju-sized demon lets out a satisfied grunt.
beats.gist: Carl realises Ysalte is holding Amayon back, and Donut's Force Discard removes his last card.

recap.text: Carl reaches level 65 and Donut 57, and they collect a rare mystic card called Force Discard, which tosses a random card from the opponent's hand onto the discard pile. Against the keymaster, Donut flips it onto Judge Lucian as he looks ready to throw another totem, and his card vanishes in a puff of smoke. Against Amayon, she tosses it at his last card, and it disappears with a Poof.

tagline.text: Hole in the Bag is a snare card that drains a totem's mana. Unlike Hobbled, it is not consumable, so it can be played fight after fight.

beats.headline: Picked up on the road
beats.text: On the way south toward the swamp where Samantha and the boss spider wait, Carl and Donut grind through mobs, most of them talking birds, none of them worth a flag. Among the cards they collect is one more snare card, called Hole in the Bag, which drains a totem's mana. Unlike their Hobble card, this one is not consumable. They also find a rare mystic card called Force Discard.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut pick up a non-consumable snare card, Hole in the Bag, which drains a totem's mana.

beats.headline: One of three snares
beats.text: In the first eighteen-card deck Carl and Donut build for practice, Hole in the Bag is one of three snare cards, beside the consumable Hobble and the new Damnation. None of them can do anything in the simulation, since snares only work against card-carrying opponents. Carl wants them in anyway, and suspects snares may be worth more than utility cards, of which the deck has six.
beats.gist: Hole in the Bag is one of three snare cards in Carl and Donut's practice deck.

recap.text: Hole in the Bag, a snare card that drains a totem's mana, turns up on the road south among the cards Carl and Donut collect from mobs, mostly talking birds. Unlike their Hobble card, it is not consumable. In their first eighteen-card practice deck it sits beside Hobble and the new Damnation, though snares do nothing in the simulation, since they only work against card-carrying opponents. Carl wants them in anyway.

entities.name: Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly

tagline.text: The Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly is a simple silver-coloured tiara from the gnome jeweller at the Desperado, set with Donut's citrine for 25,000 gold. It halves her potion cooldown, adds ten intelligence, cancels the dexterity debuff when she is drunk, and gives her a level-10 Hover five times a day.
Donut has set the dragonfly tiara on a charging pillow, which drains an item of all its magic and stores it for a like item.

description.text: Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly. There’s a children’s story out there about a dragonfly who gets so drunk that his wife won’t let him come home, so he hovers in the air above their nest, waiting for her to go to sleep, so he can get to bed. The thing is, the wife knows he’s out there, and she ain’t moving. So the dragonfly either hovers all night or moves to the highest point, sitting on a leaf, overlooking his home, waiting for his wife to turn the light back on to signify he’s out of the doghouse. This tiara has been made to honor that poor Dragonfly with the angry wife. …

beats.headline: The citrine, set at last
beats.text: Donut is walking on air, two feet off the ground, on the fourth Hover of the day. Her Flawless Jeweler's Gem is a large citrine, not her colour. They have kept her Tiara of Mana Genita and bought a blank tiara from the gnome jeweler at the Desperado Club; it took her twenty minutes to pick a simple silver-coloured one, and 25,000 gold to have the jewel installed. Her dislike of the colour ended with the description: half the potion cooldown, ten intelligence, no dexterity debuff when drunk, and a level-10 Hover, five a day for about ninety seconds, a dollar-store version of Elle's.
beats.gist: Donut hovers two feet up, her citrine set in a silver tiara for 25,000 gold.

beats.headline: Off, for the sailor hat
beats.text: Wearing a dead man's sailor hat means giving up her new Hover skill and ten intelligence, Carl points out. Donut has already talked to Mordecai about it: she will wear the hat until she runs out of cards, then put her new dragonfly tiara back on. The hat lowers the draw countdown by two seconds, and it is quite jaunty.
beats.gist: Donut will wear the sailor hat until her cards run out, then return to the tiara.

beats.headline: Showing off the Hover
beats.text: Carl has just learned in chat that Lucia means to kill Donut and her pet dinosaur on the next floor, and he looks nervously at Donut. She is standing on the edge of Tran's flying wheelchair module, and she laughs with delight, switches into her dragonfly tiara, and casts Hover to show them all her new skill. Carl holds himself back from chiding her for wasting a five-times-a-day skill. Tran smiles and pets her.
beats.gist: Donut laughs, switches into her dragonfly tiara and casts Hover on Tran's flying wheelchair module.

beats.headline: On the purple pillow
beats.text: A box gives Donut a second charging pillow, purple instead of red: it drains any magical item, but transfers only to a like item. Mordecai wants hats draining before they move on. Grumbling, Donut sets the pillows on the counter, her new boonie hat on the red one and the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the other, and each clicks as it touches. When talk turns to which of her spells and skills Quan's cloak might raise to fifteen, she remembers that her Hover is part of the dragonfly tiara and wants it back on. Hover would not be worth it, Mordecai thinks, and her pool of skills runs to thousands anyway. Okay, she sniffs.
beats.gist: Donut sets her hat and tiara on the two pillows; Mordecai says Hover isn't worth it.

relations.note: the blank tiara came from its gnome jeweller
drained on a charging pillow

recap.text: Donut hovers two feet off the ground in the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly, whose large citrine is not her colour. The gnome jeweler at the Desperado Club set it for 25,000 gold. She will wear a dead man's sailor hat until her cards run out. When Carl learns Lucia means to kill her and her pet dinosaur, Donut casts Hover to show off, and Carl bites back his scolding.

A box gives Donut a second charging pillow, purple to go with the red one. Grumbling, she sets her new boonie hat on the red pillow and the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the other, and each clicks. She wants her Hover, which is part of the tiara, back on, but Mordecai thinks it is not worth it, since her skills run to thousands. Okay, she sniffs.

tagline.text: Liquid Therapy is a protection potion Mordecai brews against Shi Maria's Unending Insanity and Lights Out, which nothing short of divine intervention can cure. One dose a day lasts until the drinker sleeps, and it covers a host of other fear-based debuffs besides.

beats.headline: One dose a day
beats.text: Reading the entry on the spider that swallowed Samantha, Carl finds two level-15 spells, Unending Insanity and the blindness spell Lights Out, neither of which can be cured without divine intervention. Mordecai has prepared for this. His potion is called Liquid Therapy: taken once a day, it protects until the drinker sleeps, against both spells and a host of other fear-based debuffs and afflictions. The ingredients are expensive, but he makes enough for the whole guild, and Carl has spent both his table upgrade coupons on Mordecai's alchemy table. Carl and Donut have taken theirs; Mongo's is not ready yet.
beats.gist: Liquid Therapy shields the drinker from Unending Insanity and Lights Out until sleep.

recap.text: Mordecai's potion, Liquid Therapy, answers the two level-15 spells in the spider's entry, Unending Insanity and the blindness spell Lights Out, which no one can cure without divine intervention. Taken once a day, it protects the drinker until sleep against both spells and a host of other fear-based debuffs and afflictions. Carl spent both his table upgrade coupons on Mordecai's alchemy table, and Mordecai makes enough for the whole guild. Carl and Donut have drunk theirs; Mongo's is not ready.

tagline.text: Damnation is an uncommon T'Ghee snare card. It does not kill an enemy totem; it makes sure the totem goes to the discard pile when its time runs out, dead or not.

beats.headline: Dropped by La Ciguapa
beats.text: Samantha smells something off the path, and under a pile of dead undergrowth at the foot of a kapok tree Mongo pounces on a sleeping hairy woman with backward feet and chomps her before she fully wakes. La Ciguapa, legendary, charming and hard to kill except by pets: a wasted chance for the deck. But she drops two cards. One is an uncommon snare called Damnation, which sends an enemy totem to the discard pile once it times out, whether it is dead or not. Good against powerful monsters they could not otherwise kill.
beats.gist: Mongo chomps the sleeping La Ciguapa, who drops Damnation, a snare card that discards an enemy totem.

beats.headline: Turned on Shi Maria
beats.text: The second of three deck fights is against a muddy blob guy whose deck is all tanks and snares, and Carl holds back on purpose to see his strategy. The blob hits Shi Maria with the same Damnation card they own, and she wastes her time on a rolling mud ball with a high dodge. When she times out, the snare sends her to the discard pile, enraged and screaming. Other snares freeze Raul and Asojano, and both die. With no totems left, a mud ball rolls up and explodes over them, and they lose the fight.
beats.gist: Shi Maria's deck loses: snares discard her and freeze Raul and Asojano, then a mud ball explodes.

relations.note: an opponent's copy

recap.text: Mongo pounces on a sleeping La Ciguapa and chomps her before she wakes, and she drops Damnation, a snare that discards an enemy totem when it times out, dead or not. Carl holds back against a muddy blob whose deck is tanks and snares. The blob hits Shi Maria with Damnation, and she times out chasing a mud ball, discarded and screaming. Snares freeze and kill Raul and Asojano, and a mud ball explodes over the rest.

tagline.text: Glow-Up is a mythic, one-use T'Ghee special card that fixes a card as it stands at that moment, buffs and all, so a totem stretched by a Time Extend keeps the longer summoning in every fight after.
Ren has handed Carl a second Glow-Up along with all of her cards but her totems.

beats.headline: Not on the list
beats.text: The second card La Ciguapa drops is a mythic special effect card that is not on the list of known card types: Glow-Up, consumable. Cast on any active card or totem, theirs or an enemy's, it changes the card so it permanently reflects its current state. A totem that summons for 120 seconds, buffed with a Time Extend and then given a Glow-Up, summons for 240 in future battles. One use only. Stack the buffs cleverly, and an already strong card becomes practically immortal.
beats.gist: The Glow-Up card, dropped by La Ciguapa, permanently locks in a card's or totem's current buffed state, once.

beats.headline: Spent on a fusion
beats.text: From the practice arena Donut reports that Shi Maria wanted the Glow-Up used on her. Donut spent it otherwise, on her own judgment. To fit Katia's Jola into the deck, she combined two of the problem cards with the consumable Combo card, used up all the utility buffs on them, and then cast the Glow-Up to make the change permanent. Getting rid of Shi Maria, or combining her, was considered and dropped: they need her to survive what comes next.
beats.gist: Donut spent the Glow-Up herself, fusing two problem cards with Combo so Katia's Jola fits.

beats.headline: Frozen with its buffs
beats.text: Church organ music, fat digital cherubs and a herd of digital street dogs: the new totem's reveal is the craziest of all their cards. After the fight Carl reads its orange card. Unique. Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang. Level 140. Created via Combo, and frozen in place via a Glow-Up with active buffs, its available utility slots lowered as a result. Summoning duration two hundred seconds; Constitution eighty.
beats.gist: Carl reads the orange card: Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, level 140, made by Combo, frozen by Glow-Up.

beats.headline: Ren's last cards
beats.text: Ren has rearranged her deck and taken out everything but her totems, and she gives Carl all the rest, a few rare specials and mystics among them that she never got to use. The last two are a consumable Glow-Up card and a consumable special called The Midnight Express, two large men in tights. The cards will not go into his inventory, so he sticks them in the waistband of his boxers. Make them suffer, she says.
beats.gist: Ren gives Carl her leftover cards, and he tucks two into his boxers.

beats.headline: Lazarus and Skylar, for good
beats.text: Alpha Male Carl is in the deck only because they were a totem short: Donut used the Golden Combo to fuse Lazarus with Skylar Spinach, and then added Ren's other consumable card, the Glow Up, to make the combination permanent. The stronger versions of Asojano and Uzi Jesus make it a great, powerful combo, the more so since a single card may come with them onto the next floor.
beats.gist: Donut fuses Lazarus with Skylar Spinach using the Golden Combo, then makes the Glow Up permanent.

recap.text: La Ciguapa drops a Glow-Up, which freezes a card in its current buffed state for good. Donut spends it on a Combo of two problem cards, not on Shi Maria, whom they need alive, to fit Katia's Jola. It yields Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, level 140. Ren hands Carl her cards, and Donut spends her Glow Up fusing Lazarus with Skylar Spinach for good.

tagline.text: Glory Bound is the worst of the drugs Katia has been taking and by far the most addictive: it puts her in a coma to relive a memory. She has taken it once. The cure, Mordecai says, is a bad trip of the same drug.

Mordecai's modified Glory Bound is a fizzing green gel: two hits of the drug compounded with a subdermal gel and a potion called Tough Love. Under it Katia must relive her worst memory, and Carl, with Removal Order added to his dose, is meant to enter the spider's.
The treatment has worked, for Katia as far as Carl can tell, and for him sort of: Shi Maria is trapped, though the eye on his chest remains.

beats.headline: The bad one
beats.text: Katia vomits again, and Carl sends Mordecai a private message: tell me about these drugs. Mordecai lists them. Travis Priest, a strong painkiller, cured first. Creamsicle Charm, ground-up fairy wings. The blitz sticks. Finally there is Glory Bound, which she has taken only once, thank goodness. It is the bad one, by far the most addictive: it puts her in a coma and lets her relive a memory, like blitz but much stronger. Without more she will slowly go insane, unable to tell then from now. So the cure is a bad trip of Glory Bound, a regular dose with some stuff added, and she will have to relive one of her worst memories.
beats.gist: Mordecai says Katia's cure is a bad Glory Bound trip through one of her worst memories.

beats.headline: One jar, two treatments
beats.text: In a new field hospital at the base, Mordecai sets a fizzing green jar on the counter, thick carbonated slime: two hits of Glory Bound compounded with a subdermal gel and a potion called Tough Love, brewed since the last floor and now in its short window of potency. Carl's dose gets Removal Order as well, so that, Mordecai hopes, he will visit the spider's memories instead of his own, and at the end he can choose to lock Shi Maria in hers. The drug began outside the inner system as a medication for learning difficult tasks, and it lingers in the dungeon in quests and traps. Mordecai rubs the gel on Katia's neck and slops a cold, fizzing blob on Carl.
beats.gist: Mordecai doses Katia with Glory Bound gel and Tough Love, and gives Carl Removal Order too.

beats.headline: Waking up somewhere else
beats.text: Carl blinks awake on the other side of the map, in what he thinks is the high elf castle, with no idea how he got there. The memory they shared is a jumble, like a real dream. He suspects Katia's treatment worked. His own worked, sort of: the spider's husband, a god called Hapanzi, reappeared at the end and told him he has her now, good and trapped, and not to set her free unless all is lost. The eye on Carl's chest is still a tattoo, but now he can see from it when it opens.
beats.gist: Carl wakes far from where he fell, and Hapanzi tells him to keep the spider trapped.

relations.note: the modified dose

recap.text: Katia vomits again, and Carl messages Mordecai to ask about the drugs. Mordecai lists them: Travis Priest, a painkiller, already cured; Creamsicle Charm, ground-up fairy wings; the blitz, which sticks; and Glory Bound, taken only once. Glory Bound is by far the most addictive, and without more she will slowly go insane, unable to tell then from now. The cure is a bad trip of it, in which she relives one of her worst memories.

Mordecai sets a fizzing green jar on the counter: two hits of Glory Bound, a subdermal gel, Tough Love potion, plus Removal Order in Carl's dose. He rubs the gel on Katia's neck and slops a cold blob on Carl. Carl blinks awake across the map, in what he thinks is the high elf castle. Hapanzi, the spider's husband, has her trapped and tells him not to free her unless all is lost.

tagline.text: The sailor hat belonged to Robert the Human, a hunched old man in a white sailor's outfit much too small for him, until Mongo took his throat. It is the first thing Donut collects.
Donut's white sailor hat cuts two seconds off her card-draw countdown, at the price of her Hover skill and ten points of intelligence, so it goes on when the deck comes out.

beats.headline: Robert the Human
beats.text: Donut's first opponent in the house is a hunched man of about seventy, twitching, in a white, old-school sailor's outfit much too small for him, with a nametag reading Gene and a note floating over him that says Robert the Human, level 40. A tall, faceless doll in a sailor suit fights on his side. Just as Geraldo goes for the doll, Mongo flies through the air and chomps onto Robert's throat, and the fight is over. The first thing Donut does is collect the dead man's sailor hat.
beats.gist: Donut's first opponent, Robert the Human, falls when Mongo chomps his throat, and Donut takes his sailor hat.

beats.headline: Nice dixie cup
beats.text: Donut wears the white sailor hat cockeyed on her head, and it looks ridiculous. Nice dixie cup, Carl says: she looks like she is in the navy. She thinks it divine. It costs her the new Hover skill and ten intelligence, but she has talked to Mordecai: she will wear it until she runs out of cards, then put her new dragonfly tiara back on. It lowers the card-draw countdown by two seconds, and it is quite jaunty. Carl did not know there was magic gear made for the cards.
beats.gist: Donut wears a white sailor hat cockeyed, trading Hover and ten intelligence for faster card draws.

beats.headline: Under eight seconds
beats.text: In a card duel under the heat lamps, Donut holds a single card when another appears in her hand, giving her two. The next will come in just under eight seconds, thanks to her sailor hat, while the turkey guard roars, charges toward Carl, and turns gobbling on Skylar Spinach when the snake smacks him with its tail.
beats.gist: Donut's sailor hat gives her a second card, and the turkey guard charges Carl.

beats.headline: Sunglasses and the hat
beats.text: A poet is charming them with poetry, and Donut finds it very unrealistic. Carl casts Wisp Armor on himself against the charm, and Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on Mongo. Calmer now after her first panic, she pops her sunglasses back on and switches to her sailor hat, with its two seconds off the draw countdown on her cards.
beats.gist: Donut calms, switches to her sailor hat, and she and Carl cast Wisp Armor and Clockwork Triplicate.

beats.headline: Back to the sailor cap
beats.text: Two decks to handle at once: offence against Amayon, whose six totems must die before he can be talked to, and defence against the Vinegar Bitch, whose deck must not run dry for ten minutes. Donut looks terrified and puts on a brave, determined face. She has switched back to her sailor cap. It used to look ridiculous on her, especially with the sunglasses, but now it seems more appropriate, in a way Carl cannot explain.
beats.gist: Donut switches back to her sailor cap while facing Amayon's six totems and the Vinegar Bitch's ten-minute deck.

recap.text: Mongo chomps onto Robert the Human's throat, and Donut collects the dead man's white sailor hat. She wears it cockeyed, and Carl calls it a nice dixie cup. It costs her the new Hover skill and ten intelligence, but it cuts two seconds off her card-draw countdown. Facing Amayon's six totems and the Vinegar Bitch's deck, she switches back to it, and Carl no longer finds it ridiculous.

tagline.text: A Scroll of Build Trench lays down a permanent trench two point three metres deep and two wide, as long as its user's intelligence plus strength allows. Scrolls can be combined to add sleeping quarters and other front-line accessories.
Build Trench scrolls keep turning up in crawlers' inventories. Carl has about fifty, and Louis likens them to the bandages and torches of the first floor.
Thousands of Build Trench scrolls carried down from the eighth floor have become a labyrinth of trenches on the front, with bunkers, hospitals and fall-back positions.
A Build Trench line laid across an enemy trench can be enjoined to it. It is a long-standing exploit: the scroll is craft magic and ignores most protections.

description.text: Scroll of Build Trench. Boy, I hope you’re up on your knowledge of the fighting techniques of the first world war. Allows for the placement of a permanent trench two point three meters deep and two meters wide. Length of trench is variable based on user’s intelligence plus strength. Combine scrolls to add reinforced sleeping quarters and other front-line accessories.

beats.headline: Five in a Silver Spam box
beats.text: Donut's rewards are mostly card moves from her first and last fights; Carl's are mostly bronze adventurer boxes. The Silver Spam box holds a pile of scrolls, five Scrolls of Build Trench, its description hoping he is up on the fighting techniques of the first world war. Each lays a permanent trench two point three metres deep and two wide, its length set by his intelligence plus strength, and scrolls combine into reinforced sleeping quarters and other front-line accessories. He puts them away and waits for the Prepotente box to open.
beats.gist: Carl's Silver Spam box holds five Scrolls of Build Trench, each laying a permanent trench.

beats.headline: Fifty of them
beats.text: The stairwell doorways are breaking, and the game is balancing that unfairness in a really messed-up way. Carl sees it now. He asks everybody who can hear him whether they have been getting Build Trench scrolls in their inventories; he has about fifty. Mandla has a ton of them too, and Louis says they are like the bandages and torches on the first floor.
beats.gist: Carl finds he has about fifty Build Trench scrolls, and Mandla and Louis report the same glut.

beats.headline: Tunnel under the chamber
beats.text: Carl's instructions go out to everybody who has lost a key: clear the stairwell chamber of debris and isolate it, nothing on it, above it or around it, and blow it up fast if need be. Then find a Build Trench scroll and tunnel underneath the chamber, with room for the whole party under the room. Mordecai is to put the satchel bombs from Carl's studio on the market for the demolition. Elle asks whether this is a sure thing. It is a theory, Carl admits, not a sure thing.
beats.gist: Carl has the keyless tunnel under the stairwell chamber, calling the plan a theory.

beats.headline: A labyrinth on the front
beats.text: Literal thousands of Build Trench scrolls, collected on the previous floor, have made a labyrinth of trenches along the front: traps and soldiers, fortified bunkers, hospitals, fall-back positions and more. No Man's Land between the two lines is only about two hundred and fifty metres. The forward-most trench is about twelve feet deep, with scaffolding at the front so soldiers can engage the enemy, and red-tinged mud in the bottom that smells of smoke and earth and sweat.
beats.gist: Thousands of Build Trench scrolls have dug a labyrinth of trenches along the front.

beats.headline: Into the enemy's trench
beats.text: Caught in an unprotected crater, Carl tells the band to keep back and reads a scroll. It takes about ten seconds. A translucent line appears with a map, and he turns it ninety degrees so it meets the enemy trench in a T. Enjoin? Yes. His elevation is lower; proceed? Yes, and Dig. At the end of the new channel a Saccathian soldier drops as the ground disappears beneath him. All around, soldiers in other craters do the same with their own scrolls, cutting into the enemy trenches and past most of the protections.
beats.gist: Carl reads a scroll in an open crater and digs a trench that drops a Saccathian soldier.

recap.text: Carl finds five Scrolls of Build Trench in a Silver Spam box, each laying a permanent trench two point three metres deep and two wide, and puts them away. Seeing the stairwell doorways break, he asks everyone about their scrolls: he has about fifty, Mandla a ton. He orders a tunnel dug beneath the stairwell chamber. Elle asks if it is sure. It is a theory, Carl admits.

Carl reads a Build Trench scroll in an unprotected crater, after telling the band to keep back. He turns the translucent line ninety degrees so it meets the enemy trench in a T, then answers Yes to Enjoin and Yes to Dig. A Saccathian soldier drops as the ground vanishes under him, and soldiers in other craters cut their own channels past most of the enemy's protections.

tagline.text: Lamp is a consumable snare card that paralyses a totem for ten seconds and makes it glow brightly. Carl and Donut take ten of them from the deck of one deckmaster, a Nightgaunt.

beats.headline: Ten of them, from a Nightgaunt
beats.text: Deckmaster number seven of ten is a Nightgaunt, and Carl's cloak aggravates it so much that it ignores its own deck to try spells on him until Jola slams it to the ground and kills it. It drops thirty cards. Eighteen are totems, one a legendary Demon Queen and the rest Quench Moths, which gain speed and constitution when touching a light. Ten are consumable snare cards, all called Lamp: each paralyses a totem for ten seconds and makes it glow brightly. Played, snares and moths would have made a hard fight. Carl and Donut take the token and all the cards they can, and leave the totems.
beats.gist: Jola kills a Nightgaunt, and Carl and Donut take its token and ten Lamp snares.

beats.headline: Stuck in her hand
beats.text: In a collapsing building, with demons coming from both sides and Imani holding them off where she is trapped with Tran, Donut reads out her hand: Alpha Carl, Shi Maria, the Golden Combo and the Lamp snare. Her Hole spell is loaded into her staff totem, and the staff is not in her hand. She cannot discard for a bit. Carl tells her to discard when she can, especially the snares, and play everything else until the staff comes up.
beats.gist: Donut reads out Imani's hand; Carl says to discard the snares and play the rest.

recap.text: Deckmaster number seven of ten, a Nightgaunt, is so aggravated by Carl's cloak that it ignores its own deck to try spells on him, until Jola slams it down and kills it. It drops thirty cards: eighteen totems, a legendary Demon Queen, Quench Moths, and ten snare cards called Lamp. Carl and Donut take the token and every card they can, leaving the totems.

tagline.text: The Sentient Necro Staff, the Worm Fulcrum, is what the ogre deckmaster Sharp Elbows summons from a mystic Necro card combined with a Walking Stick totem: a living tree of a staff that raises the dead turkeys around her as zombies. It is both a totem and a mystic card, Donut protests.

The staff card is Princess Donut's now. It is not consumable and takes no totem slot; before a fight she imbues it with one of her own spells, to cast once, and the staff looks different depending on the spell it holds.

description.text: Remember when you were extra naughty, and your daddy told you to go fetch his belt? This is kind of like that, but a lot more gross. Combination of a mystic Necro card and a Walking Stick totem, it's the Worm Fulcrum! Sentient Necro Staff. Level 50.

beats.headline: The Worm Fulcrum
