beats.text: In the turkey barn, to the riff of a Muse song, a small tree rises out of the floor: gnarled roots and leaves, feathers and turkey claws, a black human heart beating on a branch, and on top the golden skull of a large lizard with gems for eyes. The ogre deckmaster Sharp Elbows tosses her walking staff aside and yanks the tree out of the ground, spewing earthworms. The AI announces a Necro card combined with a Walking Stick totem. Donut protests that it is both a totem and a mystic card. Purple light spreads, and the dead turkeys rise.
beats.gist: Sharp Elbows yanks a tree from the barn floor, and the dead turkeys rise.

beats.headline: Snapped by a crab
beats.text: Carl kicks the turkey deckmaster to pieces, and the barn starts to slide toward the cliff. The ogre, still clutching her staff, slams into him like a truck and holds on, her spikes in him, her face against his. Then a loud crack of wood, and the music stops: Raul the crab has snapped the necro staff in half, killing her last totem. He decapitates the ogre next.
beats.gist: Raul the crab snaps the ogre's necro staff in half, killing her last totem, then decapitates her.

beats.headline: In Donut's deck
beats.text: While Carl was out, Donut grabbed every card left floating at the edge of the fight, and Sharp Elbows had a lot. The magical staff card is in their deck now. It is a special card but not consumable; it takes no totem slot, though it holds a card slot while active. She must imbue it with one of her spells before a fight, and can then cast that spell once. The staff works like a totem and looks different depending on the spell. She has already set it up and tried it on Geraldo, and they all started fighting each other until she yelled at them.
beats.gist: Donut's deck now holds the staff card, imbued with one spell for one cast.

beats.headline: Brass, and snatched
beats.text: Against the Reminiscence Hydra, Donut throws her new staff totem. It plants itself beside her with a thrum, brass now with a little cog spinning on top, imbued with Clockwork Triplicate, its card still floating in her hand. At once Judge Lucian throws a snare onto it, and the whole staff reappears next to the hydra. Snatched. Lucian uses it, and three Monobrow Sam heads turn their death ray on Shi Maria together. Dying, she snaps the staff with her legs.
beats.gist: Donut throws her brass staff totem, but Judge Lucian snares it, and Shi Maria dies snapping it.

beats.headline: The Hole spell, out of reach
beats.text: Donut has loaded the Hole spell into her staff totem, in the hope of cutting an enemy totem or deckmaster in half. Now, in a collapsing building with Imani and Tran trapped and demons coming up from both sides, a hole is exactly what they need, and the staff is not in her hand. Carl tells her to discard or play everything she can until she gets it.
beats.gist: Donut's Hole spell is loaded in her staff, out of reach, as Imani and Tran are trapped.

recap.text: Sharp Elbows yanks a tree of feathers, turkey claws and a beating black heart, topped with a golden lizard skull, out of the barn floor, and the dead turkeys rise. Raul the crab snaps her staff in half, and Donut has already grabbed the staff card from the cards left floating. Judge Lucian snares Donut's thrown staff, imbued with Clockwork Triplicate, and three Monobrow Sam heads fire on Shi Maria, who snaps it with her legs as she dies.

tagline.text: The Golden Combo is a unique T'Ghee card that works like the Combo, fusing two totems for a time, but it is not consumable, so it can be played over and over.
When a Golden Combo's intended target dies mid-play, it proceeds to the next available minion target, and that is how Carl has been combined with Shi Maria.

beats.headline: Not consumable
beats.text: Carl's head is starting to clear, and Donut reels off the haul. They got another combo card, a unique one called Golden Combo: it works the same way as the last, but it is not consumable, so she can do it over and over. Imagine the possibilities. With the new cards, she says, she is pretty much indestructible, and maybe she can do this last fight by herself. Carl asks whether that is a joke. Not even a little bit.
beats.gist: Donut says the new Golden Combo card isn't consumable, so she can reuse it, and fight alone.

beats.headline: In Carl's hand
beats.text: On the beach with the deck in his control, Carl draws a hand of the Midnight Express, still persistent, the Golden Combo, which would let him temporarily combine two totems, a Time Extend, and the card he wants, Raul the crab. They are a totem short because Donut used the Golden Combo to fuse Lazarus with Skylar Spinach and then made the fusion permanent with Ren's Glow Up.
beats.gist: Carl's hand is a totem short because Donut fused Lazarus with Skylar Spinach.

beats.headline: Combined with Shi Maria
beats.text: Donut's hand: Alpha Carl, Shi Maria, the Golden Combo and a snare, and no Flee cards anywhere in the deck. Carl tells her to summon Shi Maria and Alpha Carl and combine them. Both appear, the spider far too tall for the hallway, metal snapping as her legs snake in. Donut tosses out the Golden Combo. Shi Maria shoves a leg through the back of Alpha Carl's head. The intended target of the Golden Combo has been incapacitated, the System announces, so it proceeds to the next available minion target. That's you. Carl has been combined with Shi Maria.
beats.gist: Donut summons Shi Maria and Alpha Carl; the Golden Combo, thrown at Alpha Carl, falls on Carl instead.

beats.headline: Not that one either
beats.text: One card may come with them past the collapse. Donut had meant it to be Lazarus or the Golden Combo, and now she offers Paz's card instead, in case there is a way to set him free. Carl remembers Paz's face the last time Sister Ines summoned him: please, no more. They should never have let her turn him into a card, and it was his fault. And they are not taking the Golden Combo card either.
beats.gist: Donut offers Paz's card to take past the collapse, and Carl refuses both it and the Golden Combo.

recap.text: Donut reels off the haul to Carl: a unique card called Golden Combo, which works like the last combo card but is not consumable. On the beach, she has already spent it fusing Lazarus with Skylar Spinach, then made the fusion permanent with Ren's Glow Up. In the hallway, the System sends it to its next minion target after Shi Maria shoves a leg through Alpha Carl's head: Carl, now combined with Shi Maria.

tagline.text: Carl's father's Glock is a 9mm pistol, the only gun his father had, and Carl takes it, along with two boxes of ammo, from his father's bedroom in the floor's recording of the trailer.
The Glock came from outside the dungeon, so Carl cannot fire it as it is: once he handles them the rounds are overpowered, and the gun would probably explode.
Carl keeps his father's Glock in his inventory and has no intention of wearing it or using it, even after a fan box sends him ammunition and a shoulder holster with his name on it.

beats.headline: The only gun he had
beats.text: With five minutes left in the recording, Carl goes to the master bedroom so he does not have to listen, and takes everything he can. Three packs of Marlboro Reds from the bottom drawer of the old dresser. A folder of court documents. A 9mm Glock, with two boxes of ammo. The keys to the motorcycle and the Ford truck. Then the dresser itself, the bed and the clothes. His father had only the single gun. A Centipede cabinet stands in the too-small room, and Carl takes that too: his gun, his motorcycle, his arcade cabinet.
beats.gist: Carl takes his father's only gun, a 9mm Glock, and his motorcycle keys.

beats.headline: You're not a gun guy
beats.text: Waiting for the fight, Carl turns his dad's Glock over in his hands. It has been well looked after; his dad always had guns and never let him touch them. Donut sniffs at it: he is not a gun guy. He had training in boot, Carl says, in the Coast Guard. But it came from outside the dungeon. Fired, it would probably explode, because the rounds are overpowered once he handles them, and he would have to adjust each round's yield in his bomber's studio. Donut wants a pink holster for it and suggests Florin. Carl puts the gun away.
beats.gist: Carl turns over his dad's Glock, which Donut sniffs at, and puts it away unfired.

beats.headline: A holster from the fans
beats.text: The first gold box Carl opens is a fan box: several boxes of ammunition, about 2,000 rounds, and an unenchanted black leather shoulder holster of the kind detectives wear on television, with Carl pressed into the leather in English. They do not know you very well, Donut says. The holster holds no gun, but Carl knows what they want him to do. He still has his father's Glock in his inventory, and he has no intention of ever wearing it outside his inventory, or of ever using it.
beats.gist: Carl's first gold box holds a fan holster and ammunition, but he will never wear his father's Glock.

recap.text: Carl goes to his father's master bedroom for the last five minutes of the recording and takes three packs of Marlboro Reds, court documents, a 9mm Glock with two boxes of ammo, and the keys to the motorcycle and Ford truck. Waiting for the fight, he turns the Glock over and admits its overpowered rounds would likely make it explode. Donut asks for a pink holster.

Carl opens his first gold box, a fan box, and finds about 2,000 rounds of ammunition in several boxes, plus an unenchanted black leather shoulder holster of the kind detectives wear on television, with Carl pressed into the leather in English. The holster holds no gun, and Carl knows what the fans want. Donut says they do not know him very well: his father's Glock stays in his inventory, and he has no intention of wearing or using it.

tagline.text: A folder filled with court documents is one of the things Carl takes from his father's bedroom in the floor's recording of the trailer. He takes it without looking at it.

Carl has left his father's papers on the table in Donut's room, unread. Donut has read them: money Carl's grandparents set aside for him that his father tried to get at, a marriage certificate, and court documents from several arrests.

beats.headline: Taken without looking
beats.text: With five minutes left in the recording of the trailer, Carl moves to the master bedroom, not wanting to eavesdrop any more, and takes everything he can. From the living room he hears his father say something, desperate and slurred, with nobody there to hear his final words. In the bedroom Carl takes three packs of Marlboro Reds, and then picks up a folder filled with court documents. He takes it without looking at it.
beats.gist: Carl takes three Marlboro Reds packs and an unread court folder while his father's last words go unheard.

beats.headline: Donut has read them
beats.text: Across a table from Princess Chandra and her stack of papers, Donut says Carl has some legal papers just like these, from his father's trailer on the eighth floor. He left them on the table in her room and is too scared to look, she thinks, but she read them. Carl's grandparents set money aside for Carl, and his father was trying to get at it without Carl knowing. There is a marriage certificate for his father and his new wife, and court documents from several arrests. Put together, Donut says, they paint a very distinct picture of who Carl's father was as a person.
beats.gist: Donut tells Chandra she read Carl's father's papers: a hidden trust, a marriage certificate, arrest records.

relations.note: she reads them

recap.text: Carl stops listening to the recording of his father's trailer and goes to the master bedroom, taking everything he can with five minutes left. From the living room his father says something desperate and slurred, with nobody there to hear it. Carl takes three packs of Marlboro Reds and a folder of court documents, which he picks up without looking at it.

Across a table from Princess Chandra, Donut says Carl left legal papers from his father's trailer on the eighth floor lying in her room, too scared to look, she thinks, so she read them. Carl's grandparents set money aside for him, and his father was trying to get at it without Carl knowing. The pile also holds a marriage certificate for his father and his new wife, and court documents from his arrests.

tagline.text: The Champion Pack goes only to a squad that has defeated the keymaster. Its leather bag, in the squad's own boxer pattern, holds a backup slot for two more totems, a champion trophy, a cooler of yellow Gatorade and two Flee cards.
The Champion Pack's backup slot is where Donut keeps the card of Paz, which Katia let her take after the goddess died.

description.text: Champion Pack. Offered only to those who have defeated the keymaster, the champion pack contains the following items: Backup slot: Allows space for two extra totems to be kept on reserve. With this pack you may now carry a total of eight totems, but you still may only keep six in your active deck. A champion trophy to display in your personal space. A cooler filled with yellow Gatorade in case you want to do that dump-Gatorade-on-your-head-in-celebration thing. Two Flee cards. Warning: Flee card mechanics will change during the final phase. Listen for the upcoming announcement for details.

beats.headline: Gatorade for the keymaster
beats.text: The hydra is dead, its deck strong and theirs stronger. Beside the pile of its cards sits a bulky leather bag decorated with the same boxer pattern as their team flag. Carl is not the squad leader, so he cannot grab it, only read it: a backup slot for two extra totems, eight carried and six active; a champion trophy for the personal space; a cooler of yellow Gatorade for the dump-it-on-your-head thing; two Flee cards, with a warning that their mechanics will change in the final phase. Donut gasps. They got a trophy, and they are going to need a trophy case.
beats.gist: Carl can only read the bag: two extra totem slots, a trophy, Gatorade, two Flee cards.

beats.headline: Paz in the backup slot
beats.text: With the goddess dead, Donut pulls a card from her inventory and floats it down into Carl's hand. She has been keeping it in their backup slot; Katia let her grab it. It is Paz, and Carl feels dirty holding it. Donut had meant to keep Lazarus or the Golden Combo past the collapse, and now wonders whether to take this one instead, in case there is a way to set him free.
beats.gist: With the goddess dead, Donut floats a card named Paz down into Carl's hand, and he feels dirty.

relations.note: his card, in the backup slot

recap.text: Donut gasps at the leather bag beside the dead hydra's cards, which bears the boxer pattern of their team flag. Carl, not being squad leader, can only read it: a backup slot for two extra totems, a champion trophy, a cooler of yellow Gatorade, two Flee cards. With the goddess dead, Donut floats Paz down into Carl's hand, and Carl feels dirty holding it.

tagline.text: The Book Burner patch is an embroidered upgrade patch of a burning book, out of a Gold Talk of the Town box. Fixed to a garment, it adds fifteen percent to Intelligence and the Book Burner benefit: once a day, an opponent forgets a spell for thirty hours.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Medium. This patch depicts a burning book. I think this might be a metaphor for knowledge being dangerous. Or maybe it’s a metaphor saying you should burn books that suck. I don’t know. Just because I recently took everything over doesn’t mean I know what everything means. Most metaphors are bullshit. They’re not clever. They’re used by people so they can pretend they’re smarter than other people. There. I said it. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: +15% to Intelligence. The Book Burner benefit. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: A book on fire
beats.text: Carl sits down to his loot boxes: a dozen adventurer boxes with more trench scrolls, then a turkey deep fryer from the Gold Gobble box. The Gold Talk of the Town box is shaped like an opened newspaper on a pedestal, and it opens on a medium-sized rectangle of a patch with a book on it. The book is on fire. It is embroidered, not screen printed, which Donut will like. The benefit is really an anti-magic skill: once a day, an opponent his level or lower forgets a spell for thirty hours, with a five percent chance of failing for every level above his. Whoa. Too bad it is only once a day.
beats.gist: Carl opens a Gold box and finds a burning-book patch that makes an opponent forget a spell.

recap.text: Carl opens a dozen adventurer boxes of trench scrolls, then a turkey deep fryer from the Gold Gobble box. The Gold Talk of the Town box, shaped like an opened newspaper on a pedestal, holds a patch of a burning book, embroidered, not screen printed, which Donut will like. Once a day, an opponent his level or lower forgets a spell for thirty hours, with a five percent chance of failing for every level above his.

tagline.text: The Wand of Nighty-Night is a gnarled wooden wand with ten charges. Each casts a level-10 Sleep on a single non-boss target for five minutes, broken by physical damage, and more casts compound the effect.

description.text: Wand of Nighty-Night. 10 Charges. Knocks an opponent out onto their ass. Casts a level-10 Sleep on a non-boss, single target for a period of five minutes. Opponent will reawaken if they sustain physical damage. Multiple casts compounds the effect, which is why this wand is so fancy. If you don't know what that means, ask a math nerd.

beats.headline: The wand box
beats.text: Opening his loot boxes in his room, Carl gets a patch with a burning book from the Gold Talk of the Town box, and from the wand box a simple, gnarled wooden wand that clatters onto the table and disappears before he can examine it. When he picks it up, it is a Wand of Nighty-Night, ten charges: a level-10 Sleep on a single non-boss target for five minutes, broken by physical damage, compounding with every cast. He pulls it into his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl opens his loot boxes and gets a wooden wand that is a Wand of Nighty-Night.

beats.headline: Sinner
beats.text: Carl pulls his new Nighty-Night wand and opens the door, and a glowing Sister Ines is already running full tilt down the hallway at him, screaming Sinner at the top of her lungs. She is too close. He zaps the wand, and she drops unconscious and slides to a stop at his feet, a two-minute timer over her. Combat starts, but she is out. Louis kills her with a dagger, and a god's marked-for-death symbol appears over his head.
beats.gist: Carl zaps the charging Sister Ines asleep with his Nighty-Night wand, and Louis kills her with a dagger.

beats.headline: Sorry, Burcu
beats.text: Architect Houston begs Carl not to press the button, talking about the Beautiful Place and the changelings. Carl finds what he is looking for in his inventory. Sorry, he tells Burcu, bound on a table, and pulls out the wand of Nighty-Night. Her eyes go wide and she starts to thrash as he points it at her and casts. She conks out under a five-minute timer, he hits the switch, and her magical bindings disappear. Getting onto her table will be tricky: he has to land around her, not on her.
beats.gist: Carl apologizes to Burcu, zaps her with the Nighty-Night wand, and frees her from her bindings.

recap.text: Carl opens the wand box in his room, and a gnarled wooden wand clatters onto the table and vanishes before he can examine it. Picked up, it is a Wand of Nighty-Night, ten charges, a level-10 Sleep on one non-boss target for five minutes. When he opens the door, Sister Ines runs at him screaming Sinner, and he zaps her; she drops at his feet. Louis kills her with a dagger.

Carl finds the wand of Nighty-Night in his inventory while Architect Houston begs him not to press the button, talking about the Beautiful Place and the changelings. Telling Burcu sorry, he points the wand at her where she lies bound on a table. Her eyes go wide and she thrashes, and he casts. She conks out under a five-minute timer, and when he hits the switch her magical bindings disappear.

entities.name: The Bull Rush, Bespoke Personal Shield

tagline.text: The Bull Rush is a bespoke tech shield from Hereford War Machines, a Taurine-owned company that outfits elite mercenary squads, taken off a hunter. Unlocked with a Cracker Jack scroll and pinned to Donut's collar, it wraps her in a bubble that moves with her and can stretch, more weakly, over a mount or a whole vehicle.

beats.headline: A longhorn on her collar
beats.text: Imani's squad is dead. While the others sit with her, Carl trains, builds, and spends two of his three Cracker Jack scrolls unlocking alien shields from the pile of hunter tech. Donut's is a small, opalescent pin shaped like a longhorn cow, which he attaches to her neck collar; she likes the design. Mordecai says it is the more powerful of the two. They took it off a Soother mercenary in the last days before the Butcher's Masquerade, whose rich family spent a lot keeping him safe. It makes a bubble round her, and its mount option covers Mongo or a vehicle. The moron never turned it on, so nobody has seen it work.
beats.gist: Donut gets a longhorn-shaped pin shield on her collar, though she never turns it on.

relations.note: unlocked it and pinned it on her

recap.text: Imani's squad is dead, and while the others sit with her, Carl trains, builds, and spends two of his three Cracker Jack scrolls unlocking alien shields from the pile of hunter tech. He pins Donut's, a small opalescent longhorn cow, to her neck collar, and she likes it. Mordecai calls it the stronger of the two. It makes a bubble round her, but the moron never turned it on.

entities.name: Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus
aka: Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus

tagline.text: The Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus is Carl's old strength ring, his first in the dungeon, re-forged by the Temple of Emberus against a loan of 990,000 gold. It holds back most disease and health-seeping debuffs for a worshipper of Emberus, and to everyone else it still looks like a strength ring.
Too many debuffs at once overload the ring, and then the slugpox it holds back breaks through.
Carl has taken the ring off and left the faith of Emberus, standing in front of the god himself.

description.text: Enchanted Pauper’s Ring of the Steadfast Emberus. Ah, Emberus. Wholly sane, reasonable Emberus. I’m sure any jewelry that bears his name will be a perfectly fine, normal piece of magical gear. When working properly, this ring will remove most health-seeping and disease-based debuff effects. Has a variable numbing effect on various other debuff types. This will not remove the debuff itself. Too many active debuffs of any kind may temporarily mute or overheat this ring. Warning: This ring may only be worn by a worshipper of Emberus. This will turn into a cursed item if worn by a non-worshipper. …

beats.headline: A loan from the temple
beats.text: Mantaurs bang on the door, and Carl has his slug condition. Pater Coal, the cleric, does not charge interest to martyrs, but Carl must trade in a piece of jewellery he has worn a long time. He hands over his strength ring, the first ring he got in the dungeon, and takes an interest-free loan of 990,000 gold from the Temple of Emberus; while he owes it, he may not renounce his religion. The goat-legged satyr jeweller, twin tattoos on his hands like Carl's, dunks it in bubbling lava. It comes out cool, looking the same, still labelled a strength ring.
beats.gist: Carl swaps his first dungeon ring for a 990,000-gold Emberus temple loan; the lava dunk changes nothing visible.

beats.headline: Soul Poisoning
beats.text: A burning pang rips across Carl's midsection out of nowhere, and his Emberus ring flashes and grows warm. He keeps the pain out of his voice and moves to his health menu. His first thought is the tattoo on his chest, but the notification says otherwise: Soul Poisoning, its effects partially blocked by his Pauper's ring of the Steadfast Emberus, and worsening, a very minor case of stop-carrying-stored-souls-on-your-back.
beats.gist: Carl's Emberus ring flashes warm as a burning pang hits; his health menu names Soul Poisoning.

beats.headline: Overloaded
beats.text: Carl comes to on his back with a list of debuffs, Shit-Faced and Stiff Legs among them, and his finger burns. It is the Emberus ring, overloaded. He still has slugpox, because he never had Imani cure it, and with the ring not working a big boil rises on his back. He wonders what level the slugs are at now.
beats.gist: Carl wakes among his debuffs, his finger burning from the overloaded Emberus ring, a boil rising.

beats.headline: Catching up
beats.text: Carl's legs still will not bend, his fingers still end in suction cups, and screaming worms still flow out of his nose, but the Emberus ring seems to catch up at last: some of the other debuffs are contained, the slugpox among them. He sits up in the empty room beside the sluggalo.
beats.gist: Carl's debuffs mostly persist, but the Emberus ring catches up and contains some, including the slugpox.

beats.headline: Slugpox on purpose
beats.text: Donut calls for Imani: Carl's stupid slugpox is back. He kept it active on purpose, because the Emberus ring keeps it under control and he wanted it ready, arguing that the birth of Bigs on the previous floor saved him. Pretty much everyone thought it a terrible idea. Mordecai made a potion to cure it, and it is still sitting on the crafting table with the backpack. They forgot to bring it.
beats.gist: Donut calls Imani because Carl kept his slugpox active on purpose, and the cure was left behind.

beats.headline: Off the finger
beats.text: Emberus is roaring for the one who killed his son. Carl lies that he is coming, and that he was only one of two. Then he pulls the Emberus ring off his finger, puts it in his inventory, goes into his menus and makes a selection. The System asks whether he is sure. He clicks Yes: he no longer worships Emberus, and a smite is coming. The tattoos on the backs of his hands burst into flame, and he waves away a notification about the ring. The other one to kill the god's son, he says, was him.
beats.gist: Carl pulls off the Emberus ring, renounces the god, and lies to him while his tattoos burn.

relations.note: arranged the loan from the church
only a worshipper may wear it

recap.text: Mantaurs bang on the door while Carl has his slug condition, so he takes a 990,000-gold interest-free loan from the Temple of Emberus. Pater Coal, the cleric, asks him to trade in his strength ring, the first ring he got in the dungeon. While Carl owes the debt, he may not renounce his religion. The goat-legged satyr jeweller dunks the ring in bubbling lava, and it comes out cool, looking the same, still labelled a strength ring.

Carl's Emberus ring flashes and warms as a burning pang rips across his midsection, and the health menu names it Soul Poisoning, only partly blocked by the Pauper's ring. He wakes on his back with a burning finger, the ring overloaded, and a slugpox boil rising on his back. Then the ring catches up and contains the slugpox, though worms still flow from his nose.

Carl pulls the Emberus ring off his finger and puts it in his inventory, though the ring keeps his slugpox under control and he kept the slugpox active on purpose. Mordecai's cure potion sits forgotten on the crafting table. Carl tells the roaring Emberus he was one of two who killed the god's son, then clicks Yes when the System asks if he is sure. The tattoos on his hands burst into flame.

tagline.text: The Knife of Frozen Tears is a small knife of Sylvan crystal that looks like a butter knife and glints with red light. It is not very sharp and not worth much, but it can kill Garret, because Sylvan crystal is one of his weaknesses, and Ren uses it on him herself.

beats.headline: The last thing in her inventory
beats.text: With one key left and the building sagging round them, Ren will not fight Carl and Donut for it. She kicks her flamethrower to Carl and empties her inventory onto the floor: rings, clothing, potions, scrolls. The last item she pulls out is a small crystal knife that looks like a butter knife and glints with red light. It is called the Knife of Frozen Tears, she says, made of something called Sylvan crystal. It is not very sharp and not all that valuable, but it can kill Garret. Each time he regenerates he gets another weakness. He is up to four now, and Sylvan crystal is one of them. She breaks at that sentence.
beats.gist: Ren empties her inventory for Carl and Donut and offers a crystal knife that can kill Garret.

beats.headline: Into the side of her pet
beats.text: Garret pushes himself against Ren, whimpering. He is a tummy acher, she explains through tears: practically immortal, and every five deaths he resets to level one and has to bond again. This will be the first time. She tells him he is going to live with Carl and be a good boy, then stabs the knife into his side. He dies instantly, like a switch flipped, and his corpse starts to shrink. His weaknesses so far, she says, are sylvan crystal, consuming hobgoblin sweat, the bite of a rivenwing and consuming undead flesh.
beats.gist: Garret, a tummy acher, whimpers against Ren, who stabs him with the knife and he dies.

recap.text: Ren kicks her flamethrower to Carl and empties her inventory onto the floor, and the last item is the Knife of Frozen Tears, a small crystal knife that looks like a butter knife. It is made of Sylvan crystal, which is one of four weaknesses Garret has gained by regenerating. Ren tells Garret he will live with Carl, then stabs the knife into his side, and he dies instantly.

tagline.text: The Midnight Express is a consumable special card with two large men in tights on its face. Tserendolgor never got to use it, and she gives it to Carl with the rest of her cards.
Played, the Midnight Express makes a teammate the deckmaster for three minutes, which leaves the squad leader free to cast spells and use inventory. Princess Donut has spent it.

beats.headline: One of Ren's last two
beats.text: Ren will not fight for the last key. Her gear is already on the floor for Carl, and then she hands over her cards: she cannot give him her totems, but she has rearranged her deck and taken everything else out. There are a few rare specials and mystics in there, she says, including two she never got to use. One is a consumable Glow-Up. The other is a consumable special card featuring two large men in tights, called The Midnight Express. Carl cannot take the cards into his inventory, so the pile goes into the waistband of his boxers until he can give it to Donut.
beats.gist: Ren hands Carl her cards, and he stuffs them into his boxers.

beats.headline: Frozen mid-match
beats.text: On the roof of a skyscraper, the card match against Amayon freezes for a quest update: the demon lord is trapped in his true form, there are not enough souls left in this dying world to power his spell, and the crawlers have to refill it with the same kind of souls that set the event off. Carl asks Donut whether the totem he needs is in her hand. It is not. The Midnight Express is. Carl tells everyone to talk Amayon into waiting, and Donut to message him when she pulls it, then cast the card.
beats.gist: Carl has everyone stall Amayon while Donut pulls the Midnight Express and messages him.

beats.headline: Tag, you're it
beats.text: As Samantha flies Carl toward the beach, Donut messages that she has the totem now. The card lasts three minutes, she tells him; he says wait ten seconds, then play it. He drops onto a rocky beach covered with dead fish, birds, seals and crabs, and Donut plays the Midnight Express. For the next three minutes Carl is the deckmaster: the cards float huge in front of him, one of the four slots held by the card itself, a pair of tag-team wrestlers on its face. Up on the building, Donut is free to cast her spells and use her inventory. Carl flips Raul the crab into the water.
beats.gist: Donut's Midnight Express card makes Carl deckmaster for three minutes while he flips Raul the crab.

beats.headline: The timer runs out
beats.text: Raul arrives bewildered by the carnage on the beach and has to be told to do his thing, and Carl, still in charge of the deck, asks Alpha Carl to beat him to within an inch of his life. Alpha Carl would rather hug it out. Carl tosses the Time Extend in his hand onto Raul just as the Midnight Express timer ends. The cards in front of him disappear, and he is no longer the deckmaster. The consumable card is gone.
beats.gist: Carl hands Raul the Time Extend just as the timer ends, losing the deck and the card.

relations.note: made deckmaster for three minutes

recap.text: Ren gives Carl her gear and her deck, keeping only her totems, and the cards go into the waistband of his boxers. Among them is The Midnight Express, a consumable showing two large men in tights. Donut plays it, and Carl is deckmaster for three minutes on a beach of dead fish, birds, seals and crabs. He flips Raul the crab into the water, throws a Time Extend on him, and the timer runs out.

tagline.text: Velma is Tserendolgor's enchanted flamethrower, part breastplate and part weapon. She did not name it. Sitting on the floor of a building about to collapse, she unsnaps it and gives it to Carl with the rest of her gear.
Rosetta's team in the crafting room has refitted Velma to Jamal's harness. The flamethrower hangs under the hammerhead's belly now, and little tendrils of flame keep leaking from it.

beats.headline: Donating to the war effort
beats.text: Ren sits down heavily on the scorched, broken tiles beside Garret, unsnaps her flamethrower attachment and lets the whole apparatus topple; she was really looking forward to torching some of those assholes on the next floor. There is one key left, and she will not fight Carl and Donut for it. She kicks the flamethrower at Carl. Take it, she says, take it all, fast, and rings, clothes, potions and scrolls appear on the floor. She is donating to the war effort. Her flamethrower is named Velma, by the way. She did not name it.
beats.gist: Ren won't fight for the last key and kicks her flamethrower at Carl instead.

beats.headline: Among the best prizes
beats.text: Carl makes a quick inventory of everything looted from Quan and from Ren, though he cannot examine it properly until a saferoom. So far the best prizes look like the Eye in the Sky scrolls, the magical tomes, Velma the Flame Thrower and Quan's celestial cloak. It is, Carl realises, the loot Quan took off the crawlers he killed, and the least Carl can do is make certain it is put to good use.
beats.gist: Carl lists the loot from Quan and Ren, noting Velma the Flame Thrower among the best prizes.

beats.headline: This won't do
beats.text: Shi Maria has control of Carl's body, and she goes through his inventory for what she needs. An empty beaker from the first floor appears, with a sliver of toraline root placed inside. Then she examines Ren's flamethrower, and rejects it: no, no, this won't do. She pulls up his magic menu instead, warns everyone to step back, and casts Self-Immolation, which burns a hole through the floor and leaves the beaker bubbling with black ink.
beats.gist: Shi Maria, in Carl's body, rejects Ren's flamethrower and casts Self-Immolation, filling the beaker with black ink.

beats.headline: Under the hammerhead
beats.text: On the line at the edge of the woods, shields glowing up and down it, Jamal bounces on his new legs, excited to battle with his upgrades, and lets a little burst of flame out of the new attachment on his underbelly. It is Velma, Tserendolgor's flamethrower. Rosetta's team in the crafting room has modified it to fit his harness. Please excuse Jamal and Velma, he says. Carl tells him to be careful with that thing, and Jamal promises to flame only on purpose from now on.
beats.gist: Jamal lets a burst of flame from Velma, Tserendolgor's flamethrower, now on his harness.

beats.headline: Into the honeycombs
beats.text: Hunter seekers come in silently, automatons with no dots on the map, and they are going to explode. Shields up, Carl calls, falling back. Jamal is firing his flamethrower, Jamal announces from his position up in the honeycombs, and he roars and fires, a gout of flame filling the enclosed space. An alarm klaxon starts in broken bursts as the shark moves across the honeycomb and fires into a different hole, then another.
beats.gist: Jamal fires his flamethrower from the honeycombs while silent hunter seekers close in.

beats.headline: Through the arena
beats.text: In the arena the tenth-floor vehicles are in play, upgraded to the max, and it is a demolition derby. Jamal's Tundra lies in a smoking heap where it crashed into the wall. Jamal jumps through the arena with his flamethrower roaring, landing on monsters and snapping them in half, while Samantha sits right on his head, also screaming a war cry.
beats.gist: Jamal and Samantha cross the arena, flamethrower roaring, snapping monsters in half amid upgraded vehicles.

recap.text: Ren sits down on the scorched tiles beside Garret, unsnaps her flamethrower and kicks it at Carl, since she will not fight him and Donut for the last key. She dumps her rings, clothes, potions and scrolls on the floor as well, and the flamethrower is named Velma. Carl sorts the loot, counting Velma among the best prizes. Shi Maria, in control of his body, rejects Velma with a "no, no, this won't do" and casts Self-Immolation instead.

Jamal bounces on his new legs at the edge of the woods and lets a little burst of flame out of Velma, Tserendolgor's flamethrower, which Rosetta's team in the crafting room has fitted to his harness under his belly. Carl tells him to be careful, and Jamal promises to flame only on purpose. Hunter seekers then come in silently, and Jamal roars and fires Velma into the honeycombs, hole after hole.

Jamal's Tundra lies in a smoking heap against the arena wall, where it crashed among the tenth-floor vehicles, all upgraded to the max in a demolition derby. Jamal jumps through the arena on foot with Tserendolgor's flamethrower roaring, landing on monsters and snapping them in half. Samantha sits right on his head, screaming a war cry of her own.

tagline.text: The Tier 3 Doggie Door is a personal space upgrade that lets a crawler leave their space by any door they have already used on the floor, a fast-travel network shared with guests and party members. Lucia Mar dropped five of them, and Mordecai thinks she stole them when she went on a show.
A Doggie Door is installed in Carl and Donut's room and in Katia's, and the plan is to fast travel by it between the city and the guild's headquarters.
A doggie door works for anyone who has one, and off-world sponsors can buy the upgrade too: an enemy who ever came in through the bait shop can come back the same way.

description.text: Personal Space Upgrade. Tier 3 Doggie Door. So, you're out adventuring, and you suddenly have a hankerin' for those sweet pancakes you had two weeks back at some dive that's now over two hundred kilometers away. What are you gonna do? Travel for several hours in the wrong direction just to get another taste? Psshh. Okay, loser. The cool kids use the doggie door. Upgrades the door in your personal space to allow a selectable exit via any door you have previously utilized on this same floor, effectively creating a fast travel waypoint system. Allows shared gated access amongst guests and party members.

beats.headline: Five, from Lucia Mar
beats.text: Li Jun tells Carl how they got here: Lucia Mar. After what they are calling the Battle of Beijing, they thought she had gone down the stairs, but she was waiting for them, really friendly, which was unsettling; Florin had messaged her to help. She dropped five personal space upgrade modules on the ground and went down. One is already installed in Imani's room. It is a tier 3, Katia adds, which Mordecai says should not be available until the ninth floor. He thinks Lucia stole them when she went on a show.
beats.gist: Li Jun says Lucia Mar dropped five personal space upgrade modules, and Mordecai thinks she stole them.

beats.headline: Through Imani's door
beats.text: Carl reads the module: the cool kids use the doggie door. It lets a personal space door open onto any door its owner has already used on the floor, a fast-travel waypoint system, shared with guests and party members. With one in Imani's room, Katia says, the whole Meadowlark party can go out into the church, or into Washington or Detroit, or Belgium. Giving it to the entire guild would cost twenty-five million for a tier three, Imani says; in the meantime they have four more for single doors.
beats.gist: Katia says a doggie door lets Imani's door open onto any door used before; guild-wide costs twenty-five million.

beats.headline: Our room and Katia's
beats.text: Florin, Imani and Elle are leaving the city for the headquarters, to meet the adjutant and get it ready. Once they are set up, the plan is to use the doggie door upgrade to fast travel from the city to the headquarters. In the meantime, Carl and Donut have already installed the doggie door upgrade in their room, along with Katia's.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut have already installed the doggie door upgrade in their room and Katia's.

beats.headline: Out the college door
beats.text: Carl and Donut go to Katia's personal space and, thanks to the new Doggie Door upgrade, leave by the college entrance, several rings higher, which gives them the chance to recruit along the way. Katia and Elle have been working the chats, but a recruit has to be physically touched to be officially enlisted, so people will meet them on the road.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut use the Doggie Door to leave by the college entrance, meeting recruits on the road.

beats.headline: A door into the castle
beats.text: Donut shouts in the chat that Bomo has noticed an extra door in the situational space, a saferoom door for the Reaver team: they are sneak attacking through it, into the castle. It hits Carl too late. Every time they left the guild saferoom for the FUPA through the bait shop, that space was a long corridor of doors from all the crawlers coming and going. Off-world sponsors can use personal spaces as well, and can buy a doggie door upgrade, so any of them who ever came in through the bait shop can come back that way. The bait shop is inside the castle now.
beats.gist: The Reaver team sneak attacks through an extra saferoom door into the castle.

beats.headline: Dialled to Larracos
beats.text: With minutes to spare, the last of the group files into the saferoom behind Carl, and he quickly dials the Larracos gate on the doggie door. Dong Quixote is riding Gonk, and rather than the pet stables Carl orders him to Shanty Town, which has an exit fit for a swamp yak. The door beeps, ready. Rend goes first; the stairs are steep.
beats.gist: Carl dials the Larracos gate; Dong Quixote and Gonk go to Shanty Town, and Rend steps through first.

recap.text: Lucia Mar, unsettlingly friendly after the Battle of Beijing, drops five personal space upgrade modules and goes down. One is already installed in Imani's room, a tier 3 that Mordecai says should not be available before the ninth floor. Carl reads that the doggie door opens onto any door its owner has used, so the Meadowlark party can step out to the church, Washington, Detroit or Belgium. The whole guild would cost twenty-five million; four single-door modules remain.

Carl and Donut install the doggie door upgrade in their room and Katia's, while Florin, Imani and Elle leave to ready the headquarters. Donut shouts that Bomo has spotted an extra door in the situational space, and the Reaver team sneak attacks through it into the castle. With minutes to spare, Carl dials the Larracos gate and sends Dong Quixote, riding Gonk, to Shanty Town, whose exit fits a swamp yak. Rend goes first down the steep stairs.

tagline.text: Annie – Útburður is one of Katia's T'Ghee totem cards: a level 80 raven the size of a cat whose head is the skull of a human infant, the little holes in it filled with teeth. Katia plays a Timeless card on it so it stays summoned.
Annie is the card Katia brought down from the floor before, and the skull-headed crow rides on her shoulder even inside her dream. It shares its name with Annie, the baby girl in that memory.
Katia left the card on a table when she went, and Donut took it.

beats.headline: A raven with an infant's skull
beats.text: The card fight against Ysalte and Amayon erupts all at once. Katia summons her scary-ass bird creature, then a consumable utility card called Timeless, which will keep it summoned forever. It lands on her shoulder in a fanfare of colourful, burning embers and dancing baby pacifiers: a large raven, cat-sized, whose head is the skull of a human infant, the little holes in it filled with teeth. Annie – Útburður. Level 80. Katia leans in and whispers instructions to it.
beats.gist: Katia summons Útburður, a cat-sized raven with an infant's skull for a head, and Timeless.

beats.headline: On Katia's shoulder, in the dream
beats.text: At a field ruling adjudication, the dream Carl and Katia shared plays on a floating screen. There is the memory of Katia pleading with a faceless woman, who answers with Annie's medical needs, and sweeping everything off the woman's desk. And there is the Katia who watched it with Carl and cried on his shoulder. That Katia had a crow on her own shoulder, the card she brought from the floor before: a crow with the skull of an infant. The crow's name is also Annie. Carl does not know what that means, but it seems important.
beats.gist: Katia's dream plays on a screen, and her crow, a card bearing an infant's skull, shares Annie's name.

beats.headline: Out, and covered in blood
beats.text: Inside Club Vanquisher, Carl stiff-legs around a corner as Katia, Prepotente, Li Jun and Zhang round the far end of the hall. Bianca is out and roaring. So is Annie, Katia's totem. The skull-headed bird is covered in blood, and it disappears in a puff of smoke. A sap-like substance drips from the ceiling, the walls shake, and Prepotente presses a wall panel to open the hidden door they all rush through.
beats.gist: Katia's totem Annie, covered in blood, vanishes in smoke as Carl's group rushes through a hidden door.

beats.headline: A comfort in the dream
beats.text: Several days earlier: Carl lands in Katia's dream, not the one from Shi Maria's point of view he was meant to have. No, she says, not this. A bird appears on her shoulder, a bird with the skull of a child, and it rubs its small, ghoulish head against hers in comfort. This is her card from the floor before, and its name is Annie. When Katia tells him how the little girl died with nobody to call her own, she reaches up and strokes the other Annie, the bird. She was like me in that way, she says. All alone.
beats.gist: Carl lands in Katia's dream, where Annie, her child-skulled bird card, comforts her.

beats.headline: Left on the table
beats.text: Emberus is three minutes from destroying the floor, and Katia is gone. On the table she left a pair of items. One is her card from the floor before, the one depicting Annie the skull-headed bird. Donut takes it. The other is a bra with Carl's face on one cup and Time to pay the daddy tax on the other, and Elle grabs that. Carl assumes it came from the Dungeon Sidekicks show and was left as a joke.
beats.gist: Donut takes Katia's Annie card, and Elle grabs a bra bearing Carl's face.

relations.note: a totem card
taken from the table Katia left it on

recap.text: Katia's card fight against Ysalte and Amayon erupts all at once, and she summons her scary-ass bird creature, then plays a consumable utility card called Timeless to keep it summoned forever. Annie – Útburður lands on her shoulder in a fanfare of burning embers and dancing baby pacifiers: a cat-sized raven with a human infant's skull for a head, its little holes filled with teeth. It is Level 80, and Katia leans in and whispers instructions to it.

Katia's totem card, Annie, is a crow with the skull of an infant, and Carl first sees it on her shoulder in a dream, where it rubs its small head against hers while she tells him a little girl died with nobody to call her own. Days after that dream, Annie comes out covered in blood in Club Vanquisher and vanishes in a puff of smoke. Katia leaves the card on a table, and Donut takes it.

entities.name: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride

tagline.text: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride is an eye tattooed into Carl's chest by Shi Maria herself, while she had control of his body, so that he could not leave her behind as a card. It blinks once and closes, and its description gives nothing but its name.

Shi Maria is trapped inside Carl now, and the eye on his chest is his to control. He can see through it and keeps it shut on purpose. He can summon her once, and then she may choose to take his body or go back to her own form.
When Vinata, fighting Carl with his shirt open, stares into the eye on his chest, it drives her mad. Shi Maria is still trapped behind it.
The eye has followed Carl into a dog's body, to the middle of his forehead, where he opens it on reflex and freezes a mimic in place. Shi Maria asks to take over, and he says no.
Carl is back in his own body, and he has made sure the Eye of the Bedlam Bride is back in its proper place.

description.text: Tattoo. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

beats.headline: Something he cannot discard
beats.text: Combined with Carl by the Golden Combo, Shi Maria has his body. She brews ink in a beaker with a sliver of toraline root and Self-Immolation, strips off his trollskin shirt and takes out the stick and poke tattoo kit. When Li Jun slides down to help, she jabs the stick into his eye and eats it. If Carl will not bring her card to the next floor, she says in his mind, she will attach herself to something he cannot discard so easily, and she pokes the inked stick into the centre of his chest, faster than possible. When he times out and is himself again, the eye blinks, and closes.
beats.gist: Shi Maria jabs an inked stick into Carl's eye, eats it, then tattoos his chest.

beats.headline: A bruise under the skin
beats.text: Carl has just said they will not keep the Golden Combo card when Donut asks what that crazy spider lady did to him. The tattoo on his chest is invisible, because the eye is closed, and it feels like a bruise. Only Li Na, Li Jun and Imani have seen it. It is not important right now, he tells her.
beats.gist: Carl's chest tattoo is invisible and feels like a bruise; he tells Donut it is not important.

beats.headline: Rosetta's cold hand
beats.text: Rosetta, newly arrived with Tipid, pushes her hand down the front of Carl's shirt and lays it on the Bedlam Bride tattoo, her fingers like ice. Then she wants the toraline, and the ink the spider used to make the tattoo. He hands over a finger-sized slice of the root and the glass container, still hot to the touch, with only a few thimblefuls of ink left, and feels the eye blink on his chest, as if her touch has woken it.
beats.gist: Rosetta puts her icy hand on Carl's tattoo, takes toraline and spider ink, and his tattoo's eye blinks.

beats.headline: Glory Bound and Removal Order
beats.text: Shi Maria grows stronger with every attempt on Carl's mind. The eye on his chest is open, blinking, looking angrily back and forth and trying to cast, and despite his Wisp Armor she has just spoken in his head. So Carl takes the Glory Bound treatment, which will carry him into the spider's worst memory, with Mordecai's Removal Order added, so that he can choose to lock her in the dream for good. The tattoo would stay on his chest, under his control. If he fails, he wakes up with a very pissed-off entity inside him.
beats.gist: Carl takes Glory Bound and Removal Order to lock Shi Maria in the dream.

beats.headline: It worked, sort of
beats.text: Carl comes round from the treatment on the other side of the map, with no idea how he got there. His treatment worked, sort of, according to Shi Maria's husband Hapanzi, who reappeared at the end of the dream to say he has her now, good and trapped. Carl can see from the eye on his chest now. It is still a tattoo, but he can feel it when it is open, and he has to make a conscious effort to keep it closed.
beats.gist: Carl wakes across the map with a tattoo eye on his chest that he can see through.

beats.headline: Trapped, says Hapanzi
beats.text: Watching the replay of the ballroom, Carl knows that at that moment, in the dream, Shi Maria vanished and her husband Hapanzi came back as a spider to tell him she is trapped in his own body. Carl now controls the eye and the containment she is in. He can summon her again, once, and then she may choose to take over his body or expel herself into her own form: one more bomb in his inventory, an especially dangerous one. She does not look nearly as trapped as Hapanzi said. The eye on his chest is clenched closed.
beats.gist: Hapanzi, as a spider, tells Carl that Shi Maria is trapped in his body.

beats.headline: Vinata stares into it
beats.text: Wrapped round Carl, Vinata crushes him, chokes him with one pair of hands, stabs at him with another, and with the upper pair slams his head against the ground by his hair until his skull cracks. You killed my people, she says. Choking and inebriated, Carl realises his shirt is open, and the eye on his chest is open with it. Vinata is staring straight into it. She has been driven mad by the Eye of the Bedlam Bride.
beats.gist: Vinata, maddened by the Eye of the Bedlam Bride, chokes and crushes Carl while staring at his chest.

beats.headline: Open for Eris
beats.text: Eris shows Carl a five-sided coin: one of its results has to happen, she says, and she hands it to Uzi Jesus to flip. Carl panics. The rushing feeling is back, all around him at once, and on his chest the long-dormant Eye of the Bedlam Bride is open, burning a hole in his shirt. He offers to worship her right now if she stops. She wants a true worshipper, she says, and tells Jesus to flip it.
beats.gist: Eris has Uzi Jesus flip a five-sided coin while Carl's Eye of the Bedlam Bride burns open.

beats.headline: On a dog's forehead
beats.text: In a dog's body, Carl remembers the tattoo only when it tries to wrench itself open: it has moved to the centre of his forehead, hidden. Let me take over, Shi Maria says. He tells her she is trapped and will stay trapped. If you say so, she answers; she is here when he needs her. Then the mimic Mitch lurches forward to consume him, Carl opens the eye on reflex, and Mitch freezes, sparkling, crying that it is too cold, until Donut's magic missile kills him.
beats.gist: In a dog's body, Carl remembers the forehead tattoo and opens its eye, freezing the mimic Mitch.

recap.text: Shi Maria, joined to Carl's body by the Golden Combo, brews ink in a beaker from a sliver of toraline root and Self-Immolation, then eats the stick she jabs into Li Jun's eye. She tells Carl in his mind that if he won't bring her card to the next floor, she will attach herself to something he can't discard, and pokes the inked stick into his chest. When he times out, the eye blinks and closes.

Rosetta pushes an ice-cold hand down Carl's shirt onto the tattoo, and he hands over a finger-sized slice of toraline and the glass container with a few thimblefuls of ink left. The eye blinks. Carl takes the Glory Bound treatment with Mordecai's Removal Order to lock Shi Maria in the dream, and Hapanzi says she is trapped. Vinata cracks his skull against the ground, then stares into the open eye and goes mad.

Eris shows Carl a five-sided coin and hands it to Uzi Jesus to flip. Carl offers to worship her if she stops, but she wants a true worshipper, and the Eye of the Bedlam Bride burns a hole in his shirt. In a dog's body, Carl opens the eye on reflex when the mimic Mitch lunges. Mitch freezes, sparkling and crying that it is too cold, until Donut's magic missile kills him.

tagline.text: Shi Maria, in control of Carl, burns a sliver of toraline in a beaker and gets a little bubbling black ink, which she pokes into his chest with the stick from a tattoo kit.
Carl has a few thimblefuls of the spider's ink left and a finger-sized slice of toraline, and Rosetta wants both.
Ink mixed with a willing donor's blood lets another crawler borrow their spell or skill as a tattoo; the donor loses levels for a while, not the skill.
Imani borrows Carl's Tripper through a small toraline tattoo, but there is barely any of the vegetable left to make more.
Edgar, with tips from Milk, has learned to make a similar ink that does not need the toraline.

beats.headline: Ink from a beaker
beats.text: With Shi Maria in control of Carl's body, an empty beaker he looted on the first floor appears in his hand, and into it goes a small sliver of the toraline root his sponsor sent. She casts Self-Immolation; the fire burns a hole in the floor, and Carl falls into the apartment below. When he picks up the burning hot beaker, it holds a small amount of bubbling black liquid. Ink. Then the stick and poke tattoo kit is in his hands. After the stick goes into Li Jun's eye, it is dipped in the beaker and poked rapidly into Carl's own chest. You will likely be doing more of this soon with the remaining ink, she tells him.
beats.gist: Shi Maria burns through the floor; toraline root becomes ink in a beaker.

beats.headline: Rosetta wants it
beats.text: In the Meadowlark saferoom, Rosetta puts an icy hand on the Bedlam Bride tattoo and asks how much he has left. Of the toraline, and of the ink the spider used to make that tattoo. Carl pulls out a finger-sized slice of the vegetable and the glass container of Shi Maria's ink, still hot to the touch, a few thimblefuls left; Mordecai has more toraline, but not much. Give me access to your saferoom and your bomber's studio, Rosetta says, and three million gold. Better make it four.
beats.gist: Rosetta demands access to Carl's saferoom, the bomber's studio and four million gold for his toraline and ink.

beats.headline: Freely given
beats.text: Katia sets a vial on the table with the ink already mixed. If the blood is freely given, she explains, the potion lets you choose the spell or skill, and it is not permanent for the donor: Li Na lost five levels temporarily. Her brother, whose eye was taken with violence, is another matter. The tattoo itself is permanent, and its size follows the level of what it carries. Making the ink took up a third of the potion, and a level-13 skill takes almost all of the vial, leaving just enough for a small tattoo for Imani.
beats.gist: Katia's ink, made with freely given blood, lets the drinker choose a skill.

beats.headline: Tripper, borrowed
beats.text: Carl feels a searing pain in his chest and gets a notification: Imani has used his Tripper, and lots of traps have just gone off. After his chain dragon they reversed the process: Carl drank the associated potion, picked the spell, and lost six levels when Katia drew his blood, which his bandana covers anyway. Imani's tattoo, toraline yam ink mixed with Carl's blood, is a small barbed-wire symbol round her ankle, and it is permanent. The spell will fade from her, and Carl can re-energize it with the yam potion, except that they have barely any of the vegetable left.
beats.gist: Imani borrows Carl's Tripper through a permanent yam-ink tattoo, setting off traps.

beats.headline: No longer needed
beats.text: Rosetta's new plan for Donut needs a tattoo. Edgar extracted the spell properly, she says, and with some ink tips from Milk they no longer need the toraline. Edgar explains as he prepares the ink: the ink Carl had from the toraline lets one borrow spells and skills temporarily from willing subjects, and take them permanently from unwilling ones. His new ink is similar but not identical. It captures the essence of the fallen crawler in a unique way, and he does not know how it will form.
beats.gist: Edgar drops the toraline and mixes new ink that captures a fallen crawler's essence.

recap.text: Shi Maria, in control of Carl's body, summons an empty beaker and drops in a sliver of the toraline root his sponsor sent. She casts Self-Immolation, the fire burns a hole in the floor, and Carl falls into the apartment below. The burning-hot beaker holds bubbling black liquid: ink. She drives the stick from the tattoo kit into Li Jun's eye, dips it in the beaker, and pokes it rapidly into Carl's chest.

Imani uses Carl's Tripper, and Carl feels a searing pain in his chest as lots of traps go off. Katia had mixed toraline yam ink with his blood, and Carl lost six levels when she drew it. The ink is a small barbed-wire symbol round Imani's ankle, and it is permanent. Rosetta's new plan for Donut needs a tattoo, and Edgar's new ink no longer needs the toraline.

tagline.text: A ghillie suit comes with Donut's new class, a long-range sniper and assassin called Deathbed Hellcat, along with a hat. Donut has no idea what a ghillie suit is. Carl does, and keeps it a surprise.
It is a cat-sized camouflage suit of shredded, colour-changing fabric that covers her whole body, adding Blend into the Background and a Cone of Silence, and Donut is absolutely not wearing it.
Donut wears it after all, invisible at the top of the Nest tower while she shoots magic missiles from it.

beats.headline: What's a ghillie suit?
beats.text: Mordecai warns Donut off any deity-themed class this floor. She turns down the Consecrated Enchantress and the Halloween Aficionado, then gasps at one that comes with a hat, and something else: what's a ghillie suit? Muddy, she tells Carl what she picked: a long-range sniper and assassin class, every spell's range quadrupled, invisibility at will, and it comes with a hat and a ghoulie suit. Deathbed Hellcat, Carl says. And it's ghillie suit. Mordecai had no idea; Carl knows, and keeps it a surprise.
beats.gist: Mordecai warns Donut off deity-themed classes, and she picks a sniper class with a ghoulie suit.

beats.headline: Like a tassel
beats.text: Laid out on the floor, it looks to Donut like one of Signet's tattoo people fell through a paper shredder, and she will not look like a tassel. It's camouflage, Carl says; it's supposed to look like that. Long, shredded strips of colour-changing fabric blend into the background. It takes a jacket slot, yet magically covers her whole body, adding Blend into the Background and a Cone of Silence, and with the hat on too, everything is buffed further. Crupper, cloak and suit can all be worn at once.
beats.gist: Donut finds her ghillie suit looks like a tassel; Carl says camouflage is supposed to look like that.

beats.headline: The stupid ghoulie suit
beats.text: A god is here, and Carl tells Donut to get out of the Nest tower. She can see that, she answers: he has stopped at the edge of the city, and he cannot see her anyway, because she is wearing the stupid ghoulie suit and is invisible. Carl points out that she is on top of the biggest tower on the floor, shooting magic missiles. Rosetta agrees with him. A magic missile arcs down from the tower into a crowd of ghouls.
beats.gist: Donut, invisible in her ghoulie suit atop the tower, shoots magic missiles while Carl tells her to leave.

beats.headline: She looks like a sniper
beats.text: Carl rushes into the top level of the Nest to find Donut atop her seat, dressed in her ghillie suit, leaning against the parapet with her face pressed to the invisible shield. The camouflage is a strange contrast to her tiara, which glows like a lighthouse beacon. She has no weapon, and his first thought is sniper. Aiming, aiming, she mutters, and a fiery magic missile drops a distant tower in Larracos. Not so tough with your head blown off, she growls.
beats.gist: Donut, in her ghillie suit and glowing tiara, drops a distant Larracos tower with a magic missile.

beats.headline: Lifted for the needle
beats.text: Donut never agreed to a tattoo, she protests, but Edgar asks for someone to lift her camouflage suit and crupper: he needs a spot on her right flank about as big as his foot. Donut fears a scar on the outside, then agrees on condition that Carl gets a matching one. Once she agrees, the ghillie suit disappears, then the crupper, and she turns her tail toward Rosetta.
beats.gist: Donut agrees to a tattoo on her right flank if Carl gets a matching one.

relations.note: both come with the class, and buff each other

recap.text: Donut picks a long-range sniper and assassin class that comes with a hat and what she calls a ghoulie suit. Carl corrects it to ghillie suit, and she says its shredded strips of colour-changing fabric make her look like a tassel. Wearing it atop the tallest tower, she turns invisible, though her tiara glows like a lighthouse beacon, and she drops a distant tower in Larracos with a magic missile.

tagline.text: The beige, extra-floppy boonie hat that came with Donut's sniper class adds a Targeting skill for examining mobs from afar and stretches the range of all her spells. Worn with the ghillie suit, every benefit is buffed further.
It is the first hat on the tiara's red charge pillow, where it will give up all its magic over ten hours.
Its Targeting skill is in Donut's tiara now.

beats.headline: What snipers wear
beats.text: Donut likes the hat, at least, even if she already has a few from the babababoons on the fourth floor. It is beige, which she does not care for, but extra floppy, which she does, though it clashes with her fit. They are boonie hats, Carl says, not bucket hats: what snipers wear. It adds a Targeting skill to zoom in and examine mobs from afar, like the gnomish farseerer but less awkward, and increases the range of all her spells. With the suit as well, she could snipe enemies from well over a mile.
beats.gist: The beige boonie hat gives Donut a Targeting skill and longer spell range.

beats.headline: First on the pillow
beats.text: The first thing to put on the new tiara's charge pillow, Mordecai says, is the hat she just got with the targeting ability. And set a timer for ten and a half hours to be safe, because the pillows give no notice when a transfer is done, a bug for a very long time. Donut sets her new boonie hat on the red pillow, and it clicks into place.
beats.gist: Mordecai says Donut's new boonie hat goes on the tiara's charge pillow first, with a ten-and-a-half-hour timer.

beats.headline: In the crown
beats.text: The virtual sun rises over an army of tens of thousands, glinting like a blade. Donut studies the orc prince across the field with her new Targeting skill, which has just been added to her crown. She yelps: Carl, that's not Prince Stalwart. Carl looks again from afar. The orc is bigger than he first thought.
beats.gist: Donut's Targeting skill shows the orc prince is not Prince Stalwart, and Carl sees it is bigger.

relations.note: drained on the charge pillow for its Targeting skill

recap.text: Donut likes the beige boonie hat for being extra floppy, though it clashes with her fit, and Carl insists it is a boonie hat, not a bucket hat. It adds a Targeting skill and extends the range of all her spells. Mordecai tells her to set a ten-and-a-half-hour timer and put it first on the new tiara's red charge pillow, where it clicks into place.

tagline.text: Revitalize Pet was a Heal Pet potion, Donut says, until Carl set it on the ground before Paz blew Ysalte's head off; now it is purple, full of glitter, and super rare. Mordecai says it will grow Mongo's missing wing back in about an hour.
Mordecai knows the recipe now, though the ingredients are really rare. Carl has smashed the vial on Mongo's backside, and the Healing buff has appeared over his head.
Mongo's wing is starting to grow back.

beats.headline: Super sparkly
beats.text: Before the achievements, Donut wants Mongo healed. A Heal Severe Injury potion Carl made while he was part spider has already mended his burns, but the wing is still missing. Donut pushes forward a Heal Pet potion that Carl put on the ground before the vinegar goddess lost her head to Paz; now it is super sparkly and calls itself Revitalize Pet. It is purple and looks as if someone dumped half a jar of glitter into it. Super rare, Mordecai says, and expensive, but with his newest table upgrade he can learn the recipe without ruining it. It will grow the wing back in about an hour, though there may be scars.
beats.gist: Donut has Mordecai turn her glittery Revitalize Pet potion into a new wing for Mongo.

beats.headline: Glass on his bum
beats.text: Mongo looks at his missing right wing as if noticing it for the very first time, and Donut wants the potion now. Mordecai warns that it is expensive: he knows how to make them, but the ingredients are really rare. Donut tells Mongo to drink every drop and Carl to be gentle. Carl walks over and smashes the vial on Mongo's butt at the base of his tail. That was mean, Donut cries, but the Healing buff appears over Mongo's head. A potion thrown at someone else works, and for Mongo it is a lot safer than pouring it down his throat.
beats.gist: Donut has Carl smash a Revitalize Pet vial on Mongo's butt, and the Healing buff appears over Mongo.

recap.text: Donut wants Mongo healed before the achievements. The Heal Severe Injury potion Carl made while he was part spider has mended Mongo's burns, but his right wing is still missing. Donut pushes forward the Heal Pet potion Carl left on the ground before the vinegar goddess lost her head to Paz, now purple, glittering and calling itself Revitalize Pet. Carl smashes the vial on Mongo's butt, and the Healing buff appears over his head.

tagline.text: The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion was Quan Ch's, and it is the first celestial item of this crawl. On Donut it is a shawl. Over the coming days and weeks it raises her lowest stat to match her highest and lifts four spells and a skill to fifteen, as long as she keeps it on.
It is one piece of a matched set of four now. The Crupper of the Benevolent Champion repeats its powers and adds to them.

description.text: The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion. This is a unique item. This item was originally awarded in a Celestial Quest Box during the third floor. […] This magical cloak offers the following benefits: A level-five Find Weakened skill, so you'll always know who to protect first. Your lowest base stat will, over the course of the next 66 hours, become equal with the highest base stat at the time of first equip. Four random spells from your current arsenal will increase to level 15. …

beats.headline: Quan's cloak
beats.text: Before Carl opens his boxes, Mordecai has him pull out Quan's cloak. Watching Quan on the recap, they had assumed his flying, power bolt and shields came from the cloak; in fact its abilities are tailored to the wearer, with a focus on magic and the lowest stat, which is why Carl wants it for Donut. It is long and glows with a soft white light, silky, black on one side and blue on the other, with short arms. The system calls it a cloak, so it will fit a quadruped. Quan used its Find Weakened skill to pick off the weakest.
beats.gist: Carl wants Quan's cloak for Donut because its abilities adapt to the wearer, favoring magic.

beats.headline: Thirty points, for two minutes
beats.text: Mordecai's new potion was once called Charisma Cheat, and the system now calls it MySpace Photo. For two minutes it makes the system read Donut's base charisma as 193 instead of 163, so the cloak will raise her constitution, base two, to 193. She learns Shield first, drinks the potion, collects a very rude Catfish achievement, and the cloak appears over her shoulders, ridiculously short on her. It's like a shawl, she says. Bad Attitude is level fifteen at once. Wall of Fire, Heal Critter and Puddle Jumper are to follow.
beats.gist: Donut drinks Mordecai's potion to lift her charisma to 193, and the cloak appears, absurdly short on her.

beats.headline: Her lovely shawl
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx has slid to a stop in a circle of words of power that stops her teleporting, shaking with rage, and Donut stalks a circle around her. She has shown off her new knee pads. She has also upgraded a skill because of her lovely shawl, she says; it is not quite at fifteen yet, but it is getting there. Does Huanxin want to know what it is? Stay the hells away from me, the heiress answers. I am a god.
beats.gist: Donut shows off her knee pads while trapped Huanxin Jinx insists she is a god.

beats.headline: A matched set
beats.text: One of Donut's celestial boxes held the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion, part of a matched set of four with the cloak; find the third, and the fourth will come in a box. Its abilities copy the cloak's, and the set adds more: the constitution the cloak raised is buffed another twenty per cent, Find Weakened rises to ten, and one spell the cloak brought to fifteen may go to sixteen. The cloak raised Wall of Fire, Heal Critter, Bad Attitude and Puddle Jumper, and she has to choose now. She picks Puddle Jumper, now level 16.
beats.gist: Donut must choose among four cloak-raised spells, and she picks Puddle Jumper, now level 16.

relations.note: Carl took it from Quan on the floor before
drunk just before the cloak went on, to raise the stat it matches
a matched set

recap.text: Mordecai has Carl pull out Quan's cloak, whose abilities are tailored to the wearer, with a focus on magic and the lowest stat. Donut drinks a potion that makes the system read her charisma as 193 for two minutes, so the cloak raises her constitution to 193; it settles over her shoulders, ridiculously short. Circling the trapped Huanxin Jinx, Donut boasts of her lovely shawl, and Huanxin tells her to stay the hells away.

Donut holds a second piece of her celestial set, the Crupper of the Benevolent Champion, one of four that match the cloak. Finding the third brings the fourth in a box. The set raises her constitution another twenty per cent, lifts Find Weakened to ten, and lets one spell go from fifteen to sixteen. The cloak had raised Wall of Fire, Heal Critter, Bad Attitude and Puddle Jumper, and she picks Puddle Jumper, now level 16.

tagline.text: A platinum box from the Apothecary gives Donut a second charging pillow for her tiara, purple where the first is red. It drains any magical item, not only hats, but a buff passes only to a like item, so a ring's goes into a crystal set in a ring.

description.text: Warning: This will drain any magical item, but it will only transfer to a like item. If you drain a ring, the stored buff will only be transferred to an absorption crystal affixed to a ring. If you attempt to transfer to an incompatible item, the buff will be lost.

beats.headline: Not a hat
beats.text: Donut has just received the Tiara of a Thousand Lights when a second benefactor box arrives, a platinum from the Apothecary. It is not a hat, as Carl expected, but another charging pillow, almost identical to the one that came with the tiara: ten hours to transfer fully, and the item ruined after one. This one is purple instead of red, and the warning at the end of its description is different. Almost a universal charger, Carl says, and tells Donut to check that an item is listed as a hat first. With two, she can fill the tiara twice as fast.
beats.gist: Donut's platinum box holds a purple charging pillow, not a hat, so the tiara fills faster.

beats.headline: Two hats, two pillows
beats.text: Donut puts the pillows on the counter, her new boonie hat on the red one and her Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the other. Each makes an audible click as it touches; there is no other notification. What if the cleaner bot knocks it over, she asks. Mordecai tells her not to worry: once locked in place, an item has to be peeled off, like a magnet. She can move them to her room if she likes.
beats.gist: Donut clicks her hat and tiara onto two pillows; Mordecai says locked items must be peeled off.

beats.headline: The catch-all, left empty
beats.text: Katia pulls two of Donut's drained hats off the charging pillows and sets the tiara on each in turn, and three more of its jewels light up: twenty-three buffs, seventy-six to go. She puts a plastic baseball cap on the pillow next. The other, catch-all pillow she leaves empty for the moment. They agree that for the next one, the pillow will go in a different room.
beats.gist: Katia fills one charging pillow with Donut's drained hats and the tiara, leaving the catch-all pillow empty.

relations.note: a platinum benefactor box
a second charger for the tiara

recap.text: A platinum box from the Apothecary holds not a hat but a purple charging pillow, near twin to the red one: ten hours to transfer fully, the item ruined after one. Donut sets her boonie hat on the red and her Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the purple, and each clicks as it touches. Katia pulls two drained hats off and sets the tiara on each in turn, lighting three more jewels: twenty-three buffs, seventy-six to go.

tagline.text: MySpace Photo, once called Charisma Cheat, is a two-minute potion of Mordecai's that makes the system think Donut's Charisma is thirty points higher, so that the cloak she puts on lifts her Constitution to match.

beats.headline: Catfishing the system
beats.text: Before Donut puts on her new cloak, Mordecai pulls out a potion he has just made. It used to be called Charisma Cheat, but the system now calls it MySpace Photo. It tricks the system into thinking her base Charisma is 193 instead of 163, so that when she puts the cloak on it will raise her Constitution to 193 instead of 163 in time. That is why he wanted her to wait, and it lasts two minutes. From a base Constitution of two, Carl says, that is almost Katia-level resilience. Donut drinks it, gets a very rude Catfish achievement, and the cloak appears over her shoulders, so short on her it is like a shawl.
beats.gist: Donut drinks Mordecai's MySpace Photo, which fakes her Charisma at 193, so her cloak lifts Constitution higher.

recap.text: Before Donut puts on her new cloak, Mordecai hands her a potion he has just made, once called Charisma Cheat and now called MySpace Photo. It tricks the system into reading her base Charisma as 193 instead of 163, so the cloak raises her Constitution to 193 instead of 163, for two minutes. Donut drinks it, earns a very rude Catfish achievement, and the cloak appears over her shoulders, so short it is like a shawl.

entities.name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced

tagline.text: A Legendary Spicy Box gives Carl a plain silver toe ring for his left pinky toe, and the System insists on the toe. It holds one potion to fire automatically, guards his mind against Enslavement and Conscription, and grants Extra Steady Balance and Walk on Air, a skill the description marks as already obtained.

Its Mind Balance has been blocking hundreds of attempts to cast through Carl that he never made, and it is climbing fast; trained this high, he would keep the skill, less five levels, without the ring.
The treatment meant Imani had to pry it off him while he slept, and that is the moment a teleport invitation was accepted in his name.
Its Mind Balance is level sixteen now, trained past fifteen on the battlefield.
