description.text: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced. This special, dainty, perfectly delightful toe ring (which, by the way, must be equipped on your left pinky toe. Don't test me on this) represents balance. […] When properly equipped, (again, left pinky) this toe ring imbues the following effects: Heart Balance, Level 5. Allows you to store one auto-trigger potion item if health reaches a certain criteria. Mind Balance, Level 5. Allows protection from Enslavement and Conscription. Physical Balance, Level 5. At level five, this skill imbues both the Extra Steady Balance skill and the Walk on Air Skill (already obtained.)

beats.headline: Left pinky. Don't test me
beats.text: The Legendary Spicy Box is shaped like a giant strawberry that sizzles as it opens, and inside is a simple, silver, unadorned toe ring. The description insists, twice, on the left pinky toe. Walk on Air, already obtained: that makes no sense to Carl. He knows what the skill does, and he did not have it. It is what Li Jun used when he fought, and the taste of Li Jun's eye floods his mouth. He slips the ring on, sets a gold-standard healing potion to trigger at two per cent health, and gets an ominous notice. Mind Balance is currently triggered.
beats.gist: Carl slips on the silver toe ring from the strawberry box; Mind Balance triggers.

beats.headline: Hundreds of attempts
beats.text: Carl turns his interface back on and reads the suppressed notifications. Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Mind Balance prevented activation. Your attempt to disable Mind Balance was prevented by Mind Balance. It is level nine, up from five a few hours ago, over pages of attempts to cast that he never made. Shi Maria, the tattoo on his chest, is trying to use him; had the phase gone off, it would likely have set off the ogre's non-magical bombs, and Donut would have died. Even so the spider breaks in for a moment. Watch out, Carl.
beats.gist: Carl's toe ring blocks Shi Maria's hundreds of attempts to cast Gloom Wraith Phase.

beats.headline: Pried off
beats.text: Before three adjutants, the night of the treatment plays on a screen. A warlord's teleport invitation reached Carl's interface while he was still conscious. Then Rosetta, Bucket Boy and Mordecai stand over him on the cot while Imani pries off his toe ring, as the cure required once he was out. The moment the ring comes off, the request is accepted, by the entity controlling him.
beats.gist: Imani pries off Carl's toe ring, and the entity controlling him accepts the warlord's teleport.

beats.headline: Level sixteen
beats.text: Slapped awake, Carl is hammered with psionic debuffs: ten more Endless Threads of Distraction, Self Harm, Intrusive Thoughts. His Mind Balance is overwhelmed, and he thinks of surrendering. A voice tells him to look at his feet, bare and buried in an All Tree root. Mind Balance is level sixteen now, trained past fifteen on battlefield conditions, and it wakes him. When Eris casts Bear Witness over almost the whole floor, everyone around him freezes. His Mind Balance negates it.
beats.gist: Carl's Mind Balance, now level sixteen, wakes him from psionic debuffs and negates Eris's Bear Witness freezing everyone.

beats.headline: Soul Suck
beats.text: On the road into the cannibals' village, a huge man with a staff stands in the way and pulls off his ape-skull mask: a human, balding, red hair in a bone-pinned bun. He starts to chant. Soul Suck has been negated by your Mind Balance skill. Donut is immune anyway, thanks to her constitution and charisma. Carl reads the description and can hardly believe it.
beats.gist: Soul Suck is negated by Carl's Mind Balance skill, and Donut is immune anyway.

relations.note: its Mind Balance blocks her attempts to cast through Carl

recap.text: Carl slips on the silver toe ring from the Legendary Spicy Box, and Mind Balance blocks hundreds of casts by Shi Maria, the tattoo on his chest, that would likely have killed Donut. A screen shows Imani prying the ring off his toe as he lies on the cot, and the entity controlling him accepts a warlord's teleport invitation. At level sixteen, Mind Balance wakes him from psionic debuffs and negates Eris's Bear Witness.

On the road into the cannibals' village, a huge man in an ape-skull mask blocks the way with a staff, then pulls the mask off to show a balding human with red hair in a bone-pinned bun. He starts to chant. Carl's Mind Balance skill negates the Soul Suck, and Donut is immune anyway, thanks to her constitution and charisma. Carl reads the description and can hardly believe it.

entities.name: Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe

tagline.text: A Celestial skill potion in a bottle shaped like a horned skull, which gives one random combat skill of level 10 to 15 taken from a Sheol mob of level 200 or more. Carl drinks it and comes away with the level-13 Gloom Wraith Phase.

description.text: Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe. In case you haven’t figured this out yet, we’re trying to kick things up a notch this year. If we’re gonna do this, we want all of you fuckers as deadly as possible. Hence, this prize. It’s time to bring out your inner demon. Drinking this potion will give you a random level 10 to 15 Celestial-tier skill. The skill will be combat based, and it will be something you don’t already have. This skill potion is hell-kissed. That means this skill will be any combat-based skill from any Sheol-level mob level 200 or higher. Go ahead and drink it. Do it. Do it.

beats.headline: Out of a drum kit
beats.text: The Celestial Heavy Metal box arrives as a full drum kit with pyrotechnics, Amayon's face on both bass drums and an ethereal demon playing speed metal behind it. Mongo screeches. The kit explodes, 666 hangs in the air in smoke, and all that is left is one glittering potion in a horned-skull bottle with a note tied round the top: Drink Me, and a demon hand giving the devil horns. The liquid is black and bubbling. Mordecai, shaking, calls it a Celestial-quality skill potion, and once Carl has examined it he rushes it off to his table. He comes back whispering that he could make these, with a few more table upgrades and some pretty specialized ingredients.
beats.gist: Mordecai wants to copy the black skill potion that the Celestial Heavy Metal box leaves in smoke.

beats.headline: Drink me deep
beats.text: Mordecai tells Carl to take it right away, since whatever it gives him he will need to train with. The bottle speaks up in a deep, demonic voice: drink me, drink me deep. Carl pops the cork and drinks it manually, which is a mistake, because it tastes like ass. The potion groans as it dissipates into dust. For a fraction of a second he sees the burning hellscape of Sheol, smells the sulfur and feels worms crawling over him. A demon-skull button appears in his interface: the level-13 Gloom Wraith Phase, a non-corporeal lunge that passes through unenchanted weapons and flesh and scrambles any living thing unarmored against non-corporeal attacks.
beats.gist: Mordecai tells Carl to drink the potion, and it gives him a level-13 Gloom Wraith Phase lunge.

recap.text: Carl takes the Celestial Heavy Metal box, which arrives as a full drum kit with Amayon's face on both bass drums and an ethereal demon playing speed metal behind it. The kit explodes, leaving 666 in smoke and a horned-skull bottle marked Drink Me. Mordecai, shaking, urges him to drink it at once, and Carl pops the cork and tastes ass. The potion groans into dust, and a demon-skull button appears: the level-13 Gloom Wraith Phase, a non-corporeal lunge.

entities.name: Reaper Spider Minion merchant patch
entities.role: Carl's key to the Midnight Market

tagline.text: A small black-and-silver upgrade patch of a Reaper Spider Minion merchant, from a Platinum box. Affixed to a garment, it opens the Midnight Market, warns of traveling merchants nearby and adds five percent to Dexterity; Mordecai calls the market a place Carl needs to stay out of.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Small. This upgrade patch depicts a traveling Reaper Spider Minion merchant. These guys are known for their sense of humor, and I highly recommend the first thing you do the next time you meet one is to insult them. They’ll love it. Affixing this patch to an eligible garment will imbue the following benefits: Access to the Midnight Market. Safety or Sanity not guaranteed. You will receive a notification if any traveling merchants are nearby. Plus 5% to Dexterity. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: A spider with baskets
beats.text: The Platinum Hell in a Handbasket Box holds a small patch of a spider. It's Shi Maria, Donut says; just a regular Reaper Spider Minion, says Carl. Mordecai grunts that it will give him access to a place he needs to stay out of, and Donut points out that telling Carl not to do something never works. Examined, it is black and silver, die cut in her horrifying shape but with a shorter neck and shorter hair, and wicker baskets lashed over the bulbous body. It grants access to the Midnight Market, a notice when traveling merchants are near, and five percent Dexterity. Carl is pretty sure the market is a bazaar hidden in the Desperado Club's bottom floor, and thanks to his Scavenger's Daughter, every patch he installs raises his stats, so this one should go on right away.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut open a box and find a spider patch that opens the Midnight Market.

recap.text: Carl opens the Platinum Hell in a Handbasket Box and finds a small spider patch, which Donut calls Shi Maria and Carl calls a regular Reaper Spider Minion. Mordecai grunts that it opens a place Carl must stay out of, and Donut notes that telling Carl no never works. The black and silver patch grants Midnight Market access, a notice of traveling merchants, and five percent Dexterity, so Carl installs it.

tagline.text: Jamal is a seventeen-foot hammerhead shark who breathes air and can only flop, so Carl has built him a voice-controlled harness of eight double-jointed automaton legs. It holds his weight fine, but its joints cannot take the landing when he tells it to hop, which he keeps doing.
Jamal has new legs, and he has broken them again; Justice Light says he can fix them without going into the saferoom.
On his mechanical spider legs, newly enhanced and fortified, Jamal can move terrifyingly fast.
Carl's No Disassemble has wrecked Jamal's legs, the fifth set he has been given, because they were not shielded. Katia has made him another set, and Mordecai has it.
Jamal is bouncing up and down on a new set of legs.
Mordecai has given Jamal's front legs grabbers that look like hands.
Jamal's legs now have new and improved sticky feet, good enough to walk upside down on a ceiling and get stuck there.
Jamal's legs are wrecked and have fallen off him again, though he is alive.

beats.headline: Three hops, three harnesses
beats.text: Behind Carl in the forest, Jamal apologizes: he did a little hop, and the metal pieces broke again. It is the third harness Carl has hastily built him, like the conveyance Katia built for Tran but much bigger: eight double-jointed legs and a harness for the seventeen-foot shark, who now breathes air and, no longer one of Signet's paper tattoos, cannot fly. It makes him look like a horrifying spider hybrid. Carl's prototype takes spoken orders; Katia's version is to read his thoughts. The joints can handle the jump but not the landing, and Carl is out of extra-large leg joints. Jamal must wait for Katia.
beats.gist: Carl builds Jamal a third harness, eight spider legs for the shark, but his hop breaks it.

beats.headline: Broken again
beats.text: Donut's message from the base, all in capitals, runs through the news: the new wall is coming along nicely, they have painted the castle pink, and Jamal broke his new legs again. Justice Light says he can fix them without going into the saferoom. Katia and Li Na are almost done with the clock tower, and Katia is on her way to Carl.
beats.gist: Donut's all-caps message reports the pink castle and that Jamal broke his new legs again.

beats.headline: A spear swiped away
beats.text: Jamal hops in circles round two terrified crawlers, Selvi and Tuba, while Bigs ties them up. Carl had ordered the shark and the slug not to hurt them, but Tuba bleeds profusely from a wound in her side: Jamal was forced to swipe her spear away with one of his mechanical legs. Neither woman can be healed, a side effect of refusing to fight while under Conscription.
beats.gist: Jamal swipes Tuba's spear away with a mechanical leg while Bigs ties up Tuba and Selvi.

beats.headline: The fifth set
beats.text: Jamal flops along behind the group, complaining loudly: these were the fifth set of legs he has been given, and he was led to believe they were top quality. Katia calls over her shoulder that the bomb ruined the cybernetics, and not only his; there are more in the saferoom. Jamal has seen the ones in her workshop, and they are much too small for him. Don't worry, Katia says: she made another set for him, and Mordecai has it. Carl tells Donut the legs failed because they were not shielded, on the very edge of the No Disassemble's pulse.
beats.gist: Jamal complains about his fifth set of legs; Katia blames the bomb and says Mordecai has another set.

beats.headline: A new set
beats.text: Jamal stayed in the saferoom through the Zerzura, and he is one of the few NPCs who have decided to stay with Carl and Donut. Now he bounces up and down on a new set of legs, very excited at the thought of seeing a goddess like Eileithyia, who he has heard is quite beautiful, though not as beautiful as her retainer, Yemaya.
beats.gist: Jamal bounces on his new legs, excited to see the goddess Eileithyia.

beats.headline: Hands on the front legs
beats.text: Donut tells Jamal he is not hacking down a tree: gentle but firm. He is practising with the new grabbers on his front legs, designed by Mordecai, which make his front spider legs look like they have hands and him look even more terrifying. He holds one brush in each, one on Donut and the screaming one on Carl, both of which give them their daily buffs, and he brushes them inexpertly.
beats.gist: Jamal practises brushing Donut and Carl with Mordecai's new hand-like grabbers while Donut coaches him.

beats.headline: Stuck on the ceiling
beats.text: Jamal is up on the ceiling. He wanted to see whether he could walk upside down with his new and improved sticky feet, and now, he apologizes, he finds himself in quite the inverted conundrum. He is stuck, and has been for quite a bit. Then, talking fast and sad, he says he is happy to have his legs, but he wishes he could just go back to the ocean, and he came up there so he could see everything all at once.
beats.gist: Jamal gets stuck on the ceiling testing his sticky feet and says he misses the ocean.

beats.headline: Smashed against the wall
beats.text: In the wreck of the arena, Imani calls for everyone to check in. The RV is broken in half, and the Tigran APV lies on its side. Mongo stands shaking his head, Rend is on his feet, and Gonk hides behind Simoom. Jamal is smashed against the far wall, his legs absolutely wrecked and fallen off him. But he is alive.
beats.gist: Jamal is smashed against the far wall with his legs wrecked and fallen off, but he is alive.

relations.note: the prototypes
Katia-designed spider legs
the grabbers on the front legs

recap.text: Jamal, a seventeen-foot shark who now breathes air and cannot fly, hops a little and breaks his third harness of eight double-jointed spider legs, because Carl is out of extra-large leg joints. Katia says the bomb ruined the fifth set, which had no shielding at the edge of the No Disassemble's pulse. Jamal swipes Tuba's spear away with one leg, leaving her bleeding, then bounces on a new set Mordecai holds.

Jamal practises brushing Donut and Carl with the new grabbers Mordecai designed for his front legs, which make his spider legs look like hands, and Donut tells him to be gentle but firm. Jamal then climbs onto the ceiling to test his new sticky feet, gets stuck, and says he wishes he could go back to the ocean. In the wrecked arena, he lies smashed against the far wall with his legs fallen off, alive.

tagline.text: Dazzlers are part alarm, part spotlight trap, one of the few trap modules allowed in a trebuchet. Each strobes coloured light into the eyes of the nearest enemy soldier, and all of them play the same song at the same time.
When every war protection on the field is stripped away, the Dazzlers keep flashing and playing.

beats.headline: Fifty in the trebuchet
beats.text: The army has one trebuchet of its own, a small one Carl and Donut looted from some Dream elves on the sixth floor. It is loaded with about fifty contraptions called Dazzlers, with almost two hundred more piled nearby. They are basically an alarm and a spotlight trap combined: they shine only toward the eyes of the closest enemy soldier, strobing powerful multi-coloured beams into their faces, and they all play the same song at the same time. They are one of the few trap modules Victory allows in a trebuchet.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut load a small looted trebuchet with about fifty Dazzlers, strobing, song-playing spotlight traps.

beats.headline: Killing in the Name
beats.text: The trebuchet fires the first of four salvos, spreading Dazzlers in and around the middle of Louis's craters. The announcement is louder than Carl expects, even from this far away: Justice Light's tips on enhancing them have worked. He slips his earplugs in. They barely help. Peaking at number three on June 20, 2020, despite first coming out in 1992, it's Killing in the Name. The Rage Against the Machine song shakes the ground louder than the explosions, and anyone within a few hundred meters takes immediate, painful hearing damage.
beats.gist: The trebuchet fires Dazzlers into Louis's craters; Killing in the Name wrecks hearing nearby.

beats.headline: Still playing
beats.text: A big one: Deshrouded. The war protections are gone, all of them. The illusions vanish, the smoke clears, and every temporary protection spell snaps off, the ear protection included. The lights and music from the Dazzlers do not turn off. Donut and Mongo both seem to be screaming with pain, and Mongo rears at the sound. For a moment there is an unobscured view across the dim battlefield, where several of the enemy have turned from the painful light and most have their hands over their ears or eyes.
beats.gist: Deshrouded strips every war protection, yet the Dazzlers' lights and music keep hurting Donut, Mongo and the enemy.

relations.note: loaded into his army's one trebuchet
his tips on enhancing them

recap.text: Carl and Donut's trebuchet, looted from Dream elves, holds about fifty Dazzlers: alarm-and-spotlight traps that strobe the closest enemy's eyes and all play one song. The first of four salvos lands in Louis's craters, and Killing in the Name shakes the ground louder than the explosions. Deshrouded then strips every war protection, ear protection included, but the Dazzlers keep playing. Donut and Mongo scream, and most of the enemy cover their ears or eyes.

tagline.text: War Crime is a spellbook Donut drew from her 1914 box. The book itself is bleeding and crying, and she is not sure she should read it.
War Crime is one of Donut's Atrocity-class spells, which the Nest tower is built to amplify, and it is the part of the plan Carl prays they will not need.

War Crime combines two of Donut's spells in a way most governments would call unconscionable, once a floor and only on the Scolopendra levels, three times in all. Nobody it catches can die of it, so it needs a finisher.
Donut has cast War Crime with Bijanbi and Astral Paw, and thousands of soldiers and a god have been slammed through Li Na's chains. It made her The Oak Fell, Champion of Nekhebit.
Donut has cast War Crime once and cannot cast it again before the twelfth floor; asked which three spells she would combine next, she says nothing is off the table.

description.text: War Crime. As this spell is unable to be properly trained, it will start at level 5, and it will increase by 5 each time it is cast. Type: Atrocity. Target: A line-of-sight beam extending from caster’s eyes that shoots in a narrow cone. Area of effect: See description. Cost: 1 mana point. Duration: See description. Cooldown: This spell can only be cast once per floor, and it can only be cast on the Scolopendra Levels, meaning levels 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18. It can only be cast a total of 3 times. This spell has been cast 0 times so far. …

beats.headline: Bleeding and crying
beats.text: Carl is taking in a rare moment of silence, still processing what happened when they confronted D'Nadia, when two messages arrive at once. Donut has opened her 1914 box and got a spellbook called War Crime. She is not sure whether she should read it. The book itself is bleeding and crying, and it is disgusting. The other message is Florin, falling back as the enemy finally shows its armor, and then the trap notifications start.
beats.gist: Donut opens her 1914 box and finds War Crime, a bleeding, crying spellbook, as Florin reports traps.

beats.headline: Built into the Nest
beats.text: When they built the Nest tower they could assign its synergy to several skills, spells and classes. A straight-up sniper tower was the first idea, but Donut's tiara made that unnecessary, so the Nest was built instead to have synergy with something called Atrocity-class spells. Donut has several, including her new one, War Crime. It is the one part of the day's plan Carl prays they will not have to use.
beats.gist: Donut's Nest tower is built for Atrocity-class spells, including War Crime, which Carl prays they will not use.

beats.headline: An act of fiendish cruelty
beats.text: In a note to the Cookbook, Carl writes that he used an old dictionary in the guildhall to look up Atrocity: an act of fiendish cruelty. Perhaps the definition is right and the system is wrong to call Donut's War Crime spell one; or perhaps the true act of fiendish cruelty was giving her the spell at all. It came in the Legendary 1914 box they received after killing D'Nadia, the same box as his Run, Little Günter, Run. For the first time he prays a plan of his own will not succeed.
beats.gist: Donut's Atrocity spell came in the same Legendary 1914 box as Carl's Run, Little Günter, Run.

beats.headline: Two spells and a finisher
beats.text: Rosetta changes the plan: Bijanbi, a Dinner Bell variant from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, and Wall of Fire, both amplified by War Crime, to drag the enemies out and drop them into a ring of fire, with the fleshers as the finisher, because War Crime keeps its victims alive. Carl has the spell's extra-long description in his scratch pad. It starts at level 5, combines two spells in a creative way, can be cast once a floor and only on the Scolopendra levels, knocks the caster to 1% health, and cannot kill anyone directly. They will want to die. They won't.
beats.gist: Rosetta amplifies Bijanbi and Wall of Fire with War Crime, keeping enemies alive for the fleshers.

beats.headline: Anything but fire
beats.text: The Nest is at 8% health, and a net Lucia Mar left behind keeps Donut from leaving the tower. Carl wants to abort, but Li Na says it is a little late for that: the ball is about to break. Donut, don't cast War Crime, Carl shouts, but she has to cast the moment it breaks, or everyone will be mixed in together, the gods included. If she does not cast it, Donut says, all of this will be for nothing. Cast it, Carl tells her, but don't pick fire; the Nest has to stay intact. Anything but fire. The ball has broken, Li Na says. Cast now!
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut to cast War Crime when the ball breaks: anything but fire.

beats.headline: The Oak Fell
beats.text: Casting now, Donut shouts. She has committed a third Atrocity, received a new class, and will be called The Oak Fell, Champion of Nekhebit. Her two spells are Bijanbi and Astral Paw. Out of the broken ball, thousands of soldiers and the god Meatus float up in slow motion and bunch beneath an enormous glowing cat's paw while fleshers dissolve them. Li Na builds a lattice of chains below. Trembling in Carl's arms, Donut swipes downward, and the paw slams them through the chains, again and again, dozens of times.
beats.gist: Donut casts her third Atrocity, and a glowing cat's paw slams soldiers and Meatus through Li Na's chains.

beats.headline: Two Celestial boxes
beats.text: Going through her achievements, Donut finds two Celestial boxes from her War Crime spell: a celestial slap-chop box and a celestial godslayer box. The last box to open, the smoky godslayer one, forms into the shape of Meatus as a smoky paw slams down on it, and leaves no physical reward behind. Then Donut stares at her forward right paw, the same paw she used for War Crime, her voice full of fear. Something's happening. The paw glows, and Mordecai says he knows what this is.
beats.gist: Donut finds two Celestial boxes from War Crime; the godslayer box takes Meatus's shape, and her paw glows.

beats.headline: A second casting
beats.text: At a table of goats passing judgment, one of the big ones finds Donut worthy and asks her a question: has she given any thought to which three spells she might combine if she cast War Crime a second time? She stiffens, then composes herself. It will depend on the circumstances, she says. Nothing is off the table, but she won't be able to cast it until the twelfth floor, and she and Carl must first get through the next two.
beats.gist: Donut tells a goat judge she can't cast War Crime again until the twelfth floor, after two more.

recap.text: Donut opens a Legendary 1914 box and gets War Crime, a spellbook that bleeds and cries. With the Nest at 8% health and Lucia Mar's net keeping Donut in the tower, Carl tells her to cast it, anything but fire. She commits a third Atrocity and becomes The Oak Fell, Champion of Nekhebit. A glowing cat's paw slams thousands of soldiers and the god Meatus through Li Na's chains, dozens of times.

Donut finds two Celestial boxes from her War Crime spell, a slap-chop box and a godslayer box. The smoky godslayer box forms into the shape of Meatus as a smoky paw slams down on it, and leaves no physical reward. Donut's forward right paw begins to glow, and Mordecai says he knows what this is. Asked which three spells she would combine in a second casting, she says nothing is off the table, but not before the twelfth floor.

tagline.text: A necklace of Indelible Woe trades a random spell of its wearer's for one of a target's, and for one of the target's five highest-level spells if the wearer kills the target. It works only on crawlers and people like Tipid, and Tipid reckons King Rust has one.
King Rust's body is in Carl's inventory, and with it a second Ring of Divine Suffering and the necklace.
Li Na asked about the necklace and decided against it, because it could cost her one of her level-15 dreads. It stays in Carl's inventory.

beats.headline: How a copycat levels
beats.text: King Rust has turned up as a war chief, riding a swamp yak named Gonk, and Donut's Size-Up reads him: level 78, dozens and dozens of spells, most at level one but some from 11 to 15, Protective Shell at 15 among them. How did he level so fast? Tipid says he likely has a ring of Divine Suffering for the stats and a necklace of Indelible Woe for the spells. It is in the same collection as the ring, and it trades a random spell of the wearer's for one of a target's; kill the target and it is one of their five highest. It was popular long ago, until they all agreed to stop using it, because combatants were farming crawlers to power it up. The necklace, Tipid says, is much worse than the ring.
beats.gist: King Rust's Necklace of Indelible Woe trades spells with a target; Tipid calls it worse than the ring.

beats.headline: In the dead king's pockets
beats.text: Walking the wrecked base with Boomer, Carl remembers: Donut has not really turned King Rust's body into a rug. Carl has him in his inventory. That means he now has a second Ring of Divine Suffering, and he has that damn necklace too. The dead king had several other magical items on him as well, most of which would not work on Carl. He will need to sit down with the others and talk about what to do with all of it.
beats.gist: Carl remembers King Rust's body is in his inventory, along with the necklace and a second ring.

beats.headline: We don't need that necklace
beats.text: Donut wants to know, in capitals, what Carl did with King Rust's ring and the necklace. Don't worry, he tells her. He can only wear one Ring of Divine Suffering at a time; he checked. Two rings cannot mark the same person on this floor anyway. And they do not need that necklace. The king had some other magical gear, which they will distribute around, and they will work out what to do with it all when there is time.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut they do not need King Rust's necklace, since he can wear only one ring.

beats.headline: Li Na turns it down
beats.text: When Li Na first asked for Carl's spare Ring of Divine Suffering, his instinct was no. Imani agreed with him; Katia and Elle did not, and Donut, without saying why, begged him to give it to her as soon as he could. Li Na also asked about the Necklace of Indelible Woe, and then decided she did not want it, now that she has several level-15 dreads she could lose if she used it. It remains in Carl's inventory for now.
beats.gist: Li Na turns down the Necklace of Indelible Woe, so it stays with Carl.

relations.note: the same collection

recap.text: Tipid guesses that King Rust, level 78 on his swamp yak Gonk, leveled on a ring of Divine Suffering and a necklace of Indelible Woe, which trades a random spell of the wearer's for one of a target's. Carl, who has the dead king's body in his inventory, now holds both. He tells Donut they do not need the necklace. Li Na asks about it, then refuses because she could lose her level-15 dreads, so it stays with Carl.

entities.name: Carl's chain dragon tattoo
entities.role: Li Na's skill, on Carl's arm

tagline.text: Katia is tattooing a chain shaped like a dragon on Carl's right arm. It carries a level-13 skill Li Na gave freely, at the cost of five of her levels for a while, and if it is drawn well it should last him the rest of the floor.
The tattoo's skill is Profane Iron, a once-a-day burst of chains that rip out of Carl's skin for about thirty seconds. He can truly control two of them; Li Na controls ten.

beats.headline: A chain shaped like a dragon
beats.text: Katia sets a vial of ink on the table, already mixed, and Carl lays the poke and stick tattoo kit beside it. Li Na lost five levels temporarily but can still use the skill; intention matters, and with blood freely given, the potion allows the spell or skill to be chosen. The tattoo itself is permanent. A level-13 skill needs a big one and almost all the ink, and a properly themed design will last longer. Katia has never done a real tattoo, and Edgar is off scouting. Donut messages that it must be drawn in the voodoo book first for her approval. Carl's idea: a chain. A chain shaped like a dragon.
beats.gist: Katia mixes the ink, Carl sets out the kit, and Donut demands a drawn design first.

beats.headline: Expert quality
beats.text: Donut jumps into Carl's lap and examines the new, shining tattoo on his right forearm with a paw. She grunts. He is starting to look like one of those white rapper doodle notebook guys, she says, and it is a little crooked; she should have been there. It is not crooked, Carl tells her. The system says it is expert quality, which Edgar says is the second highest there is.
beats.gist: Donut examines Carl's new tattoo and calls it crooked, but Carl insists the system rates it expert quality.

beats.headline: Profane Iron
beats.text: As the mantaurs charge, Carl activates the skill he received from Li Na. Profane Iron. His skin tears as dozens of chains rip from his flesh, at a small cost to his health. Two chains pluck the Black Nimbus potions from his hands and smash them into two mantaurs; a third wraps round a neck, a fourth trips two more, and two strike scorpion-like into a guard's clavicles and rip his head away with part of his spine. The fight is over in seconds. It is a once-a-day skill: he gets about thirty seconds and two chains he can truly control, where Li Na gets ninety seconds and ten.
beats.gist: Carl activates Profane Iron, and chains tear from his skin to wreck the charging mantaurs in seconds.

relations.note: her skill, lent with her blood

recap.text: Carl and Katia settle on a chain shaped like a dragon, drawn first in Donut's voodoo book for her approval. Donut grunts at the finished tattoo on his right forearm and calls it a little crooked, though the system rates it expert quality. When the mantaurs charge, Carl uses Profane Iron: chains tear from his skin, smash two Black Nimbus potions into two mantaurs, and rip a guard's head away.

entities.name: Spellbook of Run, Little Günter, Run

tagline.text: A special-edition spellbook from Carl's 1914 box that grows centipede legs, drips black goo and begs not to be read. Its spell summons Little Günter, a one-hit creature who stores whatever attack hits him and carries it to a target.
Carl uses Run, Little Günter, Run to double a bomb: Günter should come through the blast unhurt and carry it down the hallway to the god, and a second, distant explosion follows.
Little Günter carries a mallet blow just as well as a bomb, and he still says hello first.

description.text: Spellbook of Run, Little Günter, Run. This spellbook is a Special Edition. This means you will learn this spell at level 5, and it will train up faster than usual. Run, Little Günter, Run. Cost: Variable. Minimum 20 mana. Target: This is a summoning spell. It will summon a small, hominid creature named Little Günter. He will appear directly in front of caster. Duration: Once activated, Little Günter will last 20 seconds plus one second per mana point added above the minimum. Higher spell levels decrease mana cost per second. You must activate Little Günter within 30 seconds of summoning him, otherwise he will dissipate. …

beats.headline: The book that cried
beats.text: The spellbook from Carl's 1914 box grew little centipede legs and skittered away the moment it came out. It is bigger than spellbooks usually are, drips a foul-smelling black liquid, whimpers like a dog, and shrieks in a caricatured Austrian accent: stay away, don't touch me, I'll die if you read me. It does not show on the minimap, and Katia cannot examine it. The potion from his Celestial box was like that, Carl says, and so was Donut's War Crime spellbook. The cleaner bot settles it, sucking the book up and dropping it angrily into Carl's arms, and he pulls it into his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl's summoning spellbook sprouts legs and shrieks until the cleaner bot sucks it up and Carl pockets it.

beats.headline: Read anyway
beats.text: The spell is a summoning. Little Günter, a small, fat, child-like creature with a single point of health, appears in front of Carl and waits to be attacked. The attack is stored, Günter runs as fast as he can toward a designated target, or away at random, and the stored attack lands when he gets there or times out. Carl's mind whirls: his Daughter's Kiss, a bomb. Katia asks whether Donut could store a trigger spell on him. There is only one way to find out, Carl says, and applies the book. Warmth spreads over him as he learns the spell.
beats.gist: Carl learns the Little Günter spell, which stores an attack on a one-health summoned creature.

beats.headline: Get the god
beats.text: In Khepri's temple, with its endless hallway, as Vinata's three guards charge, Carl casts it. A short, fat, pink-skinned kid in lederhosen appears, licking a massive lollipop. Hi, I'm Günter! Get the god, Carl yells, meaning Khepri, and then the very big bomb goes off. Günter, in theory, should be unhurt by the blast and now running down the hallway toward the deity with it stored, effectively doubling the attack. While Carl's body re-forms, a second explosion comes, distant. That, he suspects, is Günter finally catching up to the bug god.
beats.gist: Carl casts the spell in Khepri's temple, and a lollipop-licking Günter in lederhosen appears to chase the god.

beats.headline: A mallet blow, delivered
beats.text: The kangaroo boss is level 170 and heals himself by eating gremlins. Carl casts the spell, and the chunky, pig-nosed kid in lederhosen appears with a lollipop of a new colour: Hi, I'm Günter! Pontiff, already in his backswing, wallops him with his glowing mallet and bounces back as if he had hit a wall. Nein, nein, Günter shrieks, and runs straight at the kangaroo, who coos at the baby. When Günter reaches him, the delayed mallet strike lands, and the massive kangaroo flips through the air onto his back.
beats.gist: Carl casts the spell, and Günter's act as a baby distracts the kangaroo until Pontiff's mallet flips him.

recap.text: Carl casts the summoning spell from the spellbook that skittered off on centipede legs, and a short, fat, pink-skinned kid in lederhosen appears in Khepri's temple, licking a massive lollipop. Carl yells for him to get the god and sets off the very big bomb as Vinata's three guards charge. Günter runs down the endless hallway with the blast stored. A second, distant explosion sounds while Carl's body re-forms.

Carl casts the spell against the level 170 kangaroo boss, who heals himself by eating gremlins. A chunky, pig-nosed kid in lederhosen appears, lollipop in hand, and says hi, he is Günter. Pontiff, already mid-backswing, wallops him with his glowing mallet and bounces back as if he had hit a wall. Günter shrieks nein, nein and runs at the kangaroo, who coos at the baby. The delayed strike lands, and the kangaroo flips onto his back.

tagline.text: Carl held a potion of Conscription behind his back when Prepotente landed, the other way of bringing him into the army, and put it away the moment Prepotente asked to be recruited.

The war mages are conscripting gods with hell-kissed versions of it, level 18, five of them bought at the Midnight Market with the Gate of the Feral Gods. One worked on Yarilo, and the war mage who threw it blew up.
Li Na duplicated one taken off a dead war mage and gave Carl the copy, a screaming glass bottle brewed in the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, and he broke it over Lucia Mar's head.
Lucia Mar and Harpocrates are both conscripted into the Princess Posse until the floor ends.

description.text: Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18. This works like a regular potion of Conscription, but it has been hell-kissed. At level 18, it will work against pretty much any non-affiliated entities, regardless of their protections, including most deities. Most. It was brewed in the dark recesses of the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, who is said to yearn for domination, which was why she'd been banished there in the first place. […] Conscription potions only work on the 9th, 12th, 15th, 17th, and 18th floors.

beats.headline: Behind his back
beats.text: Prepotente lands on Bianca, now level 70 and full-sized; he is level 99 himself, by far the strongest crawler in the dungeon. They cannot talk unless he joins the army, Carl begins. I know, Carl, says Prepotente. Recruit me. Behind his back, in his other hand, Carl pulls the potion of Conscription back into his inventory. It probably would not have worked on Prepotente, and the moment it is stowed, a strange relief and clarity hit him. No. Not like that. Never like that.
beats.gist: Carl pulls the Conscription potion back into his inventory unused and feels sudden relief.

beats.headline: Hell-kissed versions
beats.text: Two war mages have gone for the gods, and Victory bursts out in disbelief. Fopsy reckons it would take the spell at nineteen, maybe eighteen, and it will not work on sponsored gods. They are using potions, not the spell, says Victory: hell-kissed versions, level 18, likely suicide for a caster too far below the target. Fopsy checks his menus. They traded the Gate of the Feral Gods at the Midnight Market for five of them. Then Samantha reports a war mage tossing one on Yarilo. It worked, and the war mage blew up.
beats.gist: A war mage's hell-kissed potion works on Yarilo, and the war mage blows up.

beats.headline: Screaming glass
beats.text: A chain from Li Na's shoulder drops a potion in front of Carl, the one he asked her to loot from the war mage who flew at Harpocrates. The large, warm bottle is an eyeless demonic head with many tentacles, which wave though they are glass, and when he grabs it, every mouth screams. Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18. She used Jun's scroll of potion duplication; the original she will use on Harpocrates herself. If the level gap is too high, it is dangerous, Carl calls after her. She does not wait.
beats.gist: Carl asks Li Na for a potion; she brings a screaming, tentacled glass demon head and walks off.

beats.headline: Never like this
beats.text: In the tower's stairwell, Raul holds Lucia Mar up in his claws, and she does not fight back. Please, she begs: she doesn't want to play anymore. Raul snaps again, and her shield winks out. A regular one might work, but Carl needs to be sure. He pulls out the potion Li Na has just duplicated for him. No. Not like this. Never like this. Sometimes we do what we have to do to survive. He smashes the screaming, hell-kissed Conscription potion against Lucia's head.
beats.gist: Carl smashes a screaming, hell-kissed Conscription potion against Lucia Mar's head after Raul strips her shield.

beats.headline: Under orders
beats.text: The potion works, and a pink glow appears around Lucia's dot. Ordered to cancel any spell meant to hurt them, her terrified face switches to malice: she was faking. Her protections drop on command, and however hard she lunges, she cannot attack him. Then a warlord message: Harpocrates, level 250, has been successfully conscripted into the Princess Posse. Li Na is alive and at full health. She found a way to use the potion without hurting herself.
beats.gist: The potion conscripts Harpocrates, level 250, into the Princess Posse, and Li Na survives at full health.

relations.note: the War Mages traded the Gate at the Midnight Market for five
the hell-kissed ones, brewed in the Nothing by Krakaren Prime

recap.text: Carl smashes the screaming, hell-kissed Conscription potion against Lucia Mar's head while Raul holds her up in his claws in the tower's stairwell. He had pulled the earlier potion back into his inventory when Prepotente, level 99, asked to be recruited. Li Na used Jun's scroll of potion duplication on her own potion, and Harpocrates, level 250, is conscripted into the Princess Posse.

tagline.text: Mordecai brewed this potion for the push into Club Vanquisher. For an hour it closes the drinker off from aura effects, Blessings and Dreads alike, though it does not cancel effects already in place or the drinker's own auras, and it does not work on pets.

beats.headline: Closed Off
beats.text: Rend goes into his pet carrier and Bianca is stored, because Mordecai's aura potion does not work on pets. At the door of Club Vanquisher, Carl hands Prepotente one of the yellow, bubbling potions. Mordecai made it, and it lasts an hour; the ones Prepotente had before lasted two minutes. He drinks it manually and finds it similar to a Crodino. Carl drinks his through the menu. You have been Closed Off: no longer susceptible to aura effects, Blessings or Dreads. Everyone in the area, take your aura potions, Carl orders. We're going inside.
beats.gist: Carl and Prepotente drink Mordecai's hour-long potions and become Closed Off; Rend and Bianca stay out.

relations.note: a shield against auras, and Li Na's are called Dreads

recap.text: Carl and Prepotente reach the door of Club Vanquisher after Rend goes into his pet carrier and Bianca is stored, since Mordecai's aura potion does not work on pets. Carl hands Prepotente a yellow, bubbling potion that lasts an hour, where his earlier ones lasted two minutes. Prepotente drinks his by hand and finds it similar to a Crodino. Carl drinks his through the menu and is Closed Off, then orders everyone to take theirs.

tagline.text: The Waffle Maker is Carl's thermobaric bomb: about the punch of the one that needed wheels, minus the Fear, in a device the size of a thermos. It incinerates everything within a hundred meters, and Louis carries fifty of them on Party Planner.

beats.headline: Dropped in a narrow room
beats.text: Carl has been tinkering with this bomb for a while. The first version, Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home, was so big it had to have wheels; this one packs about the same punch, minus the Fear, into a device the size of a thermos, a thermobaric explosion that incinerates anything within a hundred meters. Louis has fifty of them on Party Planner, and only fifty because the explosive dust is a pain to make. The AI has helpfully called it The Waffle Maker. In Khepri's narrow temple, as Vinata's three guards leap at him, it goes off. Fwummm-bam. Only his immortality holds Carl's atoms together.
beats.gist: Carl's thermos-sized bomb, The Waffle Maker, explodes in Khepri's narrow temple as three guards leap.

beats.headline: Liquified
beats.text: Among Carl's achievements from the raid is Liquified: while immortal, he blew himself up, dropping a bomb at his own feet. The AI loved the slow-motion replay. It only worked, it adds, because he had god-tier immortality; most versions of that spell would have splattered him into so many pieces he would never have reconstituted in time. And don't even think about trying it with that other, bigger bomb in his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl blows himself up with a bomb at his own feet while immortal, earning the Liquified achievement.

beats.headline: Bombs away
beats.text: Over the target, Samantha shouts from the cockpit, every bomb aboard Louis's airship arms itself, and Carl puts Overclocked on each one. Louis calls bombs away, and several spots in the floor slide open. The square, shield- and tech-busting No Disassembles clink out of their holders first, then the round, high-yield Waffle Makers, shaped like tubes, clunking out heavier and vanishing into the freezing mist. The whole load is gone in seconds.
beats.gist: Louis's airship arms every bomb, Carl overclocks them, and the No Disassembles and Waffle Makers drop.

beats.headline: Shit Just Hit
beats.text: Carl's plan was to aim the massive-payload waffle makers at the theater housing the generator for the zarogoths. Instead, levitating up out of Larracos, he drops the entire contents of one inventory folder, titled Shit Just Hit, toward the Piccadilly: about twenty waffle makers, two no disassembles, a pair of anti-personnel cheese cutters, about five hundred impact hob-lobbers and more dynamite than he can count. His Walk on Air gives out three-quarters of the way to the edge. When the bombs hit, every window in the area shatters.
beats.gist: Carl drops a whole inventory folder of bombs on the Piccadilly, and every window nearby shatters.

relations.note: fifty of them

recap.text: Carl shrinks his thermobaric bomb to the size of a thermos, and the AI names it The Waffle Maker. In Khepri's narrow temple, as Vinata's three guards leap at him, he sets one off at his own feet, and only his god-tier immortality holds him together. Over the target, he overclocks Louis's bombs, then drops a whole folder called Shit Just Hit toward the Piccadilly, shattering every window nearby.

tagline.text: Carl's third celestial item is a hairbrush of shining gold with a jewelled handle that screams like a concert crowd as he brushes. Five minutes through long hair buys thirty hours of Shining Charisma, Speedster, a quarter more constitution and Entourage, so the hair stays long.

description.text: The Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster. This item may only be used on a male with an average hair length of 25 centimeters or longer. This item may only be used on a single person, once per day. Samson. Fabio. Michael Bolton. Jim Morrison. The entire band Stryper. Yanni. Your history is filled with luscious men whose power resided in their lovely locks. Now, it's your turn. If you use this magical hairbrush upon your head for five minutes straight, you will receive the following benefits for the next thirty hours: The Shining Charisma benefit. The Speedster benefit. Plus 25% to your constitution. Level 10 Entourage. Plus your hair will be shiny and healthy, and it will goddamn glisten.

beats.headline: It screams
beats.text: Katia notices Carl no longer ties his hair back; with his new hairbrush, he says, it is easier to keep it out. In the interview bubble, Kevin calls up Carl's very different celestial item, his third. Unlike Donut's magic hairbrush, which looks ordinary, it is shining gold with a jewelled handle, and every stroke through his hair screams like women cheering at a rock concert. When he stops, it shouts Encore! Encore! for two minutes. It works only on a man whose hair averages twenty-five centimetres, once a day.
beats.gist: Katia sees Carl's hair untied; his new gold, jewelled hairbrush screams like cheering women with each stroke.

beats.headline: Too good to give up
beats.text: The constitution alone makes the brush frustratingly invaluable, just like his boxers: now too good to give up, so the haircut he planned for when the tonic's regrowth ebbed is off. Shining Charisma lends his party a fifth of his charisma. Entourage, a bard skill for Donut, mirrors party members in illusion. Speedster flashes him across short distances in seconds, and combined with Gloom Wraith Phase it carries him much further phased. Mordecai has never seen Speedster awarded like this.
beats.gist: Carl's hairbrush is now too good to give up, so he drops his planned haircut.

beats.headline: Under the hood
beats.text: Every food box now comes out liquefied, fish-smelling and burned to a crisp, and Carl still has to eat once a day to keep his buffs. In the suit he cannot reset his foot buff, so it will expire. Nor can he brush his hair, because the hood is firmly attached to his head.
beats.gist: In the suit, the hood stays attached, so Carl cannot brush his hair.

recap.text: Katia notices Carl no longer ties his hair back; his new hairbrush, he says, makes it easier to keep out. In the interview bubble, Kevin calls up the brush: shining gold with a jewelled handle, unlike Donut's ordinary-looking one, it screams like women cheering at a rock concert with every stroke, then shouts Encore! Encore! for two minutes. It is now too good to give up, so Carl drops the haircut he had planned.

Every food box now arrives liquefied, smelling of fish and burned to a crisp, and Carl still has to eat once a day to keep his buffs. Inside the suit he cannot reset his foot buff, so it will expire. He cannot brush his hair either, because the hood is firmly attached to his head.

entities.name: Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Munificent Goddess Kina
aka: Enchanted Spiked Knee pads the Munificent Goddess Kina

tagline.text: Katia's celestial award from Club Vanquisher is a pair of divine knee pads made of a sea goddess's eyelashes: melee damage reflected, breathing underwater, swimming, and skills for eating magic items and corpses. Katia has already taken them off and given them away.
Donut wears them now, a celestial gift from Katia, and they fit her.
Penelope the pig wears them now, and they give her the same temporary deity effects as Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch.

description.text: The Enchanted Spiked Knee pads the Munificent Goddess Kina. This is a Unique item. This is a Divine Item. These are knee pads. They are literally made of the eyelashes of the sea goddess Kina, who is really just a weird, horny—and when I say horny, I am using both versions of that term—sea-urchin-like, bottom feeder of a goddess who is into some really weird stuff that makes even me blush. This item imbues the following effects: Plus 25% Damage Reflect for melee attacks. The Breathe Underwater benefit. Level 15 Swim skill. Level 10 Iron Stomach skill. Level 10 Eater of the Dead skill. As a divine item, These knee pads will imbue additional, varying benefits when they are in the presence of divine entities.

beats.headline: Made of eyelashes
beats.text: In the interview bubble, Drick calls Katia's knee pads a bit of a waste, since she plans to leave the dungeon one way or another; they were clearly awarded hoping she gives them to Carl, and they even look like his. She does not have them on, Katia says with a panicked look at Carl: she left them in the guild. The AI's voice reads the description. Iron Stomach is new this season: eat a magical item and it is destroyed, and enough of them raise intelligence a point, one to one at level ten, cursed items included. Before she unequipped and gave them away, Katia ate her way to twenty more intelligence. Eater of the Dead is the same with corpses, and raises constitution, strength or dexterity.
beats.gist: Drick calls Katia's knee pads a waste, but she left them in the guild.

beats.headline: Divine, like the patch
beats.text: Kevin asks whether Carl's divine Scavenger's Daughter patch and Katia's knee pads give the same benefits near the same deity. Generally, says Victory, but these are from Kina, so Katia's benefits would be far stronger in Kina's presence, or near certain enemies of Kina. If Katia gave a second divine item to Carl, only the more powerful benefit would apply. There are matched sets of divine armour, Victory adds, and this was prepared far ahead of time.
beats.gist: Kevin asks if Carl's patch and Katia's knee pads match; Victory says Kina's give stronger benefits.

beats.headline: They fit me
beats.text: Huanxin Jinx has slid to a stop in a circle of words of power, unable to teleport. Do you see my new knee pads, Donut asks. Aren't they lovely? A celestial item she got from Katia, and they fit her. She does not really need this with Huanxin, she admits, but the Eileithyia boon is a five hundred per cent bonus against enemies, and being partied with Carl gives her another five hundred. She starts to stalk in a circle around the heiress.
beats.gist: Donut shows off her new celestial knee pads, which fit, and starts circling Huanxin Jinx.

beats.headline: A goddess in the realm
beats.text: Eris has stopped the world, and Donut hovers in midair, frozen with a yowl. She is wearing her knee pads, which means she has also received a notification that Eris has entered the realm. The last time the goddess came, Donut was unconscious.
beats.gist: Eris freezes the world; Donut, in her knee pads, hangs yowling in midair.

beats.headline: On the pig
beats.text: Before Emberus, Carl sets Penelope down out of the line of fire and checks that she still wears the collar with the trap module, and the knee pads: the Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Munificent Goddess Kina, gifted to Katia on the ninth floor, given to Donut, and now equipped by Penelope. Among their benefits is breathing underwater. Most importantly, they give the pig the same temporary deity effects as his Scavenger's Daughter patch.
beats.gist: Carl checks that Penelope still wears the knee pads, which give the pig temporary deity effects.

relations.note: given to Donut

recap.text: Drick calls Katia's knee pads a waste, and Katia says with a panicked look at Carl that she left them in the guild. Before she gave them away, she ate magical items with Iron Stomach until she had twenty more intelligence. Victory tells Kevin that if Katia gave Carl a second divine item, only the stronger benefit would apply. Donut, wearing the pads, which fit her, stalks a circle around Huanxin Jinx.

Penelope wears the Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Munificent Goddess Kina, gifted to Katia on the ninth floor, then given to Donut. Eris stops the world, and Donut hangs frozen in midair with a yowl. Before Emberus, Carl sets Penelope down out of the line of fire and checks her collar and the knee pads, which give the pig the temporary deity effects of his Scavenger's Daughter patch.

tagline.text: The Engine of Tomorrow is Li Jun's new celestial eye, a swirling black orb that becomes a tiny clockwork engine when it works. It shows him muscles tensing and slows his sense of time in short bursts, so he sees a strike coming.
Li Jun is dead, and his sister has put his eye into herself.

beats.headline: Bullet time
beats.text: The show has already interviewed Li Jun about his celestial-tier robotic eye. On the way to the brig, Li Jun claps Carl on the shoulder, and the eye unnerves him: a swirling orb of black that, when it works, turns into a miniature clockwork engine inside the round eye. Even the name is a little freaky. The Engine of Tomorrow. It lets him see muscles tensing and slows his own perception of time in short bursts, so he can predict a strike and react with amazing speed, like bullet time in the Matrix films. He and his sister train with it nonstop.
beats.gist: Li Jun's celestial eye, the Engine of Tomorrow, lets him see muscles tense and slow time.

beats.headline: Installing
beats.text: Li Jun is dead. Over the chat Li Na tells Donut not to break the ball apart, and when Donut asks where she is, the answer comes back: she was installing her brother's eye into herself. She has also stopped the mage who was going for Harpocrates, though she is not yet strong enough to stop the god on her own.
beats.gist: Li Na stops the mage and installs her dead brother Li Jun's celestial eye into herself.

beats.headline: A face of blood
beats.text: Someone rushes into the tower behind Carl: Li Na. He had heard her say she was installing Li Jun's fake eye into herself, but the meaning hits him only now. The front of her demonic face is covered in blood. She has gouged out her own eye and replaced it with her brother's celestial-quality one, which lets her slow down time and move with incredible speed. When Carl starts to say he is sorry about her brother, she holds up a hand and stops him.
beats.gist: Li Na, her face bloody, gouges out her own eye and replaces it with her brother's celestial one.

beats.headline: Who does that?
beats.text: Zhang wipes his eyes, and then the words tumble out of him. She ripped Jun's eye out of his face after he died, and then she ripped her own eye out to install it. Who does that? That was when he should have known she was gone. He used to think he could keep her from going too crazy.
beats.gist: Zhang says she ripped out dead Jun's eye, then her own eye to install it.

beats.headline: Gears spinning
beats.text: Li Na sits in the middle of the common room, hovering a foot off the floor. She glows, and her good eye stays closed. The other, mechanical eye twitches, its clockwork gears spinning. Mordecai, Mistress Tiatha and Rosetta stand beside her, the white cleaner bot hovers nearby, and a large group has formed around them.
beats.gist: Li Na hovers a foot off the floor, her mechanical eye's gears spinning, while a crowd gathers.

relations.note: installed in place of her own eye

recap.text: Li Jun's celestial-tier eye, a swirling black orb that turns into a miniature clockwork engine, lets him see muscles tense and slow time in bursts. After Li Jun dies, Li Na tells Donut over the chat not to break the ball apart. She gouges out her own eye, installs her brother's, and rushes into the tower with her face covered in blood. When Carl starts to say he is sorry, she holds up a hand.

Zhang wipes his eyes and says she ripped Jun's eye out of his face after he died, then ripped out her own eye to install it. Who does that, he asks. Li Na hovers a foot off the common room floor, glowing, her good eye closed, the mechanical eye twitching as its clockwork gears spin. Mordecai, Mistress Tiatha and Rosetta stand beside her.

tagline.text: The patch from a Legendary Lucky Bitch Box shows a bare foot crushing four-leaf clovers. Sewn on, it deflects one fatal blow a floor into a party member instead, and Carl has no intention of wearing it.
Carl has sewn the four-leaf-clover patch onto his jacket above the Midnight Epicure patch: once a floor, a blow that would kill him goes into someone in his party.
The Four-Leaf Clover Patch has fired once on this floor, passing a spell meant to kill Carl to his party member, Penelope the pig.

description.text: Upgrade Patch. Small. This upgrade patch depicts a perfectly-perfect, mouthwatering human foot treading upon a patch of four-leaf clovers, creasing them as it presses down with gentle but oh-so-firm force. Despite their non-sentient nature, the clovers have a brief moment of awareness as they suffer, and it is fucking delicious. Delicious. Affixing this patch to an eligible garment will imbue the following benefits: Lucky Shot. A fatal blow will be deflected into the body of a party member instead. This benefit may only be used once per floor. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: Something he would never wear
beats.text: Carl dropped a bomb at his own feet, and it only worked because he had god-tier immortality; the achievement says so, at length, and pays out a Legendary Lucky Bitch Box. Inside is a small patch of four-leaf clovers smashed under a bare foot. Sewn on, it deflects a fatal blow into the body of a party member, once per floor. Carl sighs. Even with Donut's Cockroach skill he would never risk wearing it, however valuable, and he does not want the others to know what it does, in case they try to talk him into it.
beats.gist: Carl's bomb at his own feet earns a clover patch he won't wear.

beats.headline: Sewn on, not straight
beats.text: Carl has said he is still leaving Donut's party for this floor. With nowhere else to work, he takes off his jacket at the table, grabs a sewing kit and sews on the four-leaf-clover patch, above the Midnight Epicure patch. Lucky Shot: a fatal blow deflected into the body of a party member, once per floor. Donut, coming in with news of an upgrade for Mongo's saddle, suddenly notices what he is doing. Carl, she says, it's not straight.
beats.gist: Carl sews the four-leaf-clover patch above his Midnight Epicure patch, and Donut says it's not straight.

beats.headline: Penny takes it
beats.text: Emberus, pinned and vulnerable, hurls a fire incineration spell straight at Carl's chest, one that under any other circumstances would have finished him instantly. Your Four-Leaf Clover Patch has activated! His party member Penny receives the attack. Donut swapped her out moments ago, to Taranis's feet outside and the same area as Khepri, whose god effect has made her invulnerable for ninety seconds. Out at the arena entrance, Taranis is bent over the tiny bubbling pile of plasma that is Penelope. She is not dead, but she will be if she does not heal within the next ninety seconds.
beats.gist: Penny takes the fire spell meant for Carl, because his Four-Leaf Clover Patch swaps her into its path.

recap.text: Carl drops a bomb at his own feet and survives only because he has god-tier immortality, and the achievement says so at length before paying out a Legendary Lucky Bitch Box. Inside is a patch of four-leaf clovers smashed under a bare foot. Sewn on, it deflects a fatal blow into a party member, once per floor. Carl sighs, refuses to wear it even with Donut's Cockroach skill, and hides what it does from the others.

Carl has told Donut he is still leaving her party for this floor. At the table he sews the four-leaf-clover patch on above the Midnight Epicure patch, and Donut, arriving with news of an upgrade for Mongo's saddle, says it is not straight. When pinned Emberus hurls a fire incineration spell at Carl's chest, the patch activates and Penny takes the blow. Taranis bends over the bubbling plasma that is Penelope.

tagline.text: Zhang's Cape of Odds is his celestial prize from the fight at Club Vanquisher, a white cape printed with an archery target. It adds fifteen per cent to every stat and, once an hour, offers a spin of three hundred and thirty-three outcomes, sixty-six of them bad.
Zhang ripped the cape off and threw it on the table when he despaired of stopping Li Na, and pulled it back on to go and tell her the new plan.

beats.headline: Three hundred and thirty-three outcomes
beats.text: On the way to the brig, Zhang's new cape flutters behind him: white, with the black, blue, red and yellow circles of an archery target. It was his prize in the celestial box. Unactivated, it gives fifteen per cent to every stat and a level 10 Dodge skill, taking his Dodge from eleven to fourteen. Once an hour it offers Roll the Dice: 333 outcomes, most great, a few epic such as Death Ray, and 66 bad, none fatal, all temporary, the worst Summon the God Who Hates You Most. After 19 spins he may pick. He will not use it unless he must.
beats.gist: Zhang's celestial cape offers an hourly Roll the Dice of 333 outcomes, and he will avoid it.

beats.headline: Thrown on the table
beats.text: In the next race, Zhang says, he will kill Torpedo, their octopus mount, so the system kills Li Na, and him with her. Carl tells him that will not work any more. She is killing people, Zhang says, and she has stopped talking to him. He meets Carl's eyes, rips the target cape off and throws it on the table. He wishes he had died in the temple. Carl stares at the cape. The AI gave it to Zhang after he survived the battle inside Club Vanquisher, a fight he went to only because they needed his help.
beats.gist: Zhang says he will kill Torpedo so Li Na dies, then throws down his cape.

beats.headline: Back on, with purpose
beats.text: Elle, Zhang and Tran pull back from the table with a new plan. Zhang grabs his target cape and pulls it back on, standing straight and tall and with purpose. The three of them are going back to the safe room to try to reach Li Na and tell her what they mean to do. Carl whispers good luck to Elle, and she returns it, looking over her shoulder at Donut.
beats.gist: Elle, Zhang and Tran return to the safe room to tell Li Na their plan.

recap.text: Zhang's new cape, white with the black, blue, red and yellow circles of an archery target, flutters behind him on the way to the brig. Unactivated, it gives fifteen per cent to every stat and a level 10 Dodge skill, lifting his Dodge from eleven to fourteen. Once an hour it offers Roll the Dice, 333 outcomes, 66 of them bad. After 19 spins he may pick. He will not use it unless he must.

Zhang tells Carl that in the next race he will kill Torpedo, their octopus mount, so the system kills Li Na and him with her. Carl says that will not work any more, and Zhang answers that she is killing people and has stopped talking to him. He rips off the target cape the AI gave him after Club Vanquisher and throws it on the table.

tagline.text: Edgar is inking a tattoo onto a shaved patch of Donut's right flank to carry Bijanbi, a Dinner Bell variant taken from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, and Milk is to etch words of power over it to raise the spell's level. He is drawing a dog.

Edgar inked Donut's dog tattoo on her right flank in a hurry: a simple line drawing of a dog that lifts its leg and licks itself. It holds Bijanbi, a variant of Dinner Bell, and Milk's words of power have pushed it to fifteen until the ink fades.
Donut can cast Bijanbi together with her Astral Paw, and she thinks the stupid dog tattoo has just bitten her.

beats.headline: It has to be a tattoo
beats.text: It has to be a tattoo, Rosetta says, and Milk will etch words of power over it to raise the spell's level. Hamzo would not reach wide enough, so they chose a Dinner Bell variant from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, which Edgar has extracted; it used to be called Heel, and this season it is Bijanbi. Donut never agreed to a tattoo. She will do it only if Carl gets a matching one. Rosetta shaves a small, round bald patch on her right flank, and Edgar, the poker in his mouth, says what he is drawing: a dog.
beats.gist: Rosetta shaves Donut's flank and Edgar draws a dog, because Donut wants Carl tattooed too.

beats.headline: Two very rude achievements
beats.text: Donut does not look at the tattoo on her flank. She stares forward with quiet dignity while Edgar works, and then he drops his tattoo stick and asks if it worked. Why are you asking me, she cries. She has two very rude achievements, one calling her a traitor, one paying out a stolen catalytic converter. And the spell, Bijanbi, only level two, came from a god called Wepwawet in the Court of Nekhebit; she may worship him now, and Odette too. Cover it up, she says; they will get it lasered off on the next floor.
beats.gist: Donut sits through Edgar's tattooing, then learns the tattoo gave her two rude achievements and the spell Bijanbi.

beats.headline: Words of power
beats.text: Not quite yet, says Milk: it must be temporarily above level eight. Her pen writes over the tattoo in a script the system calls Words of Power, first in black ink and then purple, a calligraphy-guild magic. The letters glow and move, and under them Carl sees the shape: a simple, rather adorable line drawing of a dog. It lifts its leg and starts to lick itself. Edgar doubts it is sentient. Donut gasps: the spell is level fifteen. Temporary, Milk says; it fades with the ink, but it helps the training.
beats.gist: Milk's pen writes Words of Power over Donut's dog tattoo, and a line-drawn dog starts licking itself.

beats.headline: It bites
beats.text: Cannibals throw themselves at the truck's shield. Donut's Astral Paw sweeps the bridge clear, far smaller than her War Crime, which she cannot cast again until the twelfth floor; the Paw is stronger now, with an eight-hour cooldown. The combined version with Bijanbi is not a new spell, she says: she can cast the two together. Then she jumps, hits the cab's roof and spins round. She thinks the stupid dog tattoo on her butt just bit her.
beats.gist: Donut's Astral Paw sweeps the bridge clear of cannibals, then the dog tattoo on her butt bites her.

relations.note: words of power written over it
her plan, and she shaves the patch
Rosetta's plan ties the spell in with the bonus from War Crime

recap.text: Donut lies still while Rosetta shaves a round bald patch on her right flank and Edgar, the poker in his mouth, tattoos a dog over it. She agreed only because Carl gets a matching one. Milk writes Words of Power over it in black and then purple ink, and the line-drawn dog lifts its leg and licks itself. Bijanbi, from Wepwawet, jumps from level two to a temporary level fifteen.

Donut's Astral Paw sweeps the bridge clear of the cannibals throwing themselves at the truck's shield. It is far smaller than her War Crime, which she cannot cast again until the twelfth floor, and the Paw is stronger now, with an eight-hour cooldown. She says the combined version with Bijanbi is no new spell, only the two cast together. Then she jumps, hits the cab's roof and spins round, certain the stupid dog tattoo on her butt just bit her.

tagline.text: The adept's fountain pen is the most basic of all the calligrapher's implements, and the System calls it the most versatile item anyone can own. Milk gives it to Carl along with a wineskin of Stayfast Ink.

description.text: Adept’s fountain pen. The most basic of all the calligrapher’s implements. How much grief, how much suffering has been caused by one of these things? Yet, how much joy? That whole saying, the pen is mightier than the sword, is one of the few human world metaphors that I believe to be universally true, especially since swords are terrible, barbaric weapons. This is the most versatile item anyone can own. What will you do with it? Write a book that changes everything? …

beats.headline: Something else from Milk
beats.text: Milk has told Carl about the book she once wrote her recipes in, and how all she wrote after she changed inks faded and disappeared. She hands him a wineskin of Stayfast Ink, and then something else: a fountain pen. Adept's fountain pen, the most basic of all the calligrapher's implements, and by the System's reckoning the most versatile item anyone can own. Carl has a recipe book, says Donut, with goblin and chicken recipes. I heard, says Milk. He also has another book, one they all have: the Book of Voodoo. Anything he writes in it will be given to everybody who already has it.
beats.gist: Milk gives Carl a wineskin of Stayfast Ink and Adept's fountain pen.

relations.note: given together

recap.text: Milk tells Carl that every recipe she wrote after changing inks faded away. She hands him a wineskin of Stayfast Ink and an Adept's fountain pen, the most basic calligrapher's implement and, by the System's reckoning, the most versatile item anyone can own. Donut mentions Carl's goblin and chicken recipes, and Milk replies that he also has the Voodoo one they all have: whatever he writes in it goes to everyone who already holds it.

tagline.text: Stayfast Ink comes in a wineskin, 825 ml, enough for several chonky books, and nothing will ever make it fade. Milk gives it to Carl with an adept's fountain pen, after telling him the recipes she once wrote in a different ink have faded away.

description.text: Stayfast Ink, 825 ml. Enough ink for several chonky books. Warning: this shit stains, so be careful. Nothing will ever make it fade. Nothing. Not even distance or time or the death of a star.

beats.headline: Ink that does not fade
beats.text: After Donut's dog tattoo, Milk tells Carl there are more magic systems than he can imagine, dozens with ink and calligraphy and maps alone, and that inks and letters that shine the brightest burn out the fastest. She had a book once and wrote her recipes in it, then switched to a different ink to share them more widely, and only recently learned that all she wrote after the change faded and disappeared. She hands him a wineskin: Stayfast Ink, 825 ml. Then a fountain pen, the adept's, the most basic of a calligrapher's implements. He has another book, she adds, the Book of Voodoo, and anything he writes in it reaches everyone who has it.
beats.gist: Milk gives Carl Stayfast Ink and an adept's fountain pen, since her old ink faded.

relations.note: Carl takes Milk's story of her book to be about the Cookbook

recap.text: Milk tells Carl that dozens of magic systems exist in ink, calligraphy and maps alone, and that the brightest inks and letters burn out fastest. She switched inks in her recipe book to share it more widely, and only now learns that everything she wrote after the change has faded. She hands him a wineskin of Stayfast Ink, 825 ml, and an adept's fountain pen.

tagline.text: A Mini Tactical Nuke rides on the back half of the biggest Reaver sentry dogs. When Elle froze one solid, Carl hauled the burning block of ice into his inventory before it could go off.
Carl still has his, attached to its dog, and keeps quiet about it; Samantha has one of her own hidden up her neck hole.

beats.headline: Into the inventory, frozen
beats.text: Robot sentry dogs pour out of the holes in the Reaver castle's great wall: Reaver Industries Security Sentry Dog, the Ditch Digger, optional anti-personnel explosive. One of the larger ones, the size of a lion, carries a massive glowing bomb notification on its back half, and before Carl can examine it, an Elle spell turns it into a ball of ice. He rushes forward and lifts the block. It burns, but it goes into his inventory before the dog can explode. The bomb says Mini Tactical Nuke. Fall back, he shouts.
beats.gist: Carl lifts an iced sentry dog's glowing bomb into his inventory before it explodes, then shouts fall back.

beats.headline: The castle goes up
beats.text: Carl tells Juice Box to drop the No Disassembles Louis carries and get clear, then runs with the others, shouts for everyone to hit the deck, dives atop Donut and triggers them remotely. The pulse should fry every robot dog at once, but the bombs themselves would still... The Reaver castle explodes from the inside out, flinging them all. Carl's bones break and his hearing goes again, and he decides the bombs are much smaller than he feared: probably only one of the mini nukes went off, maybe two. Everyone seems okay but Jamal, whose legs the initial No Disassemble has wrecked.
beats.gist: Carl sets off the Reaver castle's dog bombs from atop Donut; the blast wrecks Jamal's legs.

beats.headline: Up her neck hole
beats.text: Samantha thinks her child died in the acid, and she is quite certain it is Tish's fault, so once this is done she is going to plant the nuke she stole from Buster, the robot dog she bonded with, up at the college. You have a nuke up your neck hole, Carl asks. He has one too, still attached to one of the dogs, but he is not about to tell her he has one of the dangerous robots. Nobody is nuking anyone, he says. Tell us the plan to save Louis.
beats.gist: Samantha blames Tish for her child's death and wants to nuke the college; Carl says no.

beats.headline: Still in stock
beats.text: Carl dropped every bomb he carried when he fled out of Larracos, and he needs to restock. All he has left are the big bombs, such as Carl's Doomsday Scenario and the tactical nuke still attached to a robot dog. That reminds him that Samantha also has a nuke hidden up her neck hole, and it has to come out as soon as possible.
beats.gist: Carl, low on bombs after fleeing Larracos, remembers that Samantha has a nuke up her neck hole.

relations.note: carried by the sentry dogs guarding the Reaver castle
one of her own, taken from her robot dog

recap.text: Carl shouts a retreat after an Elle spell freezes a lion-sized Reaver sentry dog carrying a Mini Tactical Nuke, and he lifts the burning block into his inventory before it can explode. He dives atop Donut and triggers the other bombs remotely, and the Reaver castle blows apart from the inside out, wrecking Jamal's legs. Samantha says she will plant her stolen nuke at the college, and Carl keeps his own quiet.

Carl dropped every bomb he carried when he fled Larracos, and now he needs to restock. All he has left are the big ones: Carl's Doomsday Scenario and the tactical nuke still attached to a Reaver sentry dog. The sight of that robot dog reminds him that Samantha has a nuke hidden up her neck hole, and it has to come out as soon as possible.

entities.name: A Banquet Fit for a Princess

tagline.text: A Banquet Fit for a Princess is Donut's own book from the crawlers leaving the dungeon: pictures and kind words about her, and on each page a skill or spell its painter gave up. Eating a page lends her the spell for a short while.
Every page in it that offered lightning magic has been removed, and Donut carries a dozen lightning spells into Club Scolopendra.

beats.headline: A present in Larracos
beats.text: In the rings around them, thousands of crawlers who mean to take a deal on the next floor, and former crawlers going home, look down as Milk announces a present. Carl's Book of Voodoo splits in two. Donut shouts that she has a book called A Banquet Fit for a Princess, filled with pictures and nice things about her, and spells. Milk taught the leavers to take out a skill or spell and paint it onto a page, three each: one for Carl, one for Donut, one for anyone. They lose it for good.
