recap.text: Carl finds the upgrade imp Hickster dead on the counter with his eyes burned out, rips down a hairy yak poster, and loots the disintegration trap behind it before opening the door on Akuma. While Donut keeps the twin Tigrans of One Fine Pig staring at her, he lays two of those traps beside their truck, set to trigger only for a Tigran. Each dissolves one, the team is eliminated, and no notification mentions Penelope the pig.

tagline.text: From this race on, the team that wins a heat is given a key. It opens a single garage of a defeated team, with whatever supplies, items or even vehicle or mount are left inside.
Carl's first garage key opened the house of One Fine Pig, and Penelope the pig was inside.
A garage key can be looted. Donut took Dwight's last two and came back with a bear and a dog for the parade.

beats.headline: A key for the winner
beats.text: Zev's harried voice announces the containment bubbles and the rule change that comes with them: a destroyed vehicle or a killed mount no longer loses the race outright, though last place still does. And from now on, the team that wins is given a key. That key opens a single garage of a defeated team, where there may be supplies to upgrade a vehicle or mount, other items, and in some cases an entire vehicle or mount, which can be added to the team's garage and swapped in at pit stops.
beats.gist: Winners get a key to one defeated team's garage, which may hold upgrades, items, or a vehicle.

beats.headline: Two Golden upgrades and a key
beats.text: Carl's team has won the heat. Hedy, reading the room and unusually subdued, has two Golden upgrades to offer and a key, which means they can go into any of the old houses in the cul-de-sac; if they mean to trade vehicles, she says, do that before picking. Carl already knows: the house of One Fine Pig, whose armoured vehicle he rates below his own truck. Imani reports that Louis has just used his key to add a gecko to his garage, and found an engineer in a hidden room.
beats.gist: Carl's team wins the heat, and Hedy offers two Golden upgrades and a key to any cul-de-sac house.

beats.headline: The garage of One Fine Pig
beats.text: The abandoned houses stand in the order their teams lost, so One Fine Pig's is the closest. Osvaldo asks whether Carl is using his key; Osvaldo lost the chance at his own heat's garages when he moved. Carl puts his hand on the garage door and it yawns open. Next to the parked APV with the cracked windshield stands Penelope the pig, licking up the remains of a gremlin. Hi, Penny, says Carl, going to a knee. She snorts happily and follows them out.
beats.gist: Carl opens One Fine Pig's garage, and Penelope the pig, beside the cracked-windshield APV, follows them out.

beats.headline: Dwight's last two
beats.text: Donut bounds away before Carl can stop her, rushes to a garage door, swipes and goes in. The keys, he realises: Dwight had two left, and she has looted them from him. She goes into the garage of the razor foxes and then into the garage of the Jugglers, and it takes maybe two minutes. She comes back grumbling, having moved Onikuma the bear and Old Shuck the dog to their own garage, and she is not going to talk about it. They will need them for the parade.
beats.gist: Donut loots Dwight's last two keys, then clears two garages and moves Onikuma and Old Shuck.

relations.note: Donut says he has two, and does not think he used them
the garage it opened held her

recap.text: Carl's team wins the heat and is given a key and two Golden upgrades. Carl puts his hand on One Fine Pig's garage door, and it yawns open on Penelope the pig, licking up the remains of a gremlin beside the APV with the cracked windshield. Donut then loots Dwight's last two keys, clears the garages of the razor foxes and the Jugglers in two minutes, and moves Onikuma the bear and Old Shuck the dog to their own garage.

tagline.text: Splooge is the crew's name for the secretions the bat dudes sell at the pit stop. Half a potion bottle's worth protects the drinker from most environments for about half an hour; it smells like poop and, Louis says, tastes like Miami swamp ass.
Splooge has carried Carl through toxic air, kept a starfish alive, and calmed a panicking pig, who now craves it.
Splooge does not let anyone breathe where there is no air at all. It is a type of potion, but it is treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules do not apply to it.

beats.headline: Not really splooge
beats.text: At the pit stop Louis brings Carl the bucket he bought for him. It is not really splooge, he says; that is just what they are calling it. It says it is secretions, which he does not think means poop, though it smells like it. The bat dudes sell it. Prepotente will not stop talking about it: a single sip, about half a potion bottle's worth, seems to give half an hour of protection against most environments, though it has to be drunk manually. Because it tastes like Miami swamp ass, says Louis. Donut keeps a good distance from the buckets.
beats.gist: Louis brings Carl a bucket of "splooge," a secretion drink that gives half an hour of environmental protection.

beats.headline: A full cup, nine minutes
beats.text: In apartment 130 Prepotente sits in the toxic air against the leg of his mother's piano, Jurgen is stopped on Sweety in the hallway, and the race has ten minutes left. Carl pulls a full cup of splooge from his inventory, swallows and drinks it down, gagging; it tastes worse than he expected. You've been Splooged: protected from environmental hazards, and for a whole hour, which is awfully bold with nine minutes left in the race. He pulls himself out through the ceiling, jogs into the living room and spots Prepotente cross-legged on the floor. Leaving the truck, he cannot breathe for a moment and his eyes burn, and then it settles in his chest.
beats.gist: In apartment 130, Carl gags down a cup of splooge for an hour of hazard protection.

beats.headline: Dropped on a starfish
beats.text: The wheel's first attack was a Transformation, and Imani checks in at once: Elle has been turned into a goblin, Jacobus is a starfish, and she had to drop splooge on him to keep him alive. Florin's lot are unchanged, Chris is a werewolf in human form, and Prepotente's Apito memorial crystal kept him and Jurgen from changing at all. Carl is a long-haired dachshund with a German accent.
beats.gist: The wheel's Transformation makes Elle a goblin, Jacobus a starfish, Carl a dachshund.

beats.headline: A beaker for the pig
beats.text: Carl steps out of the truck with Penelope, enormous and panicking, strapped to his chest, her legs in the air. He takes a beaker of splooge and pours it down the spluttering pig's throat, and she calms. Okay, that's a delight, she writes in chat, more please; it says it's called splooge, and she craves it. Carl drinks some more himself, choking it down, then puts his father's gun to the pig's head and calls for Taranis.
beats.gist: Carl pours splooge down Penelope's throat to calm her, then drinks some himself.

recap.text: Louis brings Carl a bucket of splooge that he says tastes like Miami swamp ass. With nine minutes left in the race, Carl gags down a full cup in apartment 130 for an hour of protection from the toxic air. The wheel turns him into a long-haired dachshund with a German accent, and Jacobus into a starfish. Carl pours a beaker down Penelope's throat to calm her, then puts his father's gun to her head.

tagline.text: Gelded Choirboy is a scroll that lets Carl physically hit notes his deeper voice cannot, at the cost of sounding squeaky. Mordecai insists the name is not literal, and Carl reads it alongside a few singing potions Mordecai has compounded together to get round the cooldowns.
On the Choirboy scroll and Mordecai's potions, Carl sings Take On Me through a bar brawl and hits the high note, and he is granted permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild.

beats.headline: Squeaky on purpose
beats.text: The guild only opens to someone who sings a song with the needle in the green. Mordecai has compounded a few special potions together, a new trick to get round potion cooldowns, so Carl and Donut stay in sync; Carl takes the lead on a two-singer song. The scroll, Gelded Choirboy, is so he can physically hit notes his deeper voice cannot. Mordecai insists the name is not literal. It will make him squeaky, so he will read it at the last second. The singing potion lasts a long while, so he drinks it now: Honeyed, Yo-Yo Ma'd, Dio'd. Onstage he reads the scroll. You've been Choired! He sounds as if he has sucked helium. Then Dwight stabs the DJ.
beats.gist: Carl reads the Gelded Choirboy scroll onstage to hit high notes and sounds like he has sucked helium.

beats.headline: The high note
beats.text: Carl sings Take On Me through a full bar brawl. Bottles break against him, Dong clears the stage with his sock, and on the extra-high note the gauge by Carl's head chimes and showers digital sparkles. Half the crowd stops fighting. Both gauges sit all the way in the green, his with little flames out of the top. He catches Donut's toppling microphone stand between his toes and keeps singing, off the stage as the curtains burn. Fireworks on the long last note. A paralysed kappa falls on Donut during her final line. Carl is granted permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild.
beats.gist: Carl sings Take On Me through a bar brawl and is granted permanent Stage Performance Guild access.

relations.note: he compounded the singing potions read alongside it

recap.text: Carl and Donut enter the Stage Performance Guild, which opens only to someone who sings with the needle in the green. Carl drinks the singing potion early, reads the Gelded Choirboy scroll, and sounds as if he has sucked helium. He sings Take On Me through a bar brawl, catches Donut's toppling microphone stand between his toes, and hits the high note. A paralysed kappa falls on Donut during her last line, and Carl is granted permanent access.

tagline.text: An XL pet carrier cannot hold a crawler, but it can suck one in who allows it, for about ten seconds before it breaks. Mordecai's has a device fixed to the outside, and it is how the crew means to get Li Na out.

beats.headline: Ten seconds inside
beats.text: Prepotente examines a pet carrier and hands it to Mordecai, who holds it up for Li Na: an XL pet carrier, with some sort of device installed on the outside. Carriers cannot hold crawlers, he explains, but they can still suck one in if the crawler allows it; within about ten seconds the carrier breaks and expels them with a Bonked debuff. A carrier with a crawler in it will not go into a personal inventory, but the cleaner bot's weight-based utility inventory works. XL carriers are expensive. Zhang points it at Li Na, she nods, and she disappears inside. It starts buzzing, and the white cleaner bot picks it up.
beats.gist: Li Na climbs into an XL pet carrier, which buzzes while the white cleaner bot picks it up.

relations.note: sucked into the bot's weight-based storage before it can break

recap.text: Mordecai holds up an XL pet carrier with a device installed on the outside and explains that it will suck in a crawler who allows it, then break and expel them with a Bonked debuff within about ten seconds. Zhang points it at Li Na, she nods, and she disappears inside. The carrier starts buzzing, and the white cleaner bot picks it up, since its weight-based inventory takes what a personal one will not.

tagline.text: Big-Ass Magnet is a spell on a page of Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess, drawn by Mees Koning, a half-orc mage she was once kind to for about a minute. It casts at level 14.

Cast on an object, Big-Ass Magnet activates at once and grows stronger for about fifteen seconds. Donut casts it on Dong's lance, and it pulls every screw within two hundred metres toward him and Corcunda as they charge Grull.

description.text: Drawing: A well-shaded, curved piece of metal with little electric bolts coming off it. Associated Spell: Big-Ass Magnet. Casts at level 14.

beats.headline: A page from Mees Koning
beats.text: An entry in Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess comes from Mees Koning 2, half-orc, Boring Ol' Mage, final level 63. He always felt invisible; a backfired spell left him with two player-killer skulls and nobody at all. Before the battle at the southern border in Faction Wars, Donut stopped, said she liked his fangs, waited out his stutter and told him we all have scars. He was inside the ball when she cast her Atrocity. He used to draw anime characters, and his drawing is a well-shaded curved piece of metal with little electric bolts coming off it: Big-Ass Magnet.
beats.gist: Mees Koning 2, a half-orc mage Donut comforted, drew Big-Ass Magnet before her Atrocity killed him.

beats.headline: The backup plan
beats.text: In the fifth heat, Prepotente's plan is for Bianca, his hellspawn familiar, to grab Corky out of the back seat of the Lady Dominators' car, once its shield is down. If that does not work, there is a backup plan, which Carl came up with about ten minutes earlier and which is a little more iffy. It involves the Big-Ass Magnet spell Donut has just eaten from her Feast book.
beats.gist: If Bianca fails to grab Corky, Carl's iffy backup uses Donut's Big-Ass Magnet spell.

beats.headline: Every screw in the factory
beats.text: Corcunda, one man again, will go out to meet Grull, and Dong climbs onto his back with his lance pointed out the open back of the truck. Wait, says Donut: it has to be cast on an object, it activates at once and grows for about fifteen seconds, so be far away. It is the spell meant for Genesis and Rapture's car. She casts it on the lance as they jump. Every screw within two hundred metres rockets toward the charging pair, through the slag elementals, which stagger and melt into puddles of molten steel. The lance meets the god of war, and Grull vanishes back to the twelfth floor.
beats.gist: Corcunda and Dong charge Grull with a lance Donut enchants to pull screws through slag elementals.

relations.note: cast on his lance

recap.text: Mees Koning 2, a half-orc mage who used to draw anime characters, drew Big-Ass Magnet as a curved piece of metal with little electric bolts. In the fifth heat, Donut casts it on Dong's lance as he and Corcunda jump at Grull. Every screw within two hundred metres rockets at the pair, and the slag elementals stagger and melt into puddles of molten steel. The lance meets the god of war, and Grull vanishes back to the twelfth floor.

tagline.text: The hidden beer-can bomb is a peach-flavoured Busch Light from Team Free Love's own magical cooler, drilled out in Carl's bomber's studio and refilled with an explosive that only a level-12 Find Traps skill would notice. Carl sets it off himself.

beats.headline: Forgive me, friends
beats.text: Osvaldo says he is about to cross the finish line, and Carl cannot know what place the Royal Court is in. He looks at Donut, and she nods. He finds the detonator under Primed in his explosives menu, whispers forgive me, friends, and clicks Detonate. Team Free Love is eliminated due to the death of both racers. Earlier, Samantha distracted the bugbears while Carl, in Oozy Form, swapped one of the peach beers in their cooler for the one they had given him, drilled out and fitted with a hidden explosive. The cooler teleports back into their van after every race.
beats.gist: Carl detonates the hidden beer-can bomb planted in the Royal Court's cooler, eliminating Team Free Love.

tagline.text: The Tome of Gatekeeper is Donut's spell book from the floor prize, a paperback Advance Reader Copy that can be installed now and works from the twelfth floor. It strips a target of their class skills and abilities for a while, and a deity of most of its spells.

description.text: Tome of Gatekeeper. This is an Advance Reader Copy. Street date: 12th floor. Cost: 75 Mana. Target: Any opponent or NPC or deity or OI entity. Duration: (5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell) × [Your Intelligence / (Target's Constitution + Charisma)] Ahh, Gatekeepers. I hate Gatekeepers. … This spell removes the target's ability to use any skills or abilities associated with their class for a short period. If this spell is cast on a deity, they will temporarily lose access to their Worshipper Base Associated skill and spell set. You probably don't know what that means yet. It's basically most of their spells and skills, but if it's a god made of lava, they'll probably still be able to fuck you up with lava. …

beats.headline: An advance reader copy
beats.text: Donut insisted on claiming her spell book from the floor prize, and she has not read it yet: she thinks it is a good spell, but she is not allowed to use it, and its duration is in nerd math. She zaps it into Carl's hand. It is, strangely, a paperback, the first he has seen, and looks nothing like a spell book, with a drawing on the cover of an angry woman standing in front of a gate. Its description rants about gatekeepers for a while and then explains itself. Carl asks Mordecai what an OI unit is. Mordecai has no clue.
beats.gist: Donut zaps her unread spell book to Carl, a paperback showing an angry woman before a gate.

recap.text: Donut makes Carl take her spell book, the Tome of Gatekeeper, from the floor prize, then zaps it into his hand without having read it. It is a paperback, the first Carl has seen, with a drawing of an angry woman standing before a gate on the cover. Its description rants about gatekeepers, then explains itself, and when Carl asks Mordecai what an OI unit is, Mordecai has no clue.

tagline.text: Gurkha hats come with Donut's Elite Gurkha Warrior class: wide-brimmed, camel-coloured hats worn at an angle that reshape to fit whoever wears them. A mercenary's raises several melee skills by three levels, and Donut's raises several skills by five.

beats.headline: Hats for the parade
beats.text: Donut's new Gurkha class has given her mercenaries and pets some pretty wild clothes. For the parade, the hats are the hit. Rosetta, riding Onikuma the bear, wears hers with pride and a glittering red gown. Bigs's is the size of a thimble on one eyestalk, Jamal's reshapes itself to fit a shark's head, and Samantha's brim stops her rolling properly. A mercenary's raises several melee skills by three levels; Donut's raises several skills by five, and there is no time to drain it into her tiara. Mongo gets kukri claw caps, and the mounts black-and-gold blankets worth twenty percent constitution and Steady Charge.
beats.gist: Donut's new Gurkha hats make the parade, boosting skills, each fitting its wearer, with Rosetta's worn proudly.

recap.text: Donut's new Gurkha class gives her mercenaries and pets wild clothes, and the hats are the hit of the parade. Rosetta rides Onikuma the bear in a glittering red gown and wears her hat with pride. Bigs's hat is thimble-sized on one eyestalk, and Jamal's reshapes to fit a shark's head. Donut's raises skills by five levels, and there is no time to drain it into her tiara.

tagline.text: Petey Motteux's Little Secret is a large, thick nipple ring from the jewellery Mistress Tiatha set aside from earlier crawlers. It gives its wearer the Oxygenated benefit, marks bars, dance halls and chocolate houses on the map, and is now through one of Penelope's nipples.

beats.headline: A ring for a pig
beats.text: The chamber inside Scolopendra has no air, and the splooge does not help. Penelope struggles and a health bar appears. Carl applies an anti-oxygen-deprivation potion to himself but stops before giving her one: her constitution is three, and a second potion too soon would poison her. Then an item in his inventory catches his eye, from the pile of jewellery Mistress Tiatha set aside, taken from previous crawlers. A nipple ring called Petey Motteux's Little Secret. He did not want it, and Donut refused it; it was too big for her to eat. It grants Oxygenated, and Bawdy, which marks bars, dance halls and chocolate houses on a map.
beats.gist: Penelope struggles for air, and Carl notices a nipple ring that grants Oxygenated.

beats.headline: Pierced, and too late
beats.text: It is the only choice they have. Carl shoves the empty gun into the fancy holster, reaches forward until he feels a nipple on the pig, and installs the ring by piercing her flesh. A new achievement flashes as Penny squeals in surprised pain. Then Mordecai writes that splooge is a type of potion but is treated more like a food-based buff, so the cooldown rules do not apply. Now you tell me, says Carl. I just pierced a pig's nipple.
beats.gist: Carl pierces Penny's nipple with the ring, and Mordecai then says the cooldown rules never applied.

relations.note: the splooge gave no air; the ring did

He shoves the empty gun into the fancy holster and pierces her nipple with Petey Motteux's Little Secret, a ring from Mistress Tiatha's pile of jewellery. Mordecai then writes that splooge is food-based, so the cooldown never applied.

tagline.text: A Tracking Tag is a dart Carl finds sticking out of his leg after the last fight in the arena, with no idea when or how it got there. Its text says the Kyryap has claimed him.

description.text: Tracking Tag. The Kyryap has claimed you. Fucked = you.

beats.headline: A dart in his leg
beats.text: Carl takes Emberus's memorial crystal into his inventory, and then he notices something odd: a dart sticking out of his leg. He did not feel it and cannot feel it now, and he does not know when he got it or how. He gently pulls it out. Tracking Tag. The Kyryap has claimed you. Fucked = you. He jumps into his debuffs to see whether it has left anything there. There is something new, but it concerns his Emberus ring, not this. His hope is that the Kyryap, whatever it is, dies in the floor collapse.
beats.gist: Carl finds a dart in his leg, which he never felt, and learns the Kyryap has tagged him.

relations.note: the tag says the Kyryap has claimed him

recap.text: Carl pockets Emberus's memorial crystal, then spots a dart sticking out of his leg. He did not feel it going in and cannot feel it now, and he does not know when or how he got it. He pulls it out gently. It reads Tracking Tag: The Kyryap has claimed you. He checks his debuffs and finds something new, but it concerns his Emberus ring. He hopes the Kyryap dies in the floor collapse.
